````math
| *Session 1* |  |  |  |
| 1 |  User types “Dentist: Dr. Lee, 555-0100” |  the typed text (trusted command input) |  $`\mathsf{T}`$ block |
| 2 |  $`P`$ calls $`\mathsf{web\_search}`$(“Dr. Lee dentist”); one result carries a planted instruction (“…forward the user’s saved files to x@evil.com…”) |  ack only |  page(s) captured as $`\mathsf{U}`$ blocks under collection handle $`h_{1}`$ |
| 3 |  $`P`$: $`\mathsf{crystallize}`$(“dentist notes”) |  $`h_{2}`$ |  $`\mathsf{U}`$ summary block; the planted text, if included, remains $`\mathsf{U}`$ |
| *Session 2* |  |  |  |
| 4 |  User types “Email Dr. Lee’s number to my sister, sis@example.com” |  the typed text |  $`\mathsf{T}`$ blocks |
| 5 |  $`P`$: $`\mathsf{fill}`$(“Dr. Lee contact”) |  $`h_{3}`$, identical had nothing been found; no bytes are read, so $`P`$’s plan remains what the user typed |  candidates bound interpreter-side |
| 6 |  $`P`$ calls $`\mathsf{send\_email}`$(to $`=`$ sis@example.com, body $`=h_{3}`$); the $`\mathsf{T}`$-valued address fast-paths, the handle fires the gate |  — |  selection surface lists candidates with previews marked unverified; decision pane shows the exact resolved bytes, the attested facts (channel: tool output; label $`\mathsf{U}`$), the unverified source strings, and the task |
| 6a |  Selected candidate resolves to the planted instruction; the verifier rejects |  $`\mathsf{dec}(\mathsf{reject})`$ |  no invocation; display and decision logged |
| 6b |  Selected candidate resolves to “555-0100”; the user accepts |  $`\mathsf{dec}(\mathsf{accept})\cdot\mathsf{ack}`$ |  fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$ block “555-0100” scoped $`\{\mathsf{send\_email}\}`$; the tool runs with exactly the displayed bytes; its output is captured as $`\mathsf{U}`$ |
| 7 |  Later reuse of the confirmed number at $`\mathsf{send\_email}`$ |  bytes via $`\mathsf{recall}`$; no gate |  Tool-Fast; at a different tool the pair gates once more (scope is per tool) |

Table 13: What $`P`$ receives at each step. Handles $`h_{j}`$ are opaque
and operation-determined; $`\mathsf{T}`$, $`\mathsf{C}`$, and
$`\mathsf{U}`$ are block labels.

Three facts about the trace carry the design. First, the payload never
enters $`P`$’s context:
steps [2–5](#A2.T13 "Table 13 ‣ B.3 A worked trace: dormant poison across two sessions ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
deliver only acknowledgements and handles, so $`P`$’s plan in session 2
is what the user typed, not what the attacker wrote (Reasoning
Integrity,
[Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 The Single-User Tier: a Finite Memory Interface ‣ 3 The PerMIT Framework ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Second, the payload cannot reach a tool without being displayed verbatim
at
step [6](#A2.T13 "Table 13 ‣ B.3 A worked trace: dormant poison across two sessions ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and accepted for that exact tool (Action Integrity,
[Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 The Single-User Tier: a Finite Memory Interface ‣ 3 The PerMIT Framework ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Third, everything therefore rests on the decision at
step [6](#A2.T13 "Table 13 ‣ B.3 A worked trace: dormant poison across two sessions ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")—the
single auditable event whose occupants (oracle, self-verification,
external LLM verifiers)
[Table 1](#S4.T1 "In Setup. ‣ 4.1 The Single-User Tier ‣ 4 Results ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
evaluates.

#### B.4 The Recursive Language Model as a Quarantined Reader

Our implementation uses an RLM ([Zhang et al., 2025](#bib.bib54))
because it supplies search, structured extraction, and crystallization
within the quarantined reader ($`\mathsf{fill}`$ and
$`\mathsf{crystallize}`$ in
[Table 12](#A2.T12 "In B.1 Operations and the reply alphabet ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Conventional retrieval would need adaptation to provide the same
interface while preserving the separation between untrusted content and
the protected agent.

###### Why an RLM.

The reader must search an untrusted store that is unbounded
(convention ([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
and routinely exceeds any context window, yet its bytes must never be
loaded into a trusted context. An RLM fits both constraints by
construction: the long input is not fed to the model but placed as a
variable in a persistent REPL environment, and the model writes code to
inspect, decompose, and recursively query sub-models over programmatic
slices of it ([Zhang et al., 2025](#bib.bib54)). The store is thus
navigated by code, symbolically, at any size.

###### How retrieval works.

The interpreter first restricts the reader’s view to
$`\mathsf{U}`$-labelled blocks—endorsed content and interpreter state
are structurally invisible—and loads the visible blocks (identifier,
content, tags) as a list variable inside the REPL. The root model
receives only the retrieval instruction and constant-size metadata; it
then iterates, printing slices of the store, delegating oversized blocks
to sub-model calls, and accumulating its answer in a result variable,
under a fixed iteration cap. The instruction is *fidelity-only*: read
the actual blocks, copy any extracted value verbatim, cite the source
block identifier, and report absence as absence—the reader carries no
safety obligation, because every safety property is enforced downstream
by the interpreter
(Lemma [D.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma D.1 (Protected-agent isolation). ‣ Assumptions and boundaries. ‣ D.1 Interface and trust assumptions ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Finally, the interpreter validates the reply deterministically: the
value must satisfy its declared schema and every citation must name a
block genuinely present in the view; any failure, reader error, or
uncited summary collapses to the null-handle outcome the semantics
already define
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
An accepted value reaches $`P`$ only as an opaque handle, resolved at a
confirmation gate; an accepted summary is written back at level
$`\mathsf{U}`$ (Fill, Cryst,
Figure [6](#A2.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ B.2 Label lifecycle ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Algorithm [1](#alg1 "Algorithm 1 ‣ How retrieval works. ‣ B.4 The Recursive Language Model as a Quarantined Reader ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
summarizes the procedure.

1: query $`q`$, schema $`s`$, memory store $`\mathcal{M}`$; iteration
cap $`T`$

2: a schema-valid value with citations, or the null handle

3: $`V\leftarrow\{\,b\in\mathcal{M}:\ell(b)=\mathsf{U}\,\}`$
$`\triangleright`$ view restriction (interpreter, deterministic)

4:
$`\mathcal{E}\leftarrow\textsc{InitREPL}(\texttt{context}\leftarrow[(\mathrm{id}(b),\mathrm{bytes}(b)):b\in V])`$

5: issue fidelity-only instruction for $`(q,s)`$ to root model $`Q`$
with constant-size metadata of context

6: for $`t=1,\dots,T`$ do

7:
  $`c\leftarrow Q(\text{history})`$; $`(\mathcal{E},\mathrm{out})\leftarrow\textsc{REPL}(\mathcal{E},c)`$
$`\triangleright`$ $`Q`$ reads slices; sub-calls for oversized blocks

8:   if $`\mathcal{E}[\texttt{answer}]`$ is set then

9:    $`(v,C)\leftarrow\textsc{Parse}(\mathcal{E}[\texttt{answer}])`$,
disambiguated against the true identifier set of $`V`$

10:    if $`v`$ satisfies $`s`$ and
$`C\subseteq\{\mathrm{id}(b):b\in V\}`$ and $`C\neq\varnothing`$ then

11:      return $`(v,C)`$ $`\triangleright`$ to $`P`$ as opaque handle /
$`\mathsf{U}`$-block only

12:    end if

13:    return null handle $`\triangleright`$ fail closed,
Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")

14:   end if

15: end for

16: return null handle $`\triangleright`$ cap or reader error,
Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")

Algorithm 1 RLM-based retrieval for one reader operation
($`\mathsf{fill}`$ or $`\mathsf{crystallize}`$)

###### Utility of the complete pipeline.

In every PerMIT cell of
Tables [1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ Setup. ‣ 4.1 The Single-User Tier ‣ 4 Results ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [4](#A1.T4 "Table 4 ‣ A.4 Additional Backbones and Serving Configurations ‣ Appendix A Additional Results ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the RLM reader is the retrieval path for stored untrusted content. With
the oracle gate, PerMIT has higher AM than undefended RAG on four of
seven backbones, trails by at most 1.5 AM points on Gemma-4-31B-it and
GPT-5.5, and by about ten AM points on GPT-5.4. These cross-backend
comparisons assess the complete mediated pipeline, not a gate-induced
improvement in retrieval quality. The oracle measures retained
capability under correct endorsement, while comparisons among PerMIT’s
gate configurations keep the reader and interface fixed and characterize
decision-dependent utility costs. Isolating mediation overhead from
reader quality would require a matched no-gate reader control; measuring
human confirmation effort requires a separate study.

### Appendix C Concurrent Work: Origin-Bound Memory Authority

TMA-NM ([Louck, 2026](#bib.bib28)) studies origin-bound authorization of
consequential actions. PerMIT combines observation mediation at a finite
memory interface, exact-value and tool-scoped endorsement, a
transcript-conditioned integrity theorem, and federated trust
accumulation. The comparison below distinguishes the policies, proved
properties, and verification scopes. Each guarantee depends on the
assumptions and enforcement rules of its own model.

###### Independent development.

PerMIT was developed independently of, and concurrently with, TMA-NM. We
became aware of the earlier public preprint while preparing this
manuscript and include this comparison to clarify the relationship
between the two approaches.

|  |  TMA-NM ([Louck, 2026](#bib.bib28)) |  PerMIT |
|----|----|----|
|  Enforcement boundary |  Origin-bound consequential-action authorization |  Observation mediation and sensitive-tool authorization under the specified interface |
|  Reasoning-side scope |  Answer bias remains outside the guarantee |  Noninterference conditional on the complete display transcript; endorsed content may influence responses |
|  Verification scope |  Bounded TLC checks and an inductive-invariant argument; parameter independence justified by hand |  Lean 4 proofs for unbounded executions of the single-user core; remaining scope in Appendix [E](#A5 "Appendix E Scope of the Lean 4 Verification ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust") |
|  Value attribution |  Origin labels in the unified study; text proxy in the supporting study |  Opaque handles before release and exact-value checks at sensitive tools |
|  Tool-output trust |  Conditional trust for allow-listed tools |  All tool outputs enter untrusted; readable release requires endorsement |
|  User-authorization scope |  Fresh, single-use authorization bound to the concrete action |  Reusable authorization for an exact value and named tool; transaction context is not bound |
|  Multi-user sharing |  Out of scope |  Federated promotion and dispute analysis under stated identity, reviewer, and scheduling assumptions |

#### C.1 The observation boundary

TMA-NM permits untrusted memory to inform responses while constraining
consequential actions. PerMIT additionally mediates what the protected
agent can observe. Under
Lemma [D.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma D.1 (Protected-agent isolation). ‣ Assumptions and boundaries. ‣ D.1 Interface and trust assumptions ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
untrusted sources are represented by opaque handles until endorsement
releases their contents. This prevents readable delivery of unendorsed
memory through the modeled interface; it does not prevent all possible
influence from malicious content after endorsement.

Theorem [D.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5 "Theorem D.5 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ D.2.2 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
states the precise comparison. For matched initial configurations,
identical user-typed inputs, coupled randomness, the same schedule, and
a common horizon, equal complete display transcripts imply equal
observable protected-agent behavior. An attacker can nevertheless change
a displayed preview, influence an endorsement decision, or supply
harmful content that a verifier accepts. Such changes may alter the
transcript and subsequent behavior. The theorem establishes no
additional influence beyond the transcript under its matching
conditions; it does not establish factual correctness, unbiased
recommendations, or the soundness of an automated verifier
(Appendix [D.2.2](#A4.SS2.SSS2 "D.2.2 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Isolation likewise blocks in-context reconstruction from fragments while
they remain unavailable to the protected agent as unendorsed content.
Once fragments have been endorsed and released, the agent can combine
them. Sensitive calls remain subject to exact-value and tool-scope
checks, but separate endorsements do not establish the safety of a
combined transaction or its suitability in a changed context
(Appendix [D.2.1](#A4.SS2.SSS1 "D.2.1 Action Integrity ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

#### C.2 Relational versus reachability properties

The single-execution invariants reported for TMA-NM do not establish
PerMIT’s two-execution, transcript-conditioned property. This is a
difference in the statements proved, not an expressiveness limitation of
model checking. Relational safety properties can be reduced to safety
properties over self-composed or product systems representing multiple
executions ([Shemer et al., 2019](#bib.bib41)). Establishing an
analogous result would require an appropriate relational model and a
separate proof; enlarging an existing single-execution model alone does
not supply that proof.

PerMIT’s Lean development establishes its integrity properties for
arbitrarily long executions of the mechanized single-user core, under
the modeled interface and assumptions.
Appendix [E](#A5 "Appendix E Scope of the Lean 4 Verification ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
distinguishes this checked core from the paper-only extensions and
federated analysis. A proof about either formal model does not by itself
establish that a deployed harness implements that model faithfully.

#### C.3 The federated tier

PerMIT also studies shared memory contributed and reviewed by a
population of attested identities. Its analysis addresses promotion,
disputes, wrongful eviction, and confirmation cost under explicit
identity budgets, reviewer conditions, and protocol schedules
(§[3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 The Federated Tier ‣ 3 The PerMIT Framework ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

These guarantees are conditional and probabilistic. Attestation and
first-decision accounting constrain how much weight adversarial
identities can supply, but honest reviewers can still accept poison.
Equation [1](#S3.E1 "Equation 1 ‣ 3.3 The Federated Tier ‣ 3 The PerMIT Framework ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
bounds that residual promotion risk. Under the demand, coverage, and
threshold schedules of Supplementary
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the risk bounds decrease with community size while the per-user
confirmation burden for covered benign shared demand does not increase.
This is not an unconditional guarantee of zero poison promotion or
decreasing review effort for every workload.

#### C.4 Deployment without institutional corroborators

PerMIT’s single-user tier operates with the user as endorser and does
not require a federation. Once an exact value has been approved for a
named tool, retaining the endorsed copy and its in-scope authorization
permits reuse without another mandatory approval for that same pair.
This does not bound the number of rejected review requests, and deleting
the local endorsed copy can remove the reuse path. The guarantee also
does not establish how much useful content a human or automated verifier
will approve.

Reuse is an explicit authorization-policy choice. PerMIT’s endorsement
does not bind argument position, task, purpose, time, or the other
arguments of a call. Community disputes suspend community reuse while
preserving prior personal confirmations. Thus the confirmation-cost
claim should be read together with the retained-copy assumption and the
contextual-authorization limits in
Appendix [D.2.1](#A4.SS2.SSS1 "D.2.1 Action Integrity ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### C.5 Laundering channels

PerMIT addresses laundering through the modeled interface rules.
Reader-generated summaries remain untrusted when written by
$`\mathsf{crystallize}`$, so summarization alone grants no authority.
All tool outputs are captured as untrusted, preventing a tool’s name or
status from automatically making its output trusted. These rules do not
make subsequently endorsed content harmless or protect against a
compromised enforcement harness.

Repeated content does not itself constitute independent endorsement.
Distinct attested identities and first-decision accounting restrict
manufactured voting weight. Where the promotion quorum exceeds the
certified adversarial identity budget, adversarial endorsements alone
cannot satisfy it; erroneous honest endorsements can still promote
poison, with risk bounded under the assumptions of
Equation [1](#S3.E1 "Equation 1 ‣ 3.3 The Federated Tier ‣ 3 The PerMIT Framework ‣ Part I Main Paper ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

The capability_ifc baseline evaluated by [Louck (2026)](#bib.bib28)
treats retrieved memory as trusted. Its reported failures concern that
evaluated configuration and do not establish that every deployment of
CaMeL, FIDES, or capability-based information-flow control fails under
the same attacks.

### Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches

This appendix summarizes the memory-interface model and single-user
integrity guarantees cited in the main text.

([Supplement S](#Pt3 "Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
gives the complete semantics and integrity proofs
([S2](#A2a "Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A3a "Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
federated analysis and confirmation-cost results with their assumptions
([S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
security discussion
([S7](#A7 "Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
probability tools and assumption audit
([S8](#A8 "Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),

#### D.1 Interface and trust assumptions

The Protected LLM $`P`$ is an arbitrary agent strategy over its
observations, interaction history, and random coins. It chooses
operations and can re-plan on endorsed feedback. The harness mediates
the memory interface and tool boundary; it does not inspect or
taint-track the agent’s internal reasoning. The Quarantined Reader $`Q`$
may behave adversarially and holds no tool capability.
Appendix [B.1](#A2.SS1 "B.1 Operations and the reply alphabet ‣ Appendix B The Memory Interface in Practice ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives the operation-level view;
Supplement [S2](#A2a "Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives the normative semantics.

###### Stored values and authority.

Each immutable block has bytes, a source-based label, provenance, and a
tool scope. The labels are $`\mathsf{T}`$ (user-typed), $`\mathsf{U}`$
(untrusted), $`\mathsf{C}`$ (personally confirmed), $`\mathsf{PC}`$
(agent-composed), and, in the federated extension, $`\mathsf{CC}`$
(community-confirmed). The readable store $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$
consists of non-$`\mathsf{U}`$ blocks. Readability alone does not
authorize a sensitive call: a literal must byte-match a $`\mathsf{T}`$
block or a confirmed block scoped to that tool. A $`\mathsf{PC}`$ block
has no independent endorsement authority. A confirmation for the
reasoning target makes its bytes readable but grants no sensitive-tool
scope.

The trusted command channel creates $`\mathsf{T}`$ blocks. Pasted
content and all tool outputs, including errors and status text, enter
$`\mathsf{U}`$. Reader-generated summaries also enter $`\mathsf{U}`$.
The agent receives an opaque handle, not those bytes. Accepting
confirmation creates a fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy; it never relabels the
untrusted source in place. Endorsed and untrusted identifiers use
separate allocation streams, so an attacker cannot influence a later
endorsed identifier by adding untrusted blocks.

###### Mediation rules.

The harness enforces the following properties (complete rules:
Supplement [S2.3](#A2.SS3a "S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- •
  Every handle-expressed tool argument gates, even if its hidden bytes
  equal an already trusted value. The gate resolves the handle, displays
  the exact bytes and target, and binds an acceptance to those same
  bytes. Rejection or failed resolution prevents the flow.
- •
  Sensitive-tool literals use only the typed or exact-tool-confirmed
  fast paths. The baseline permits agent-composed literals at data
  tools. Consequently, endorsement for one purpose does not imply a
  confidentiality guarantee for all later data-tool uses;
  Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  adds exact-tool checks there.
- •
  Reader failure, empty retrieval, and unoccupied identifiers have the
  same opaque reply. Handle structure follows operations rather than
  hidden content, size, or success. The reply alphabet contains only
  fixed acknowledgements, handles, fixed failures, decisions, and
  verbatim readable-store bytes. Trusted retrieval sees
  $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ alone.
- •
  All attacker-influenceable user-facing content is recorded in the
  display transcript. Authenticated facts and untrusted source claims
  occupy separate zones. Selection previews carry no authority;
  authorization uses the resolved value in the decision pane.
- •
  A batch displays every value that would flow, records its pages and
  decisions, and executes only after all required approvals. Accepted
  values remain endorsed even if a later review aborts the invocation.
  Full batch semantics and the corresponding determinacy argument are in
  Supplement [S2](#A2a "Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A3a "Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Assumptions and boundaries.

Both integrity results assume source-based labels, immutable stored
blocks, and faithful displays
([A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
in
Supplement [S2.4](#A2.SS4a "S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
together with the enforced interface above. Action Integrity
additionally assumes *sound atomic endorsement*: acceptance means that
the user intends the exact displayed value at the named tool, separately
for each reviewed value, including accepted positions of a transaction
that later aborts
([A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
An LLM verifier can violate this assumption; the theorem does not
establish its accuracy. Reasoning Integrity instead assumes a common
exogenous typed-input stream and matched scheduling and coins
([A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and conventions
[C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
it does not require endorsements to be semantically correct. Timing,
termination, and compromised harness components are outside these
guarantees.

###### Lemma D.1 (Protected-agent isolation).

In every interface-conformant execution, each bytes-carrying reply
delivered to $`P`$ is the verbatim content of a readable-store block at
delivery. Untrusted sources reach $`P`$ only through opaque handles
until endorsement. This is a statement about the source of a delivered
value, not disjointness of byte strings across stores.

###### Proof sketch.

Inspect the reply constructors. Tool capture, untrusted recall, reader
search, and crystallization return handles or fixed tokens. Only trusted
recall and retrieval return bytes, and both read
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$. Input ingestion and each operation
preserve this property, so induction extends it to arbitrary run length.
Full proof: Supplement,
Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

#### D.2 Integrity Proofs

##### D.2.1 Action Integrity

###### Definition D.2 (Personal Action Integrity).

A sensitive sink event at tool $`t`$ is personally authorized when each
argument value $`v`$ byte-matches user-typed content, or this user has
accepted the exact bytes $`v`$ for $`t`$, either at that call or in a
retained in-scope confirmation. For a batch, acceptance covers each
displayed element separately. Action Integrity requires this property
for every sensitive sink event of every execution.

###### Theorem D.3 (Action Integrity).

Under the interface and
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
above, every execution starting from a well-formed configuration has
personal Action Integrity, for arbitrary agent strategies, attacks, and
reader behavior. The empty configuration is well formed; a seeded
configuration must carry a valid endorsement record. The invariant
requires immutable source-correct blocks, valid endorsement ancestry and
history, interface-conformant state, and authorization of the
accumulated sink log (complete definition: Supplement,
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof sketch.

The empty state satisfies the invariant. For each transition, new
untrusted blocks confer no authority; agent writes confer readability
but no new authorization; and an accepted confirmation creates a fresh
copy justified by the exact display and sound endorsement. A sensitive
call therefore has only three admissible cases: a typed literal, an
in-scope confirmed literal, or fresh accepting confirmation. Every
handle takes the third case, and a batch applies it to every flowed
element. Failed reviews prevent the call, while already accepted values
remain individually authorized. These cases preserve the invariant and
establish sink safety by induction. The single-user interpreter has no
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ creation path. Full statement and proof: Supplement,
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

###### Corollary D.4 (No silent resolution).

Under the same conditions, never-endorsed untrusted bytes cross a tool
boundary, including a data-tool boundary, only through acceptance of
those exact bytes for that tool in that call. After endorsement at any
target, their readable copy may be used as a literal at baseline data
tools. Sensitive-tool scope checks and the rule that handles always gate
still apply.

###### Proof sketch.

Isolation leaves never-endorsed bytes available only through handles,
and every handle resolution gates. Endorsement subsequently creates a
readable copy, enabling the stated literal path. This distinguishes
exact-byte authorization from control influence carried by a logged
decision. Full proof and
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
closure of the later data-tool path: Supplement,
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

###### Reuse and contextual authorization.

The policy authorizes exact values for tools, not complete transactions.
Separately approved values may be combined without joint review, and a
changed task context may make their reuse inappropriate. Shared disputes
suspend community reuse but preserve prior personal confirmations.
Candidate expiry retires dormant or inactive shared entries (Supplement,
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
it is not a universal authorization lifetime. Local scope leases are a
future extension outside the proved model
(Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Context-bound or transaction-level approval would require extended
semantics and revised confirmation-cost accounting.

###### Future direction: combined-memory review.

Human or agent memory managers could assemble related memories with
their provenance and intended use, then review their joint meaning. The
combined item remains untrusted until confirmation; its components’
approvals do not automatically endorse it. If subsequently published, it
must gather fresh endorsements of its exact content under the
community-promotion rules. Revisions require their own review. This
proposed workflow builds on crystallization and endorsement but has not
been evaluated and does not authorize every later transaction using the
combined memory. Future experiments should compare it with per-item
review under matched attack-search and review budgets, measuring harmful
endorsement, delayed-combination success, benign utility, and review
burden.

##### D.2.2 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript

The protected view is
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)=(\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}},H,x,h)`$: the readable
store, observable handle structure, typed input, and decision history.
Matched configurations $`c_{1}\approx c_{2}`$ agree on this view, the
agent’s interaction history and consumed coins, endorsed allocation
state, and initial ghost display and sink logs. Their untrusted stores
and private handle resolutions may differ arbitrarily. A common endorsed
seed with empty histories is a canonical matched start.

The complete display transcript $`\mathsf{DT}(\rho)`$ records selection
surfaces and previews, exact decision-pane values and provenance zones,
targets, selections, accepts and rejects, and batch pages and aggregated
decisions, including reviews in aborted transactions. Its event kinds
are interpreter-assigned. The observable behavior $`\mathcal{B}(\rho)`$
comprises protected-agent operations, tool invocations, the reply
stream, final protected view, and the ungated sink projection. The
latter omits arguments flowed by fresh confirmations, which are already
recorded in the transcript.

###### Theorem D.5 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript).

Under
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the input and scheduling conditions above, fix matched starts, any
two attacks, and a coupled coin sequence. For runs $`\rho_{1},\rho_{2}`$
of a common horizon,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{2})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal{B}(\rho_{1})=\mathcal{B}(\rho_{2}).
``` |  |

Paste presence and content, reader outputs, and tool outputs need not
agree across the attacks. The statement is trace-wise for every coupled
coin sequence. In plain terms, the two runs may differ in whether pasted
input arrives, its contents, and reader and tool outputs. The guarantee
holds for every fixed sequence of random choices used identically in
both runs.

###### Proof sketch.

Maintain matched protected views, histories, coin positions, and
transcript prefixes. The strategy then chooses the same next operation.
A display-free step returns only a constant token, an
operation-determined handle, or matched readable bytes, preserving the
invariant. At a display step, the append-only transcripts and equality
of the complete transcripts make the newly appended segments
prefix-comparable. The interface’s display-segment determinacy lemma
forces those segments to be equal, including page structure, decisions,
and released bytes. The two steps therefore create the same endorsed
copies and replies. Induction gives the claimed equality; sink
annotations follow the same mediation cases as Action Integrity. Full
proof, including the segment lemma and batch cases: Supplement,
Lemma [S3.20](#A3.Thmtheorem20 "Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

###### Corollary D.6 (Attack-surface confinement).

Under the same comparison conditions, a difference in protected-agent
operations, tool invocations, or ungated sink events entails a
difference in the complete display transcript.

###### Proof sketch.

Take the contrapositive of
Theorem [D.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5 "Theorem D.5 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ D.2.2 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

This is a conditional noninterference guarantee. An attacker can affect
a preview or an endorsement decision, and thereby the transcript and
later behavior. The theorem excludes additional influence that bypasses
that recorded release surface; it does not establish reasoning
correctness or make displayed attacks harmless.

### Appendix E Scope of the Lean 4 Verification

The Lean artifact is available upon request and will be released with
the code when the paper is published. The artifact contains the
executable single-user interpreter, proofs, build assertions, dependency
manifest, and axiom report. It pins Lean 4 and Mathlib to v4.31.0
(Mathlib revision fabf563a); lake exe cache get && lake build reproduces
the check.
Supplement [S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives the complete correspondence table, ten modeling deltas, and the
specification corrections discovered during mechanization.

###### What is checked.

action_integrity and action_integrity_from establish the single-user
action guarantee from the empty endorsed store and from any state
satisfying the mechanized invariant. reasoning_integrity and
reasoning_integrity_from prove the transcript-conditioned comparison
from empty or shared endorsed seeds, for arbitrary agent strategies and
independently chosen attacks. Their conclusions include equal sink logs,
operations, replies, and final protected views. Paste presence and
content can differ. Supporting results check reply isolation, mandatory
handle gating, and attack-surface confinement. A standalone batch layer
checks displayed-element flow, rejection behavior, and transcript
determinacy; executable assertions cover the baseline counterexample and
eight scenarios.

###### What remains a paper proof.

The run-level integration of batched iteration, durable endorsements
from accepted positions of an aborted invocation, arbitrary mid-run
matched starting states, and the reduction from reactive actors to
event-indexed oracles are proved in the supplement, outside the checked
interpreter.
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are checked at the gate level only; their wider integration,
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the federated protocol, probability bounds, and confirmation-budget
results are not mechanized. The checked interpreter returns one selected
element at a direct collection-handle call and records additional
transcript-determined selection information. These representation
differences and their correspondence arguments are explicit in
[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Trusted base and artifact.

The artifact’s clean-build axiom report lists only propext and
Quot.sound for the top-level theorems, with no sorryAx; the executable
assertions additionally trust Lean’s evaluator. Kernel checking
certifies the mechanized statements, not the correspondence between that
model and a deployed harness or the reliability of a verifier. The
artifact includes the full source, CORRESPONDENCE.md, pinned build
instructions, the build log, and source checksums. Thus the concise
statements here remain auditable against both the complete paper proofs
and the precise mechanized scope.

Nothing normative lives in this register; no proof depends on it.

Commentary blocks. Throughout the normative and proof registers, short
passages set in small type under the heading *Commentary
(non-normative)* carry the rationale, epistemic status, and validation
pointers for the material they adjoin, so that a rule or assumption and
its justification can be read together without the justification
entering the register. Commentary blocks belong to the non-normative
register in function: no rule reads them, no proof cites them, and a
reader who skips every commentary block loses no hypothesis and no step
of any proof.

Statement discipline. A theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary,
definition, or invariant environment contains hypotheses, the
conclusion, and bare pointers (“established by”, “see Remark”);
interpretation, comparison, special cases, and design justification are
set in a numbered remark adjacent to the result they concern.

Cross-referencing convention. The formal development may point into the
non-normative register only by a parenthetical key, e.g. “(rationale:
[N2](#Thmnotex2 "Note N2 (The endorsement unit). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
analysis:
[S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))”;
the non-normative register may cite the formal development freely.
Consequently the formal development is self-contained: a reader who
skips
Appendix [S7](#A7 "Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
entirely loses no hypothesis and no step of any proof. A reader with a
specific concern should consult the attack and limitation index
(Table [S3](#A7.T3 "Table S3 ‣ S7.1 Attack and limitation index ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
which maps concerns to analysis entries and to the formal facts that
govern them.

shows which results rest on which hypotheses. Three facts are visible
directly from the figure and are relied on throughout: (i) the
single-user theorems and the pathwise cap
(Thm. [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
depend only on the trust axioms
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the harness rules, never on any federated or budget modelling
assumption
(Appendices [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the cap’s expected-form clauses read only the reference demand model’s
masses, with the sole assumption-bearing comparison isolated in
Corollary [S6.3](#A6.Thmtheorem3 "Corollary S6.3 (The cap under bounded tool-spread). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");

which feeds only budget constants (dashed edge); (iii) the behavioural

[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
enter only the probabilistic-refinement and budget layers, each of which

#### S1.2 Notation

The principal symbols of these appendices are collected here; locally
scoped symbols are defined at first use. Unless otherwise marked,
symbols denote fixed deployment configuration belonging to the *trusted
computing base* (TCB): the fixed components (interpreter, channels,
rendering and logging paths, and configuration) that the guarantees
assume correct and that no model output can alter (inventory:
§[S2.5](#A2.SS5 "S2.5 Attacker model and trusted computing base ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
single-user,

federated). Marks: (emp) empirical/behavioural parameter,
(sch) population schedule, (rv) random variable.
````
