````math
#### S1.3 Standing conventions

1.  (C1)
    *Determinism modulo coins.* A single coin sequence $`\omega`$
    jointly covers the sampling randomness of $`P`$ and of
    $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$; given $`\omega`$, both are deterministic
    functions of their inputs. All two-run comparisons
    (Thm. [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Prop. [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Prop. [S8.20](#A8.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S8.20 (Gradual release). ‣ S8.4 Knowledge-based formulation of Reasoning Integrity ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    couple $`\omega`$, the user’s typed stream
    ([A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and (in the federated setting) the exogenous federation-log prefix
    ([A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    local suffixes derived equal,
    Def. [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    identically across the compared runs.
2.  (C2)
    *Probability space and adversary.* All federated-protocol randomness
    lives on the filtration $`(\mathcal{F}_{s})`$ generated by logged
    protocol events and display events; the adversary’s strategy
    (presentation, submission, stopping, self-dispute) is predictable
    with respect to it. The construction, and the two structural
    constraints on adaptivity it implies, are given once in
    §[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and used everywhere.
3.  (C3)
    *Log order.* The federation maintains a single linearizable,
    append-only log of protocol events: a TCB *log service* (a trusted
    sequencer or a consensus layer) supplies the total order, and its
    history is materialized as a Certificate-Transparency-style Merkle
    tree for tamper-evident audit — the tree authenticates the history;
    the sequencing service, assumed correct as TCB, provides the
    linearizability. It supplies the total order on decisions, demand
    events, and verdicts that Rules
    [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    invoke. “The federation log,” “the log,” and “log order” all refer
    to this object and the order it induces. The hash-chained audit log
    that materializes the display transcript
    (Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    is a distinct, per-deployment TCB component and is never called “the
    log.”
4.  (C4)
    *Epochs, leases, rounds.* Three multiplicities the development keeps
    distinct. *(a) Epochs.* An epoch is a fixed span of the federation
    log (a fixed number of sequence numbers or a fixed calendar period),
    common to all items and identities, readable off the log (TCB);
    every renewable per-epoch quantity ($`\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$,
    $`E_{\max}`$, notification deduplication, the accountability
    allowances of
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v),
    (vii)) is indexed to it. *(b) Leases.* A lease is the
    deployment-selected local scope lifetime of the requirements-level
    option
    [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    ([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    not part of the formal semantics);
    $`E_{\mathrm{lease}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ counts lease periods per
    (user, item) in the extension-level accounting of
    [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e).
    *(c) Rounds.* A re-verification round re-presents a
    community-confirmed item to inspectors with no prior decision on its
    bytes; $`E_{\mathrm{rv}}`$ counts rounds. *(d) Permanence and
    boundaries.* Decision freshness
    (Def. [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and verdict capacity
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
    are *permanent* and attach to none of the three: they never renew.
    Promotion weight and banked credits persist across epoch boundaries
    until the item retires. Finalisation windows are contained within
    epochs: a window that would cross a boundary closes at the boundary,
    banking its accrued endorsements to the item’s next entry exactly as
    a dormant-interval decision would
    (Def. [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    a boundary never finalises a promotion early and never discards
    honest effort. A boundary-spanning dispute counts toward
    Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
    in the epoch in which it opened.
5.  (C5)
    *Byte identity.* Items, freshness, disputes, and panels are keyed to
    exact byte strings. Paraphrase variants are distinct items
    (consequences:
    [S1](#Thmobjx1 "Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
6.  (C6)
    *Confirmations.* A *confirmation* is a user approval—an accepting
    gate decision; it is durable (its fresh endorsed copy is written
    even when another review aborts the enclosing invocation,
    Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and is counted once per (value, tool) pair per gate transaction
    (Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Rejecting decisions, abandoned dialogs, batch-element page
    approvals, and repeated within-transaction reviews of an
    already-accepted pair are attention cost, counted separately
    ([N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    *Required*, *voluntary*, and *redundant* confirmations are defined
    in
    §[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
    the confirmation cap
    (Thm. [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    counts required pair-confirmations, the ledger
    (Lem. [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    required and voluntary; redundant confirmations are protocol-inert
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
    and excluded from both. Here, required means needed for the user’s
    intended use, not an obligation to accept.
7.  (C7)
    *Store idealization.* The store is idealized as unbounded: no
    operation’s defined behaviour depends on aggregate store volume. A
    deployment enforcing quotas must apply them to the untrusted tier by
    silent eviction, never by an error visible to $`P`$ (otherwise store
    exhaustion reopens exactly the channel
    Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    closes;
    [S7](#Thmobjx7 "Analysis S7 (Store-exhaustion side channel). ‣ S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
8.  (C8)
    *Constants vs. schedules.*
    $`N,k,m,W,D_{\mathrm{pool}},T_{\mathrm{win}},T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$,
    $`E_{\max},\rho_{\mathrm{sub}},r_{\max},c_{\mathrm{ceil}},c_{\mathrm{batch}},c_{\mathrm{cand}},c_{\mathrm{p}}`$
    are fixed TCB configuration at any deployment;
    Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    additionally studies *schedules* $`N(M),k(M),\dots`$ along a growing
    population, and every scheduled claim is confined to the corridor
    stated there. All caps and multiplicity constants are positive
    integers where integral; in particular $`E_{\max}\geq 1`$ and
    $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\geq 1`$ (used by
    Lemma [S8.18](#A8.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S8.18 (Explicit forms of 𝐴(𝑀) and 𝐵_fl). ‣ S8.3 Explicit ledger constants ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
9.  (C9)
    *Environment scheduling.* An interpreter step has a fixed slot
    structure: first the channel slots deliver at most one typed event
    (W-Typed) and at most one paste event (W-Paste), in that order; then
    $`P`$ emits exactly one operation, whose environment interaction
    (tool returns, reader outputs, retriever selection, gate decisions)
    occurs synchronously within that operation’s atomic transition.
    Two-run comparisons
    (Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    couple only this *slot skeleton* and the typed stream
    ([A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
    paste *presence and content* are uncoupled and may differ
    arbitrarily across the compared attacks, as may every tool output
    and reader output. Channel-slot transitions acknowledge the channel,
    never $`P`$: nothing is appended to $`P`$’s reply stream by W-Typed
    or W-Paste
    (Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    convention [(vi)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Two-run comparisons are always taken at a *common horizon*: the
    compared runs consist of the same number of interpreter slots, and
    transcript equality means equality of the two full transcripts at
    that horizon.

#### S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties

The following six named facts are cited constantly and are collected
here; together they are the structural core of the design. They are
heterogeneous in kind, and each entry declares its kind: *rule property*
(a direct consequence of the cited rule and definition clauses);
*conditional inductive invariant* (preserved by every transition, under
the named first-party exceptions); *protocol property* (a fact of the
counting and pacing rules); *bound metaproperty* (a property of the
*bounds* of the cited theorems, holding under those theorems’
hypotheses). None is an axiom: each is established at the location
cited, and nothing beyond the cited hypotheses is assumed. Invariants
[INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are stated in the vocabulary of the federated protocol, defined in
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness).

An attested identity’s first *logged* decision on a byte string — its
first decision taken while the bytes have a shared-tier presence
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— is its only weight-bearing inspection of those bytes, ever: every
later accepting decision by that identity (at any tool, in any pipeline
entry, in any epoch, in any later shared-tier presence of the same
bytes) carries no promotion weight and no verdict capacity. Freshness is
decidable from the federation log
(convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
and never renews; personal decisions outside any shared-tier presence
are not logged and are outside this guarantee
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Kind: rule property. *Established by*
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the counting rule
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(Byte-keyed: paraphrase variants are distinct items,
([C5](#A1.I2.i5 "Item C5 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
[S1](#Thmobjx1 "Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry).

A rejecting decision can freeze promotion, corroborate an open dispute,
or trigger post-promotion review; it can never promote and never
vindicate. A *repeat* acceptance carries no promotion weight and no
verdict
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Hence re-exposure of bytes to a *previously logged-decided* inspector
can only add rejection opportunities; exposure to a log-fresh inspector
adds both a rejection opportunity and a possible weight-bearing
acceptance, priced by the hypotheses of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Kind: rule property. *Established by*
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(iii)
with
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)).

No user is ever required to confirm a given *(value, tool) pair* more
than once over the deployment’s lifetime: a user’s first accepting
review of value $`v`$ at tool $`t`$ — at any gate transaction, including
one whose enclosing invocation aborts
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— durably writes the local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy with
$`t\in\mathsf{scope}`$, which covers all their later use of $`v`$ *at
$`t`$* and survives every third-party protocol event; and within one
transaction, confirmations are counted once per pair
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
A first use of the same bytes at a different tool $`t^{\prime}`$ is a
distinct required confirmation, of the pair $`(v,t^{\prime})`$, itself
once ever; the pairs per item are bounded by
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
in the budget model. The disclosed exception within the formal semantics
is first-party: the owner’s own agent’s ungated $`\mathsf{evict}`$
([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
a deployment adopting a conforming instantiation of the
requirements-level
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
additionally admits lease expiry, an extension outside this document’s
semantics
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Kind: conditional inductive invariant (exception: first-party evict,
[N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
extension-level:
conforming-[O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
lease expiry,
[O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Established by*
Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(from
Rules [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
reasoning pairs covered per the reasoning-coverage clause of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i);
*consumed by*
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i).

###### Invariant INV-4 (Banking safety).

A banked credit (a first decision logged during dormancy or during a
freeze with no open entry) raises only the *starting* weight of the
item’s next pipeline entry. Nothing finalises promotion except an open
entry’s window end, so banking never bypasses a window’s rejection
opportunity and never accelerates finalisation past a window boundary;
and each banked decision remains its identity’s single fresh inspection
of the bytes, so successive entries’ weight-bearing sets stay
identity-disjoint
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Banked credits expire if the item retires first. Every banked decision
is logged after its attempt’s anchor
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so banking never lets a credited decision precede the conditioning point
of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Kind: protocol property. *Established by*
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv).

###### Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal).

An identity casts at most one verdict on a given dispute instance, for
the instance’s entire life, across any number of epoch boundaries.
Verdict capacity is consumed only by cast verdicts (abandonment consumes
nothing) and, like freshness, never renews. Kind: rule property.
*Established by*
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii).

###### Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness).

The federated safety bounds depend only on protocol constants
($`N,k,m,D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$) and the adversary’s resources
($`f,f_{\mathrm{s}},W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$), never on the number of honest
identities to whom a poisoned item is presented: the same stated upper
bound applies at every reach. (No monotonicity in reach is claimed:
presenting the bytes to log-fresh inspectors creates both rejection
opportunities and possible weight-bearing acceptances,
[INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
what is proved is that the bound does not degrade with reach.)
Reach-freeness is relative to the stated parameters: the bounds’ *form*
is reach-independent, while the behavioural constants
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ are weakest-target infima over all
cohorts the adversary can reach
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so widening reach can lower the applicable constants without changing
the bound’s form. Kind: bound metaproperty. The property is
Definition [S4.8](#A4.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S4.8 (Reach-free bound). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
it is a property of the stated bounds of
Theorems [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
holding under their hypotheses, not a property of reachable
configurations; contrast with the reach-dependent no-dispute baseline,
Theorem [S8.9](#A8.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S8.9 (No-dispute baseline: reach-dependent). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

### Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface

PerMIT places no restriction on which tools the Protected LLM may invoke
or on how it reasons; the *harness* (the fixed interpreter code of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
together with the display and logging paths) bounds two things only:
what $`P`$ can *observe*, and what may *cross* a tool boundary. The
bounded surface is the memory interface: the $`P`$-facing operation
surface

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\displaystyle\Sigma_{P}\;=\;\Sigma\;\cup\;\{\mathsf{tool}(\bar{a}):\ \mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}\}\;\cup\;\{\mathsf{retrieve}\},
``` |  |
|  |
``` math
\displaystyle\Sigma=\{\mathsf{write}_{P},\mathsf{recall},\mathsf{fill},\mathsf{crystallize},\mathsf{display},\mathsf{confirm},\mathsf{evict}\},
``` |  |

($`\mathsf{write}`$, where it appears in prose, abbreviates the sole
$`P`$-emitted write operation $`\mathsf{write}_{P}`$.) together with one
interpreter-internal derived form ($`\mathsf{map}`$). Every completeness
claim below
(Lemmas [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
enumerates over $`\Sigma_{P}`$, which coincides arm-for-arm with the
mechanized operation type (POp,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Because this surface is finite, its *interface transition schema* is
specified *clause-complete at the interface alphabet*: every operation
of $`\Sigma_{P}`$ and channel event has its store effect, reply,
transcript events, and sanitized-history events fixed by
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with these rules, with totality per
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b);
the full run state these transitions carry is fixed by
Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
What the figures deliberately do not formalise is $`P`$’s internal
computation (a strategy,
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and the UI-side rendering internals of
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the channel analysis of
Appendix [S3](#A3a "Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
needs only the interface schema, and is verified clause by clause
against it, with the totality clause of
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
ensuring that no invocation has undefined or distinguishing behaviour.
(Model lineage and design rationale:
[N1](#Thmnotex1 "Note N1 (Model lineage). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

#### S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles

###### Definition S2.1 (Trust lattice and labels).

The integrity lattice has two levels, $`\mathsf{U}\sqsubset\mathbb{E}`$.
Each block carries a label
$`\ell(b)\in\{\mathsf{U},\mathsf{T},\mathsf{C},\mathsf{CC},\mathsf{PC}\}`$;
the level map $`\mathrm{lvl}`$ sends
$`\mathrm{lvl}(\mathsf{U})=\mathsf{U}`$ and
$`\mathrm{lvl}(\ell)=\mathbb{E}`$ for
$`\ell\in\{\mathsf{T},\mathsf{C},\mathsf{CC},\mathsf{PC}\}`$. The four
$`\mathbb{E}`$-level labels are provenance-and-reuse tags, not a finer
trust ordering: $`\mathsf{T}`$ (user-typed; reusable by its owner),
$`\mathsf{C}`$ (single-user confirmed; admissible only to the tools in
its scope, reusable without re-confirmation only by its owner),
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ (community-confirmed,
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
admissible only to the exact targets endorsed (tools, or the reasoning
pseudo-target,
§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
reusable by anyone), $`\mathsf{PC}`$ ($`P`$-composed; empty tool scope,
hence never eligible for the sensitive fast path of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Label combination is the meet on levels: an operation combining inputs
yields level $`\mathsf{U}`$ if any input is at level $`\mathsf{U}`$,
else level $`\mathbb{E}`$; no operation in $`\Sigma`$ raises an
untrusted value to level $`\mathbb{E}`$ by combination.

###### Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration).

A block is
$`b=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{bytes}(b),\ell(b),\pi(b),\mathsf{scope}(b))`$
with interpreter-only provenance
$`\pi(b)\in\{\mathsf{typed},\mathsf{pasted},\mathsf{ingress},\mathsf{cryst},\mathsf{pcomposed},\mathsf{confirmed},\mathsf{cache}\}`$,
assigned only by the interpreter (provenance is interpreter-private and
not part of $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}`$), and, for endorsed blocks, a tool
scope
$`\mathsf{scope}(b)\subseteq\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$
(a set of individual tool identifiers). Every block-creating transition
of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
instantiates one of the total constructors

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\operatorname{newT}(v)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{\bullet},v,\mathsf{T},\mathsf{typed},\varnothing),`$ | $`\displaystyle\operatorname{newPC}(v)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{\bullet},v,\mathsf{PC},\mathsf{pcomposed},\varnothing),`$ |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle\operatorname{newC}(v,t)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{\bullet},v,\mathsf{C},\mathsf{confirmed},\sigma(t)),`$ | $`\displaystyle\operatorname{newCache}(v,t)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{\bullet},v,\mathsf{C},\mathsf{cache},\sigma(t)),`$ |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle\operatorname{newU}(v,\pi)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(\mathrm{id}^{\mathsf{U}}_{\bullet},v,\mathsf{U},\pi,\varnothing),`$ |  |  |  |

where $`\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{\bullet}`$ (resp.
$`\mathrm{id}^{\mathsf{U}}_{\bullet}`$) is the next identifier of the
endorsed (resp. untrusted) sort
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g))
and $`\sigma(t)=\{t\}`$ for a tool target,
$`\sigma(\mathrm{reasoning})=\varnothing`$; the cache confirmations of
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
use $`\operatorname{newCache}`$, all other accepting confirmations
$`\operatorname{newC}`$. Tool identifiers are canonical, fixed TCB
configuration, so scope membership is a decidable syntactic test. Block
identifiers are two-sorted and operation-determined
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g));
the sorts separate the tiers: an endorsed-sort identifier resolves only
to an $`\mathbb{E}`$-level block, an untrusted-sort identifier only to a
$`\mathsf{U}`$-block.

A configuration is $`c=(\mathcal{M},\sigma_{P},\sigma_{Q},h)`$: the
store, the Protected-LLM state, the Reader state, and the interpreter’s
sanitized decision history $`h`$: a sequence of (target, decision)
records, one appended at each reached gating review (one per reached
gating position; for a batch, one per gating non-$`\diamond`$ body
position plus one aggregate element decision) — never bytes, never a
block identifier of either sort, never a selection ordinal, never a
candidate multiplicity, collection cardinality, or page count;
selections, candidate lists, page renderings, and per-page decisions are
recorded in the display transcript only
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
A null-handle abort appends the same (target, reject) record a user
rejection appends
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Hence $`h`$ contains no $`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes, exposes no untrusted-sort
identifier
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)),
and carries no occupancy, cardinality, or pagination information
(Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
this is the form machine-checked as HEvent
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ denote the
restrictions of $`\mathcal{M}`$ to levels $`\mathsf{U}`$ and
$`\mathbb{E}`$.

###### Endorsement unit.

The endorsement unit throughout is the *(value, tool) pair*: every
confirmation names an exact byte string and an exact tool, and there is
no endorsement transfer between tools, however similar. (Exact-target
discipline governs the sensitive fast path and all endorsement,
promotion, and counting; the *baseline* data-tool path of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
is scope-blind,
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
and
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
extends the exact-target discipline to data tools.) Combinations,
orderings, and timings of separately endorsed values are ungated by
design (rationale and residual:
[N2](#Thmnotex2 "Note N2 (The endorsement unit). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
hardening:
Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Individuation of trusted blocks.

$`\mathsf{T}`$-blocks are individuated at write time: each field the
user explicitly supplies (or, absent field structure, the command as one
atomic unit) is one $`\mathsf{T}`$-block. The individuating parser is
fixed interpreter code inside the TCB; the fast-path test of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is byte-equality against these stored blocks.

###### Two scopes and one selector.

The agent is a transition system over configurations whose steps are
tool invocations, control flow, and the operations of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
executed in one of two scopes: the *privileged scope* $`P`$ may invoke
any tool and reaches memory only through $`\Sigma`$. Throughout the
formal development $`P`$ is modelled as a *strategy*: a function from
its interaction history, its own emitted operations, the reply stream of
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
its view $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$, and the coins $`\omega`$
(convention ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
to its next operation. Its internal state $`\sigma_{P}`$ is therefore an
abbreviation for that history and carries no independent degrees of
freedom: two runs agreeing on the history agree on $`\sigma_{P}`$ by
definition. This is not a restriction on $`P`$ (the strategy is
arbitrary, adversarial included) but the standard
determinism-modulo-coins reading of
([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and it is the form in which $`P`$ is machine-checked
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The *quarantined scope* $`Q`$ has read-only access to the whole store
and no tool access. A third model role, the *trusted-store retriever*
$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$
(Rule [R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
is a stateless selector over $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$: it reads only
the endorsed store and returns only block identifiers, which the
interpreter dereferences. (The asymmetry between $`Q`$’s and
$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$’s vision is forced by the theorems:
[N3](#Thmnotex3 "Note N3 (The reader asymmetry). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Definition S2.3 (Protected-LLM view).

For a configuration $`c`$, let $`H(c)`$ denote the handle structure of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and $`x(c)`$ the trusted command input received so far; $`h`$ is the
decision history. The *Protected-LLM view* is

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)\;=\;\big(\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}},\;H(c),\;x(c),\;h\big).
``` |  |

By
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and Rules
[R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$ together with the reply stream of
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the entirety of what $`P`$ can observe
(Lemma [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Remark S2.4 (Information interface vs. effect interface).

$`\Sigma`$ is the interface of *effects*; $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$ is the
interface of *information*. Granting $`P`$ direct sight of
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ in its view is a deliberate, conservative
strengthening: every theorem quantifies over all strategies of this
better-informed $`P`$, so it a fortiori covers any $`P`$ that must
acquire the same data operationally, and the two-run theorem is *harder*
under it (a more informed $`P`$ has more ways to diverge).
$`\mathsf{recall}`$ on endorsed identifiers is consequently
informationally redundant and is retained as the operational access
path; the sentence “$`P`$ reaches memory only through $`\Sigma`$”
concerns effects, not information. The mechanization adopts exactly this
reading
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
obs is computed through memEOf).

###### Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations).

A *sensitive sink event* is a call $`\mathsf{tool}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})`$
with $`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$.

A *gating position* of a tool invocation is an argument position that
does not pass the fast path of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The invocation’s gating positions are processed left to right as one
atomic *gate transaction*
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
at each reached position the interpreter resolves the argument, displays
its bytes with zoned provenance
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and reads the user’s selection (if among candidates) and decision
$`z\in\{\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\}`$; a null resolution renders
the fixed no-value display of
Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and takes the standard reject outcome, consuming no decision; a
rejecting outcome aborts the review of the remaining positions.

An accepting review of resolved bytes $`v`$ at target $`t`$ is a
*confirmation event* $`\mathsf{confirm}(v,t)`$. Confirmations are
*durable*: at the close of the atomic transaction the interpreter
writes, for every accepted gating position, one fresh endorsed copy of
its displayed bytes scoped to the target
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
*whether or not the transaction as a whole succeeds*. The tool itself
executes iff every gating position was accepted and none was null; on
execution the bytes that flow at each position are exactly the bytes
displayed for it, and on abort no argument flows.

*Counting unit.* For all accounting
(Appendices [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
confirmations are counted per *(value, tool) pair per gate transaction*:
accepting reviews of the same exact pair at several positions of one
transaction are one pair-confirmation; the repeated reviews themselves
are attention cost
([N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

A standalone $`\mathsf{confirm}(v,t)`$ with $`t`$ a tool or “reasoning”
is the single-position special case. The “publish” target is not a local
confirmation: it creates no local block and is defined by the Publish
transitions of
Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Batch-element page approvals under
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are call-local: they authorize the displayed elements for that
$`\mathsf{map}`$ instance only and create no durable copy; gating
non-$`\diamond`$ arguments of a map body are ordinary durable
confirmations
(convention [(vii^(′))](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

#### S2.2 Operational semantics

Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
give the *interface transition schema* of the memory interface: complete
at the level of the interface alphabet (every operation’s store effect
and reply is fixed here, with totality per
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
with the remaining components of the run state — fixed by
Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— evolving by the deterministic bookkeeping stated in the rules and
conventions. Every transition is fixed interpreter code; no model
participates in any label assignment or any reply. Replies to $`P`$ are
drawn from the grammar at the top of
Figure [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and nothing else
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the side conditions cite the Rules of
§[S2.3](#A2.SS3a "S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which constrain naming, atomicity, display, and gating. Transitions
triggered by the user or the environment (channel events, gate
decisions, tool returns) are marked with their trigger; all others are
$`P`$-emitted.

###### Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration).

The full run state comprises: the store $`\mathcal{M}`$; the two
identifier allocators of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)
(endorsed-sort and untrusted-sort); the interpreter-private
handle-resolution table (index $`=`$ handle identifier; never read by
any reply,
Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
$`P`$’s reply stream
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the decision history $`h`$; the trusted command input $`x(c)`$; the
executed-tool, confirmation, and reader-event counters that index the
environment’s oracles; and three ghost logs used only by the theorems —
the display transcript $`\mathsf{DT}`$
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the sensitive-sink log
(Definition [S3.7](#A3.Thmtheorem7 "Definition S3.7 (Ungated sink projection). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and $`P`$’s emitted-operation log. $`P`$-visible components are exactly
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$ and the reply stream
(Lemma [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
all others are interpreter-private or ghost. A block is *readable* iff
it is at level $`\mathbb{E}`$, i.e. dereferenceable to bytes by
$`\mathsf{recall}`$ (Recall-E); $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks are never readable
to $`P`$. For the map-free fragment, the executable interpreter of
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
realizes this extended configuration verbatim (IState), and the figures
are its human-readable projection onto the store and reply components.

Replies to $`P`$
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle r\;::=\;\mathsf{ack}\;\mid\;h_{j}\;\mid\;\mathsf{fail}\;\mid\;\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{accept})\;\mid\;\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{reject})\;\mid\;\mathsf{bytes}(b),\ b\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ |  |

Replies to $`P`$ form a *stream*; the grammar above is its *alphabet*. A
single transition may append more than one token (e.g. Tool-Gate-Acc
appends $`\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{accept})\cdot\mathsf{ack}`$), per
convention [(iii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

Judgment. $`\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\;o\;\Downarrow\;r\;}\mathcal{M}^{\prime}`$:
operation $`o`$ yields reply $`r`$; components of $`c`$ other than
$`\mathcal{M}`$ are suppressed when unchanged; $`h_{j}`$ is the $`j`$-th
operation-determined handle
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Transitions triggered by the user or the environment are marked by their
trigger; all others are $`P`$-emitted. Conclusions suppress the
operation label over the arrow where the premises display it; the
components of the extended configuration
(Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
other than $`\mathcal{M}`$ evolve by the deterministic bookkeeping
stated in the rules and conventions, and the figures are the store/reply
projection of that full-state transition, realized executably (for the
map-free fragment) by the mechanization (IState,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
````

````math
right={$h$ extended; fresh copy, scope $\sigma(t)$ (conv.~\hyperref@@ii[S-sos:vii]{(vii)})}}\frac{\text{gate }\mathsf{confirm}(v,t),\quad t\ \text{a tool or reasoning}\quad\text{user rejects, or null handle (Rule~\ref{S-r:null})}}{\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\;\Downarrow\,\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{reject})\;}\mathcal{M}}\quad\textsc{lab=Conf-Rej,

provenance }\mathsf{confirmed}\quad\text{owner accepts on the decision pane (Rule~\ref{S-r:display})}}{\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\;\Downarrow\,\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{accept})\;}\mathcal{M}\quad\text{emitting }\mathsf{submit}(v)\ \text{to the federation
log}}\quad\textsc{lab=Publish-Acc,

(Rule~\ref{S-r:share}), or null (Rule~\ref{S-r:null})}}{\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\;\Downarrow\,\mathsf{dec}(\mathrm{reject})\;}\mathcal{M}}\quad\textsc{lab=Publish-Rej,

(\ref{S-r:nobit})}}\frac{P\ \text{emits }\mathsf{evict}(\mathrm{id})\quad\text{interpreter-side: if }\mathrm{id}\text{ resolves to a block
of the owner's local store,}\quad\text{that block is removed; otherwise the operation is a no-op}\quad\text{resolution status consumed interpreter-side

right={uniform reply; no label change}}
````

Figure S3: Interface transition schema of the memory interface (2/2):
search, crystallization, confirmation, eviction, iteration, and failure,
continued from
Figure [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
