Every transition is fixed interpreter code; no model assigns any label
or composes any reply. Conventions for both figures follow below.

Conventions (apply to
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(i) $`\mathrm{capture}(o)`$ stores the outputs $`o`$ as
$`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks $`\operatorname{newU}(\cdot,\mathsf{ingress})`$
bound to a single fresh collection handle $`h_{j}`$
(Rules [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the identifier is operation-determined, computable by $`P`$, and never
returned. A call whose captured output count is zero binds its
collection handle with _null_ resolution
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
a zero-cardinality capture and an empty search result are the same
null-resolution case. The capture operation exposes no direct
cardinality or resolution bit to $`P`$
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
any later distinction surfaces only through the logged null-collection
display and its standard aggregated reject
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
(ii) Element calls inside Map are interpreter-iterated, not
$`P`$-emitted: individually neither handle-producing nor acknowledged.
If the argument collection has null resolution (an empty search result
or zero-output capture,
convention [(i)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the tool-free form $`\mathsf{map}(\mathsf{crystallize}(\diamond),H)`$
writes no summaries, binds the map’s operation-determined output
collection handle with null resolution
(Rules [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),(c), [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
returns the ordinary $`\mathsf{ack}`$, and appends no display or
decision event; the tool-bearing form takes the null-collection batch
treatment of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b).
(iii) In Tool-Gate-Acc and Tool-Gate-Rej, gating positions are reviewed
left to right; one decision is recorded per reached gating position, and
the displayed bytes of an executed call are exactly the bytes that flow;
the entire step is atomic
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Every accepted position’s fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy is written at the
close of the step, on the accepting and the aborting branch alike;
rejected and null positions never flow and write nothing. The reply
stream carries _one_ decision token per gated invocation, regardless of
the number of gating positions; per-position decisions are recorded in
the transcript and in $`h`$ only
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)(i),(iv)).
Whether an invocation is gated at all is a deterministic function of
$`P`$’s own emitted argument list and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
hence already $`P`$-computable; the token-shape difference between
Tool-Fast, Tool-Gate-Acc, and Tool-Gate-Rej therefore carries no
information beyond trusted data and the logged decisions
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
(the $`\mathsf{CC}`$ branch’s live-entry bit is $`\mathbb{E}`$-level log
data, coupled under
[A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
in two-run comparisons (exogenous prefix coupled; local suffixes derived
equal,
Def. [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
and within the reject class, user rejection and null-handle abort remain
indistinguishable in the reply and in $`h`$
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(iv) *Totality*
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)):
every well-formed invocation with any argument is covered: unresolvable
arguments take Recall-O-style opaque-handle replies, failed
deterministic preconditions take Fail; no invocation is undefined and
none distinguishes attacker-influenced states.
(v) $`\mathcal{M}\ominus\mathrm{id}`$ denotes
$`\mathcal{M}\setminus\{\mathrm{id}\}`$ when $`\mathrm{id}`$ resolves to
a block of the owner’s local store, and $`\mathcal{M}`$ otherwise. The
reply is the constant $`\mathsf{ack}`$ in every case; the realised
outcome (removal of the owner’s block, at either level; no-op on an
identifier not resolving to a block of the owner’s local store,
including an unoccupied one) is recorded in the audit log
interpreter-side and never returned to $`P`$. The effect on
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ is $`P`$-visible trusted data
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
any effect on $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$, and the absence of any
effect, are indistinguishable to $`P`$. A _handle_ argument to
$`\mathsf{evict}`$ is a deterministic malformation of $`P`$’s own
emission and takes the generic failure outcome
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)(iii)).
(vi) Channel-triggered transitions (W-Typed, W-Paste) acknowledge the
channel; nothing is appended to $`P`$’s reply stream, so the presence or
absence of a paste event is not $`P`$-observable
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
(vii) *Fresh-copy endorsement; block immutability.* An accepting
confirmation never relabels a block in place: Conf-Acc and Tool-Gate-Acc
write, per accepted value, one _fresh_ $`\mathsf{C}`$-labelled block
carrying exactly the displayed bytes, at the next endorsed-sort
identifier
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)),
with scope $`\sigma(t)=\{t\}`$ for a tool target and
$`\sigma(\text{reasoning})=\varnothing`$ (readable, but never eligible
for the sensitive fast path of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the resolved source block, where one exists, is unchanged and remains at
its level, and the publish target
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is a shared-tier act creating no local block. Endorsement is _durable_:
the accepted positions’ fresh copies are written at the close of the
atomic step whether or not the enclosing invocation executes
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Consequently no transition of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
alters an existing block’s bytes, label, or scope: blocks are immutable
once written, and the store changes only by creation of fresh blocks and
by Evict. (vii^(′)) *Batch acceptance is call-local for elements.* An
accepting batch confirmation
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
authorizes each $`\diamond`$-element’s bytes for its own element call of
that $`\mathsf{map}`$ instance only: no persistent endorsed copy of any
element is created, and the elements remain $`\mathsf{U}`$-labelled in
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$. Fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$-copies are written
for the accepted _gating non-$`\diamond`$ arguments_, one each, scoped
$`\{\mathsf{tool}\}`$, exactly as at Tool-Gate-Acc, and durably so: they
persist even when a later element page rejects and no element call
executes (Map-Tool-Rej). This is forced by the identifier discipline of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g):
per-element copies would allocate $`|H|`$ endorsed-sort identifiers with
$`|H|`$ attacker-chosen, exposing an attacker-dependent quantity in
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$; the non-$`\diamond`$ count is fixed by
$`P`$’s emitted body.
Convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
per-accepted-value fresh copy, and the endorsed-copy clause of
Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
are read with this carve-out: they govern Conf-Acc and Tool-Gate-Acc;
batch-accepted elements flow under
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
displayed-bytes binding without entering $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$.
Consequently re-processing the same elements in a later $`\mathsf{map}`$
is gated afresh — call-local authorization caches nothing — and the
single-approval cap
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
does not extend to map elements, whose confirmations are per-task cost
(Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Scope).

- Commentary (non-normative; the Map rules and the mechanization
  boundary). The split fixes, per body form, the decision token (none
  for the tool-free form), the store effect ($`\mathrm{capture}`$ of
  element outputs vs. schema-bound $`\mathsf{U}`$-summaries
  $`s_{1},\dots,s_{|H|}`$ written as in Cryst), and the endorsement
  effect (fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$-copies for gating non-$`\diamond`$
  arguments only; elements are authorized call-locally,
  convention [(vii^(′))](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  In every case, including rejection, exactly one collection-handle
  index is consumed, on rejection with null resolution — so handle
  structure is independent of the outcome
  (Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
  closing the identifier channel a skipped index would open.
  $`\mathsf{map}`$ is normative here; its batch-confirmation surface —
  pagination, per-page decisions, the aggregated decision,
  all-or-nothing displayed-bytes flow, and batch determinacy — is
  mechanized as a standalone layer (BatchGate.lean,
  §[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  while its store-level integration into the run-level interpreter
  remains outside the mechanized surface
  (delta ([6](#A9.I3.i6 "Item 6 ‣ Modeling deltas. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).

#### S2.3 Interface rules

The rules below constrain the transitions of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Each clause is normative and implementable as stated; all rationale
lives in
Appendix [S7](#A7 "Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
under the keys cited, or in the marked commentary blocks of
§[S1.1](#A1.SS1a "S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers).

1.  (a)
    Handle identifiers (including collection-handle identifiers) are
    drawn from the sequence of $`P`$-emitted operations alone: the
    $`j`$-th handle-producing operation of a run binds identifier
    $`h_{j}`$. Identifiers never encode, count, or depend on store
    contents.
2.  (b)
    Handle-producing operations: ingress capture (the triggering tool
    invocation is $`P`$-emitted; $`P`$ computes the collection handle’s
    identifier from its own operation count; nothing is returned);
    $`\mathsf{recall}`$ returning a handle; $`\mathsf{fill}`$;
    $`\mathsf{crystallize}`$; $`\mathsf{map}`$.
3.  (c)
    A $`\mathsf{map}`$ invocation is exactly one handle-producing
    operation regardless of collection cardinality: its per-element
    outputs are captured as $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks bound to a single
    fresh collection handle determined by the $`\mathsf{map}`$’s
    position in $`P`$’s operation sequence. Element calls are
    interpreter-iterated, not $`P`$-emitted, and are individually
    neither handle-producing nor acknowledged.
4.  (d)
    $`P`$ reaches captured element outputs only through
    $`\mathsf{fill}`$/$`\mathsf{crystallize}`$ searches. No handle
    identifier depends on collection size.
5.  (e)
    A collection handle admits exactly two uses: as the argument of
    $`\mathsf{map}`$, or as a tool argument — the latter defined by
    desugaring: an invocation $`\mathsf{tool}(\dots,h,\dots)`$ with a
    collection-handle argument $`h`$ _is_ the instance
    $`\mathsf{map}(\mathsf{tool}(\dots,\diamond,\dots),h)`$, the
    desugaring applied before the invocation matches any transition of
    Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (it never instantiates Tool-Fast or Tool-Gate-\*), batch-gated per
    Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and subject to the body grammar of clause (f) (in particular at most
    one collection handle per invocation and no other handle argument;
    violations take the generic failure outcome, deterministic in
    $`P`$’s own emission,
    Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    A collection handle exposes no length, no indexing, and no
    per-element access.
6.  (f)
    _Map bodies._ The body $`\hat{o}`$ of $`\mathsf{map}(\hat{o},H)`$ is
    a single operation template containing exactly one occurrence of the
    distinguished element placeholder $`\diamond`$, of one of exactly
    two forms: (i) one tool invocation
    $`\mathsf{tool}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})`$ in which one argument is
    $`\diamond`$ and every other argument is a $`P`$-supplied non-handle
    value, subject per argument to the ordinary mediation of
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (fast-path values flow; a gating argument is confirmed once for the
    whole batch, at the batch confirmation of
    Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    alongside the elements); or (ii) one tool-free
    $`\mathsf{crystallize}(\diamond)`$ template. The body may not
    contain $`\mathsf{map}`$, $`\mathsf{recall}`$, $`\mathsf{fill}`$,
    $`\mathsf{evict}`$, $`\mathsf{confirm}`$, $`\mathsf{display}`$, the
    write operation $`\mathsf{write}_{P}`$, or a handle argument (the
    interpreter-side captures of forms (i)–(ii) are transitions of the
    interpreter, not body operations); nesting is not defined.
    Well-formedness is a syntactic test on $`P`$’s emitted operation
    alone, and a body outside this grammar takes the generic failure
    outcome, deterministic in $`P`$’s own emission
    (Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Multi-step per-element pipelines are expressed as successive
    $`\mathsf{map}`$s: each $`\mathsf{map}`$ yields a fresh collection
    handle (clause (c)), which clause (e) admits as the argument of a
    further $`\mathsf{map}`$, each step batch-gated independently; the
    grammar restricts the shape of one step, never the depth of a
    pipeline.
7.  (g)
    _Two-sorted block identifiers._ Block identifiers are drawn from two
    disjoint sorts, _endorsed_
    ($`\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{0},\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{1},\dots`$)
    and _untrusted_
    ($`\mathrm{id}^{\mathsf{U}}_{0},\mathrm{id}^{\mathsf{U}}_{1},\dots`$),
    each allocated in sequence. Endorsed-sort identifiers are allocated
    by exactly the local endorsed-block-creating transitions: W-Typed,
    W-P, Conf-Acc, and, per _accepted gating position_, Tool-Gate-Acc,
    Tool-Gate-Rej, Map-Tool-Acc, and Map-Tool-Rej (for maps, gating
    non-$`\diamond`$ body positions only — a count fixed by $`P`$’s
    emitted operation, never by the collection cardinality,
    convention [(vii^(′))](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    A publish decision allocates no identifier of either sort
    (Publish-Acc). The $`j`$-th endorsed block of a run sits at
    $`\mathrm{id}^{\mathbb{E}}_{j}`$, a position determined by the
    coupled event sequence (the typed stream, $`P`$’s emitted
    operations, and the logged decisions) alone, hence computable by
    $`P`$ and identical across runs whose coupled events agree.
    Untrusted-sort identifiers are allocated by the untrusted-writing
    transitions (W-Paste, ingress capture, Cryst) and may depend on
    attacker-chosen multiplicities; no untrusted-sort identifier is ever
    exposed to $`P`$ by any reply or view
    (Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
    An endorsed-sort identifier never resolves to a $`\mathsf{U}`$-block
    and an untrusted-sort identifier never resolves to an
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-block, so the sorts separate the tiers syntactically.
    Like handle identifiers, block identifiers of either sort never
    encode, count, or depend on store contents beyond this allocation
    order.

- Commentary (non-normative; role of the identifier
  discipline). Clause (g) closes the identifier channel that in-place
  endorsement would open: identifiers visible to $`P`$ (those of
  $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$) depend only on coupled events, while
  every attacker-dependent multiplicity can influence only
  untrusted-sort identifiers, which no reply and no view exposes. It is
  consumed by
  Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  (Step [4](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  and is machine-checked as the two-sorted id space of the mechanization
  (§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement).

When confirmations gate a tool call, the reviews of all gating
positions, the writing of the accepted positions’ fresh endorsed copies,
and the invocation (or its abort) form one atomic interpreter step: no
step may interleave between display, decision, endorsement, and flow.
The bytes that flow at an executed call are the displayed bytes, bound
to that call instance. If any gating position is rejected or null, the
invocation aborts entire: no argument flows; the accepted positions’
endorsed copies are nevertheless written, their accepting decisions
being recorded in the transcript like any confirmation. When a batch
confirmation gates a $`\mathsf{map}`$
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the aggregated accepting decision and the batch of element invocations
form one atomic step, and the bytes that flow at each element call are
exactly the element bytes displayed for that call; accepted gating
non-$`\diamond`$ arguments are endorsed durably exactly as at a direct
call, whatever the element pages’ outcome.

- Commentary (non-normative; severability and durable
  endorsement). Soundness of durable endorsement on an aborting
  transaction is the severability clause of
  [A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
  intent is per displayed value, severally. A commit-on-success variant
  — discarding accepted positions’ copies on abort — would be
  safety-monotone but _sacrifices the once-per-pair cap_
  ([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
  a transaction that accepts one pair and aborts on a later position
  leaves no durable copy, so re-presentations of the same pair re-force
  it without bound. Durability is adopted precisely because the cap is
  load-bearing
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured).

Tools partition into $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$ (sensitive,
effectful) and $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$ (data readers); the
partition and the canonical tool identifiers are fixed deployment
configuration, per capability, inside the TCB. The interpreter captures
_every_ tool output, including the status and error responses of
sensitive calls, to $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ with label
$`\mathsf{U}`$, and returns to $`P`$ only a single constant
acknowledgement token per invocation: never the bytes, never a success
bit, never a count, size, or identifier derived from captured content.

###### Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary).

1.  (a)
    A value $`a`$ passed to a tool in $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$
    flows without confirmation _iff_ $`a`$ consists of readable
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-level bytes and the interpreter verifies that $`a`$
    byte-equals a stored $`\mathsf{T}`$-block, or byte-equals some
    $`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$-block $`b`$ with
    $`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$ (for $`\mathsf{CC}`$, the
    matched block is the live shared-tier entry, checked valid at call
    time;
    §[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    ($`\mathsf{PC}`$ blocks have empty scope and never pass this test.)
2.  (b)
    A value passed to a tool in $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$ flows
    without confirmation iff it consists of readable
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-level bytes.
3.  (c)
    A handle argument never flows silently to any tool: it always
    triggers $`\mathsf{confirm}(a,\mathsf{tool})`$, at data tools
    exactly as at sensitive ones, regardless of whether its resolved
    bytes coincide with stored endorsed content. There are no per-tool
    exceptions.
4.  (d)
    The fast-path check is membership in $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$
    plus a scope test, not taint-tracking of $`P`$’s code.

###### Rule R5 (Readable local endorsement).

Every accepting confirmation with target
$`t\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}\cup\{\mathrm{reasoning}\}`$
writes a fresh block $`\operatorname{newC}(v,t)`$
(Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
$`\operatorname{newCache}(v,t)`$) carrying exactly the displayed bytes,
labelled $`\mathsf{C}`$ (or, under community promotion, the shared tier
carries $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status;
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
at the next endorsed-sort identifier
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g));
its bytes are readable by $`P`$ via $`\mathsf{recall}`$, the identifier
being computable by $`P`$ from its own coupled event history. The
originating untrusted block, where one exists, is unchanged and remains
untrusted. Before confirmation, a crystallized summary is
$`\mathsf{U}`$-labelled, lives reader/interpreter-side, and is not in
$`\sigma_{P}`$. An accepting _publish_ decision creates no local block
and allocates no endorsed-sort identifier: it emits only the shared-tier
submission event of
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(Publish-Acc).

###### Rule R6 (Null handle).

A $`\mathsf{fill}`$ or $`\mathsf{crystallize}`$ search over
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ that finds nothing returns a _null handle_:
the handle’s existence and identifier are fixed by the requesting
operation
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
only its resolution differs, and that difference is hidden from $`P`$.
Likewise, $`\mathsf{recall}`$ on an identifier that does not resolve to
a readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-block returns a handle of the same kind:
whether it resolves to $`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes or to nothing (in
particular, whether the identifier is occupied at all) is hidden from
$`P`$. If a null handle is passed to any tool, the gate fires as usual
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the decision pane renders a fixed “no value resolved” display, recorded
in the display transcript like any confirmation event, the call aborts,
and $`P`$ receives the standard reject decision, indistinguishable in
the reply stream and in the sanitized history $`h`$ from a user
rejection
(Definition [S2.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the no-value display itself is recorded on the transcript like any
confirmation event.

###### Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability).

The success/failure of a $`\mathsf{U}`$-store search, and the resolution
status of any $`\mathsf{recall}`$, is consumed interpreter-side to
choose the null-vs-real handle; no reply and no sanitized-history record
exposes it. A handle’s private resolution may later be displayed at a
gate: that display and the user’s logged decision are an explicit
transcript release
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
not a failure channel. Any reader error, reader crash, or reader budget
exhaustion arising during an operation over $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$
is likewise consumed interpreter-side: the operation returns the same
operation-determined handle it would return on success
(Rules [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
whose resolution to bytes, to nothing, or to an aborted computation is
hidden from $`P`$. The generic failure outcome ($`\mathsf{fail}`$,
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is reserved for failures that are a deterministic function of $`P`$’s
own emitted operations, $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, and the coupled
coins $`\omega`$ alone (malformed invocations, failed preconditions on
$`\sigma_{P}`$, and the retrieval failure of Retrieve-F). Search
outcomes over $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ are trusted data and may be
exposed. (Rationale and the store-quota corollary:
[N4](#Thmnotex4 "Note N4 (Failure indistinguishability, operationally). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S7](#Thmobjx7 "Analysis S7 (Store-exhaustion side channel). ‣ S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention ([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).)

###### Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface).

1.  (a)
    The display surface is split into a _decision pane_ and auxiliary
    _selection surfaces_.
2.  (b)
    The decision pane shows exactly the resolved bytes that will flow
    (or be recorded as endorsed content), plus a provenance line in two
    visually separated zones: (i) _attested facts_ (channel, label
    history, timestamps, signature-verification status), rendered in an
    interpreter-controlled region: TCB-authenticated, not
    attacker-forgeable or -alterable in content (event _timing_ may be
    attacker-influenced, e.g. a captured tool output’s timestamp
    reflects when the attacker acted; what is guaranteed is that the
    recorded facts are true and unmodified); (ii) _source-identification
    strings_ originating in untrusted content (sender names, subjects,
    citations), rendered verbatim and visibly marked _unverified_. Where
    a transaction aborts after some accepting reviews, the pane states
    that the accepted values remain authorized for their targets.
3.  (c)
    The decision pane contains no reader-generated prose outside the
    confirmed payload region; where the payload itself is a crystallized
    summary, it is reader-generated by construction, rendered verbatim,
    and governed by
    Assumption [A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
4.  (d)
    Selection surfaces may show reader-generated previews, visibly
    marked unverified; previews are rendered UI-side only and never
    returned to $`P`$, and carry no endorsement authority.
5.  (e)
    Both surfaces are recorded in the display transcript and the audit
    log
    (Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
6.  (f)
    On a rejection, the displayed bytes are not returned to $`P`$; $`P`$
    receives only the decision. (Preview rationale:
    [N8](#Thmnotex8 "Note N8 (What previews can and cannot do). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration).

1.  (a)
    A tool call reached inside $`\mathsf{map}`$ over a
    $`\mathsf{U}`$-collection — including the desugared form of a
    collection-handle tool argument
    (Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e))
    — takes no fast path of
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
2.  (b)
    The map is gated as a single _batch_ confirmation whose decision
    pane displays the collection’s cardinality _and the full resolved
    bytes of every element_, together with the resolved bytes of any
    gating non-$`\diamond`$ argument of the body
    (Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)),
    displayed once for the batch, paginated as needed, the cardinality
    displayed and recorded on the first page; per-page cardinality is
    capped at $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$; the interpreter performs any
    split, presenting a larger collection as successive pages of one
    batch confirmation. A deployment may additionally fix a
    total-cardinality cap (TCB configuration): a $`\mathsf{map}`$ over a
    collection exceeding it renders a fixed oversize display — recorded
    in the transcript like the no-value display of
    Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    — and takes the standard aggregated reject of clause (c), consuming
    no decision, indistinguishable in the reply stream and in $`h`$ from
    a page rejection or a null collection. A _null collection_ (a
    collection handle with null resolution: an empty search result, or a
    zero-output capture,
    convention [(i)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    Rules [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
    [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    is handled identically: the interpreter renders the fixed no-value
    display of
    Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    recorded in the transcript as a batch event exactly like the
    oversize display, and the map takes the standard aggregated reject
    of clause (c), consuming no decision (Map-Tool-Rej; mechanized as
    batchGate_null,
    §[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    The no-value and oversize displays are distinct event kinds
    (Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    so the first recorded batch event determines the size class
    (Lemma [S3.20](#A3.Thmtheorem20 "Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
3.  (c)
    $`P`$ receives a single aggregated decision for the whole map
    (accept iff every page was accepted, else the single standard
    reject), regardless of page count. The number of pages, like the
    cardinality itself, is never returned to $`P`$ in any form; both are
    displayed to the user and recorded in the transcript only.
4.  (d)
    Each page’s rendering and decision is recorded in the transcript;
    the aggregated decision is recorded once. By
    Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    the bytes that flow at each element call are exactly the element
    bytes displayed for it. The user may reject at any page, aborting
    the remainder. The oversize and null-collection displays are
    recorded under their respective fixed-display event kinds
    (Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    each with its standard reject and the aggregated batch decision.
5.  (e)
    Per-element results are captured to $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and
    never returned to $`P`$ (the map returns one ack token).
    (All-or-nothing rationale and $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$ sizing:
    [N6](#Thmnotex6 "Note N6 (The batch gate is all-or-nothing). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S12](#Thmobjx12 "Analysis S12 (Batch-gate attention). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality).

1.  (a)
    Every value the interpreter returns to $`P`$ is of one of two kinds.
    The first kind is drawn from a fixed finite alphabet independent of
    the attack and the environment: (i) one constant acknowledgement per
    _executed_ tool invocation or $`\mathsf{map}`$, independent of
    outcome and of the number, size, or content of captured blocks; a
    gate-rejected invocation does not execute and returns only the
    reject decision of item (iv) (Tool-Gate-Rej); (ii) opaque handles
    named by
    Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"); (iii)
    the generic failure outcome of
    Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    deterministic in $`P`$’s emitted operations,
    $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, and the coupled coins $`\omega`$; (iv)
    the user’s decision at a confirmation, with the null-gate abort of
    Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    rendered as the reject decision. The second kind is (v): verbatim
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes dereferenced from $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$.
2.  (b)
    _Totality._ Every syntactically well-formed invocation of every
    operation of
    Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    with any argument, has its behaviour defined by the figures and
    these rules; failed preconditions and unresolvable arguments are
    rendered, uniformly, as the generic failure outcome or as an
    operation-determined opaque handle, never as a distinguishing error.
    In particular, whether a given identifier is occupied by a
    $`\mathsf{U}`$-block is never observable to $`P`$ through any
    operation: $`\mathsf{recall}`$ and $`\mathsf{evict}`$ alike return
    operation-determined replies (an opaque handle; the constant
    $`\mathsf{ack}`$) uniformly across resolving, non-resolving,
    $`\mathsf{U}`$-occupied, and $`\mathbb{E}`$-occupied arguments,
    resolution consumed interpreter-side
    (Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval).

$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ (i) reads only $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, never
any $`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes; (ii) has no tool access; (iii) returns only
block identifiers, which the interpreter dereferences against
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ verbatim; non-dereferencing output is
discarded. $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$’s sampling randomness is coupled
alongside $`P`$’s
(convention ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
(Why neither reader’s vision can be relaxed:
[N3](#Thmnotex3 "Note N3 (The reader asymmetry). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Deployment-selectable hardening.

Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are formally instantiated: each strictly gates more flows, and their
monotonicity is proved as
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is a requirements-level extension, outside the formal semantics and
outside
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
quantifier
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values).

$`\mathsf{T}`$-blocks require a first-use confirmation per sensitive
sink, after which scope-caching applies. Blocks created by these
confirmations carry the interpreter-only provenance mark _cache_ and are
ineligible for submission
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools).

The data-tool clause of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
is replaced by the sensitive-tool test of clause (a): a value passed to
a tool in $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$ flows without confirmation
_iff_ it byte-equals a stored $`\mathsf{T}`$-block, or byte-equals some
$`\mathsf{C}`$/$`\mathsf{CC}`$-block $`b`$ with
$`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$ (for $`\mathsf{CC}`$, the live
shared-tier entry, checked valid at call time,
§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Any other data-tool argument — a freshly composed value, or endorsed
bytes whose scope does not admit this data tool (in particular every
reasoning-target copy, whose scope is empty,
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— is confirmed once; the fresh copy is scoped $`\{\mathsf{tool}\}`$ per
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
so it scope-caches and covers all the user’s later use of the pair
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Blocks created by these confirmations carry the interpreter-only _cache_
mark and are ineligible for submission
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
their gate events are cache confirmations, accept-inert per
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)).

$`\mathsf{C}`$-scopes carry a deployment-set lease
(convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))):
expiry withdraws the expired copy’s tool authorization, so the pair’s
next scope-checked use with no other currently authorizing witness
re-confirms once. Unlike
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is specified at the requirements level only: it is _not_ part of the
formal semantics of this document, no theorem quantifies over it, and
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
does not cover it. A conforming instantiation is a future extension
obligated to satisfy all of the following, and to prove analogues of
Lemma [S3.20](#A3.Thmtheorem20 "Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the ledger accounting of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
for the extended semantics.

1.  (a)
    _Immutability._ Blocks stay immutable
    ([A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
    a lease is a validity predicate computed interpreter-side from
    creation-time metadata (creation epoch or slot index, never
    wall-clock time) and the current index; expiry is never a block
    mutation or removal.
2.  (b)
    _Determinism on matched data._ Validity inputs are functions of the
    coupled event sequence, and lease state is added to the matched
    components of
    Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and carried through the unwinding, so matched runs gate identically.
3.  (c)
    _Witness-level expiry at tool targets._ For tool targets, expiry
    invalidates only the expired local authorization witness (an
    ordinary or cache-marked $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy), and the two
    authorization tests it touches are kept distinct. _Literal
    authorization_, on a scope-checked literal path, is existential over
    whichever witnesses the deployment’s selected formal options
    recognize there — byte-equal $`\mathsf{T}`$-blocks (per
    [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
    per-sink treatment where selected), live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ entries,
    and lease-valid in-scope $`\mathsf{C}`$ copies; the baseline
    data-tool path of
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
    is scope-blind, so lease enforcement at data tools requires
    [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    — and a literal use gates iff no such witness currently authorizes
    the pair. _Handle coverage_
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
    is narrower: a handle use gates in every case
    (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
    and is _covered_ iff the identity holds a lease-valid, in-scope
    local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy; a $`\mathsf{T}`$ or live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$
    witness never makes a handle use covered, exactly as in the base
    semantics. The reasoning-coverage branch of
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
    remains readability-based and lease-insensitive: reasoning-target
    reuse never requires another approval.
4.  (d)
    _Classification and renewal._ An expiry-induced gate whose pair
    lacks any currently authorizing witness is _required_ — whether a
    literal gate fired by expiry or a handle gate reclassified from
    covered to required because no lease-valid in-scope $`\mathsf{C}`$
    copy remains. Any required approval so caused writes the fresh copy
    prescribed by the _triggering rule_ — an ordinary $`\mathsf{C}`$
    copy at an ordinary confirmation, a cache-marked, federation-inert
    copy at an
    [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")/[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    cache gate
    (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
    — and starts a new lease, so subsequent literal or handle use within
    the new period is fast-pathed or covered: at most one required
    confirmation per pair per lease period. The class is determined by
    the gate that fired, never by any expired duplicate witness;
    rejection and abandonment renew nothing; duplicate matching copies
    are resolved by the existential tests of clause (c), never by a
    selection among witnesses.
5.  (e)
    _Accounting._ With each (user, item) seeing
    $`E_{\mathrm{lease}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ lease periods, the extension’s
    pathwise floor is the once-per-pair cap per lease period, an
    $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$ multiplicative factor on
    Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
    constants — an extension-level claim, to be proved with the
    extension. No saturation-vanishing conclusion follows from
    $`E_{\mathrm{lease}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ alone: expiry re-fires of
    promoted pairs are residual required confirmations, so the extension
    additionally requires an
    [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-augmented
    analogue of the _complete_ residual bound of
    [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and
    Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
    — the per-pair $`D_{0}+\varepsilon\,n`$ form with expiry re-fires
    included, together with its product and residual-fraction rate
    conditions — not merely a substitute for $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$.

([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the single-user twin of the federated re-verification queue:
[N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

#### S2.4 Trust axioms
