###### Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling).

$`\ell(b)`$ is a function of the channel/source of $`b`$ alone, never of
$`\mathrm{bytes}(b)`$. Hence the attacker cannot change any label.

###### Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability).

Blocks are immutable once written: no party and no transition alters an
existing block’s bytes, label, or scope; the store changes only by the
deterministic block-creating transitions of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and by $`\mathsf{evict}`$. Trust is raised only by the creation of a
fresh endorsed block at an accepting $`\mathsf{confirm}`$, or by
deterministic community promotion of a shared-tier entry
(Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the attacker can do neither.

###### Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display).

At a confirmation, the decision-pane bytes are exactly the bytes that
will flow or be recorded; the attested-fact zone is TCB-authenticated
and not attacker-forgeable
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b));
untrusted source-identification strings appear only in the marked zone;
previews are confined to selection surfaces, visibly marked
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement).

The user returns $`\mathrm{accept}`$ on a displayed value $`v`$ at tool
$`\mathsf{tool}`$ only if the user intends exactly $`v`$ to be
authorized for $`\mathsf{tool}`$; the intent is per displayed value,
severally, and does not depend on the outcomes of the transaction’s
other reviews — which is what makes the durable endorsement of
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
sound when a later review aborts the invocation. At a batch confirmation
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the user returns $`\mathrm{accept}`$ on a page only if this intent holds
for _each_ displayed element and each displayed gating non-$`\diamond`$
argument, severally, at the batch’s tool: batch acceptance is the
conjunction of the per-value intents, never an aggregate judgment of the
collection.

###### Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement).

The user returns $`\mathrm{accept}`$ on a displayed crystallized summary
$`S`$ only if, having checked $`S`$ against its displayed source
citations, the user intends $`S`$’s content to inform reasoning.

###### Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream).

The user’s typed command-channel input is an exogenous input stream,
coupled identically across the runs compared in
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

- Commentary (non-normative; epistemic status of
  [A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). [A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  and
  [A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  are trust axioms in the sense of CaMeL [Debenedetti et al.
  (2025)](#bib.bib12);
  [A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is the human-channel idealization that any displayed-content carve-out
  requires. Their epistemic status, the regime that makes them
  defensible, and the discharge of
  [A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  practical content by logging both display surfaces are discussed at
  [N5](#Thmnotex5 "Note N5 (The human channel). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  (see also
  [S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [S12](#Thmobjx12 "Analysis S12 (Batch-gate attention). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
  [A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  realistic weakness at scale is what the community mechanism of
  Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  addresses.

#### S2.5 Attacker model and trusted computing base

###### Attacker.

The attacker controls the _content_ of every $`\mathsf{U}`$-labelled
block, all tool outputs (including sensitive-tool responses and error
strings) and paste-channel input, including the byte-length and the
number of $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks captured per call. It does not control
the user’s typed command input, the labelling, the interpreter, or the
user’s decisions. $`P`$, $`Q`$, and $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ are _isolated
from the attacker, not assumed benign_: the single-user theorems hold
under adversarial behaviour of either reader, and misdirection among the
user’s own typed or endorsed values is a utility failure outside the
threat model
(Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
offers defence in depth; scope discussion:
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Trusted computing base (TCB), single-user.

The TCB comprises: an authenticated command channel distinguishing typed
from pasted from tool input; the canonical tool identifiers and the
$`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}/\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$
partition; the interpreter’s implementation (including byte-equality and
dereference checks) and the individuating parser; the zoned rendering
path of
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
and the hash-chained audit log materializing the display transcript. The
store idealization and quota policy are
convention ([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Federated TCB additions are listed in
§[S4.3](#A4.SS3 "S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

### Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees

This appendix proves two conditional interface properties. _Action
Integrity_ is an exact-byte, exact-tool authorization property: no
untrusted-origin _value_ reaches a sensitive action unless the user
endorsed exactly that value for exactly that action; it does not
authorize the choice to invoke a tool
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
_Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript_ is a fixed-horizon,
termination-insensitive trace-equivalence property: holding fixed
everything the user ever saw and decided on the display surface,
together with the coupled exogenous inputs, untrusted memory has no
further effect on behaviour; it is not a claim of reasoning correctness
or of resistance to manipulation through displayed content
(Remark [S3.9](#A3.Thmtheorem9 "Remark S3.9 (Coverage of the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[N7](#Thmnotex7 "Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The statements are in the noninterference-modulo-declassification
tradition [Goguen & Meseguer (1982)](#bib.bib19); [Goguen & Meseguer
(1984)](#bib.bib20); [Sabelfeld & Sands (2009)](#bib.bib40); [Sabelfeld
& Myers (2004)](#bib.bib39); [Askarov & Sabelfeld (2007)](#bib.bib3);
the first is the PerMIT instance of qualified robustness [Zdancewic &
Myers (2005)](#bib.bib53); [Myers et al. (2006)](#bib.bib33). Both
theorems, the supporting lemmas, the baseline separation, the flow half
of the hardening monotonicity, and the batch-confirmation surface of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are machine-checked
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
scope, axiom audit, artifact, correspondence
Table [S5](#A9.T5 "Table S5 ‣ Checked statements. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the disclosed modelling deltas). Lineage and positioning:
[N1](#Thmnotex1 "Note N1 (Model lineage). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### S3.1 Definitions

###### Definition S3.1 ($`\mathsf{U}`$-equivalence).

$`c_{1}\approx_{\mathsf{U}}c_{2}`$ iff
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c_{1})=\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c_{2})`$: agreement on
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ (content and scopes), $`H(c)`$, $`x(c)`$,
and $`h`$, while $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ may differ arbitrarily
[Volpano et al. (1996)](#bib.bib44); [Sabelfeld & Myers
(2003)](#bib.bib38).

###### Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety).

Fix a finite sequence of display events — decision-pane confirmation
events, each carrying its displayed bytes, target, and decision
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and renderings — and a trusted typed-input stream $`x`$. A recorded
sensitive sink event is _safe_ for that history if every argument value
of the event is: (i) the exact bytes of a typed input unit of $`x`$ (a
$`\mathsf{T}`$-block’s bytes, individuation per
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
or (ii) endorsed at a prior accepting decision-pane confirmation event
of the history displaying exactly those bytes at exactly the event’s
tool (for element calls of a batch-gated $`\mathsf{map}`$, at the batch
confirmation displaying those exact element bytes,
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
or (iii) gated at the event’s own call, the flowed bytes being the
displayed bytes of that call’s accepting confirmation
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The _delegated_ form extends case (ii) by one alternative, relative to a
designated federation-log prefix (in a run, the prefix delivered at the
event’s step,
Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
the bytes byte-equal a live community entry of that prefix’s replay
naming the event’s exact tool, backed by a currently valid promotion
certificate
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A7](#Thmassumptionx7 "Assumption A7 (Federated endorsement transfer). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the personal form is the single-user predicate, machine-checked as
SinkSafe
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
It is consumed by
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)
and
Definition [S3.10](#A3.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration).

A configuration $`c`$ is _well-formed_, written $`\mathsf{WF}(c)`$, if:
(i) every $`\mathsf{T}`$-block’s bytes occur in the typed stream
$`x(c)`$; (ii) every $`\mathsf{C}`$-block $`b`$ with
$`t\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$ is backed by an accepting decision-pane
confirmation event displaying exactly $`\mathrm{bytes}(b)`$ at target
$`t`$ in the audit transcript, with the matching sanitized (target,
accept) record in $`h`$; (iii) no block carries label $`\mathsf{CC}`$
(single-user; the federated counterpart replaces (iii) by a valid
promotion certificate on the federation log,
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(iv) the handle structure $`H(c)`$ and the endorsed-sort identifier
allocation are the operation-determined structures of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
for the configuration’s interaction history, $`\sigma_{P}`$ is the
strategy state of that history
(§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and the recorded reply stream is the interface’s reply to that history
(Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(v) every recorded sink event is safe
(Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
federated form: the delegated predicate). The empty configuration is
well-formed. A _seeded_ configuration (nonempty
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, empty interaction history) is well-formed
only together with a _seed record_: a designated initial-authorization
prefix of the audit transcript (with its sanitized projection in $`h`$)
backing every seeded $`\mathsf{T}`$-block per (i) and every seeded
scoped $`\mathsf{C}`$-block per (ii) — operationally, the authorizations
imported with a migrated store; formally, the record is read as part of
$`x(c)`$, $`h`$, and $`\mathsf{DT}`$, whereupon (i)–(v) hold verbatim. A
seeded configuration without such a record is in general _not_
well-formed; it is _sorted_
(Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
which is what the two-run results require. Well-formedness is preserved
by every transition of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(this is the induction of
Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
machine-checked as the invariant Inv of
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Action Integrity and its corollaries quantify over runs from well-formed
configurations; the two-run results quantify over matched pairs of
sorted configurations
(Definitions [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

The history against which clause (v) reads
Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the configuration’s full audit history: any seed-record prefix
followed by the run transcript
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Remark S3.4.

Clause (v) is the standard inductive strengthening required to prove
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
by induction on run length (mirrored verbatim as the sinkSound field of
Inv in the mechanization,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
it tracks, through the induction, exactly the per-event predicate of
Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
whose universal form over reachable configurations is the theorem’s
conclusion — not an independent assumption, and not circular: the
predicate is defined without reference to the theorem. The
from-arbitrary-well-formed forms are _preservation_ statements; the
empty-initial-configuration forms, where the invariant is established
rather than assumed (inv_init,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
are the creation forms.

###### Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration).

A configuration $`c`$ is _sorted_ if clauses (iii) and (iv) of
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
hold of it: no $`\mathsf{CC}`$ label (federated form as there),
operation-determined handle and endorsed-sort identifier structure with
$`\sigma_{P}`$ the strategy state, and an interface-conformant reply
stream. Every well-formed configuration is sorted. Every _endorsed-seed_
configuration — an arbitrary $`\mathbb{E}`$-level
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ at endorsed-sort identifiers
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)),
an arbitrary $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$, and an empty interaction
history — is sorted, with no seed record required. Sortedness is
preserved by every transition (machine-checked as WFs, with the
endorsed-seed condition EStore;
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- Commentary (non-normative; why two classes). The split is forced by
  the theorems, in opposite directions. Action Integrity is an
  endorsement-soundness statement, so its quantifier must carry
  endorsement soundness: admitting a bare seed as well-formed would
  _falsify_
  Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  (Remark [S3.15](#A3.Thmtheorem15 "Remark S3.15. ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  — a seeded $`\mathsf{C}`$-block with $`t\in\mathsf{scope}`$ flows to
  $`t`$ ungated, with no endorsing confirmation anywhere in the run.
  Reasoning Integrity, by contrast, never consumes endorsement
  soundness: its unwinding needs only the matched view, the
  operation-determined naming of
  Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  and the strategy reading — precisely the sorted clauses — so its
  quantifier is deliberately the weaker class, admitting arbitrary
  shared endorsed seeds. The mechanization enforces exactly this split:
  action_integrity_from requires the full invariant Inv, while
  reasoning_integrity_from requires only EStore/WFs
  (§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations).

Two sorted configurations
(Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are _matched_, $`c_{1}\approx c_{2}`$, if
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c_{1})=\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c_{2})`$; $`P`$’s interaction
histories coincide (the same emitted-operation sequence, the same reply
stream, and the same consumed coin prefix — hence
$`\sigma_{P,1}=\sigma_{P,2}`$, by the strategy reading of
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and the ghost display transcripts and sink logs coincide. Matched views
and histories also fix the endorsed-sort allocation state
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)),
so subsequent endorsed blocks are created at equal identifiers in the
two runs. $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and the interpreter’s private
handle _resolutions_ may differ arbitrarily; the handle _count_ is
matched through $`H(c)`$
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Matched implies $`\approx_{\mathsf{U}}`$; the converse fails on
$`\sigma_{P}`$ and the ghost logs, which is why the two-run results are
stated over matched pairs. The canonical matched pair is two runs
launched from a shared endorsed-seed configuration
(Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
with empty histories and empty ghost logs under two different attacks
(the form mechanized as initE,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
matched pairs need not be well-formed, and
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds without any endorsement-soundness hypothesis on the seed. This
relation is mechanized, field for field, as MatchW
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S3.7 (Ungated sink projection).

For a finite run $`\rho`$, $`\mathsf{Sink}(\rho)`$ is the sequence of
sensitive sink events, each with its arguments, except that arguments
displayed and accepted in the immediately preceding atomic gating
confirmation
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
including, for element calls of a $`\mathsf{map}`$, the batch
confirmation of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are stripped from the annotation. Stripping makes
$`\mathsf{Sink}(\rho)`$ well-defined for baseline comparisons in which
transcripts may be empty
(Proposition [S3.27](#A3.Thmtheorem27 "Proposition S3.27 (The taint-gating baseline fails Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
under $`\mathsf{DT}`$-equality the stripped arguments are equal in any
case, so the projection hides nothing in
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Definition S3.8 (Display transcript).

For a run $`\rho`$ from a designated starting configuration,
$`\mathsf{DT}(\rho)`$ is the ordered sequence of _all display events
appended during $`\rho`$_ (the run suffix; an audit prefix carried by a
seeded starting configuration belongs to its seed record,
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
not to $`\mathsf{DT}(\rho)`$): (i) selection-surface renderings, each
with its candidate identifiers, rendered preview bytes (marked
unverified), and the user’s selection, if any; (ii) decision-pane
confirmation events, one per reached gating review, each with the
resolved bytes (or the fixed no-value display of
Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
both provenance zones, the target, and the decision; (iii) for a batch,
_either_ the fixed oversize display of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
with its standard aggregated reject (where the deployment cap applies),
_or_ the fixed no-value display of a null collection with its standard
aggregated reject
(Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
_or_ every page’s rendering and per-page decision, the first page
recording the collection’s cardinality — which, with
$`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$, determines the deterministic pagination and
hence the page count
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b))
— and the aggregated decision, recorded once. Transcript entries carry
interpreter-assigned event _kinds_ (selection-surface rendering;
decision-pane confirmation; batch page; the fixed no-value display; the
fixed oversize display; aggregated batch decision), fixed constructors
of the TCB logging path: the fixed displays are distinguished from
ordinary pages by kind, never by comparing rendered byte strings, so
page content colliding textually with a fixed message cannot confuse the
classification (consumed by
Lemma [S3.20](#A3.Thmtheorem20 "Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Rejections are recorded as well as acceptances, and so are the accepting
reviews of transactions that subsequently abort
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The harness materializes the full audit history — any seed-record prefix
followed by $`\mathsf{DT}(\rho)`$ — in a hash-chained audit log
(operational reading:
[N7](#Thmnotex7 "Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
previews:
[N8](#Thmnotex8 "Note N8 (What previews can and cannot do). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Remark S3.9 (Coverage of the display transcript).

By
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e),
$`\mathsf{DT}(\rho)`$ comprises the totality of attacker-influenceable
content ever rendered to the user, together with everything the user
decided. Recording rejections is necessary: two runs in which the user
rejects and later accepts the same content differ in behaviour during
the interval, and a projection that forgets rejections cannot
distinguish them. Previews carry no endorsement authority; their
inclusion records them as part of the release history.

###### Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated).

PerMIT has _personal Action Integrity_ (equivalently: _argument-value
integrity_) if in every run from a well-formed configuration, under
every attack, every sensitive sink event is safe in the personal form of
Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
every value reaching a sensitive sink is a user-typed
$`\mathsf{T}`$-value, or was endorsed by _this_ user at its exact bytes
for that exact sink (now, or at a prior in-scope confirmation; for
element calls of a batch-gated $`\mathsf{map}`$, at the batch
confirmation that displayed those exact element bytes,
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
It has _delegated Action Integrity_ if the same holds with the
endorsement authority extended to a qualifying community confirmation of
the exact bytes at the exact tool ($`\mathsf{CC}`$,
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
(the delegated predicate of
Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
delegation is an assumption
([A7](#Thmassumptionx7 "Assumption A7 (Federated endorsement transfer). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
never a theorem of the single-user model.

###### Definition S3.11 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript).

PerMIT has _Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript_ if, for
every pair of _matched_ configurations $`c_{1}\approx c_{2}`$
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
every pair of attacks (coupled per
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
slot skeleton and typed stream only; paste presence and content, tool
outputs, and reader outputs uncoupled), and every coupled coin sequence
$`\omega`$
(convention ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
any two runs of a common horizon
(convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
with $`\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{2})`$ satisfy
$`\mathsf{Sink}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{Sink}(\rho_{2})`$ and emit the same
sequence of Protected-LLM operations and tool invocations. Informal
reading (a conditional statement, not an unconditional inertness claim):
any influence of untrusted memory on the listed behaviours must pass
through a display event or an endorsed release — conditional on the
transcript, hidden untrusted state has no further effect. An unrendered
untrusted byte is not claimed inert outright: it may steer which
candidates or previews the Reader surfaces, and thereby the transcript
itself; what is excluded is influence that bypasses the transcript.

The statement is trace-wise per coin sequence; the knowledge-based
formulation in the style of gradual release [Askarov & Sabelfeld
(2007)](#bib.bib3) that it induces is recorded in
§[S8.4](#A8.SS4 "S8.4 Knowledge-based formulation of Reasoning Integrity ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### S3.2 Structural lemmas

###### Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation).

In every configuration reachable from a sorted configuration
(Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
a fortiori from a well-formed one), no byte value enters $`\sigma_{P}`$
_by delivery from a $`\mathsf{U}`$-labelled source_: every
bytes-carrying reply $`P`$ receives is, at the step of its emission, the
verbatim content of a non-$`\mathsf{U}`$ block of the store, and
$`\mathsf{U}`$-derived data appears in $`\sigma_{P}`$ only as opaque
handles. This is a provenance statement, not a disjointness of byte
strings across tiers: a typed or endorsed byte string in $`\sigma_{P}`$
may be extensionally equal to the bytes of an unrelated
$`\mathsf{U}`$-block, and the flow it licenses is the trusted copy’s.
_(Machine-checked, run-level:_ bytes_reply_isolation,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")._)_

###### Proof.

Induction on run length with invariant $`I(c)`$: every bytes-carrying
value ever delivered to $`P`$ was delivered as the content of a
non-$`\mathsf{U}`$ block (reply grammar case (v)) or as trusted command
input; everything else in $`P`$’s input stream is a handle or constant
token. At a sorted start, $`\sigma_{P}`$ is the strategy state of the
initial interaction history
(§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
whose reply stream is interface-conformant: every bytes-carrying reply
in it is $`\mathbb{E}`$-level by the reply grammar, and its typed input
is trusted command input at level $`\mathsf{T}`$; an endorsed-seed
configuration has empty history and satisfies $`I`$ trivially. For the
inductive step, case-analyse the transitions of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Tool-Fast, Tool-Gate-Acc/Rej, Map: by
Rules [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
all outputs land in $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and only the constant
acknowledgement (and, for gated calls, the decision) returns; the
collection handle’s identifier is operation-determined and computed by
$`P`$, not returned
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
W-Typed stores $`\mathsf{T}`$; W-Paste is captured to
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$. W-P has precondition $`b\in\sigma_{P}`$,
hence $`\mathbb{E}`$-level by the hypothesis, and stores at
$`\mathsf{PC}`$ with empty scope. Recall-E returns $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes;
Recall-O returns an opaque handle: uniformly for $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks,
unknown, and nonexistent identifiers
(Rules [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the totality clause
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b));
$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$-retrieval returns verbatim $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes
(Rule [R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Fill and Cryst return one handle and, by
Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
no branchable bit. Display and Evict inject nothing (Evict replies the
constant $`\mathsf{ack}`$ uniformly,
Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
previews are UI-side only
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d)).
Conf-Acc/Rej return only the decision (the null-gate abort returning the
reject decision,
Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and on accept produce an $`\mathbb{E}`$-block. Fail returns the constant
$`\mathsf{fail}`$ token. $`P`$-generated content is a function of
$`\sigma_{P}`$ and the coins, hence $`\mathbb{E}`$-level by the meet
rule
(Definition [S2.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S2.1 (Trust lattice and labels). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
By
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
no transition raises the level of any existing block; an accepting
$`\mathsf{confirm}`$ writes a fresh $`\mathbb{E}`$-block and leaves its
untrusted source, if any, at $`\mathsf{U}`$. Thus every delivery to
$`P`$ carries non-$`\mathsf{U}`$ provenance; the existence of
extensionally equal untrusted copies is irrelevant. $`I`$ is preserved.
∎

###### Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class).

Every value $`a`$ passed to any tool satisfies the following, according
to the tool’s class. _(Sensitive tools.)_ If
$`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$, at least one of:
(i) $`a`$ consists of readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes byte-equal to a
stored $`\mathsf{T}`$-block; (ii) $`a`$ consists of readable
$`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes byte-equal to some $`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$-block
$`b`$ with $`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$; (iii) the call is
gated by an atomic $`\mathsf{confirm}(a,\mathsf{tool})`$ displaying
$`a`$’s resolved bytes (or, for a batch, every element’s bytes; or, for
a null handle, the fixed no-value display, whereupon the call aborts).
For a literal-expressed argument, in the _baseline_ semantics of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
— before the formally instantiated
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are applied — case (iii) is the complement of the union of (i) and (ii):
the fast path passes iff (i) or (ii) holds, and the gate fires
otherwise. Under
Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
a sensitive-tool argument satisfying case (i) may nevertheless gate
(first use of the $`\mathsf{T}`$-value per sensitive sink);
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
leaves this sensitive case analysis unchanged and modifies only the
data-tool case (D) below; the option-modified analyses are
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s.
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is requirements-level, outside this lemma and outside
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Cases (i) and (ii) themselves may hold simultaneously — the store may
contain a $`\mathsf{T}`$-block and an in-scope
$`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$-block with identical bytes, a co-occurrence
Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
manufactures by design — and either suffices for the baseline fast path;
no consumer of this lemma uses exclusivity of (i) against (ii), each
case being separately sufficient in
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Handle-expressed arguments take case (iii) unconditionally (_Handles_
clause below). _(Data tools.)_ If
$`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$, then either
(D) $`a`$ consists of readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-level bytes held by $`P`$
— that every byte value $`P`$ holds carries non-$`\mathsf{U}`$
provenance, is
Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
contribution, not
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
alone — which flow without confirmation
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b))
— in particular $`\mathsf{PC}`$-labelled and freshly $`P`$-composed
$`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes flow ungated at data tools; this is precisely the
clause
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
hardens — or the call is gated per case (iii). _(Handles.)_ Every handle
argument, at every tool, falls under (iii): an ordinary handle via
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c);
a collection handle via the batch gate of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
by the desugaring of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e).
_(Under
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
case (D) is replaced by the clause-(a) case analysis applied at the data
tool;
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)_
_(Machine-checked core:_ processArgs*spec *and* bytes_reply_isolation,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
an ungated flowed argument is a verbatim $`P`$-supplied literal, and at
a sensitive tool it passes the whitelist test over
$`\mathcal{M}*{\mathbb{E}}`$; that $`P`$ holds only $`\mathbb{E}`$-level
bytes in case (D) is bytes_reply_isolation’s contribution; witness for
case (D): Scenario 7._)_

###### Proof.

Immediate from
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with
Rules [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
clause (a) gives the sensitive case analysis: in the baseline semantics
the fast path passes iff the argument consists of readable
$`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes matching (i) or (ii), and the gate fires otherwise,
so case (iii) is exhaustive over the complement, while (i) and (ii) may
co-occur, harmlessly (the membership and scope tests are decidable
against $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$,
Definition [S2.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
$`\mathsf{PC}`$ blocks have empty scope and cannot take the sensitive
fast path); clause (b) gives case (D) at data tools; clause (c) gives
the handle case at every tool. For element calls of a $`\mathsf{map}`$,
the $`\diamond`$-substituted element falls under (iii) via the batch
confirmation
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and each non-$`\diamond`$ argument, a non-handle $`P`$-supplied value by
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f),
falls under the case its tool class assigns exactly as at a direct call,
its gating branch resolved at the batch confirmation. ∎

###### Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise).

1.  (a)
    _(Transition-level; any run.)_ The only $`\mathsf{C}`$-creating
    transitions of
    Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    are the accepting gating reviews — Conf-Acc and the accepted
    positions of Tool-Gate-Acc, Tool-Gate-Rej, Map-Tool-Acc,
    Map-Tool-Rej — each writing a fresh copy of exactly the displayed
    bytes with scope $`\sigma(t)`$
    (Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    the only $`\mathsf{CC}`$-assigning transition is deterministic
    community promotion
    (Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    and no transition alters an existing block’s label or scope
    ([A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
2.  (b)
    _(Backing; well-formed runs.)_ In every run from a well-formed
    configuration
    (Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    every $`\mathsf{C}`$-block $`b`$ and every $`t\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$
    is backed by an accepting decision-pane confirmation displaying
    exactly $`\mathrm{bytes}(b)`$ at target $`t`$, in the run suffix (by
    clause (a)) or in the seed record
    (Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii));
    and every $`\mathsf{CC}`$ scope in force is backed by its promotion
    certificate, whose threshold was met by endorsements at the scoped
    tool itself
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof.

_(a)_ is the case analysis below; _(b)_ adds the base case: at the
initial configuration, clause (ii) of well-formedness — with the seed
record where the store is seeded — supplies the backing for every
existing scoped $`\mathsf{C}`$-block, and clause (iii) (federated form)
the certificates. By
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
no transition alters an existing block’s label or scope, so a block’s
label and scope are those of its creating transition. No write
transition creates a block at $`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$; W-P creates
$`\mathsf{PC}`$ with empty scope; the only endorsement-creating
transitions are the accepting gating reviews — Conf-Acc, and the
accepted positions of Tool-Gate-Acc, Tool-Gate-Rej, Map-Tool-Acc, and
Map-Tool-Rej
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
endorsement is durable, written on the accepting and aborting branches
alike) — each of which writes scope $`\sigma(t)`$ per
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
for exactly the displayed bytes. The only $`\mathsf{CC}`$-assigning
transition is promotion [Myers et al. (2006)](#bib.bib33), which
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
adds $`\mathsf{tool}`$ to a $`\mathsf{CC}`$ scope only when the
community threshold was met by endorsements at $`\mathsf{tool}`$ itself.
∎

###### Remark S3.15.

Clause (b) is deliberately _not_ asserted over the sorted class
