(Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
an endorsed-seed configuration may hold scoped $`\mathsf{C}`$-blocks
with no backing confirmation anywhere, and clause (b) fails there, while
clause (a), a property of the transitions alone, holds in every run.
Consumers of clause (b) quantify over well-formed runs (via
Definition [S3.10](#A3.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
consumes neither clause. This is the Inv-vs-EStore split of
Definitions [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")/[S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Lemma S3.16 (No community label single-user).

In every run from a well-formed configuration with no federation
attached, no block ever carries label $`\mathsf{CC}`$: promotion is the
only $`\mathsf{CC}`$-assigning transition
(Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and it does not exist in the single-user semantics. _(Machine-checked as
Inv.noCC,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)_

###### Proof.

$`\mathsf{WF}(c_{0})`$(iii) gives the base case; no transition of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
assigns $`\mathsf{CC}`$
(Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
case analysis). ∎

###### Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness).

The sequence of values the interpreter returns to $`P`$ is a function of
the trajectory of $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$, $`P`$’s own emitted
operations and tool invocations, the coupled coins $`\omega`$, and the
user’s decisions.

###### Proof.

By the reply grammar of
Figure [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
every return is one of: (a) a constant token ($`\mathsf{ack}`$ or
$`\mathsf{fail}`$, per
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)(i),(iii)),
including the uniform acknowledgement of $`\mathsf{evict}`$, whose
resolution status is consumed interpreter-side
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(b) $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes from $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, a component
of $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$; (c) a handle whose existence and identifier
are fixed by the emitted-operation sequence
(Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
including collection handles, whose identifiers $`P`$ computes and which
are never returned, and the handles of Recall-O, indistinguishable
across resolution statuses
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b));
(d) the user’s decision, with the null-gate abort rendered as the reject
decision
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(e) the verbatim dereference of an $`\mathbb{E}`$-block selected by
$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$, a function of the query,
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, and $`\omega`$
(Rule [R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The grammar has no other productions, and
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
defines every invocation (totality); no return depends on
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ bytes except through an accepting
confirmation, which writes the endorsed copy into
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$. ∎

###### Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases).

$`P`$’s choice and ordering of operations and tool invocations is a
function of $`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$, the reply stream, and the coupled
coins alone. No _direct_ channel exists from $`\mathsf{U}`$-block bytes,
$`\mathsf{U}`$-search outcomes, $`\mathsf{recall}`$ resolution statuses,
tool-invocation outcomes, candidate multiplicities, collection
cardinalities, block-identifier occupancy, or handle-identifier
structure beyond the operation-determined naming, to any reply $`P`$
receives. Information about hidden state reaches $`P`$ only through
logged release events: the user’s recorded decisions and the endorsed
copies they create — each carried, with its displayed bytes, in the
display transcript
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— which is precisely the declassification boundary
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
conditions on.

###### Proof.

We verify against
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and Rules
[R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
that every channel is closed. (a) _$`\mathsf{U}`$-content:_ absent from
$`\sigma_{P}`$
(Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(b) _$`\mathsf{U}`$-search bits and $`\mathsf{recall}`$ resolution
status:_ consumed interpreter-side
(Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b));
the null-gate abort returns the same reject decision a user rejection
would, so $`P`$ cannot distinguish them from the reply or the sanitized
history; the resolved value, where the user later inspects it, is
released only through the displayed gate event and its logged decision.
(c) _Candidate multiplicity:_ bound interpreter-side (Fill), absent from
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$. (d) _Reader exceptions and budget exhaustion:_
absorbed into the null-vs-real handle indistinguishability
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the observable $`\mathsf{fail}`$ outcome occurs only on conditions that
are a deterministic function of $`P`$’s emitted operations,
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, and the coupled coins, identical across
matched runs. (e) _Timing/step count:_ the reply grammar contains no
clock or step-count value, so no such value exists in $`\sigma_{P}`$ to
branch on; wall-clock channels are outside the model
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S8](#Thmobjx8 "Analysis S8 (Timing channels). ‣ S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(f) _Collection cardinality and block occupancy:_ a collection handle
exposes no length or indexing
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e));
whether an identifier is occupied by a $`\mathsf{U}`$-block is not
observable
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
so the attacker-chosen number of captured blocks is invisible;
$`\mathsf{map}`$ is one emitted operation returning one acknowledgement
with per-element results captured, never returned
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e));
tool-call multiplicity inside a map is closed by the batch gate, and
pagination above $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$ is interpreter-side with a
single aggregated decision returned
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)),
so neither the cardinality nor the page count is ever returned to $`P`$
directly; the single aggregated decision is a logged release, on the
transcript, like any gate decision; both are displayed to the _user_ and
recorded in the transcript only. Under the body grammar of
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)
— which also covers collection-handle tool arguments, normalized to
$`\mathsf{map}`$ before transition matching
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e))
— the check is exhaustive per step: each $`\mathsf{map}`$ is exactly one
handle-producing operation whatever $`|H|`$
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c));
its single per-element tool call is covered by the batch gate, which
displays every element’s bytes and each gating non-$`\diamond`$
argument’s bytes
(Rules [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b), [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
per-element outputs are captured, never returned
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e));
tool-free bodies write $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks and reply once; and no
admissible body operation can generate a data-dependent reply,
$`\mathsf{recall}`$, $`\mathsf{fill}`$, $`\mathsf{map}`$,
$`\mathsf{confirm}`$, and $`\mathsf{evict}`$ being excluded from bodies
and tool replies inside the batch being captured
(Rule [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(g) _Handle identifiers:_ fixed by the operation sequence
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
identical across $`\mathsf{U}`$-equivalent runs with matched operations.
(h) _Reply values:_
Lemma [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(i) _$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$:_ a function of query,
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, $`\omega`$; never sees
$`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes; $`\mathbb{E}`$-search outcomes are trusted data
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(j) _Tool outcomes:_ captured
(Rule [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the acknowledgement is constant. (k) _Eviction:_ $`\mathsf{evict}`$
replies with the constant $`\mathsf{ack}`$ uniformly
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
whether the argument resolved, and to which tier, is consumed
interpreter-side. Its $`\mathbb{E}`$-tier effect is a function of
$`P`$’s emitted operation and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ alone,
matched across $`\approx_{\mathsf{U}}`$-related runs; its
$`\mathsf{U}`$-tier effect alters only $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$,
which no reply exposes. In particular an
$`\mathsf{evict}`$-then-$`\mathsf{recall}`$ probe learns nothing:
Recall-O is uniform across occupied, vacated, and never-occupied
identifiers, before and after any $`\mathsf{evict}`$
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
The enumeration is complete relative to the written interface:
$`\Sigma_{P}`$
(§[S2](#A2a "Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is the entire operation surface, matching
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
arm-for-arm and the mechanized POp type, the reply grammar types every
reply, and the totality clause
Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
leaves no invocation with undefined or distinguishing behaviour. ∎

###### Lemma S3.19 (Append-only transcript; prefix comparability).

Every transition of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
extends the display transcript by a (possibly empty) suffix and never
removes or alters an existing entry; hence along any run the transcript
after $`t`$ steps is a prefix of the transcript after $`n\geq t`$ steps.
Consequently, if two lists are prefixes of one common list, one is a
prefix of the other. _(Machine-checked:_ dt_execOp_prefix,
dt_runFrom_prefix, prefix_or_prefix;
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")._)_

###### Proof.

Case inspection of the figures: each transition appends its own display
events at the end of the transcript or appends nothing
(Rules [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the transcript is write-once by construction (the audit-log reading of
convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and
Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The comparability clause is elementary. ∎

###### Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy).

Let two configurations be matched
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
immediately before a common $`P`$-emitted operation, and execute that
operation in both. If the display segments the operation appends are
prefix-comparable (one a prefix of the other), then they are equal, and
so are the operation’s extensions of the reply stream, the sanitized
history, the endorsed store (identical fresh blocks at identical
endorsed-sort identifiers,
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g)),
the confirmation counter, and the sink log; only
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and the private handle resolutions may
differ. _(Machine-checked core:_ processArgs_det _and_ match_execOp _for
direct invocations, and_ batchGate_det _for the batch-confirmation case,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the batch case’s store-level integration is established by the paper
proof only.)_

###### Proof.

Case analysis on the common operation, whose inputs
($`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, the argument list, the confirmation
counter, the coins) are matched. For $`\mathsf{display}(x)`$: both
segments are the single render event of the same $`x`$. For a gate
transaction ($`\mathsf{confirm}`$, or the gating positions of an
invocation, processed left to right): the set of gating positions is a
function of the argument list and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ alone
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
both matched, so the runs gate at the same positions, and every reached
position emits exactly one confirmation event (a null resolution emits
the fixed no-value event,
Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so both segments are nonempty at each reached position.
Prefix-comparability forces the first events equal; equality of that
event pins the same resolution class (real value vs. no-value display),
the same displayed bytes, the same selection, and the same decision,
hence the same sanitized record, the same reply token contribution, the
same continuation (accept: proceed; reject or null: abort the remaining
positions in both runs), and, by
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the same durable fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$-copies at the same identifiers on
either branch. Induction along the remaining reached positions gives
segment equality and equal effects. For a batch confirmation
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
equality of the first appended events pins the size class by event kind
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— both null (the fixed no-value display, standard reject, no decision
consumed), both oversize (the fixed oversize display, likewise), or both
paginated, the cap being fixed TCB configuration — and in the paginated
case the first page event records the collection’s cardinality, and the
pagination is the deterministic $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$-split of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
so equality of the first page events pins the page partition; the
first-event argument applied page by page gives equal rendered elements,
equal decisions, and the same stopping page on rejection, whence equal
aggregated decisions, equal durable non-$`\diamond`$ endorsements
(convention [(vii^(′))](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and equal captures to $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ only.
Selection-surface renderings within these events touch only the UI and
the transcript, never $`\sigma_{P}`$
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d)).
All other operations append no display events and their effects on the
matched components are functions of matched data
(Lemma [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
∎

#### S3.3 Action Integrity

###### Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity).

Under
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the well-formedness invariant
(Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is

1.  (a)
    _(Establishment)_ satisfied by the empty configuration and by every
    seeded configuration with a valid seed record
    (Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    and
2.  (b)
    _(Preservation)_ preserved by every transition of
    Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    under every attack, with no control-flow or distributional
    hypothesis, and under adversarial behaviour of either reader.

Consequently every sink event of every configuration reachable from a
well-formed configuration is safe
(Definition [S3.2](#A3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S3.2 (Sink-event safety). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
via clause (v)): PerMIT has personal Action Integrity
(Definition [S3.10](#A3.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
per execution. In the single-user semantics the $`\mathsf{CC}`$ branch
of
Lemma [S3.13](#A3.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is vacuous
(Lemma [S3.16](#A3.Thmtheorem16 "Lemma S3.16 (No community label single-user). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the delegated extension is
Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
_(Machine-checked for clauses (i)–(iii),(v), whose conjunction is the
mechanized invariant Inv
(Table [S5](#A9.T5 "Table S5 ‣ Checked statements. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
established by inv_init, preserved by inv_execOp with
inv_ingestTyped/inv_ingestPaste, composed as inv_runFrom;
action_integrity, action_integrity_from. Clause (iv) is enforced by the
executable state and transition structure and the separate sortedness
invariant WFs;
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)_

###### Proof.

_(a)_ The empty configuration satisfies (i)–(v) vacuously; a seeded
configuration’s seed record supplies (i)–(ii) by
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
(iii)–(iv) hold of it by construction, and (v) is vacuous (no recorded
sink events). _(b)_ Preservation of clauses (i)–(iv) is the induction of
Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
for clause (v), take any newly appended sink event and argument $`a`$;
the event is sensitive
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so by
Lemma [S3.13](#A3.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
one of the three sensitive-tool cases holds. _(i)_ $`a`$ byte-equals a
$`\mathsf{T}`$-block: by well-formedness
(Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
and
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
those exact bytes were typed by the user on the command channel. The
fast path is deliberately extensional: attacker-supplied content _may_
be byte-equal to a stored $`\mathsf{T}`$-block, in which case the
flowing bytes are still a value the user personally typed, and the flow
is user-authorized content regardless of which equal copy motivated the
call; provenance of other equal copies is irrelevant to the
authorization of these bytes. _(ii)_ $`a`$ byte-equals some
$`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$-block $`b`$ with
$`\mathsf{tool}\in\mathsf{scope}(b)`$: by
Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
an accepting $`\mathsf{confirm}(a,\mathsf{tool})`$ occurred; by
[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the endorsed bytes were exactly $`a`$; by
[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the user intended $`a`$ at $`\mathsf{tool}`$. _(iii)_ a fresh atomic
$`\mathsf{confirm}(a,\mathsf{tool})`$ gates the call, in particular
every handle argument, and by
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the bytes that flow are the displayed bytes, bound to this call
instance, even if they coincide with stored content; for a batch-gated
$`\mathsf{map}`$, every element’s bytes were displayed at the batch
confirmation
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and accepted under the per-element intent clause of
[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
so each element call flows exactly the bytes displayed for it; a null
handle aborts
(Rule [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

For reader adversariality: an adversarial $`Q`$ can at worst surface a
wrong value or decorate it with a preview; it holds no tool capability,
its output is $`\mathsf{U}`$, the decision pane shows the true resolved
bytes in an interpreter-controlled region the attacker cannot influence
(Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
and
[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
reject the wrong value. $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ selects only among
$`\mathbb{E}`$-blocks, each independently in case (i)/(ii). This is
qualified robustness [Zdancewic & Myers (2005)](#bib.bib53); [Myers
et al. (2006)](#bib.bib33). ∎

###### Remark S3.22 (Extensional trust of typed values).

Case (i)’s fast path is extensional and tool-blind at the baseline: a
user-typed value is authorized as a _literal_ at every sensitive sink,
including sinks the user never contemplated when typing it, and attacker
content byte-equal to a typed value flows as the typed value (the
proof’s provenance reading). The handle discipline is unaffected: a
handle-expressed argument always gates, even when its hidden resolution
byte-equals a typed value
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)).
Deployments for which per-sink authorization of typed values matters
select
Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which re-gates $`\mathsf{T}`$-values once per sensitive sink
(Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
budget:
Corollary [S6.6](#A6.Thmtheorem6 "Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options –). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary).

Under the same assumptions:

1.  (a)
    _(Never-endorsed bytes.)_ An untrusted-derived value that has never
    been endorsed at any target is resolved at a tool boundary,
    sensitive or data, only inside an accepting confirmation displaying
    exactly those bytes at exactly that tool. In particular, no
    never-endorsed untrusted-derived value can be exfiltrated through a
    data-tool parameter (a URL, a search query, a file path) without the
    user endorsing that exact value at that exact tool, in that call.
2.  (b)
    _(Post-endorsement boundary.)_ Once bytes have been endorsed at
    _any_ target (including “reasoning”), the fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$-copy
    makes them readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-level bytes
    (Rule [R5](#Thmrulex5 "Rule R5 (Readable local endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and their subsequent _literal-expressed_ flow to _data_ tools is
    ungated
    (Lemma [S3.13](#A3.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    case (D)); a handle-expressed use of the same bytes gates at every
    tool regardless
    (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
    [S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    tool-specific endorsement is enforced only at _sensitive_ tools (the
    scope test of
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)).
    This is the disclosed _baseline_ post-endorsement channel
    ([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    closes it: under
    [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    the data-tool fast path applies the same exact-target test as the
    sensitive path, so a reasoning-target copy (empty scope) and any
    out-of-scope endorsed copy gate at every data tool, each such flow
    then requiring its own per-pair confirmation. _(Machine-checked: the
    gateCheckO2 closure witnesses of
    §[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)_

###### Remark S3.24 (Reading of “untrusted-derived”).

Clause (a) is a provenance statement about byte _values_: the
never-endorsed untrusted bytes themselves cross a tool boundary only
inside an accepting confirmation displaying them. It is not a claim of
information-theoretic independence: $`P`$ may branch on a logged gate
decision (a transcript release,
Lemma [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and encode that released bit into $`P`$-composed data-tool arguments;
all such influence is transcript-carried and governed by
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
not by this corollary.

###### Proof.

(a) By
Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
$`P`$ holds never-endorsed untrusted-derived data only as opaque
handles, so such bytes reach a tool argument only by handle resolution;
by
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
every handle argument at every tool gates; by
[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Rules [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the resolved bytes flow only on an accepting decision over exactly those
bytes at exactly that call’s tool. (b) Immediate from
Rule [R5](#Thmrulex5 "Rule R5 (Readable local endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
for literal-expressed use; handle arguments gate in every case by

a reasoning-target copy has empty scope, so the _sensitive_ fast path
remains closed to it, and
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected. _(Machine-witnessed: Scenario 8,

###### Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript).

Under

[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

PerMIT has Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript
(Definition [S3.11](#A3.Thmtheorem11 "Definition S3.11 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
for every matched pair $`c_{1}\approx c_{2}`$
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),

(convention ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
any two runs of a common horizon
(convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
with $`\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{2})`$ agree on the

operations and tool invocations, the reply stream, and the final

conclusions and with paste presence and content uncoupled across the
compared attacks, as reasoning_integrity_from; the batch case’s
