so the ungated sink projection is unaffected;
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)_

###### Proof.

We use
Lemmas [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which hold under the harness rules,
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the strategy convention of
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
alone. Fix a matched pair $`c_{1}\approx c_{2}`$
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
sorted suffices,
Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
two attacks, and a coin sequence $`\omega`$; by
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
the typed streams and the slot skeleton are coupled, while paste events
(presence and content), tool outputs, and reader outputs may differ
arbitrarily across the two attacks. Suppose, for contradiction, that
$`\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{2})`$ but the runs differ in
some Protected-LLM operation, tool invocation, or ungated sink event;
let $`t^{*}`$ be the first step at which they differ. Define the
invariant $`I(t)`$: after $`t`$ steps, (1) the configurations are
$`\approx_{\mathsf{U}}`$-related; (2) the two runs have emitted
identical sequences of Protected-LLM operations and tool invocations,
received identical reply streams, and consumed identical coin prefixes —
hence, by the strategy reading of
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
hold identical states $`\sigma_{P}`$; (3) the display-transcript
prefixes and sink logs are equal. $`I(0)`$ is
Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
verbatim: matched pairs agree on the view, the interaction histories,
and the ghost transcript and sink logs (for the canonical endorsed-seed
pairs, all ghost logs are empty). The argument is the unwinding method
[Goguen & Meseguer (1984)](#bib.bib20) with a gradual-release carve-out
[Askarov & Sabelfeld (2007)](#bib.bib3); [Sabelfeld & Sands
(2009)](#bib.bib40); alignment of operations and coins is _derived_ at
each step from $`I(t)`$ via
Lemmas [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
never assumed. Steps
[3](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[4](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
use the append-only transcript,
Lemma [S3.19](#A3.Thmtheorem19 "Lemma S3.19 (Append-only transcript; prefix comparability). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

_Step 1: $`I(t)`$ holds for all $`t<t^{_}`$, and step $`t^{_}`$ is
matched, a contradiction._ The induction is Steps
[2](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[4](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
Step
[5](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
concludes the argument.

_Step 2 (Determinacy)._ Given $`I(t)`$ with $`t<t^{*}`$, step $`t{+}1`$
opens with the channel slots of
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
disposed of first. The typed events are equal (coupled by
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
extending $`x(c)`$ and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ identically in both
runs. The paste events may differ in presence and in content; but each
lands in $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ with label $`\mathsf{U}`$ and
appends nothing to $`P`$’s reply stream
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(vi)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so after the slots the configurations remain matched, with
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ differing freely exactly as
Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
permits. $`P`$’s next operation is then, by the strategy convention of
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
a function of its emitted operations, its reply stream, its view
$`\mathsf{obs}_{P}(c)`$, and the coins; by $`I(t)`$(1)–(2) all four are
matched across the runs. Hence both runs emit the same operation at step
$`t{+}1`$, determined _before_ any display event of that step.

_Step 3 (Display-free step)._ Channel-slot effects were disposed of in
Step [2](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the cases below are the operation’s own transition. If the common
operation triggers no display event, its effects preserve
$`\approx_{\mathsf{U}}`$: tool output lands in
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ with constant acknowledgement
(Rule [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
handles have operation-determined structure
(Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
W-P writes identical $`\mathsf{PC}`$-blocks at identical endorsed-sort
identifiers
(Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g),
the allocation state being matched by $`I(t)`$); $`\mathbb{E}`$-reads
return equal bytes (Recall-E, and $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ under matched
query, $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$, and $`\omega`$,
Rule [R11](#Thmrulex11 "Rule R11 (Trusted-store retrieval). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
including its failure branch: Retrieve/Retrieve-F select or fail as a
function of $`(q,\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}},\omega)`$ alone, matched
across the runs; $`\mathsf{evict}`$ preserves $`\approx_{\mathsf{U}}`$:
its reply is constant, an evicted $`\mathbb{E}`$-block is the same block
in both runs (the identifier sorts separate the tiers,
Rule [R1](#Thmrulex1 "Rule R1 (Operation-determined naming: handles and block identifiers). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(g),
and $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ is matched), and an evicted or
non-resolving $`\mathsf{U}`$-identifier changes only
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the $`\mathsf{fail}`$ outcome is deterministic in matched data
(Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Transcript prefixes extend equally (by nothing), the coin prefixes
advance identically, and the reply streams extend equally
(Lemma [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
every reply of a display-free step is a constant token, an
operation-determined handle, or matched $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes).
$`I(t{+}1)`$ holds.

_Step 4 (Display step)._ Suppose the common operation
(Step [2](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
triggers display events. Let $`D_{r}`$ denote run $`r`$’s transcript
after step $`t`$ and $`E_{r}`$ the segment the operation appends. By
$`I(t)`$(3), $`D_{1}=D_{2}=:D`$. By
Lemma [S3.19](#A3.Thmtheorem19 "Lemma S3.19 (Append-only transcript; prefix comparability). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
$`DE_{r}`$ is a prefix of run $`r`$’s final transcript, and the final
transcripts are equal by hypothesis (at the common horizon,
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
hence $`DE_{1}`$ and $`DE_{2}`$ are prefixes of one common list, so one
is a prefix of the other, and cancelling $`D`$ makes $`E_{1}`$ and
$`E_{2}`$ prefix-comparable.
Lemma [S3.20](#A3.Thmtheorem20 "Lemma S3.20 (Display-segment determinacy). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
then gives $`E_{1}=E_{2}`$ together with equality of the operation’s
reply, history, endorsed-store (including the durable endorsements of an
aborting transaction,
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
counter, and sink-log extensions; tool outputs, reader outputs, and
private handle resolutions may still differ, but they alter only
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ and the resolution table, exactly as
Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
permits. Hence $`I(t{+}1)`$ holds. _(The determinacy core of the batch
case is machine-checked: prefix-comparable page transcripts, over
possibly different private handle resolutions, force equal pagination,
page decisions, aggregated decision, and flowed elements —
batchGate_det,
§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the store-level integration of $`\mathsf{map}`$ into the run-level
interpreter remains established by the paper proof only, and the raw
sink events of element calls are gated and hence stripped,
Definition [S3.7](#A3.Thmtheorem7 "Definition S3.7 (Ungated sink projection). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
so the ungated sink projection is unaffected.)_

_Step 5 (Output consistency at $`t^{_}`$).* By Step
[2](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
step $`t^{_}`$’s operation is matched, so the divergence must lie in an
ungated sink annotation. Sink events are sensitive
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so by the sensitive-tool case analysis of
Lemma [S3.13](#A3.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
their arguments are (a) readable $`\mathsf{T}`$ or in-scope
$`\mathsf{C}/\mathsf{CC}`$ values, equal across
$`\approx*{\mathsf{U}}`$-related configurations (they lie in
$`\mathcal{M}*{\mathbb{E}}`$; selection by $`P`$ or $`R*{\mathcal{E}}`$
is a function of matched data and $`\omega`$); or (b) freshly confirmed,
hence stripped by
Definition [S3.7](#A3.Thmtheorem7 "Definition S3.7 (Ungated sink projection). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and by Step
[4](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the same value was endorsed (or the call aborted) in both runs in any
case. The gate-or-no-gate decision is itself matched: by
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
it is a function of storage class and membership/scope in
$`\mathcal{M}*{\mathbb{E}}`$, all components of $`\mathsf{obs}\_{P}(c)`$;
hidden handle contents cannot flip it. Calls inside maps are batch-gated
and appear in the transcript
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
all other sinks have occurrence fixed by $`P`$’s matched,
cardinality-independent operation sequence
(Lemma [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
So no component of step $`t^{_}`$ differs, contradicting the choice of
$`t^{\*}`$.

At the final horizon, $`I`$ additionally yields equality of the full
reply streams (clause (2)) and of the final views (clause (1)), the two
strengthened conclusions of the statement.

Hence runs with equal transcripts never diverge. In particular, varying
untrusted bytes in a way that leaves every display event unchanged
leaves the behaviour unchanged; contrapositively, a hidden untrusted
byte influences behaviour only by changing some rendered display event
(e.g. a Reader-surfaced candidate or preview) or an endorsed release —
influence that is transcript-carried and logged
(Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— while the byte value itself never enters $`\sigma_{P}`$ undisplayed
(Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
∎

###### Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement).

If two runs of a common horizon from a matched pair
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
under any two attacks (coupled per
conventions ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
differ in any ungated sink event, Protected-LLM operation, or tool
invocation, then their display transcripts differ. Every
attacker-induced difference _in these behaviours_ — ungated sink events,
Protected-LLM operations, and tool invocations — is therefore visible in
a logged, user-facing display event: on the selection surface, on the
decision pane, or in a decision. (Differences confined to untrusted
memory, reader state, or tool outputs lie outside the compared
behaviours; timing and termination are outside the model,
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(IV).)

###### Proof.

Contrapositive of
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

- Commentary (non-normative; reading of
  Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is a visibility guarantee, not a manipulation-proofness guarantee: any
  attacker influence on the protected behaviours
  (Definition [S3.11](#A3.Thmtheorem11 "Definition S3.11 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  must pass through the logged display transcript or an explicitly
  accepted endorsement, where each relevant release or decision is
  recorded and attributable to a transcript entry — not necessarily to
  an attacker identity — after the fact; prevention is
  Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  gate, which stops any value that is neither user-typed nor endorsed —
  personally, or, under delegation, by a qualifying community quorum —
  for the exact sensitive tool from ever crossing that tool’s boundary
  (argument-value integrity; tool choice itself:
  §[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(X)).
  The operational force of the hash-chained audit log, the residual
  human channel of
  [A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  and what previews can and cannot do are discussed at
  [N7](#Thmnotex7 "Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [N8](#Thmnotex8 "Note N8 (What previews can and cannot do). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  the scope and residuals of both single-user guarantees are collected
  in
  §[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity

Let $`B`$ be the following baseline system: the transition system of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with three modifications. (i) Recall-O on an identifier resolving to a
$`\mathsf{U}`$-block returns $`\mathsf{bytes}(b)`$, so untrusted bytes
enter $`\sigma_{P}`$;
(ii) Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
is dropped, handle arguments resolving silently;
(iii) Rules [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)–(b)
gate a tool argument iff it carries $`\mathsf{U}`$-taint under standard
dynamic _data_-taint propagation through $`\sigma_{P}`$ (data taint
only, not control taint; the standard practice the witness below
exploits). $`\mathsf{DT}`$ and $`\mathsf{Sink}`$
(Definitions [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S3.7](#A3.Thmtheorem7 "Definition S3.7 (Ungated sink projection). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are read over $`B`$’s runs verbatim, $`B`$’s confirmation events being
recorded exactly as PerMIT’s.

###### Proposition S3.27 (The taint-gating baseline fails Reasoning Integrity).

Let $`B`$ be the baseline system above. There exist
$`c_{1}\approx_{\mathsf{U}}c_{2}`$ and attacks with
$`\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{1})=\mathsf{DT}(\rho_{2})=\varnothing`$ yet
$`\mathsf{Sink}(\rho_{1})\neq\mathsf{Sink}(\rho_{2})`$.

###### Proof.

Task: “check the vendor’s latest message; if it concerns the overdue
invoice, fetch the vendor’s payment history,” with
$`\mathsf{fetch\_history}\in\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$ and a
user-typed argument. Attack $`\mathcal{A}`$ plants “invoice overdue”;
$`\mathcal{A}^{\prime}`$ plants “already settled.” In $`B`$ the agent
reads the $`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes and calls the sink in one run but not the
other; no confirmation occurs; the transcripts are empty and equal while
the sink projections differ. PerMIT cannot express the divergence: the
$`\mathsf{U}`$-bytes never enter $`\sigma_{P}`$ and $`P`$’s operation is
determined by matched data
(Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the legitimate version is recovered through crystallize-and-confirm,
whereupon the deciding content appears in the transcript, as
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
requires: any difference in the compared behaviours would require a
transcript difference. ∎

_(i)_ Each option replaces a fast path of

###### Mechanization.

The checked scope, correspondence, and modeling deltas are documented in
the main paper,
Appendix [S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Proposition S3.29 (Index-oracle coverage of display-reactive behaviour).

Fix the mechanized semantics
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and inputs $`(\mathrm{cfg},A,P,R_{\mathcal{E}},\omega)`$, and a horizon
$`n`$. Call a user _display-reactive_ if its decisions and selections
are functions of the transcript prefix rendered so far (rather than of
event ordinals). Then: (i) for every display-reactive user
$`\widehat{U}`$, the run to horizon $`n`$ is constructed step by step,
each decision depending only on the already-rendered prefix; record the
finite decision-and-selection sequence $`\widehat{U}`$ realizes along
it, and extend it arbitrarily beyond its realized length (decision
ordinals need not coincide with step indices: one gate transaction can
consume several decisions). The index oracle $`U^{*}`$ equal to that
sequence replays the original run: by induction on steps, with
invariant: after $`t`$ steps the two runs agree on every
interpreter/run-state component, and $`U^{*}`$ has consumed exactly the
first $`k(t)`$ entries of the recorded sequence, where $`k(t)`$ is the
number of decisions and selections $`\widehat{U}`$’s run consumed in
$`t`$ steps. A step consuming no decision preserves the invariant
trivially (matched states, same operation, same transition); a step
consuming $`j\geq 1`$ user responses (decisions or selections) consumes
them at gate events determined by the matched state, in order, so
$`U^{*}`$’s entries $`k(t){+}1,\dots,k(t){+}j`$ are consumed at exactly
the events where $`\widehat{U}`$ gave them, and the states re-align at
the step’s close. Hence every mechanized theorem, quantifying over all
index-oracle users, covers $`\widehat{U}`$’s run. (ii) For the two-run
theorem (reasoning_integrity_from): given two attacks and a
display-reactive $`\widehat{U}`$, transcript equality pins every datum
$`\widehat{U}`$ could react to (each consumed decision and selection is
recorded with its displayed bytes,
Remark [S3.9](#A3.Thmtheorem9 "Remark S3.9 (Coverage of the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so the two realized finite sequences coincide; instantiating the
mechanized statement at that common index oracle yields the conclusion
for $`\widehat{U}`$. The same construction covers history-adaptive
attackers via their realized output sequences.

### Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest)

Only _Confirmed_ content is shared: generalizable atomic values and
crystallized knowledge an owner has verified and explicitly published;
$`\mathsf{T}`$- and $`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks are never candidates
(Lemma [S5.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S5.2 (Type-level sharing exclusion). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The tier is built on machinery network security has already formalised:
threshold endorsement [Maurer (1996)](#bib.bib31), transparency and
revocation [Laurie et al. (2013)](#bib.bib24); [Laurie et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib25), and the identity-cost requirement of the Sybil
literature [Douceur (2002)](#bib.bib16); [Dwork & Naor
(2007)](#bib.bib17), the precise reason the scaling results are
conditional on an attested or cost-bounded setting. The dispute
mechanism is a bounded, demand-paced jury whose competence condition is
the classical one [Grofman et al. (1983)](#bib.bib21). (Lineage:
[N10](#Thmnotex10 "Note N10 (Federated lineage). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

The federated layer is specified as a protocol over the log service of
convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
its state transitions (promotion, suspension, demotion, freeze) are
given by
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
as deterministic log-event semantics, each transition a function of the
prior log and the triggering event. This layer is _not_ integrated into
the single-user small-step relation of
§[S2.2](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
no theorem in this document requires that integration. The single-user
theorems consume the shared tier only through the live-entry test of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a);
in the federated two-run comparison the log is an exogenous coupled
input stream
([A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and
Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
extends
Theorems [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
on exactly this basis.

#### S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand

###### Weighted attestation and the corruption model.

Each attested identity $`i`$ carries weight
$`w_{i}\in[w_{\min},w_{\max}]`$, $`w_{\min}>0`$, assigned by the
attestation layer on cryptographic facts, never by a model. Because
endorsements and verdicts _persist_ on the log, the adversary’s
resources are counted over the deployment’s lifetime: $`f`$ is the
number of distinct identities the adversary _ever_ controls,
$`W_{\mathrm{adv}}\leq f\cdot w_{\max}`$ the total attestation weight
those identities ever carry while controlled, and
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}\leq f`$ the number of ever-controlled identities that
ever meet the panel-seat floor $`w_{\mathrm{seat}}`$. This is a
static-corruption reading: an identity once controlled is counted
adversarial forever, so a _mobile_ adversary, controlling different
identities at different times, is covered with $`f`$ counting every
identity it ever touches. Peak-simultaneous bounds would not suffice
here, precisely because persistent endorsements accumulate across
control periods. Because $`f`$, $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$, and
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are lifetime totals, reputation farming cannot carry
the adversary past any cap, and penalties that shrink adversarial
capacity leave every bound stated against them valid
([N12](#Thmnotex12 "Note N12 (Reputation farming). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S3](#Thmobjx3 "Analysis S3 (Reputation farming). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Deployments whose attestation layer revokes compromised identities may
additionally cancel their endorsements
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
counts only _un-revoked_ endorsers), tightening the effective $`f`$
below the lifetime total; no proof relies on this.

###### Canonical tools; singleton scoping.

Tool identifiers are canonical across the federation: the same
capability carries the same identifier at every deployment, fixed in TCB
configuration and covered by attestation. All community endorsement,
promotion, and reuse is per (value, tool) pair: an endorsement names the
exact tool displayed on the endorser’s decision pane, promotion accrues
one tool at a time, and a $`\mathsf{CC}`$ scope contains exactly the
tools at which the community threshold was met. There is no endorsement
transfer between tools, however similar. (Scope of this discipline: as
at the endorsement-unit paragraph of
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### The reasoning pseudo-target.

The target name $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ is registered as one more
canonical accounting target of the federation: it belongs to neither
$`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}`$ nor
$`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$, is the subject of no invocation, and
is never matched by the scope test of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
for any tool. Every per-(value, tool) counting rule of this appendix
(Definitions [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
applies verbatim to the pair $`(v,\mathsf{reasoning})`$:
reasoning-context inspections gather promotion weight at
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$, and a reasoning-context qualifying rejection
freezes the item like any other. Promotion to $`\mathsf{CC}`$ at
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ makes the entry’s bytes readable community-wide,
through the live endorsed view
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
with no personal narrative confirmation
([A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
it authorizes no tool flow through any scope test: a
$`\{\mathsf{reasoning}\}`$ scope matches no member of
$`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$, so
the sensitive fast path remains closed to it at every tool; at data
tools, the baseline
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
admits any readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes when literal-expressed — the
disclosed post-endorsement channel of
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b);
handle-expressed use gates regardless
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
— and under
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the data fast path is closed to it likewise (the exact-target test).
_Locally_, an accepting reasoning confirmation continues to write its
fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy with _empty_ tool scope
(convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
the pseudo-target names the logged decision, never a whitelist scope;
and a repeated $`\mathsf{confirm}`$ on locally readable bytes at
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ is a covered gate
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
reasoning coverage), so reasoning pairs obey the single-approval cap
exactly as tool pairs
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the budget’s $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ count including
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ on this basis
([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Two-tier storage of community status.

Community status is a property of the _shared tier_, never of any local
store. A promoted item is represented by a shared-tier entry (bytes,
per-tool scope, status), backed by its promotion certificate on the
federation log; what a user’s agent holds locally is at most a
reference. The fast-path test of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
for the $`\mathsf{CC}`$ branch is evaluated against the _live_ shared
entry at call time: a value flows on community authority iff the shared
entry is currently valid (promoted, not suspended, not demoted, not
retired) and names the tool. Demotion, suspension, and retirement
therefore act by invalidating or flagging the shared entry, withdrawing
community authority from every user who has not personally confirmed,
while no local block of any user is created, altered, or removed by any
of them: a personally confirmed $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy is a distinct local
object and continues to license the pair it was endorsed for
(Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
This is the storage reading under which
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are stated, and it is the federated form of
Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii):
every $`\mathsf{CC}`$ authority in force is backed by a currently valid
certificate.

###### Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view).

A federated configuration is $`\widehat{c}=(c,L)`$: a local extended
configuration $`c`$
(Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and the federation log $`L`$
(convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
The shared-tier state $`S_{\mathrm{sh}}(L)`$ is the deterministic replay
of $`L`$ under
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
$`\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$ denotes the set of _virtual_ community entries of
$`S_{\mathrm{sh}}(L)`$ that are currently promoted, unsuspended,
undemoted, and unretired, each carrying its exact per-tool scope from
its promotion certificate. Virtual entries are shared-tier objects in a
namespace disjoint from both local identifier sorts; they are members of
no local store. The federated endorsed view is
$`\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{fed}}_{\mathbb{E}}(\widehat{c}):=\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}(c)\uplus\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$,
and the federated Protected-LLM view replaces
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ by
$`\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{fed}}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ in
Definition [S2.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S2.3 (Protected-LLM view). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Local transitions read $`\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$ only through the
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ branch of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a);
log transitions change only $`L`$ (hence the virtual view) and never any
local block
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot).

The federated product system extends the slot structure of
convention ([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
with a _log slot_ preceding the typed slot: a federated interpreter step
first appends the step’s exogenous log-event prefix (possibly empty) to
$`L`$ — under
[A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
coupled identically across compared runs — then delivers the typed and
paste slots, then $`P`$ emits one operation, executed against the
federated view
$`\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{fed}}_{\mathbb{E}}=\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{E}}\uplus\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$
with $`L`$ as delivered by this step’s log slot. _Locally generated
federation events_ — all events the federated definitions specify for
local acts
(Definitions [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
the $`\mathsf{submit}(v)`$ of Publish-Acc and the signed
protocol-bearing gate decisions being the principal examples, realized
demand events (e.g. a dereference of a live community entry) included —
are appended to $`L`$ atomically at the close of the emitting
operation’s transition, after its local effects; the $`\mathsf{CC}`$
branch of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
is evaluated, within the invocation’s atomic step, against the prefix
delivered by that step’s log slot, so a step’s own appended events never
affect its own gate. In the two-run comparison these locally appended
events are equal across the compared runs — each is a function of
matched components (the emitted operation, the displayed bytes, and the
logged decision, all transcript-pinned; a demand event, arising from a
matched operation against the matched federated view, likewise) — so the
full delivered logs coincide: the exogenous prefixes by
[A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the local suffixes by this derivation. Log-slot transitions acknowledge
the log service, never $`P`$: nothing is appended to $`P`$’s reply
stream, no local block is created, altered, or removed
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and the only $`P`$-visible effect is through $`\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$, the
deterministic replay of the delivered prefix
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The product system is specified on paper only; it lies outside the
mechanized surface
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- Commentary (non-normative; distributed realizations of the live-entry
  test). The abstract model linearizes each invocation at a definite log
  position: the call’s $`\mathsf{CC}`$ check reads the prefix delivered
  to its step, so a call and a concurrent demotion are ordered — the
  call linearizes before or after the demotion, never against a stale
  view. A distributed deployment realizes this by pinning each
  invocation to its interpreter’s delivered log position (a per-call
  certificate); the fidelity of that delivery is a freshness obligation
  of the TCB log service
  (convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
  and the delegated guarantee
  (Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
  is stated relative to the delivered prefix.

###### Definition S4.3 (Identity pools).

The attestation layer partitions attested identities into _pools_ on
cryptographic and organizational facts (attestation provenance,
organization, deployment cohort), fixed TCB configuration, never
assigned or influenced by any model. An identity’s pool is set at
attestation and immutable thereafter; the adversary’s $`f`$ identities
occupy whatever pools their attestations place them in and can
concentrate in at most $`f`$ pools. The diversity requirement demands
that ordinary promotion’s $`N`$ endorsers span at least
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ distinct pools with at most
$`\lceil N/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ counted per pool, and panels accept
at most $`\lceil k/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ verdicts per pool
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
Deployment parameters satisfy $`1\leq D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq N`$ (with
$`N`$ endorsers one cannot span more than $`N`$ pools, so larger
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ makes ordinary promotion unsatisfiable) and
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq k`$ where panels are read against the same pool
partition. (What diversity does and does not buy:
[N11](#Thmnotex11 "Note N11 (What pool diversity buys). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S13](#Thmobjx13 "Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Definition S4.4 (Demand).

A user _demands the pair_ $`(v,t)`$ at the first interpreter event in
the epoch
(convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
at which the user’s own attempted use of $`v`$ at tool $`t`$ fires the
gate of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(because $`v`$ is unpromoted at $`t`$, disputed, outside the user’s
local scopes, or expressed through a handle — which gates at every tool
regardless of any live community entry,
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
— a covered gate
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
is not a demand event, nor is a cache confirmation of
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
a log-demand event on either branch (accept-inert on acceptance,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii);
its rejecting branch, though protocol-bearing, initiates or corroborates
without registering demand — while the attempted use firing it realizes
the user’s _latent_ indicator per the required-approval clause,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— or dereferences $`v`$ as a $`\mathsf{CC}`$-block at $`t`$, or the
user’s own accepting or gating _non-covered_ reasoning-context
confirmation of $`v`$ (a covered reasoning gate,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
is not a demand event, exactly as a covered tool gate is not), or a
dereference of a live $`\mathsf{CC}`$-at-$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ entry of
$`v`$ — demand of the pair $`(v,\mathsf{reasoning})`$. A user _demands
the item_ $`v`$ at their first demand of any pair $`(v,t)`$;
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}`$ counts distinct realized demanders of $`v`$
within the epoch and $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}`$ counts distinct
demanders of the pair: a user who uses $`v`$ at several tools
contributes to each corresponding $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}`$ and once to
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}`$, so
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}`$; the reference
model’s _latent_ counts $`n_{v},n_{v,t}`$
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
dominate these pathwise
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Demand order is the log order of these first events
(convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
The owner’s creating confirmation of $`v`$, and any publish decision
(itself federation-inert as an inspection,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
is a demand event, so every item has, in each epoch of its publication
or re-entry, $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}\geq 1`$ with its owner among its
realized demanders; in the reference model the owner-coupling convention
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
mirrors this latently, so $`n_{v}\geq 1`$ holds in those epochs as well.
A retired item is no longer surfaced
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so no further confirmations accrue to its shared-tier ledger; the same
bytes encountered later through a user’s own channels are ordinary
personal content, counted in the single-user stream, not in $`v`$’s
ledger (this ledger-residual demand is bounded pathwise by
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
persistence exceptions per
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the aggregate expected per-user contribution of its benign,
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-conforming
component vanishes under the vanishing conditions of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
while poisoned or assumption-violating demand remains in
$`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$,
Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness).

An attested identity’s inspection of a shared candidate $`v`$ is _fresh_
if the identity has no prior _logged_ decision (a protocol-bearing
decision: accepting endorsement, qualifying rejection, or panel verdict;
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
on $`v`$’s exact bytes; otherwise it is _repeat_. Decisions are logged
exactly when protocol-bearing
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so freshness is _shared-presence-first_, not life-first: a personal
decision on the same bytes taken outside any shared-tier presence
(before first publication, or after retirement) is not logged and does
not consume freshness — a disclosed boundary of the byte-permanence
guarantee
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the behavioural parameters $`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}},p_{b}`$
are accordingly read over the log-defined fresh class
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Freshness is decidable from the federation log, is permanent while so
defined, and never renews: across entries, dormancy, freezes,
suspensions, and epochs within and across the bytes’ shared-tier
presences, one logged decision per identity is final. All promotion
weight and all panel verdicts are carried by fresh inspections
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii));
