a repeat inspection can contribute only a rejection. This is
[INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the safety of the asymmetry is
[INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(rationale:
[Remark S4.7](#A4.Thmtheorem7 "Remark S4.7 (Why the freshness asymmetry is safe). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking).

A published item enters the promotion pipeline by submission
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
each pipeline entry opens a fresh finalisation window of length
$`T_{\mathrm{win}}`$ at (re-)submission. A gate decision is
_protocol-bearing_ for a shared candidate iff all of the following hold:
(i) its exact bytes have, at decision time, a shared-tier presence (a
candidate or $`\mathsf{CC}`$ entry that is not retired; frozen and
suspended presences included, since freeze- and suspension-time
decisions are precisely the verdicts, corroborations, and bankable
credits the counting rules consume); (ii) its target is a canonical tool
in $`\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}`$
or the canonical pseudo-target $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(iii) the gate is not a covered gate
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i));
and, if it is a cache confirmation of
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
its outcome is rejecting — cache gates are _accept-inert_ (their
accepting branch is never protocol-bearing), while their rejecting
branch on presence-coinciding bytes is protocol-bearing like any
rejection
([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
(iv) its outcome is a durable accepting pair-confirmation or a rejecting
review
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Only protocol-bearing decisions are appended to the federation log as
decisions on the candidate: only they consume shared-presence freshness,
carry promotion weight, initiate or corroborate disputes, or become
panel verdicts. A _publish_ decision is logged as a submission event
(Publish-Acc,
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
not as an inspection: it carries no promotion weight and consumes no
freshness, while remaining a demand event for its item
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
All other confirmations — personal content — are purely local events
with no federated effect and no freshness consequence for shared-tier
counting. Cache confirmations are _accept-inert_ regardless of whether
their bytes coincide with a shared-tier presence: their accepting branch
is never logged as a shared-candidate decision (no promotion weight, no
credit, no notification cohort, no freshness consumption); their
rejecting branch on presence-coinciding bytes remains a qualifying
rejection like any other
([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
consuming freshness as any logged rejection does. (Their accepting
branch, being unlogged, retains the identity’s freshness on the bytes;
the acceptance itself carries no weight, and any later non-cache
decision by the same identity is one more fresh decision inside the
log-defined class the weakest-target parameters
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}},p_{b}`$ are already required to
cover,
[Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
Inertness and coverage are decided by interpreter-only,
attacker-immutable attributes (provenance,
Definition [S2.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the owner-side coverage test,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).

1.  (a)
    _Once per identity per item, keyed to bytes, log-scoped,
    authority-gated._ An identity’s first _logged_ accepting decision on
    $`v`$’s bytes
    (Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    is its one weight-bearing endorsement _provided the identity holds
    dispute-initiation authority at the moment of the decision_ (not
    rejection-suspended, below its ceiling $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$, with a
    free $`r_{\max}`$ slot, and within its per-item initiation
    allowance,
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v));
    it is counted at the single tool that decision names and toward the
    pipeline entry open at the time of the decision, subject to the
    credit caps of clause (f). An accepting decision by an identity
    lacking that authority is logged, consumes freshness, and creates
    the decider’s local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy
    (Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    but is _authority-inert_: it carries no promotion weight, is never
    credited (in-entry, banked, or vindication-credited), and joins no
    notification cohort. Authority is a deterministic predicate of the
    prior log
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)),
    evaluated interpreter-side at the decision’s header atom and
    recorded with it. Every later acceptance by the same identity (at
    any tool, in any entry, in any epoch, in any shared-tier presence)
    carries no weight
    ([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
2.  (b)
    _Banking._ A first decision recorded during dormancy (window closed,
    not yet resubmitted or retired) or during a freeze with no open
    entry is _banked_: credited as endorsement weight at its tool when
    the owner’s next entry opens (subject to clause (f)), a
    deterministic relabel of the already-logged event, not a new
    confirmation and not a finalisation. Banked credits expire if the
    item retires first
    ([INV-4](#Thminvx4 "Invariant INV-4 (Banking safety). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
3.  (c)
    _Finalisation only at window end._ Within an entry, $`v`$ is
    promoted to $`\mathsf{CC}`$ at a specific tool when the weight of
    distinct, un-revoked accepting endorsers at that tool reaches $`W`$
    in credited endorsements (unweighted: $`N`$ credited endorsers;
    crediting per clause (f)), drawn from at least $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$
    diverse pools, with finalisation only at the end of the window; any
    qualifying rejection logged within the window intervenes.
4.  (d)
    _Dormancy._ Between entries the item remains surfaced and personally
    usable; a gate confirmation during dormancy is logged as a decision,
    consuming freshness, counted in the item’s ledger
    (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    banked per (b), and creating the user’s local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy,
    after which their gate never re-fires _at that tool_
    ([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
5.  (e)
    _Consequence._ The weight-bearing endorsement sets of successive
    entries of the same bytes are identity-disjoint across the entire
    deployment history, and every weight-bearing endorsement is its
    endorser’s fresh inspection of the bytes
    (Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
6.  (f)
    _Credit caps (per entry, per tool)._ Crediting is greedy in log
    order and capped: a qualifying accepting decision (in-entry, or
    banked and credited at the entry’s opening in log order of the
    original decisions) is _credited_ to the entry at its tool iff, at
    the moment of crediting, the entry holds fewer than
    $`\lceil N/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ credits from the decider’s pool
    at that tool
    (Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and fewer than
    $`N^{+}:=D_{\mathrm{pool}}\lceil N/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ credits
    at that tool in total. Crediting requires authority at decision time
    (clause (a)); the caps bind over authority-active credits only. An
    uncredited accepting decision retains every personal effect (the
    decider’s local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy,
    Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    freshness consumed,
    Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    but carries no promotion weight, joins no notification cohort, and
    is never re-credited. The caps are promotion-neutral: a pool-capped
    decision never counted toward promotion under
    Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    in any case, and the total cap binds only once the entry holds
    $`N^{+}\geq N`$ credits which, under the per-pool cap, necessarily
    span at least $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ pools — i.e. only when
    finalisation at window end is already enabled. Weighted deployments
    cap credited weight analogously (per pool and in total), bounding
    credited endorsers by $`\mathcal{O}(W/w_{\min})`$: constants change,
    never exponents
    (Remark [S5.30](#A5.Thmtheorem30 "Remark S5.30 (Weighted form). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

An endorsement is not a separate protocol act: it is the endorser’s own
accepting confirmation of $`(v,\mathsf{tool})`$ at their gate
(Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
signed and appended to the federation log. On re-entry, the interpreter
notifies exactly the weight-bearing endorsers credited to the
_immediately preceding_ entry; no earlier cohort is ever re-notified, so
the notified set per re-entry is bounded by that single entry’s credited
endorsements, at most $`N^{+}`$ per demanded tool (clause (f)),
independently of the item’s history. Notifications are deduplicated
jointly with the suspension prompts of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi),
at most one invitation per identity per item per epoch. An invitation is
valid only in the epoch of its issuance: an unopened invitation expires
at the epoch boundary and is not reissued for the same re-entry; acting
on an invitation (accepting, rejecting, or declining) is an event of the
issuance epoch. Narrowing the cohort weakens nothing: no safety bound
relies on repeat inspections
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and notifications carry no protocol authority. A notified endorser’s
re-inspection is repeat: its accepting branch carries no weight, its
rejecting branch is a qualifying rejection like any other
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
Declining costs nothing
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
[Remark S4.7](#A4.Thmtheorem7 "Remark S4.7 (Why the freshness asymmetry is safe). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- Commentary (non-normative; role of the credit caps). Clause (f)
  supplies the counting the budget ledger consumes. Without it,
  finalisation only at window end would let a popular entry accrue
  credited endorsers without bound inside one window, and the
  weight-bearing row of
  Table [S2](#A6.T2 "Table S2 ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  the notified re-entry cohort, and the reconsideration term of
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  would all grow with the item’s popularity. With it, credited endorsers
  per (entry, tool) number at most $`N^{+}<N+D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq 2N`$
  (using $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq N`$,
  Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  deterministically; the overflow — in-window accepting demanders beyond
  the caps — is within-window demand, counted by the window-bucket row
  of
  Table [S2](#A6.T2 "Table S2 ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  under
  [A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  demand clause. Safety is unaffected a fortiori: promotion still
  requires $`N`$ credited fresh endorsements,
  Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  lower-bounds honest _decisions_ (of which credits are a subset),
  rejections are never capped
  ([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  and promotion-neutrality (clause (f)) leaves
  Assumption [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  sufficiency reading unchanged.

###### Remark S4.7 (Why the freshness asymmetry is safe).

The asymmetry of
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(repeat acceptances inert, repeat rejections still qualifying) is
deliberate: a rejection can only freeze or corroborate, never promote
([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so re-exposure of bytes to a previously fooled inspector can help the
defence but never the attack, and the defence never rests on a person
catching on a second _logged_ look what they missed on the first: no
logged repeat inspection carries weight. (Unlogged personal inspections
outside a shared-tier presence are outside this discharge,
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
their calibration consequence is
[Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
Banking is safe in both directions per
[INV-4](#Thminvx4 "Invariant INV-4 (Banking safety). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(as restated there: starting weight only, window’s rejection opportunity
never bypassed, identity-disjointness preserved). Declining a re-entry
notification costs the decliner nothing: a user who has personally
confirmed holds a local in-scope $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy and reuses it at
that tool without any gate
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the floor distinguishes such voluntary repeat acts from required
confirmations
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
Remark [S6.4](#A6.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S6.4 (Voluntary effort and the cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Definition S4.8 (Reach-free bound).

A safety bound is _reach-free_ if it does not depend on the number of
honest identities to whom the item is presented (its _reach_), only on
protocol constants and the adversary’s resources
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and the stated behavioural parameters
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, read as weakest-target infima
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

#### S4.2 Protocol rules

The rules below are normative; all rationale lives in
Appendix [S7](#A7 "Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
under the keys cited, or in the marked commentary blocks of
§[S1.1](#A1.SS1a "S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Clause numbering of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
preserves the roman numerals (i)–(vii) cited throughout.

###### Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate).

Only $`\mathsf{C}`$-labelled blocks with provenance
$`\mathsf{confirmed}`$ (never $`\mathsf{cache}`$,
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are eligible for submission, by a deterministic label-and-provenance
membership test (provenance is interpreter-only,
Definition [S2.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
hence attacker-immutable); a model may _nominate_ but cannot submit;
submission requires the owner’s accepting
$`\mathsf{confirm}(v,\mathrm{publish})`$ on the decision pane
(Publish-Acc), recorded in the owner’s transcript, which emits one
signed $`\mathsf{submit}(v)`$ event to the federation log and creates
the candidate’s shared-tier presence; it creates no local block and
consumes no freshness
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Each identity emits at most $`\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$ submission events
per epoch; re-entry of an item into the promotion pipeline counts as a
fresh submission, and a submission of bytes whose per-epoch entry cap is
exhausted
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
is ineligible.

###### Required deployment parameters.

A deployment instantiating
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
fixes, as TCB configuration: the measurement window and minimum sample
size of the charged-rejection rate trigger (v)(c); the suspension and
cool-down durations of (v)(c) and (vii); the escalation schedule and the
attestation-weight reduction function of (vii); the derivation-cascade
relation of (iv); and the lifetime-account trigger of (v)(f) where
selected. The theorems below consume only the explicit caps and
threshold properties stated in their hypotheses ($`r_{\max}`$,
$`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$, $`\theta_{\mathrm{acc}}>1-p_{b}`$, $`k`$, $`m`$,
$`E_{\max}`$, $`c_{\mathrm{p}}`$); no proof depends on the unspecified
schedule shapes.

###### Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution).

1.  (i)
    _Qualifying rejection $`=`$ protocol-bearing gate rejection._ Every
    attested identity’s rejecting decision on a shared candidate at its
    own _protocol-bearing_ confirmation gate
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii):
    tool- or reasoning-target, non-covered; cache gates included on
    their rejecting branch) is automatically a signed, logged qualifying
    rejection. There is no separate filing step and no rejection weight
    floor: inspection and report are one act. A user who merely abandons
    the dialog records nothing (abstention is counted as a miss inside
    $`1-q`$;
    [Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Each identity holds at most $`r_{\max}`$ open (unresolved)
    rejections. _Covered gates are inert._ A gate event fired by a
    handle-expressed use
    (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
    of a pair for which the identity already holds an in-scope local
    $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy — a _covered gate_; a literal-expressed reuse
    takes the fast path
    (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a))
    and never gates — is protocol-inert for the shared tier, on both
    branches: its accepting decision carries no promotion weight,
    consumes no freshness, and joins no notification cohort (a
    _redundant_ confirmation,
    §[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    its rejecting decision is logged as corroboration if the item is
    frozen and as an advisory flag otherwise — no dispute initiation, no
    verdict, no accountability exposure. Coverage is decided owner-side
    on the identity’s own local store, a deterministic test independent
    of any shared-tier or attacker-influenced state. _Reasoning
    coverage._ A gate event with target $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ on bytes
    of which the identity’s local store holds _any_ readable
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-level block ($`\mathsf{T}`$, $`\mathsf{PC}`$, or
    $`\mathsf{C}`$ of any scope;
    Rule [R5](#Thmrulex5 "Rule R5 (Readable local endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    is likewise a covered gate, protocol-inert on both branches exactly
    as a tool-target covered gate: its accepting decision is a redundant
    confirmation
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    — no promotion weight, no freshness consumption, no notification
    cohort — and its rejecting decision is logged as corroboration if
    the bytes are frozen and as an advisory flag otherwise. The coverage
    test is owner-side and deterministic: it reads only the identity’s
    own local store’s readability facts, never any shared-tier or
    attacker-influenced state. Within an epoch, only an identity’s
    _first_ rejecting decision on a given byte string can take effect as
    a dispute-initiating rejection; every later rejecting decision by
    the same identity on the same bytes within the epoch is logged as
    corroboration if the item is frozen, and otherwise as an advisory
    flag (the zero-authority class above): no protocol effect, no
    accountability exposure. The allowance renews at the epoch boundary.
    A rejecting decision that is verdict-eligible under clause (iii) is
    cast as a panel verdict regardless of this cap, exactly as under
    clause (v)(e); the cap restricts dispute _initiation_ only, and
    capped rejections remain visible as flags. An identity whose
    rejection rights are under suspension (clause (v)) files _advisory
    flags_ instead: no protocol effect, no penalty; flags alert other
    users.
2.  (ii)
    _Disputed state._ A qualifying rejection freezes promotion of $`v`$
    at every tool, immediately, and visibly flags the item. (A
    qualifying rejection on bytes holding $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status at any
    tool is instead a post-promotion rejection, routed to clause (vi).)
    A frozen item remains retrievable (surfaced flagged,
    Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii))
    and personally usable through each user’s own gate confirmation; the
    freeze suspends community promotion only. The item’s pre-dispute
    endorsers are notified. Pre-dispute endorsements are retained on the
    log for audit and reputation but carry no weight in resolution.
3.  (iii)
    _Panel formation (demand-paced, fresh-juror)._ The panel is not a
    body convened in advance but a capped tally of decisions: it
    comprises the first $`k`$ _eligible verdicts_ logged on the disputed
    item, with no global deadline. Because a disputed item is
    unpromoted, every demander must personally inspect-and-confirm it to
    use it
    (Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    the interpreter displays the exact bytes at the demander’s own gate,
    visibly carrying the dispute flag and the rejecter’s stated ground.
    At the moment a demander records a decision, and only then, the
    interpreter checks eligibility on log facts:
    1.  (a)
        attestation weight $`\geq w_{\mathrm{seat}}`$;
    2.  (b)
        fresh
        (Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    3.  (c)
        no verdict already cast by this identity on this dispute
        instance; verdict eligibility is scoped to the dispute instance
        for its entire life: an identity casts at most one verdict on a
        given dispute, ever
        ([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    4.  (d)
        at most $`\lceil k/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ verdicts per
        identity pool, likewise scoped per dispute instance;
    5.  (e)
        fewer than $`k`$ verdicts so far.

    A cache gate
    (Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    is never a verdict surface: its rejecting decision may initiate or
    corroborate a dispute per clause (i), but is not verdict-eligible
    and occupies no panel seat. (Only a cache gate’s rejecting branch is
    logged,
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii);
    admitting such gates as verdict surfaces would make verdict
    membership outcome-selected there, against the benign-panel
    hypothesis of
    Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
    The exclusion is theorem-compatible and resolves an otherwise
    outcome-selected surface:
    Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and
    Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    bound tallies over verdicts actually cast, and the eligible class is
    simply defined without cache gates; no pathwise monotonicity is
    claimed.) A dispute instance opens at its qualifying rejection and
    closes at resolution or expiry; its verdict tally and pool caps
    persist unchanged across epoch boundaries
    (convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
    and a boundary-spanning dispute counts toward
    Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
    in the epoch in which it opened. If eligible, _that gate decision is
    the verdict_, recorded once, verdicts ordered by log order of
    decisions; otherwise the decision is an ordinary personal
    confirmation (a bystander rejection still logs as corroboration). A
    user who opens the dialog and abandons it records nothing and
    occupies nothing: verdict capacity is consumed only by cast
    verdicts, so abandonment cannot exhaust or stall the panel, and no
    seat allocation, timer, or release mechanism exists. The dispute,
    like freshness, is byte-level: the panel adjudicates the bytes, each
    juror inspecting them at the juror’s own attempted tool, with the
    dispute flag and the rejecter’s stated ground displayed. Pre-dispute
    endorsers cast no verdicts: a notified endorser’s re-inspection is
    repeat
    (Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    its accepting branch has no protocol effect, and its rejecting
    branch is a further qualifying rejection with no additional protocol
    effect while the item is frozen (logged as corroboration).
    Consequently every verdict-bearing inspection is the juror’s first
    _logged_ decision on the bytes
    (Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    [INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

4.  (iv)
    _Resolution (early and decisive)._ Verdicts are tallied as cast. The
    moment rejecting verdicts reach $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$: _evicted_:
    demoted to $`\mathsf{U}`$ in the shared tier, cool-down, cascade to
    shared derivations. The moment accepting verdicts reach $`m`$:
    _vindicated_: the byte-level freeze lifts and the interrupted
    pipeline entry resumes, its window clock excluding the freeze;
    vindication consumes neither the owner’s rate limit nor an entry of
    Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
    and it never directly promotes. Each juror’s accepting verdict is
    simultaneously that juror’s gate confirmation at the juror’s own
    tool (its one fresh decision on the bytes), credited toward the
    entry’s per-tool endorsement sets subject to the authority gate and
    credit caps of
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),(f);
    it joins those sets together with the retained pre-dispute
    endorsements, which carry no weight in resolution but keep their
    promotion weight, being fresh inspections the panel’s vindication
    never contradicted. Freeze-time bystander confirmations, fresh
    accepting gate confirmations by demanders whose decisions are not
    verdicts (under-weight, pool-capped, or post-capacity), are credited
    identically on vindication at their own tools (per
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),(f));
    crediting adds no confirmation event
    (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    If no entry was open at the freeze, vindication lifts the freeze and
    the item returns to dormant status, its verdict-confirmations
    credited on the next entry’s opening subject to
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),(f),
    or expiring with it
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
    [INV-4](#Thminvx4 "Invariant INV-4 (Banking safety). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Every promotion, after any number of disputes, therefore still
    requires $`N`$ fresh-inspection endorsements at the promoted tool
    itself
    (Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

    _Default bars._ The default bars are $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k+1-m`$ with
    $`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ and $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$
    (jointly forcing $`k\geq 2f_{\mathrm{s}}+1`$); their consequences
    (mutually exclusive outcomes and decisive, tally-deadlock-free
    resolution) are
    Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
    Deployments choosing looser bars ($`m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}\geq k+2`$)
    retain a neither-bar outcome, in which the item returns to
    unpromoted candidate status and re-entry consumes the owner’s rate
    limit
    (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and gathers a fresh endorsement set. A disputed item that attracts
    no new demand for $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$ expires
    (Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)):
    retired unpromoted, all open rejection slots on it freed, no penalty
    to any party.

5.  (v)
    _Rejecter accountability._
    1.  (a)
        Panel verdicts are never penalised and never charged.
    2.  (b)
        A dispute-initiating rejection is _charged_ when its dispute
        ends in vindication, at the moment the vindication is logged, to
        the epoch in which that vindication is logged. Rejections whose
        disputes end in eviction or expiry charge nothing.
    3.  (c)
        The first charge per identity per epoch carries no penalty.
        Repeated charges escalate to suspension of _rejection rights
        only_ (endorsement weight and ordinary use untouched), restored
        after cool-down. Escalation is rate-based, never count-based:
        the trigger is the identity’s charged-rejection rate _per fresh
        inspection_, over a minimum sample size, at a threshold
        $`\theta_{\mathrm{acc}}`$ calibrated strictly above the honest
        baseline $`1-p_{b}`$
        ([Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    4.  (d)
        _Hard ceiling._ Independently of (c): once $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$
        charges have accrued to an identity within an epoch, the
        identity’s further dispute-initiating rejections for the
        remainder of the epoch are filed as advisory flags (the
        zero-authority class of clause (i)); the allowance renews at the
        epoch boundary.
    5.  (e)
        Suspension and the ceiling restrict _dispute-initiating_
        rejections only: a rejecting decision that is verdict-eligible
        under clause (iii) is cast as a panel verdict regardless of the
        identity’s accountability state, so the panel arithmetic of
        Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
        and
        Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
        is independent of accountability state; freeze-time
        corroborating rejections, having no protocol effect, are logged
        either way.
    6.  (f)
        Deployments may additionally maintain a _lifetime_
        charged-rejection account per identity, with the same
        per-inspection normalisation and a comparative
        (population-outlier) trigger, suspending rejection rights
        directly for extreme outliers.
    7.  (g)
        Both layers touch rejection rights only, never endorsement
        weight or any local store
        (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

6.  (vi)
    _Post-promotion rejection._ A qualifying rejection against a
    promoted item moves it to _Suspended_. Suspension invalidates the
    shared entry for the fast-path test of
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
    (§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
    community authority is withdrawn for the duration of the review, so
    every user’s use of the pair gates — except a user holding a
    personally confirmed in-scope local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy, who
    continues through that copy
    (Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    unaffected. Suspension additionally imposes the byte-level freeze of
    clause (ii) on promotion at every tool. A fast-track panel (same
    parameters) attempts completion within $`T_{\mathrm{pan}}`$; failure
    to complete by $`T_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ leaves the item Suspended with
    verdict collection continuing demand-paced, exactly as an ordinary
    dispute. Its verdicts arise at the gates suspension re-arms:
    1.  (a)
        _Demanders during suspension:_ any user demanding the pair while
        the entry is suspended (new adopter and prior ungated adopter
        alike) gates, and verdict eligibility is decided by the log-fact
        check of clause (iii) exactly as in an ordinary dispute. In
        particular a prior ungated adopter with no logged decision on
        the bytes is fresh, while one with _any_ prior logged decision
        (a rejection, or an acceptance at another tool) is repeat and
        ineligible, its rejecting branch a qualifying rejection like any
        other (logged as corroboration while frozen).
    2.  (b)
        _Prompted re-inspection:_ the suspension notification carries a
        voluntary re-inspection prompt to current adopters not presently
        demanding the pair; accepting it re-displays the exact bytes at
        the adopter’s own gate under the dispute flag, eligibility again
        per clause (iii); an accepting inspection earns the adopter a
        local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy, covering all later use of the pair.
        Declining costs nothing beyond the suspension itself: the
        adopter’s next actual use of the pair gates once, at the floor
        (Corollary [S6.5](#A6.Thmtheorem5 "Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
        Prompts are issued to at most $`c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ adopters per
        suspension; re-inspection invitations of either kind, re-entry
        notifications
        (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
        and suspension prompts, are deduplicated jointly, at most one
        invitation per identity per item per epoch. Prompts expire at
        the end of their issuance epoch; a review left unresolved at the
        boundary continues demand-paced but issues no new prompts merely
        for having crossed it. At most $`E_{\max}`$ fast-track reviews
        are opened per item per epoch; once the cap is reached, the item
        remains Suspended for the remainder of the epoch, verdict
        collection continues demand-paced exactly as in an ordinary
        dispute, and further post-promotion rejections are logged as
        corroboration of the open review (the zero-authority class of
        clause (i): no protocol effect, no accountability exposure).

    The panel decides demotion-with-cascade or reinstatement. If $`k`$
    fresh verdicts do not arrive within $`T_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, the item
    remains Suspended and verdict collection continues demand-paced,
    exactly as an ordinary dispute; a Suspended item attracting no fresh
    demand for $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$ is retired from the shared tier
    (Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)):
    no reinstatement, no eviction, no accountability consequence for
    either side, and every personally confirmed local copy untouched
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

7.  (vii)
    _Publisher accountability._ When a panel _evicts_ an item, the
    publishing identity incurs an escalating penalty: the first eviction
    per identity per epoch triggers a submission cool-down; repeated
    evictions within an epoch escalate to suspension of _submission
    rights_ and reduction of attestation weight. The penalty touches
    shared-tier rights and attestation weight only, never any local
    store, label, or scope
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and is triggered only by a resolved panel’s eviction verdict, never
    by rejections alone and never by expiry
    (Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- Commentary (non-normative; role of clause (v)). Clause (v)’s induced
  deterministic bound $`c_{\mathrm{acc}}=c_{\mathrm{ceil}}+r_{\max}`$ is
  Lemma [S5.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma S5.4 (Deterministic accountability bound). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  these clauses enter only the budget constants of
  Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  never any safety theorem
  (Figure [S1](#A1.F1 "Figure S1 ‣ S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Calibration guidance and the honest cost analysis:
  [Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  [S15](#Thmobjx15 "Analysis S15 (Accountability mis-calibration). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Remark S4.9 (Per-pair dispute scoping (deployment variant)).

A deployment may scope disputes and panels per (value, tool) pair: a
qualifying rejection then freezes promotion at the rejected pair only,
and jurors are drawn from that pair’s demanders, adjudicating the
rejected tool’s context. This removes the cross-tool-jury residual of
[S4](#Thmobjx4 "Analysis S4 (Tool-targeted poison). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the applicable $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ becomes the targeted tool’s. The
costs are per-pair panel formation and freeze scope, panels and prompts
multiplying by up to $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ per item, and a re-keying
decision — whether freshness and verdict capacity remain byte-level or
become pair-level — that this document does not make; an analogous
per-attempt bound is plausible but not formally instantiated here, the
freshness and verdict-capacity re-keying being deliberately undecided.
No theorem of this document consumes the variant.

###### Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene).

The shared candidate store is curated by three deterministic,
interpreter-applied policies.

1.  (i)
    _Entry cap and expiry._ At most $`E_{\max}`$ pipeline entries open
    per exact byte string per epoch — promoted, evicted, and unpromoted
    entries alike, republications and re-entries included; a submission
    of bytes whose per-epoch entry cap is exhausted is ineligible
    (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and takes the uniform reject of Publish-Rej, eligibility returning
    at the epoch boundary. The cap is availability-only: banked credits
    and any live promotion status persist across the boundary
    (convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    [N14](#Thmnotex14 "Note N14 (Availability degrades gracefully, never destructively). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Additionally, a published candidate is retired from the shared tier
    when any of the following holds:
    1.  (a)
        it completes $`E_{\max}`$ pipeline entries without promotion
        within the epoch (the count is cumulative across republications
        within the epoch and resets only at the epoch boundary);
    2.  (b)
        it accumulates $`E_{\max}`$ _non-vindicated_ disputes within the
        epoch (disputes ending in vindication are exempt; under the
        default bars this trigger fires only through the optional
        neither-bar outcome of
        Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv);
        rationale:
        [N15](#Thmnotex15 "Note N15 (The vindication exemption). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    3.  (c)
        it remains dormant (window closed, not resubmitted) for
        $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$;
    4.  (d)
        it attracts no demand for $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$, including a
        _disputed_ candidate attracting no new demand for
        $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$.

    Entries and dormant intervals alternate: each pipeline entry is
    followed by at most one dormant interval, ending at the next entry
    or at retirement; by the entry cap, entries per item per epoch
    number at most $`E_{\max}`$ and dormant intervals begun within the
    epoch at most $`E_{\max}`$, deterministically (one further dormant
    interval may be carried across the boundary; the ledger’s
    conservative common bound is $`E_{\star}=E_{\max}+1`$,
    Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Because the cap and the count of clause (a) are per epoch, a
    persistently demanded benign item may re-enter in later epochs;
    safety is unaffected, every federated safety bound being per-attempt
    (Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    with lifetime exposure counted by
    Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
    The owner’s local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy is untouched
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    the owner may republish, subject to
    Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and the entry cap. Retirement of a disputed item frees all open
    rejection slots on it and is neither an eviction nor a vindication:
    no accountability consequence for any party.

2.  (ii)
    _Surfacing order._ The $`\leq c_{\mathrm{cand}}`$ candidates a
    retrieval surfaces are ordered by trust status ($`\mathsf{CC}`$,
    then undisputed candidates by endorsement weight, then disputed
    items, flagged), computed on log facts, never by a model.
3.  (iii)
    _Demotion hygiene._ Items evicted by panel verdict are removed from
    retrieval entirely for the cool-down period.

These policies only refuse entry openings, remove items, or reorder
items in the shared tier; their safety- and budget-preservation is
Lemma [S5.9](#A5.Thmtheorem9 "Lemma S5.9 (Hygiene preserves safety through bound uniformity). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions

###### Assumption A7 (Federated endorsement transfer).

A Confirmed item endorsed _at a specific tool_ by a qualifying weighted
set of distinct attested identities is authoritative for that exact tool
for any user (and likewise at the pseudo-target: a qualifying quorum at
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ is authoritative for informing any user’s
reasoning), _provided the item is context-independent_, a semantic
property judged by the publishing owner and the inspecting community,
not decided by the type system. Tool identifiers are canonical across
the federation (TCB), so “the same tool” is well-defined; there is no
transfer between tools. (Scope: as at
§[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
endorsement unit; the baseline data-tool path is governed by
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)
and
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b).)
The type-level half is discharged by
Lemma [S5.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S5.2 (Type-level sharing exclusion). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and is not assumed. (All formal guarantees are integrity guarantees;
semantic confidentiality of published content rests on the publish gate
and is not separately proved:
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log).

In the two-run comparison of
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
extended to the federated setting
(Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the _exogenous log prefix_ delivered at each step’s log slot
(Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— every federation-log event not generated by the compared local run
itself: other parties’ endorsements, rejections, promotions,
suspensions, panel verdicts, and accountability events — is an exogenous
input stream, coupled identically across the compared runs, exactly as
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
couples the user’s typed stream. The compared run’s _own_ locally
generated federation events
