(Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are not assumed coupled: their equality across the compared runs is
_derived_ in
Proposition [S5.10](#A5.Thmtheorem10 "Proposition S5.10 (Delegated Action Integrity and federated Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
from the matched components, so the full delivered logs coincide without
constraining either attack. The federated Reasoning Integrity statement
therefore isolates the effect of _unendorsed, undisplayed_ untrusted
bytes; attacker influence exercised through _legitimate_ log activity is
governed not by that theorem but by the safety bounds of
Appendix [S5](#A5a "Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(Theorems [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Assumption A9 (Verdict rate).

There is $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}\in(0,1]`$ that lower-bounds, uniformly
over disputed items, times, and histories, the conditional probability,
given all prior protocol events, that the next arriving demander of a
disputed item casts an eligible verdict
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)):
weight $`\geq w_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, fresh, no prior verdict on the
dispute instance, within the pool caps, and recording a decision rather
than abandoning. The bound is asserted _jointly over behaviour and
protocol state_: eligibility is consumed endogenously (freshness spent,
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
pool caps filled,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(d);
capacity exhausted, (iii)(e)), so
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
entails in particular that the item’s remaining fresh, seat-weighted,
pool-diverse demand does not run out while the dispute is open — a
demand-composition property, not a psychological one. The bound is read
per the conditioning convention of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
conditional on all logged atoms prior to the arrival, and uniformly over
demand realisations.

- Commentary (non-normative; epistemic status and failure mode of
  [A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). [A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  has two components with different characters. The behavioural
  component (a demander who _could_ cast an eligible verdict does so at
  rate $`\geq\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$) has the same epistemic status as
  $`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}},p_{b}`$. The structural component
  is stronger and can fail _deterministically_, with no human variation
  at all: freshness consumption and the pool caps are protocol
  mechanics, so an item pre-exposed to most of a pool’s identities, or
  whose demand is concentrated in few pools, can reach a state where
  _no_ arriving demander is eligible — the conditional probability is
  then $`0`$, and no behavioural assumption restores it. The
  consequences of failure are confined by design: every result resting
  on
  [A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is availability-side
  (Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
  the ledger’s bucket rows, and through them the budget asymptotics); no
  safety theorem consumes it
  (Figure [S1](#A1.F1 "Figure S1 ‣ S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  the unresolved dispute stalls _frozen_
  (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
  and each affected demander still pays at most the floor
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
  Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)’s
  unconditional clause). Validation: verdict-eligibility rates on
  disputed items, stratified by pool and by the item’s prior exposure
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Quantitative consequences:
  Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
  The eligible-verdict class excludes cache-gate decisions
  (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii));
  $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ is read over the class as so defined.
  $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ and $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ condition on the
  same human act consistently: an abstaining demander is a miss inside
  $`1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ _and_ a non-verdict inside
  $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$; high abstention degrades resolution speed,
  never the validity of the safety parameter
  ([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Adversary (federated).

The adversary controls, over the deployment’s lifetime, $`f`$ qualifying
identities of total weight $`\leq W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$, of which at most
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are ever seat-eligible (static corruption,
§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
It does not control honest users’ decisions, the labelling, the
interpreter, or the log. It may present a poisoned item to whom it
likes, in what order it likes, and may stop or continue as a function of
past outcomes, but never as a function of an inspection not yet
performed: formally, its strategy is a predictable process with respect
to the protocol filtration
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention ([C2](#A1.I2.i2 "Item C2 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
against which
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is stated. Two structural constraints on its adaptivity (within-entry
byte immutability, and the reading of $`q`$ as a uniform bound over the
honest identities the adversary can target) are recorded in
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
[Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification).

Fix a classification
$`\mathsf{Bad}\subseteq\mathcal{V}\times(\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{sens}}\cup\mathsf{Tools}_{\mathrm{data}}\cup\{\mathsf{reasoning}\})`$,
exogenous to the protocol: no rule reads it, no transition depends on
it, and no model computes it. An item $`v`$ is _poisoned_ if
$`\mathsf{Bad}(v,t)`$ holds for some tool $`t`$, and _benign_ otherwise;
“harmful at $`t`$” means $`\mathsf{Bad}(v,t)`$; harm at
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ means content that misleads reasoning if adopted
([A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Every behavioural parameter
($`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}},p_{b},q_{c}`$) and every safety and
budget statement of
Appendices [S5](#A5a "Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is read relative to this classification; the classification is a
modelling device for stating the bounds, not a protocol object, and the
protocol’s behaviour is identical under any choice of it.

###### TCB additions (federated).

Beyond
§[S2.5](#A2.SS5 "S2.5 Attacker model and trusted computing base ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the attestation layer and its weight assignment on cryptographic facts;
the pool assignment of
Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
canonical tool identifiers shared and attested across the federation;
and the log service of
convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
(sequencing and authenticated history). The Sybil conditions (finiteness
of $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$ and the seat margin $`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$)
require an attestation authority or identity cost [Douceur
(2002)](#bib.bib16); [Dwork & Naor (2007)](#bib.bib17). Because $`f`$,
$`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$, and $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are _lifetime_ totals
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
they are enforceable only to the extent that the attestation or
identity-cost mechanism supplies certified lifetime bounds: the issuance
policy must bound the identities and weight any party can ever acquire,
and that bound is what the constants denote. Where issuance is open or
uncosted, no finite $`f`$ exists and the federated safety results are
compatibility statements — valid for whatever lifetime totals the
deployment can certify — while the single-user layer and the cap
(Theorems [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are unaffected, consuming no Sybil bound.

### Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees

This appendix proves the guarantees of the protocol of
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the structural lemmas
(§[S5.1](#A5.SS1 "S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
then the integrity lifting, the deterministic safety theorem, panel
safety, wrongful eviction, publisher safety, denial-of-service, and
submission-budget results
(§[S5.2](#A5.SS2 "S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Dependencies are as in
Figure [S1](#A1.F1 "Figure S1 ‣ S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

#### S5.1 Structural lemmas

###### Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt).

Fix a byte string $`v`$. A _promotion attempt_ is a maximal segment of
one shared-tier presence of $`v`$ beginning at an _anchor_ and ending at
the first _finalisation_ thereafter — the close of a pipeline entry’s
window at its full length, where promotion is decided
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
— or, where no finalisation occurs, at the end of the presence
(retirement, or demotion by panel eviction) or at a loose-bar
neither-bar resolution returning the item to candidate status
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)).
Anchors are: the presence-creating submission event (first attempt), and
each attempt-ending event just listed other than the end of the presence
(each later attempt). A window closed early at an epoch boundary is
_not_ a finalisation
(convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))):
it banks its accrued endorsements to the item’s next entry, which
belongs to the _same_ attempt.

Anchors are log events, and every decision credited to an attempt’s
entries — in-window, banked in a dormant or frozen interval,
boundary-banked, or vindication-credited
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),(f),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv))
— is logged strictly after the attempt’s anchor: in-window and interval
decisions follow the preceding anchor by construction, and
boundary-banked decisions were logged in an earlier entry of the same
attempt, itself opened after the anchor. Likewise no ordinary dispute
and no fast-track review is open at any anchor: either state imposes the
byte-level freeze
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),(vi)),
which interrupts a window rather than letting it finalise
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)),
and retirement frees all open rejection slots
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i));
so every dispute or review bearing on an attempt opens, and casts all
its verdicts, after the attempt’s anchor.

Attempts partition each presence; every entry belongs to exactly one
attempt (the attempt whose anchor precedes its opening); at most one
entry of an attempt lies in any single epoch (a second entry of the same
attempt arises only across an epoch boundary, via a boundary-closed
window); and only an attempt’s final entry can finalise. An attempt
_succeeds_ if its finalisation is a promotion; an attempt with no
finalisation — ending at retirement, eviction, or a neither-bar
resolution, or with no entry ever opened — succeeds with probability
zero. Attempts whose finalisation lies in a given epoch number at most
the epoch’s entries of the item, hence at most $`E_{\max}`$ per item
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
each such finalising entry opened by a rate-limited (re-)submission of
the same epoch
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
windows are epoch-contained,
convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
Dually, the attempts _anchored_ in a given epoch are begun at that
epoch’s presence-creating submissions and finalisation events (under the
default bars; under loose bars also its neither-bar resolutions), which
is the counting
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
consumes.

- Commentary (non-normative; role of the attempt unit). The attempt is
  the analysis unit at which the per-submission safety bound is
  conditioned. Banked decisions credited to an entry precede the entry’s
  opening, and the owner — or an adversary — may decide whether to open
  the entry _as a function of_ the banked outcomes; a bound conditioned
  at the entry’s opening would therefore condition on an adversarially
  selected event (an optional-selection error). The attempt’s anchor
  precedes every decision creditable to its entries by construction, so
  conditioning at the anchor is sound; and an attempt whose intervals
  bank decisions is an attempt whether or not a further entry opens, so
  the choice not to open is a choice among attempts already counted, at
  success probability zero. No protocol rule reads attempts; like the
  ledger’s charging convention
  (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  they are a hindsight bookkeeping device over the same window/interval
  alternation the ledger’s buckets partition.

###### Lemma S5.2 (Type-level sharing exclusion).

No $`\mathsf{T}`$-block, no $`\mathsf{U}`$-block, no cache-marked block,
and no block lacking an accepting publish confirmation by its owner ever
enters the shared candidate store.

###### Proof.

Label and provenance membership are deterministic and attacker-immutable
([A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
provenance is interpreter-only,
Definition [S2.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Definition S2.2 (Store and configuration). ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the publish gate of
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is a confirmation event under
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
[A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
nomination has no authority. ∎

###### Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness).

For a fixed byte string, the weight-bearing endorsement sets of distinct
pipeline entries are disjoint in identities over the deployment’s entire
history, and every weight-bearing endorsement (in-entry or
banked-and-credited) is its endorser’s fresh, authority-active
inspection of the bytes
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)).

###### Proof.

By
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
an identity’s weight-bearing endorsement of the bytes is its _first_
logged decision on them
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
taken while authority-active
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
(when credited,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)),
counted toward exactly one entry (the entry open at decision time, or,
via banking,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
the next entry to open). Every later acceptance by the same identity is
repeat and carries no weight
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Hence no identity contributes weight to two entries, and each
contribution is by construction a fresh inspection. ∎

###### Lemma S5.4 (Deterministic accountability bound).

Fix an identity and an epoch. The identity’s dispute-initiating
rejections filed within the epoch that both take protocol effect and are
eventually charged (contradicted by vindication), in this epoch or any
later one, number at most
$`c_{\mathrm{acc}}:=c_{\mathrm{ceil}}+r_{\max}`$.

###### Proof.

By
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(b),
a rejection is charged at the moment its vindication is logged. Suppose
first that the epoch’s $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$-th charge to this identity
occurs, at some moment $`T`$. From $`T`$ onward, the identity’s further
dispute-initiating rejections in the epoch are filed as advisory flags
with no protocol effect
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(d)),
hence are never counted. Every counted rejection is therefore either
charged no later than $`T`$ (and the epoch’s charges up to and including
$`T`$ number exactly $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$, by the choice of $`T`$) or
still open at $`T`$ and charged afterward; open rejections number at
most $`r_{\max}`$ at any moment
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
The two classes are disjoint, a rejection being charged exactly once;
summing gives $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}+r_{\max}`$. If instead fewer than
$`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$ charges accrue within the epoch, at most
$`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}-1`$ counted rejections are charged within it, and
every one charged in a later epoch is open at the epoch boundary, at
most $`r_{\max}`$ again. ∎

###### Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability).

The rate trigger of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(c)
is normalised _per fresh inspection_, never per rejection. The
normalisation matters: when poison is rare, almost all of an honest
inspector’s rejections are wrongful rejections of benign items and
almost all are vindicated, so charges _per rejection_ approach one for
honest and adversarial identities alike and cannot separate them;
charges _per inspection_ sit near $`1-p_{b}`$ for an honest identity and
near its full rejection rate for a campaign. The ceiling
$`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$ is calibrated, like the rate trigger, strictly
above the honest baseline: an honest identity accrues charges at rate at
most $`1-p_{b}`$ per benign fresh inspection, and its fresh inspections
per epoch are bounded by its own required-confirmation stream (small,
and shrinking with population,
Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$ set at a high quantile of
$`(1-p_{b})\times`$(honest per-epoch fresh-inspection count), with
margin, is reached by an honest identity only rarely; an honest identity
that does reach it retains advisory flags and ordinary use — though its
acceptances are authority-inert for the duration
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— loses nothing permanent, is restored at the epoch boundary, and its
inspections during that state are excluded trials, not misses
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so no safety statement is affected. Renewal semantics: convention
([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
(the accountability allowances are the only freshness-like quantities
that renew). (This calibration concerns the per-fresh-inspection
rejection-rate trigger only; suspension-induced required confirmations
are priced separately, once per demander, per
Note [N14](#Thmnotex14 "Note N14 (Availability degrades gracefully, never destructively). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
Mis-calibration risk:
[S15](#Thmobjx15 "Analysis S15 (Accountability mis-calibration). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under [A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Under
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
for any disputed item and any adversary strategy
(convention ([C2](#A1.I2.i2 "Item C2 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))):
the number of demanders who arrive while the dispute is unresolved is
stochastically dominated by the index of the $`(k{+}1)`$-st success in
an i.i.d. $`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\rho_{\mathrm{seat}})`$ sequence, i.e. by
a sum of $`k{+}1`$ independent
$`\mathrm{Geometric}(\rho_{\mathrm{seat}})`$ variables. In particular
its expectation is at most $`\kappa:=(k{+}1)/\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, and
for any $`c_{0}>1`$ the probability that more than $`c_{0}\,\kappa`$
demanders arrive while the dispute is unresolved is at most
$`e^{-\lambda_{c_{0}}k}`$ for a constant $`\lambda_{c_{0}}>0`$ depending
only on $`c_{0}`$ and $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$.

###### Proof.

Index trials by arrivals: let $`O_{i}`$ be the event that an $`i`$-th
demander of the item arrives while the dispute is unresolved, measurable
at that arrival’s rendering atom, and let $`Z_{i}`$ indicate that this
arrival’s disposition is an eligible verdict on the dispute instance.
Under the atomic reading of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
each arrival’s disposition is realized at its own log position, so the
$`\sigma`$-algebra of atoms prior to the $`i`$-th rendering atom
contains the dispositions and protocol effects of all earlier arrivals;
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives $`\mathbb{P}[Z_{i}=1\mid\mathcal{G}_{i}]\geq\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$
on $`O_{i}`$ at exactly these $`\sigma`$-algebras, and
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
in the form of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
supplies i.i.d. $`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\rho_{\mathrm{seat}})`$ variables
$`Y_{i}`$ with $`Y_{i}\leq Z_{i}`$ on $`O_{i}`$. A dispute instance
accepts at most $`k`$ eligible verdicts in its entire life
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(e)),
and every verdict is cast at an arrival; hence on $`O_{n}`$,
$`\sum_{i\leq n-1}Z_{i}\leq k`$, so $`\sum_{i\leq n-1}Y_{i}\leq k`$,
i.e. $`n\leq G:=\min\{j:\sum_{i\leq j}Y_{i}=k+1\}`$. The arrival count
is therefore pathwise at most $`G`$, a sum of $`k{+}1`$ independent
$`\mathrm{Geometric}(\rho_{\mathrm{seat}})`$ variables. Linearity gives
the expectation; the tail is the Chernoff bound for sums of independent
geometrics. (Because dispositions resolve at arrival, the sharper count
$`\sum_{i\leq n-1}Z_{i}\leq k-1`$ in fact holds while the dispute is
unresolved, improving $`\kappa`$ to $`k/\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$; we
retain the conservative $`\kappa=(k{+}1)/\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, which
every downstream constant consumes, the slack being monotone.) ∎

###### Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars).

Under the default bars $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k+1-m`$ with
$`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ and $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$: (i)
eviction and vindication are mutually exclusive; (ii) every panel that
gathers $`k`$ verdicts reaches exactly one bar, and the first bar
reached in log order is the bar reached by the full tally of $`k`$
verdicts: early resolution changes timing, never the outcome; (iii) both
bars are reachable by honest verdicts alone, and the adversary’s at most
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ verdicts
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
alone reach neither; hence no _tally_ deadlock exists once $`k`$
verdicts are gathered, and neither bar can be reached by the adversary’s
verdicts alone; whether $`k`$ eligible verdicts arrive is the separate,
availability-side matter of
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(Remark [S5.21](#A5.Thmtheorem21 "Remark S5.21 (Resolution as a demand-side event). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof.

(i)–(ii) $`m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k+1`$, so $`k`$ verdicts cannot meet both
bars and must meet at least one; verdict counts are non-decreasing along
the verdict sequence, so a bar is reached at some prefix iff it is
reached by the full tally. (iii) From $`k=m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1`$ with
$`m,m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$: $`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}\geq m`$ and
$`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}\geq m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$, so honest verdicts alone
suffice for either bar; and $`f_{\mathrm{s}}<m`$ means the adversary’s
at most $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ verdicts alone cannot reach the $`m`$-bar,
and symmetrically $`f_{\mathrm{s}}<m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ for the other bar.
∎

###### Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores).

For every user $`u`$ and every block $`b`$ in $`u`$’s local store (the
user-owned tier: $`\mathsf{T}`$-, $`\mathsf{C}`$-, $`\mathsf{PC}`$-, and
$`\mathsf{U}`$-blocks; community status lives in the shared tier and is
referenced, never stored, locally,
§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
no protocol event initiated by any identity other than $`u`$ alters
$`\mathrm{bytes}(b)`$, $`\ell(b)`$, or $`\mathsf{scope}(b)`$. Dispute,
suspension, vindication, demotion, eviction, expiry, and every
accountability penalty of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v),(vii)
act on the shared tier alone: they invalidate or flag shared entries,
restrict shared-tier rights, or reduce attestation weight. Demotion of a
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ item withdraws community authority from users who have
not personally confirmed it, whose gates simply fire again, within the
single-user cap of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and leaves every personally confirmed $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy intact (with a
notification). Suspension likewise withdraws community authority for the
review’s duration
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),
equally without touching any local block. Consequently no third-party
protocol transition ever directly alters or removes any block of any
user’s local store; first-party removal by the owner’s own agent
($`\mathsf{evict}`$, including evictions the agent performs in reaction
to notifications or other legitimate log events) is the disclosed
residual
[N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The induced cost bound, that no campaign pushes any user above the
single-user cap, is
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which rests on the present lemma.

###### Proof.

By
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
local stores mutate only via owner-invoked $`\Sigma`$-operations and
owner confirmations
([A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
$`\mathsf{evict}`$ is owner-only (first-party eviction by the owner’s
own agent is a disclosed residual:
[N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Community status is shared-tier state
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so demotion and suspension update the shared entry and never touch a
local block; promotion, demotion, and expiry are interpreter relabels or
retirements of the shared log entry
(Rules [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the accountability penalties of clauses (v) and (vii) act on rejection
rights, submission rights, and attestation weight, none of which is a
local-store attribute; the cascade quarantines shared derivations, not
local stores; notifications are advisory. ∎

###### Lemma S5.9 (Hygiene preserves safety through bound uniformity).

The policies of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
preserve every theorem of this document. The entry cap only refuses
entry openings, and retirement and demotion hygiene only remove
shared-tier items; none of these can enable a promotion. Surfacing
_reordering_ is not monotone by event-set inclusion — reordering, and
removal of one candidate, can increase another item’s reach within the
$`c_{\mathrm{cand}}`$-capped surface — but the safety bounds are
unaffected because
Theorems [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are uniform over adaptive presentation schedules and reach-free
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
any demand redistribution hygiene induces is one more presentation
schedule inside the quantified class.
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected because no local store is touched; the ledger of
Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected at the moment of any hygiene action, which adds no
confirmation event. Retirement does redirect _later_ demand: a user who
encounters the retired bytes afterwards through their own channels
confirms them as ordinary personal content, in the single-user stream
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
bounded by the cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
its benign,
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-conforming
component vanishing in expectation under the vanishing conditions of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
and the remainder entering $`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$
(Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the shared-tier ledger rows are never increased by removal or
reordering.

###### Proof.

Each policy is a deterministic interpreter action on the shared tier:
the entry cap refuses an entry opening, retirement removes a candidate,
surfacing order permutes at most $`c_{\mathrm{cand}}`$ surfaced
candidates, demotion hygiene removes an evicted item from retrieval.
None relabels any local block, forces any confirmation, or adds any
promotion path. For the safety theorems, the relevant quantification is
over adaptive presentation and demand schedules
(convention ([C2](#A1.I2.i2 "Item C2 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
the schedules realizable under any hygiene policy are a subset of that
class, and the bounds of
Theorems [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are uniform over it and independent of reach, so they apply verbatim to
the hygiene-modified deployment. The post-retirement reclassification is
Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
retirement clause. ∎

Assume

and read the interpreter over federated product configurations
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
under the federated step of
Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with

    live-entry test), each such entry backed at that tool by qualifying

    for its endorser and authoritative by

2.  (ii)
    under
    [A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")

(i) The single-user results are personal
(Lemma [S3.16](#A3.Thmtheorem16 "Lemma S3.16 (No community label single-user). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));

(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
authoritative by
[A7](#Thmassumptionx7 "Assumption A7 (Federated endorsement transfer). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the scope test is the same singleton-membership test as for
$`\mathsf{C}`$, and handle gating is label-independent
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)).
(ii) Log-slot transitions: both runs append the same coupled prefix
([A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
producing equal $`S_{\mathrm{sh}}(L)`$ by deterministic replay
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
appending nothing to either reply stream and touching no local store
(Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Locally emitted federation events extend the two logs equally, by cases.
(1) $`\mathsf{submit}(v)`$: the publish decision is a transcript event
(matched) on bytes of a local $`\mathsf{C}`$-block of the owner

the equal delivered prefix
(Definitions [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v)).
(3) Realized demand events: fired by the matched operation against the
matched federated view, the acting identity common to both runs, and
epoch-first-demand status a deterministic predicate of the equal
delivered prefixes
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
By induction on steps: equal delivered prefixes give equal
$`\mathsf{LiveCC}(L)`$; together with the matched-local-state induction

(Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
this gives matched local transitions, and the case analysis then gives

Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
runs verbatim with $`\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{fed}}_{\mathbb{E}}`$ for

prefix
(Definition [S4.2](#A4.Thmtheorem2a "Definition S4.2 (Federated step; log slot). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
matched across the runs, so the gate-or-no-gate decision of
Step [5](#A3.SS4a "S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
remains matched. (iii) is
Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

###### Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection).

Under
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with perfect honest detection ($`q=1`$: every honest inspection of the
poisoned item rejects): if $`W>W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$ and
$`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$, then no poisoned item
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is ever promoted to $`\mathsf{CC}`$ at any tool, at any population size
and under any attack, through either the ordinary or the panel path.

###### Proof.

With $`q=1`$, every accepting endorsement and every accepting panel
verdict on a poisoned item is adversarial. The ordinary path requires
accepting weight at least $`W`$ at the tool in question, while the
adversary’s weight is at most $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$ and
$`W>W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$: impossible. The panel path requires at least
$`m`$ accepting verdicts, while the adversary casts at most
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ verdicts
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
$`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$, and honest accepting verdicts are zero:
impossible. Vindication-credited and dormancy-banked endorsements are
covered identically: with $`q=1`$ every honest decision on the poison
rejects, so every credited acceptance is adversarial and already counted
inside $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$ (respectively inside the $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$
verdict cap). Deterministic and population-free. ∎

###### Remark S5.12 (Scope of Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

The hypothesis $`q=1`$ is a behavioural idealization, the strongest in
this document, not the absence of one: the Sybil conditions
$`W>W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$, $`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ exclude _adversarial_
weight, while honest acceptances of the poison are excluded only by
$`q=1`$ itself. The theorem is therefore _not_ a fallback for the
unrecognizable-poison regime $`q\to 0`$, where honest inspectors
themselves supply the threshold and no community-truthfulness guarantee
is available within a human-judgment design. What survives that regime
is the local layer — personal Action Integrity, the single-user cap, and
no-deletion
(Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— together with the one-sided detection clause (a single honest
_effective qualifying rejection_, whenever one occurs, freezes promotion
immediately,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v))
and re-verification against never-decided inspectors
([N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
See
[S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation).

Adopt
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with the default bars of

($`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k{+}1-m`$, $`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$,
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$;
Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and the probabilistic framework of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Suppose:

1.  (a)
    ordinary promotion at a tool requires $`N`$ distinct accepting
    endorsements counted toward one pipeline entry
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    with $`N>f`$;
2.  (b)
    at most $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ of the adversary’s identities are
    seat-eligible, with $`m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$;
3.  (c)
    there are $`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}}\in(0,1]`$ such that:
    each honest _fresh, authority-active_
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a))
    inspection of the poisoned item at a non-covered, _non-cache_
    confirmation gate ends in an _effective qualifying rejection_ — a
    recorded rejecting decision that takes protocol effect under
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
    — with conditional probability at least $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$; and
    each honest _eligible verdict_ on the item rejects with conditional
    probability at least $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, _conditionally on the
    verdict being cast_, i.e. at the verdict’s header-inclusive
    $`\sigma`$-algebra
