    (§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
    Both bounds are read per the conditioning convention of
    §[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (all prior logged atoms; the demand realisation), and both are
    _uniform lower bounds over the honest identities and presentation
    contexts the adversary can target_ — the catch rate of the most
    fallible targetable honest cohort, not a population average
    ([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    — $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$’s contexts are the _unfrozen_ candidate
    contexts — in-window and candidate-dormancy inspections, any
    advisory-flag state — where an effective qualifying rejection is
    possible
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(ii));
    freeze- and suspension-time fresh inspections carry no initiation
    and belong to $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$’s province where
    verdict-eligible, their non-verdict rejections being corroborations,
    consumed by no trial of this theorem. $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$’s
    contexts include the freeze itself: verdicts are cast while the item
    is frozen. Both bounds are read over the target contexts (tools and
    $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$) in which the trials actually occur:
    $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is a uniform bound over the tool contexts of
    _eligible jurors_, which under byte-level panels may include tools
    at which the item is innocuous — for tool-targeted poison the
    applicable $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ may therefore be small
    ([S4](#Thmobjx4 "Analysis S4 (Tool-targeted poison). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    Authority-inert inspections, covered gates, and cache gates
    (Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    belong to no trial class of this theorem: an authority-inert
    acceptance carries no promotion weight and an authority-inert
    rejection no initiation
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
    covered gates are protocol-inert on both branches
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
    [Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and cache gates are accept-inert and verdict-ineligible
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
    — their rejecting branch is one more effective qualifying rejection,
    which can only deny the case-(a) path — so promotion still requires
    $`N-f`$ honest authority-active fresh _non-cache_ credits, and
    $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ is quantified over exactly the class whose
    members can both accept with weight and reject with effect.
    Abstention by an authority-active fresh inspector records nothing
    and is counted as a miss inside $`1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$; the two
    parameters deliberately live at different conditioning levels —
    $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ at the disposition of a fresh inspection, where
    abstention must count as a miss; $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ at a cast
    verdict, where abstention is already excluded by eligibility — and
    $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}\leq q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is typical but not
    assumed;
4.  (d)
    the panel margin is positive:
    $`\delta:=\frac{m-f_{\mathrm{s}}}{k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}-(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})>0`$.

Then for any poisoned
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
submission, every promotion attempt
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
succeeds with probability at most the display below, _conditionally on
the $`\sigma`$-algebra generated by all atoms up to and including the
attempt’s anchor atom_, uniformly over adaptive presentation, stopping,
and re-entry strategies and regardless of how many users the item is
shown to
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),

|     |                                               |                                                                                                                                              |     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion}]`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{N-f}+\mathbb{P}\!\big[\mathrm{Bin}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}},1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})\geq m-f_{\mathrm{s}}\big]`$ |     |
|     |                                               | $`\displaystyle\leq(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{N-f}+e^{-2\delta^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}.`$                                                          |     |

###### Remark S5.14 (Scope of Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the special case $`q=1`$. The bound covers a single promotion attempt
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
for attempts anchored while the bytes hold live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status
at some tool (additional-tool promotion of already-promoted bytes,
possible only after a prior success), hypothesis (c) is read with
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$’s contexts extended per the closing paragraph of
the proof; first-promotion attempts need no extension; entries embed
injectively into attempts, so per-entry counting statements read a
fortiori; attempts are counted at their anchors, and the
per-anchor-epoch union bound taken, in
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
No hypothesis is placed on repeat inspections: none carries promotion
weight or a verdict
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
Remark [S4.7](#A4.Thmtheorem7 "Remark S4.7 (Why the freshness asymmetry is safe). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The panel arithmetic rests on
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
alone, which is stated independently of the freshness rule precisely so
that it never depends on
[INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The default bars are a hypothesis of the theorem: case (b) uses decisive
resolution
(Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
to cap honest verdicts at $`k-a`$. Under the looser bars permitted by
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
($`m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}\geq k+2`$), the same argument bounds the
vindication event verbatim — vindication still requires $`m`$ accepting
verdicts among at most $`k`$, so the case-(b) term stands with
$`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ trials — and the additional neither-bar outcome
returns the item to unpromoted candidate status, whose re-entry opens a
new attempt with an identity-disjoint credited set, counted separately
and marginally by
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The bound therefore extends to loose-bar deployments per entry; only the
decisiveness clauses (mutual exclusivity, tally-deadlock-freeness) are
specific to the defaults.

###### Remark S5.15 (Single-parameter reading).

Every appearance of a single $`q`$ elsewhere in this document
(Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
hypothesis $`q=1`$; the corridor row $`q+p_{b}>1`$;
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the composed summary of
§[S7.5](#A7.SS5 "S7.5 Summary of composed guarantees ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the correlated rate $`q_{c}`$ of
[S13](#Thmobjx13 "Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is read as $`q:=\min(q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}})`$: the bounds of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are monotone in each parameter, so the single-$`q`$ forms are the
special case $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}=q_{\mathrm{pan}}=q`$ and remain valid
verbatim. $`q=1`$ means both acts are perfect; $`q\to 0`$
([S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is the regime where the smaller of the two vanishes.

###### Remark S5.16 (Itemwise reading; heterogeneous item difficulty).

Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is stated and proved per promotion attempt
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
nothing in its trials couples distinct items, so its hypotheses and
bound are _itemwise_ — for each poisoned item $`v`$, the bound holds
with $`v`$’s own weakest-target rates
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}(v),q_{\mathrm{pan}}(v)`$, and it is monotone in each.
Heterogeneous item difficulty is therefore inside the model,
transparently: easily recognized poison contributes a negligible term;
near-unrecognizable poison ($`q_{\mathrm{pre}}(v)\to 0`$) degrades its
own term toward the disclosed residual
[S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
leaving every other item’s bound untouched. The per-anchor-epoch union
bound of
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds in the same itemwise form,
$`\sum_{e}\big[(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}(v_{e}))^{N-f}+e^{-2\delta(v_{e})^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}\big]`$
(terms with $`\delta(v_{e})\leq 0`$ read as the exact binomial tail),
the single-$`q`$ display being the uniform special case; a
deployment-level constant is thus dominated by the hardest items the
adversary can mint — exactly the calibration duty of
[S1](#Thmobjx1 "Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
No parametric ability-or-difficulty model (jury, psychometric, or
crowdsourcing) is assumed: the weakest-target conditional floor subsumes
any such structure, at the price that the floor, not the average, is the
deployed constant
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Remark S5.17 (The certified per-attempt ceiling $`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$).

Write

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
B_{\mathrm{att}}\;:=\;(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{N-f}\;+\;\mathbb{P}\!\big[\mathrm{Bin}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}},\,1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})\geq m-f_{\mathrm{s}}\big]
``` |  |

for the right-hand side of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
bound in its exact binomial form, and call its two summands the
*ordinary term* and the *panel term*. The word *certified* names this
analytic bound and is unrelated to the promotion certificates of
Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which are log objects. Three properties are used throughout the
empirical evaluation: the first two are immediate from the display, the
third from the theorem’s statement.

The panel term is a *floor*: at fixed panel geometry
$`(k,m,f_{\mathrm{s}})`$ and fixed $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ it does not
contain $`N`$, so raising the endorsement quorum shrinks only the
ordinary term and $`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$ can never fall below it — panel
geometry, not quorum, is the binding deployment parameter, which is the
frontier
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
reads against and which the corridor of
§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
moves only by scheduling $`k`$ itself. The two terms fall in *different*
protocol constants and must be pushed down independently: the ordinary
term geometrically in $`N-f`$, the panel term as a binomial tail in
$`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ whose Hoeffding relaxation
$`e^{-2\delta^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}`$ is exponential in that constant.
And $`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$ is per promotion attempt
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and reach-free
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
deployment-wide exposure is obtained by summing over anchored attempts
and byte-distinct variants, through the union, expectation and
deterministic-cap forms of
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the lifetime ceiling of
Remark [S5.29](#A5.Thmtheorem29 "Remark S5.29 (Lifetime exposure under permanent freshness). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
never by reading the per-attempt figure as a per-epoch one.

*Reporting discipline.* Any numerical value quoted for
$`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$ is the exact binomial tail above, never the
Hoeffding relaxation that
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
displays alongside it. The two differ materially, and by different
factors on the two sides of the design: at $`k=31`$, $`m=20`$,
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}=1`$ with $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}=0.6`$ the relaxation is
$`3.81\times 10^{-2}`$ against an exact panel term of
$`8.30\times 10^{-3}`$, a factor of about $`4.6`$; on the benign side of
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
at $`p_{b}=0.9`$ and the same $`\delta`$, the numerically identical
relaxation stands against an exact wrongful-eviction tail of
$`8.91\times 10^{-5}`$, a factor of about $`430`$. A reader recomputing
either relaxation from a quoted exact value will therefore not reproduce
it, and — because the two relaxations coincide numerically while their
exact counterparts differ by two orders of magnitude — the two slacks
must never be interchanged.

###### Proof of Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

Fix the attempt and condition on the $`\sigma`$-algebra through and
including its anchor atom
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The behavioural bounds of hypothesis (c) are asserted uniformly over
histories, so the argument restarts after any fixed anchor-inclusive
history; every trial charged below occurs strictly after the anchor, and
each trial’s own conditioning $`\sigma`$-algebra
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
refines the anchor-inclusive one. Partition by whether an effective
qualifying rejection was logged after the anchor and before the
attempt’s finalisation.

Throughout, the bytes’ promotion status at every tool is constant within
the attempt: promotion occurs only at a finalisation, which ends the
attempt, and demotion by eviction ends the presence
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)),
so whether the bytes hold live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status at any tool is
decided at the anchor. Suppose first that they do not — the case of
every attempt preceding the bytes’ first promotion, hence of every
attempt the ever-promoted events of
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
require; the complementary case is scoped at the close of the proof.
Then no suspension can arise within the attempt (suspension presupposes
promoted bytes,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),
every qualifying rejection on the bytes within it is dispute-initiating
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(ii)),
and every non-freeze piece of the attempt is an entry window or a
candidate-dormancy interval (presence taxonomy,
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
every unfrozen header within the attempt is an *unfrozen candidate
context* in the sense of hypothesis (c).

*(a) Promotion with no qualifying rejection.* By
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v),
an honest *authority-active* identity’s rejecting gate decision on an
unfrozen candidate takes protocol effect, so the case-(a) event entails
that no honest authority-active inspection of the item ended in an
effective qualifying rejection before the attempt’s finalisation.
Promotion at the finalisation requires $`N`$ credited accepting
endorsements at the finalising entry (in-window, interval-banked,
boundary-banked, or vindication-credited,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
of which at least $`N-f`$ come from honest identities; each is a
distinct honest identity’s fresh, authority-active, non-covered decision
on the bytes
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
and each is logged strictly after the attempt’s anchor and before its
finalisation
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Index the trials by log order within the attempt: let $`O_{i}`$ be the
event that an $`i`$-th protocol-bearing decision at a non-covered,
non-cache gate on the item, by an honest, fresh, authority-active
identity, is logged after the attempt’s anchor and before the attempt
ends, at an unfrozen header — by the opening reduction, an unfrozen
candidate context in the sense of hypothesis (c). $`O_{i}`$ is
measurable at that record’s header atom
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
attempt membership is decided by the anchor, a past log event, and
freshness, coverage, authority, and frozen status are deterministic
predicates of the prior log
(Definitions [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(ii))
— no trial’s occurrence depends on the attempt’s future. Because no
event interleaves between a position’s rendering and header atoms
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the status at the header is the status under which hypothesis (c)’s
disposition-level bound is read. Let $`Z_{i}`$ indicate that the trial’s
content is an effective qualifying rejection. Hypothesis (c)
lower-bounds by $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ the disposition-level probability
of such a rejection at the trial’s rendering atom, on all of $`O_{i}`$
and irrespective of whether case (a) occurs — the class is confined to
exactly the unfrozen candidate contexts over which $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$
is quantified; conditioning on a recorded decision only raises the bound
(Lemma [S8.1](#A8.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S8.1 (Decision-conditioned content bounds). ‣ Dispositions. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
Hence $`\mathbb{P}[Z_{i}=1\mid\mathcal{G}_{i}]\geq q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ on
$`O_{i}`$ at the header-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebras of the
conditioning convention
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
each of which refines the anchor $`\sigma`$-algebra, so
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
applies under the anchor-conditional measure directly.

Only now is the case-(a) event used. On it, no effective qualifying
rejection is logged after the anchor and before the attempt’s
finalisation; since no dispute or review is open at the anchor
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and every freeze arising within the attempt presupposes such a
rejection, every trial of the class preceding the finalisation occurs at
an unfrozen header, and the $`N-f`$ honest credited endorsements —
in-window, interval-banked in a candidate-dormancy interval, or
boundary-banked, by the opening reduction; a vindication-credited
endorsement presupposes a panel, hence a case-(b) run — are all logged
at trials of the class, each necessarily non-cache (cache acceptances
are never logged, hence never credited,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
The case-(a) success event is therefore contained in
$`O_{N-f}\cap\{Z_{1}=\cdots=Z_{N-f}=0\}`$: at least $`N-f`$ trials of
the class are logged before the finalisation, so the first $`N-f`$
trials in log order all precede it, and each has $`Z_{i}=0`$, an
effective qualifying rejection before finalisation being a case-(b) run.
The joint all-zeros bound of
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
in the $`\sigma`$-algebra form of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
gives
$`\mathbb{P}[\text{case (a)}\mid\text{anchor}]\leq(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{N-f}`$.
Additional reach creates both rejection opportunities and possible
weight-bearing acceptances
([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
no pathwise monotonicity in reach is claimed. What the bound uses is
only the $`N-f`$ honest fresh authority-active trials promotion itself
requires, so the stated bound is unchanged at every reach
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

*(b) Promotion after a qualifying rejection.* The byte-level freeze then
blocks every tool’s pipeline until an accepting panel resolution
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)–(iv),(vi)),
so the case-(b) success event is contained in the accepting outcome
(vindication, or reinstatement under
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi))
of the first panel instance opened within the attempt — an ordinary
dispute panel or a fast-track suspension review, with the same
$`k,m,m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ parameters and bars; that panel instance opens,
and casts all its verdicts, after the attempt’s anchor
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so the argument below runs under the anchor-conditional measure
verbatim: the accepting-verdict count must reach $`m`$. Suppose the
adversary casts $`a\leq f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ accepting verdicts (at most one
per identity for the entire life of the panel instance
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
read over the instance;
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),(vi)),
across any number of epoch boundaries, by
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
seat floor and pool caps per
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii);
abandonment casts none). An accepting resolution then requires $`m-a`$
honest accepting verdicts; with the default bars, at most $`k`$ verdicts
are cast before a bar is reached
(Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so at most $`k-a`$ are honest. Each honest verdict is a recorded
decision at a fresh inspection. By the atomic decomposition of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the event that an $`i`$-th honest verdict is cast is measurable at that
verdict’s header atom, strictly before its content atom, and honest
verdicts are log-ordered with every earlier verdict’s content preceding
every later verdict’s header. By hypothesis (c), each honest verdict
rejects with conditional probability at least $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ at
its header-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebra
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
equivalently, its conditional accept probability there is at most
$`1-q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ (a cast verdict’s content is binary). Apply
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
in the $`\sigma`$-algebra form of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
at those $`\sigma`$-algebras, to the accept indicators $`Z_{i}`$ of the
honest verdicts: there are i.i.d.
$`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})`$ majorants
$`Y_{1},\dots,Y_{k}`$ with $`Z_{i}\leq Y_{i}`$ pointwise, unrealised
verdicts contributing zero, so the early decisive truncation of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
removes only nonnegative terms
(Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
On the case-(b) event,
$`m-a\leq\sum_{i\leq k-a}Z_{i}\leq\sum_{i\leq k-a}Y_{i}\leq\sum_{i\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Y_{i}+(f_{\mathrm{s}}-a)`$,
whence $`\sum_{i\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Y_{i}\geq m-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$: the
case $`a=f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ dominates, uniformly in $`a`$, and
$`\sum_{i\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Y_{i}\sim\mathrm{Bin}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}},1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})`$.
Hoeffding’s inequality
(Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
at the margin $`\delta`$ gives the second term. The events are disjoint;
sum.

*Reach-freeness.* The bound of case (a) is independent of reach: it
counts only the $`N-f`$ honest fresh decisions promotion itself
requires, however many further inspections occur; in case (b), $`k`$ and
$`m`$ are protocol constants, viewers whose decisions are not verdicts
do not vote, and logged-repeat viewers cannot vote at all
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
An expired dispute retires the item unpromoted
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
republication is a fresh submission whose endorsement set is
identity-disjoint from all prior sets
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
counted separately and marginally
(Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The case-(b) bound holds regardless of who filed the rejection, so
self-dispute gains nothing
([S2](#Thmobjx2 "Analysis S2 (Self-dispute). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Finally, the adversary’s choice whether to open an entry after
favourable banked outcomes is a choice among attempts already counted:
an attempt whose intervals bank decisions is an attempt whether or not
the entry opens, and an unopened attempt succeeds with probability zero
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

*Attempts anchored with live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status.* For an attempt at
whose anchor the bytes hold live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status at some tool —
possible only after a prior successful attempt of the same bytes, itself
bounded marginally at its own anchor — the inter-window spans are stable
promoted intervals, first decisions banked there are creditable
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and a fresh inspector’s rejection there is a post-promotion rejection
routed to
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)
rather than a dispute initiation. The two-case argument applies to such
attempts under a correspondingly extended reading of hypothesis (c):
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ quantified over the attempt’s unfrozen contexts
*including* its stable promoted intervals, with the effective qualifying
rejection there being the review-opening post-promotion rejection of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)
within its per-epoch review cap — an extension a deployment must
calibrate separately, disclosed here (cf.
[S4](#Thmobjx4 "Analysis S4 (Tool-targeted poison). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The event that any byte string is ever promoted *at all* is a union of
first-promotion events, whose attempts are anchored $`\mathsf{CC}`$-free
and need no extension. ∎

###### Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost).

The authority gate of
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
restores the quantifier compatibility that deterministic silencing would
otherwise break: without it, an adversary steering presentations toward
identities whose rejection rights are suspended, ceiling-capped, or
slot-exhausted would face inspectors whose effective rejection
probability is *zero* while their acceptances still carried full
promotion weight, and no $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}>0`$ could satisfy
hypothesis (c) uniformly over targetable cohorts. With the gate, the two
capacities are coupled at one deterministic log predicate: a silenced
identity can neither reject with effect nor accept with weight, so
targeting it gains the adversary nothing. The split is exact: verdict
*capacity* is never authority-gated
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(a),(e))
— an authority-inactive juror’s accepting verdict counts toward the
$`m`$-bar like any other, keeping the panel arithmetic of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
calibration-independent — while promotion *crediting* always is
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)):
the same verdict contributes weight only if its caster held authority at
decision time, in-entry, banked, and vindication-credited cases alike.
Honest cost is negligible: an honest identity is authority-inactive only
in the rare calibrated states of
[Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and its acceptance in that state still buys its personal $`\mathsf{C}`$
copy —
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected, the cap counting required confirmations, never credits.
Safety is monotone: authority-gating removes acceptances from the
promotion count and removes nothing from the rejection side (rejections
by inactive identities remain advisory flags or corroboration exactly as
before, and verdict-eligible rejections are cast regardless of
accountability state,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(e));
Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected (its counting is adversarial-weight only),
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ needs no gating (verdicts are never silenced,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(a),(e)),
and verdict eligibility, hence
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
is untouched. One availability-side consequence is disclosed: an
adversary who engineers charges against honest identities
([S15](#Thmobjx15 "Analysis S15 (Accountability mis-calibration). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
now also delays their *crediting* capacity, slowing benign promotion —
an exposure of the same character, availability-only, bounded by the
same calibration margins
([Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and priced inside $`\varepsilon(M)`$ where it matters
([A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
heuristic sufficiency).

###### Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter $`q`$).

$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ is the probability that an honest inspector,
presented the item at their own confirmation gate, detects the poison
*and records a rejecting decision that takes protocol effect*
(quantified over unfrozen candidate contexts,
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c));
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is the probability that an honest *eligible
juror’s* cast verdict rejects it. The split matters for calibration: the
two acts have different filters (seat weight, pool caps, and verdict
capacity apply only to jurors) and different honest baselines, so their
log validation is stratified separately
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
a deployment estimating one number reads it as
$`q:=\min(q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}})`$, under which every bound
of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds with $`q`$ in both roles
([Remark S5.15](#A5.Thmtheorem15 "Remark S5.15 (Single-parameter reading). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Both parameters are *uniform, weakest-target, conditional* lower bounds
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
conditional on all prior logged atoms and the demand factor): because
the adversary chooses whom to present the item to, each is the catch
rate of the most fallible honest cohort the adversary can reach, never a
population average, and aggregate log rates do not directly estimate
them
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Because a gate rejection is automatically qualifying
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
detection and reporting are a single act: there is no separate filing
step whose friction could decouple them. Abstention (a user who suspects
the item and abandons the dialog) records nothing and is counted as a
miss inside $`1-q`$. An honest identity whose rejection rights are
suspended, whose $`r_{\max}`$ slots are transiently full, whose
per-epoch ceiling $`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$ is reached, or whose single
per-item initiation is spent is *authority-inactive*: its inspections
are excluded trials, not silenced misses — its acceptance carries no
promotion weight and its rejection no initiation
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— and such states are rare for honest identities (honest charges accrue
at rate at most $`1-p_{b}`$ per benign fresh inspection, both the rate
trigger and the ceiling calibrated strictly above that baseline,
[Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
slots free on resolution or expiry,
Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the ceiling and the per-item allowance renew each epoch). Covered gates
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
are not silenced misses but *excluded trials*: both branches are
protocol-inert, so they belong to no trial class of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the identity’s inspection of the bytes, where one is counted at all,
is the earlier decision that created its coverage; so, symmetrically,
are authority-inactive inspections
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
and so are cache gates on the accepting side (accept-inert,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)),
whose rejections take effect as dispute initiations or corroborations
but never as verdicts
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
Freshness being shared-presence-scoped
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the fresh class can include identities with a prior *unlogged* personal
decision on the bytes (before first publication, or across a retirement
gap); $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ and $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ are lower bounds
over this log-defined class, so a previously fooled but log-fresh
inspector is inside the class the parameters must cover — one more
reason the bounds are weakest-target infima, never averages, and one the
validation strata of
[N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
must include (prior-exposure stratification). Case (a) of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
needs only $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}>0`$: one honest *effective qualifying
rejection* — a rejecting decision at a protocol-bearing gate by an
identity currently holding dispute-initiation authority
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v))
— denies the ordinary path, a one-sided disjunction, not a vote;
coverage-silenced and authority-inactive detections are excluded trials
rather than misses
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)),
the corresponding acceptances carrying no weight; post-promotion
rejections beyond the review cap of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)
concern the suspended state only and touch no case-(a) trial. The panel
is a bounded jury: joint safety and a low wrongful-eviction bound need
the better-than-chance condition $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}+p_{b}>1`$; safety
alone can be forced for any $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}>0`$ by raising $`m`$
toward $`k`$, at the price of a weaker wrongful-eviction bound. The
regime $`q\to 0`$ is the disclosed limitation
[S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The exponents $`N-f`$ and $`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are protocol constants;
the bases $`1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$, $`1-q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ are behavioural
parameters of the targeted population. Because panel verdicts are never
penalised and first charges are free each epoch
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)),
the protocol attaches no penalty to a first good-faith rejection, so it
does not disincentivise the gate behaviour that generates
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$. Finally, $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ and
$`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ condition on the same human act consistently:
an abstaining demander is a miss inside $`1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ *and* a
non-verdict inside $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$; high abstention degrades
resolution speed, never the validity of the safety parameter.

###### Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound).

Adopt the default bars, and suppose each honest juror’s fresh inspection
of a benign item
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
ends in an accepting decision with conditional probability at least
$`p_{b}`$ given all prior protocol events, read per the conditioning
convention of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
If $`\delta_{b}:=p_{b}-\frac{m}{k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}>0`$ (the
*wrongful-eviction margin*), then, uniformly over adversary strategies,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{wrongful eviction}]\ \leq\ e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}.
``` |  |

Moreover both margins ($`\delta>0`$ and $`\delta_{b}>0`$) are
simultaneously achievable by an integer $`m`$ whenever
$`(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})(q+p_{b}-1)>f_{\mathrm{s}}+1`$; in particular,
whenever inspectors discriminate better than chance ($`q+p_{b}>1`$) and
$`k`$ is large enough.

###### Proof.

Under the default bars, a resolved panel’s outcome is eviction or
vindication, exclusively
(Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)),
and eviction requires $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k+1-m`$ rejecting verdicts.
Suppose the adversary casts $`a\leq f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ verdicts (at most
one per identity for the dispute’s entire life,
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
at most $`a`$ of them reject, so eviction requires at least
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-a`$ honest rejecting verdicts, while honest verdicts
number at most $`k-a`$. For an honest verdict, writing
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}},p_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ for its conditional accept/reject
disposition probabilities at its rendering atom, with
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}\geq p_{b}`$ and
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1`$
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
Lemma [S8.1](#A8.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S8.1 (Decision-conditioned content bounds). ‣ Dispositions. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
bounds the conditional rejection probability at the verdict’s
header-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebra by $`1-p_{b}`$; these
$`\sigma`$-algebras satisfy the occurrence and measurability conditions
of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
exactly as in
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b).
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
in that form, applied to the rejection indicators $`Z_{i}`$, gives
i.i.d. $`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1-p_{b})`$ majorants $`Y_{i}`$ with
$`Z_{i}\leq Y_{i}`$ pointwise, unrealised verdicts contributing zero. On
the wrongful-eviction event,
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-a\leq\sum_{i\leq k-a}Z_{i}\leq\sum_{i\leq k-a}Y_{i}\leq\sum_{i\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Y_{i}+(f_{\mathrm{s}}-a)`$,
whence
````
