````math
$`\sum_{i\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Y_{i}\geq m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$,
uniformly in $`a`$. Since
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}=(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})-(m-1)=\big((1-p_{b})+\delta_{b}^{\prime}\big)(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$
with
$`\delta_{b}^{\prime}:=p_{b}-\tfrac{m-1}{k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}\geq\delta_{b}>0`$,
Hoeffding’s inequality
(Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
bounds the event by
$`e^{-2\delta_{b}^{\prime 2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}\leq e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}`$.
Simultaneity: an integer $`m`$ lying strictly between
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}+(1-q)(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$ and
$`p_{b}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$ exists whenever the gap between those
quantities exceeds one, i.e. whenever
$`(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})(p_{b}+q-1)>f_{\mathrm{s}}+1`$. ∎

###### Remark S5.21 (Resolution as a demand-side event).

Resolution is a demand-side property: the demand-paced panel has no
deadline, $`g_{k}(M)`$ may grow arbitrarily slowly, and an item without
demand expires with no protocol consequence, for which liveness (in the
classical, eventual-success sense) is vacuous
([Remark S5.26](#A5.Thmtheorem26 "Remark S5.26 (Roles of 𝑇_win, 𝑇_pan, 𝑇_exp; the demand-paced design). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
bound wrongful eviction unconditionally, asserting no probability for
resolution itself. As a corollary reading: conditional on resolution,
vindication has probability at least
$`1-e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}/\mathbb{P}[\text{resolution}]`$.

###### Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items).

Under
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),(vii):

1.  (i)
    the adversary’s panel verdicts alone can never trigger a publisher
    penalty against any publisher, since eviction requires
    $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ rejecting verdicts;
2.  (ii)
    with the default bars and wrongful-eviction margin $`\delta_{b}>0`$,
    write $`p^{*}:=e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}`$; each panel
    on a benign item wrongfully evicts (penalising the publisher) with
    probability at most $`p^{*}`$ conditionally on all prior protocol
    events
    (Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    whose hypothesis is conditional). Three consequences, in decreasing
    strength of hypothesis. *(Fixed instances.)* For any $`r`$ dispute
    instances on benign items of the same publisher, *predictably
    specified*: membership of an instance in the family is determined no
    later than that instance’s opening atom, measurably in the
    opening-inclusive log history and before any verdict content of that
    instance (any advance deterministic choice included); a family
    selected retrospectively from panel outcomes is not a fixed-instance
    family — it is covered by the capped tier where the deterministic
    cap $`L\leq\bar{\ell}`$ is available, and otherwise only by the
    linear random-count tier. For such a family, the probability that
    all $`r`$ instances end in wrongful eviction is at most
    $`(p^{*})^{\,r}`$, uniformly over adversary strategies and over any
    dependence among the panels. *(Random count, linear.)* With $`L`$
    the number of dispute instances opened on the publisher’s benign
    items in the epoch, indexing panel trials at their *opening* events
    (an instance unresolved at the epoch horizon evicts nobody and
    carries indicator zero), the expected number of wrongful evictions
    is at most $`p^{*}\,\mathbb{E}[L]`$, whence
    $`\mathbb{P}[\text{at least }r\text{ wrongful evictions}]\leq p^{*}\mathbb{E}[L]/r`$
    (Markov); $`\mathbb{E}[L]`$ is bounded by the dispute ledger
    (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    $`\bar{D}_{v}`$) summed over the publisher’s items, and, for
    fast-track reviews, deterministically by $`E_{\max}`$ per item per
    epoch
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)).
    No $`r`$-fold exponent is claimed at this generality. *(Random
    count, capped.)* If the deployment enforces a deterministic
    per-epoch cap $`L\leq\bar{\ell}`$ on dispute instances against one
    publisher’s items, then
    $`\mathbb{P}[\text{at least }r\text{ wrongful evictions}]\leq\binom{\bar{\ell}}{r}(p^{*})^{\,r}`$,
    decaying geometrically in $`r`$ whenever
    $`2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})>\ln\bar{\ell}`$;
3.  (iii)
    every eviction of an *adversary-published* poisoned item consumes
    the adversary’s allowance and, on repetition within an epoch, its
    submission rights and attestation weight; eviction of poison
    published by an honest-but-deceived identity penalises *that*
    publisher, by design
    ([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
4.  (iv)
    no publisher penalty ever touches a local store
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Dispute expiry
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
is neither an eviction nor a vindication and triggers no penalty on
either side. Protection is claimed for publishers of *benign* items: an
honest-but-deceived publisher of attacker-crafted content is penalised
on eviction, by design
([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof.

(i) Eviction requires at least $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ rejecting verdicts
with $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$; by
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the adversary casts at most $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ verdicts on the dispute
over its entire life, however many epoch boundaries it spans, so at
least one honest panelist must reject; with no honest rejections there
is no eviction and hence no penalty. (ii) Under the default bars a
resolved panel’s outcome is eviction or vindication, exclusively
(Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)),
so the penalising event is exactly wrongful eviction, bounded per panel
by
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
For the fixed-instance product bound, the $`r`$ predictably specified
instances are indexed in opening order, and their honest verdicts
jointly in log order of their header atoms; a verdict’s instance
membership and within-instance honest ordinal are thereby determined at
its header atom, $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurably, as
Lemma [S8.7](#A8.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S8.7 (Predictable cell allocation). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
requires
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The benign-item hypothesis of
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
bounds each honest verdict’s conditional rejection probability by
$`1-p_{b}`$ at its header-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebra — including the
outcomes of earlier-resolved panels — so
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
in the $`\sigma`$-algebra form of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
applied once to the joint sequence, supplies coupling variables with
$`Z_{i}\leq Y_{i}`$ pointwise on realised verdicts. Allocate cells:
assign the $`j`$-th specified instance’s honest verdicts, in log order,
to cells $`(j,1),\dots,(j,k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$, discarding any beyond the
$`(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$-th; a verdict’s cell is determined at its header
atom (its dispute instance and within-instance honest ordinal are log
facts prior to its content), hence $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurably and
injectively, the instances’ index sets disjoint — not necessarily
contiguous, which the argument never needs. By
Lemma [S8.7](#A8.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S8.7 (Predictable cell allocation). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the cell array $`(X_{j,\ell})_{j\leq r,\,\ell\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}`$
(coupling variables on filled cells, fresh independent uniforms on
never-filled cells) is i.i.d. $`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1-p_{b})`$. On the
all-$`r`$-evict event, instance $`j`$ resolves in eviction: with
$`a_{j}\leq f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ adversarial verdicts
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
honest verdicts number $`h_{j}\leq k-a_{j}`$, of which at least
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-a_{j}`$ reject. If $`h_{j}\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$,
every honest verdict sits among the first $`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ cells,
which then contain at least
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-a_{j}\geq m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$
rejections; otherwise at most
$`h_{j}-(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})\leq f_{\mathrm{s}}-a_{j}`$ of the rejecting
ones lie beyond cell position $`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$, and the first
$`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ honest verdicts contain at least
$`(m_{\mathrm{rej}}-a_{j})-(f_{\mathrm{s}}-a_{j})=m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$
rejections. In either case
$`\sum_{\ell\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}X_{j,\ell}\ \geq\ \sum_{\ell\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}Z_{(j,\ell)}\ \geq\ m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$,
never-filled cells contributing nonnegatively, uniformly in $`a_{j}`$.
The all-$`r`$-evict event is therefore contained in
$`\bigcap_{j\leq r}\big\{\sum_{\ell\leq k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}X_{j,\ell}\geq m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}\big\}`$;
the array being i.i.d. with the rows indexed by disjoint cell sets, the
intersection’s probability is the product of $`r`$ identical binomial
tails, each at most $`p^{*}`$ by the margin computation of
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
($`m_{\mathrm{rej}}-f_{\mathrm{s}}=\big((1-p_{b})+\delta_{b}^{\prime}\big)(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})`$,
$`\delta_{b}^{\prime}\geq\delta_{b}`$, Hoeffding via
Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
giving $`(p^{*})^{\,r}`$. For the linear tier, let $`W_{j}`$ indicate
wrongful eviction of the $`j`$-th instance opened in the epoch, indexed
at its opening event, with $`W_{j}=0`$ for instances unresolved at the
horizon; $`\mathbb{P}[W_{j}=1\mid\text{prior atoms}]\leq p^{*}`$ by
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(its hypothesis conditions on all prior protocol events, the opening
atom included), so the delayed-marks lemma
(Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with $`\mathcal{G}_{j}`$ generated by all atoms up to the $`j`$-th
opening event and $`W_{j}`$ resolved only at that instance’s resolution,
possibly after later openings) gives
$`\mathbb{E}[\sum_{j}W_{j}]\leq p^{*}\,\mathbb{E}[L]`$ and Markov the
tail. For the capped tier, fix any set of $`r`$ indices
$`j_{1}<\dots<j_{r}\leq\bar{\ell}`$; the fixed-instance argument above,
applied to the $`j_{1}`$-th, …, $`j_{r}`$-th instances opened in the
epoch (the instances being determined by their opening order, and their
honest verdicts jointly log-ordered), bounds the probability that all
$`r`$ resolve in eviction by $`(p^{*})^{\,r}`$. At least $`r`$ wrongful
evictions entails that some such index set evicts wholly; the union
bound over the $`\binom{\bar{\ell}}{r}`$ index sets gives the claim. No
direct stochastic domination of delayed, opening-indexed eviction
indicators is asserted. The same-bytes sharpening is
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
a cast verdict is a logged decision on the bytes, so its caster is
ineligible for any later dispute instance on the same bytes under
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(b).
(iii) By construction of clause (vii), read per publisher. (iv) Clause
(vii) modifies submission rights and attestation weight, which are
shared-tier attributes;
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
covers the rest. The expiry clause is
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
verbatim. ∎

###### Remark S5.23 (Reading of Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).

The escalating penalties of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii),
requiring $`r\geq 2`$ wrongful evictions within one epoch, are
exponentially rare per specified pair of instances, bounded in
expectation in general, and carry the $`r`$-fold exponent exactly where
a deterministic instance cap holds (capped tier). For repeated panels on
the *same* byte string the bounds sharpen: every verdict is a logged
decision consuming shared-presence freshness
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(b)–(c)),
so each identity casts at most one verdict across all of the bytes’
panels ever; in particular the adversary’s $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$
seat-eligible identities are spent once across those panels, not once
per panel.

###### Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service).

1.  (i)
    At any time, at most $`f\cdot r_{\max}`$ items are held in Disputed
    by adversarial rejections. Moreover, adversarial dispute-initiations
    against any single item number at most $`f`$ per epoch
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
    single-initiation clause), independently of $`r_{\max}`$.
2.  (ii)
    *(Demand-paced resolution.)* Unconditionally, with no behavioural
    assumption (persistence exceptions per
    [INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    a freeze costs each affected demander at most one accepting
    confirmation per demanded pair, and only if the demander holds no
    local in-scope copy: exactly the required confirmation any demander
    of an unpromoted pair owes regardless
    (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
    A demander who rejects or abandons incurs inspection effort, a
    distinct resource disclosed in
    [N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    not bounded by the cap. A dispute therefore suspends only the
    community amortisation for its demanders and never pushes anyone
    above the single-user cap, however long the freeze lasts. Under
    [A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    the number so affected is additionally bounded: the demanders
    affected while the dispute is unresolved number at most $`\kappa`$
    in expectation, with exponential tail
    (Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    independent of the item’s popularity and of the freeze’s wall-clock
    duration. A dispute on an undemanded item affects no user and
    expires within $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$ of its last demand
    (Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    (Wide pre-exposure:
    Remark [S5.25](#A5.Thmtheorem25 "Remark S5.25 (Wide pre-exposure). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    [S6](#Thmobjx6 "Analysis S6 (Juror exhaustion by wide pre-exposure). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
3.  (iii)
    *No panel-lapse exploitation; slot economics.* There is no panel
    lapse, hence no forced re-entry: an unresolved dispute never drains
    the owner’s submission budget. A rejection slot stays occupied until
    resolution or expiry: against demanded items, disputes resolve at
    demand rate into the accountability schedule; against undemanded
    items, the slot pins only an undemanded item and frees at expiry.
    (Remark [S5.26](#A5.Thmtheorem26 "Remark S5.26 (Roles of 𝑇_win, 𝑇_pan, 𝑇_exp; the demand-paced design). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    [S5](#Thmobjx5 "Analysis S5 (Panel-lapse exploitation and slot economics). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
4.  (iv)
    A sustained wrongful-rejection campaign alters no local store
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and costs each user at most the single-user floor
    (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    beyond the $`f`$ free first charges each epoch, it expends the
    adversary’s rejection rights at an escalating rate
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)).
    Its throughput is bounded by three deterministic caps, each in its
    own currency: *charged* dispute-initiations (those eventually
    contradicted by vindication) number at most $`c_{\mathrm{acc}}f`$
    per epoch
    (Lemma [S5.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma S5.4 (Deterministic accountability bound). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    *concurrent* open rejections number at most $`fr_{\max}`$ at any
    moment, and freezes against any single item at most $`f`$ per epoch
    (clause (i), single initiation); and uncharged *terminal* disputes
    (ending in eviction or expiry) number at most $`E_{\max}`$ per
    shared-tier presence per item per epoch
    (Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
    each retiring that presence. No single constant bounds all wrongful
    rejections across all items — a slot freed by expiry may be re-used
    against another item — and what each re-use buys is one freeze,
    resolved or expired at that item’s own demand clock, within the
    single-user cap. The allowances renew at epoch boundaries
    ([N14](#Thmnotex14 "Note N14 (Availability degrades gracefully, never destructively). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof.

(i) Each adversarial identity holds at most $`r_{\max}`$ open rejections
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
and the adversary controls at most $`f`$ identities. The per-item clause
caps each identity at one initiation per item per epoch. (ii) The harm
of a freeze is exactly the amortisation it suspends: the demanders who
must confirm personally while the item is frozen; by
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)–(iv)
the eligible deciding demanders cast the verdicts and, with the default
bars, resolution occurs by the $`k`$-th verdict; each affected
demander’s accepting confirmation, where one occurs, is the one required
confirmation they would owe on any unpromoted pair, so the per-user
floor is untouched
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the in-expectation and tail bounds are
Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
an item with no new demand meets the expiry clause of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i).
(iii) By
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
the only re-entry paths are the optional neither-bar outcome and
post-expiry republication, both owner-initiated; slots free on
resolution or expiry
(Rules [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv), [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
(iv) Every dispute-initiating rejection contradicted by vindication
charges the rejecter’s schedule and ceiling
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v));
by
Lemma [S5.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma S5.4 (Deterministic accountability bound). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the adversary’s effective charged dispute-initiations are
deterministically at most $`c_{\mathrm{acc}}`$ per identity per epoch,
bounding per-epoch *charged-initiation* throughput at
$`c_{\mathrm{acc}}f`$ as a protocol fact; the concurrency,
single-initiation, and terminal-dispute caps are
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
and
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
verbatim. By
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
no local store is altered, and each user’s required cost remains at most
the single-user cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
∎

###### Remark S5.25 (Wide pre-exposure).

An item pre-exposed so widely that few verdict-eligible demanders remain
simply stalls *frozen*: the freeze blocks promotion at every tool for as
long as the panel is unresolved, and the demand-paced panel carries no
deadline an adversary could exploit
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)–(iii));
this is the deterministic failure mode of
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and its cost is availability, never safety. For a *poisoned* item the
stall is borne by the adversary’s own submission. A *benign* item can
also be stalled this way — by pre-exposure or pool-skewed demand, with
or without adversarial help — and then the availability cost falls on
its publisher and demanders; the harm is bounded exactly as for any
freeze: each demander pays at most one required confirmation per pair,
within the single-user cap
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
unconditional clause), the item remains personally usable through each
user’s own gate
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
local stores are untouched
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and an item whose demand lapses expires harmlessly
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
([S6](#Thmobjx6 "Analysis S6 (Juror exhaustion by wide pre-exposure). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

###### Remark S5.26 (Roles of $`T_{\mathrm{win}}`$, $`T_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$; the demand-paced design).

The window $`T_{\mathrm{win}}`$ forbids the promotion race: finalisation
occurs only at window end, so any qualifying rejection intervenes even
if $`N`$ acceptances arrive first: this is what makes the partition of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
well-defined; and each attempt’s identity-disjoint credited endorsement
set
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is what makes the per-attempt marginal bounds and their union valid
(Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
$`T_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ survives only as the clock of fast-track suspension
panels, whose log-fresh jurors are drawn from demanders during
suspension and prior adopters without a logged decision on the bytes
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi));
their supply is not guaranteed by construction — prior adopters with
logged decisions are ineligible — but is availability-side, exactly
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
province; the ordinary panel carries no global deadline; it is
demand-paced: verdicts accumulate at the item’s own demand rate, so
resolution time scales inversely with demand while the harm of the
freeze scales directly with it, and their product is bounded
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
A disputed item with too little fresh demand simply waits, exactly as it
would have waited for ordinary promotion; an item nobody demands expires
harmlessly within $`T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$. Zero-tolerance designs lack an
accountability clock entirely; the demand-paced panel provides one
wherever fresh demand exists. An evict-and-restart rule would instead
multiply per-item cost by the number of rejections; the panel’s
decisive, demand-paced resolution is what keeps the dispute load an
additive $`\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}N+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\bar{D}_{v}\kappa)`$
per demanded item, with $`\bar{D}_{v}`$ the expected dispute count of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
absorbed by the cross-term and shrinking-front-loading conditions of
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
([S5](#Thmobjx5 "Analysis S5 (Panel-lapse exploitation and slot economics). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability).

Promotion occurs only at an attempt’s finalisation
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and every attempt is counted at its *anchor* — a logged event preceding
every decision creditable to the attempt, hence a sound conditioning
point
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Under the default bars, the anchors lying in a given epoch are of
exactly two kinds, each bounded by the submission rate limit:
presence-creating submissions, and finalisation events, each of which
closes an entry opened by a same-epoch rate-limited (re-)submission
(windows are epoch-contained,
convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Hence the promotion attempts of adversary-published poisoned items
*anchored* in a given epoch number at most $`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$
(paraphrase variants and re-entries included). Each such attempt gathers
an identity-disjoint credited endorsement set
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and is bounded marginally by
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
at its own anchor (under its hypotheses); the union bound, valid under
arbitrary dependence across attempts, gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{any adversary-submitted poison promoted at an attempt
anchored in the epoch}]\\
\ \leq\ 2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}\,\Big((1-q)^{N-f}+e^{-2\delta^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}\Big).
``` |  |

(Attempts anchored while the bytes hold live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ status —
additional-tool promotions of already-promoted bytes — are covered under
the extended context reading at the close of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
proof; the event that any poison is ever promoted at all consumes only
$`\mathsf{CC}`$-free anchors.) Every promotion belongs to an attempt
anchored in some epoch, so summing over the anchor epochs $`1,\dots,E`$
*from deployment inception* bounds the probability that any
adversary-submitted poison is ever promoted within that horizon by
$`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}\,E\,\big((1-q)^{N-f}+e^{-2\delta^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}\big)`$.
For an interval not beginning at deployment inception, no bound
conditional on its realised carry-in pool is asserted — the set of
attempts still live at the interval’s start is itself outcome-selected,
for the reason of
Remark [S5.28](#A5.Thmtheorem28 "Remark S5.28 (Why attempts are keyed to anchor epochs, not finalisation epochs). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— and the valid statement is the anchor-epoch bound applied to all
anchor epochs from deployment inception through the interval’s end.
(Under the looser bars permitted by
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
neither-bar resolutions are additional anchors; the numeric count
$`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$ is asserted for the default bars, and
loose-bar deployments use the expectation form below, with the
anchored-attempt count enlarged accordingly; per-attempt coverage per
Remark [S5.14](#A5.Thmtheorem14 "Remark S5.14 (Scope of Theorem ). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)

Poisoned content published by an honest-but-deceived identity
([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is not counted by $`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$. Writing
$`S_{\mathrm{anc}}`$ for the (in general random) number of poisoned
promotion attempts anchored in the epoch, whatever their publishers:
indexing attempts at their anchor atoms and applying the delayed-marks
lemma
(Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
to the per-attempt success indicators — each bounded, conditionally on
the anchor-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebra of its anchor atom, by the
per-attempt marginal bound, and each resolved only at the attempt’s
finalisation, possibly after later attempts’ anchors, which
Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
permits —

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{any poison promoted at an attempt anchored in the epoch}]\\
\leq\mathbb{E}[S_{\mathrm{anc}}]\Big((1-q)^{N-f}+e^{-2\delta^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}\Big).
``` |  |

and a deployment enforcing a deterministic cap
$`S_{\mathrm{anc}}\leq\bar{S}`$ may substitute $`\bar{S}`$ for the
expectation. (No bound keyed to the attempts *finalising* in an epoch is
asserted: that family is outcome-selected,
Remark [S5.28](#A5.Thmtheorem28 "Remark S5.28 (Why attempts are keyed to anchor epochs, not finalisation epochs). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Nor is a bound conditional on a realised value of $`S_{\mathrm{anc}}`$
asserted: the attempt count may be adaptively determined by earlier
outcomes; the expectation and deterministic-cap forms are the valid
system-wide statements.) $`\mathbb{E}[S_{\mathrm{anc}}]`$ is not bounded
in terms of the adversary’s resources alone — it depends on how often
false endorsement
([A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and publication co-occur among honest identities — though the
per-identity rate limit yields the crude default-bar cap
$`S_{\mathrm{anc}}\leq 2M\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$ over $`M`$ eligible
identities, and each such item, on eviction, penalises its publisher
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii)),
economically suppressing repeat deception. Under permanent freshness,
the credited endorsement sets of all attempts of a given byte string are
identity-disjoint over the deployment’s *entire history*, not merely
within an epoch
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
consequently the number of attempts of the same bytes that can ever
gather $`N`$ credited endorsements is at most
$`\lfloor H_{\mathrm{acc}}/(N-f)\rfloor`$, where $`H_{\mathrm{acc}}`$ is
the total number of honest identities that ever accept those bytes at a
gate. Moreover, every eviction of a poisoned attempt triggers the
publisher-accountability consequences of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii)
(cool-down; on repetition within an epoch, suspension of submission
rights and attestation-weight reduction); the quantitative effect on
future submission capacity depends on the deployment’s escalation
schedule
(§[S4.2](#A4.SS2a "S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
required parameters) and is consumed by no proof, while a benign
publisher’s exposure to the same penalty is bounded by
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii).

###### Proof.

An attempt is counted at its anchor. Under the default bars every anchor
is a presence-creating submission or a finalisation
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
distinct attempts have distinct anchors; presence-creating submissions
of adversary-published items in the epoch number at most
$`f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and each finalisation in the epoch closes an entry whose opening
(re-)submission lies in the same epoch (windows are epoch-contained,
convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
so finalisation anchors also number at most $`f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$: at
most $`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$ anchored attempts. Union bound over these
attempts, each covered marginally by
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
at its anchor on its own credited set
(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
a union bound requires no independence across the events it covers. The
horizon form sums the per-epoch display over the anchor epochs of the
horizon, every promotion belonging to the attempt anchored in some such
epoch (from deployment inception; a general interval is covered by
summing from inception through its end, no carry-in-conditional bound
being asserted). The system-wide form is the delayed-marks lemma
(Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
applied to anchor-indexed success indicators. Its occurrence events lie
in the conditioning $`\sigma`$-algebras: take $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$
generated by all atoms up to and including the $`i`$-th anchor atom, so
that $`O_{i}`$ is $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurable; the per-attempt bound
of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is stated conditionally on exactly this anchor-inclusive
$`\sigma`$-algebra, so it bounds each mark conditionally on
$`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$, the mark resolving only at the attempt’s
finalisation, which
Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
permits; the deterministic-cap form substitutes $`\bar{S}`$. The
lifetime clause is immediate from identity-disjointness of credited
decisions across all attempts. The accountability clauses are
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii)
and
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)–(iii).
∎

###### Remark S5.28 (Why attempts are keyed to anchor epochs, not finalisation epochs).

An earlier version of
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
counted the attempts whose *finalisation* lies in the epoch. That
attribution is unsound, for the same optional-selection reason the
attempt anchor exists
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
commentary): banked decisions logged during dormancy are public log
events preceding the owner’s resubmission decision, so the set of
attempts finalising in a given epoch is outcome-selected — an adversary
maintaining many anchored dormant attempts on distinct byte strings and
resubmitting only those with favourable banked outcomes makes the
per-finalisation-epoch attempt count small while the epoch’s promotion
probability is governed by the whole maintained pool. Anchors, by
contrast, precede every decision creditable to their attempts, so the
anchored-in-epoch family is determined before any of the outcomes it is
charged with, and the delayed-marks lemma applies. The per-attempt bound
of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the lifetime ceiling of
Remark [S5.29](#A5.Thmtheorem29 "Remark S5.29 (Lifetime exposure under permanent freshness). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are unaffected: only the calendar attribution of attempts to epochs
changes.

###### Remark S5.29 (Lifetime exposure under permanent freshness).

The horizon union over anchor epochs in
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the lifetime ceiling, count anchored attempts — the lifetime
ceiling, threshold-reaching attempts — whose honest endorsers are never
re-used: every pipeline entry of a given byte string that reaches its
threshold consumes $`N-f`$ honest identities’ first-and-only *logged*
decisions on those bytes, so the adversary cannot re-use a previously
logged-deciding population, and
$`\lfloor H_{\mathrm{acc}}/(N-f)\rfloor`$ is a hard ceiling on the
number of *threshold-reaching* attempts of the same bytes over the
deployment’s lifetime, independent of the number of epochs. Unsuccessful
attempts — each gathering fewer than $`N-f`$ new honest credited
acceptances — and presentations yielding no logged acceptance are not
bounded by this ceiling; they are governed by the per-epoch rate limit
$`\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$ and the per-attempt marginal bound of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
each attempt consuming its own union-bound term. The ceiling is per
exact byte string
(convention ([C5](#A1.I2.i5 "Item C5 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))):
an adversary minting byte-distinct paraphrase variants holds a fresh
ceiling per variant, each consuming its own rate-limited submission and
union-bound term
([S1](#Thmobjx1 "Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the lifetime clause therefore hard-bounds *successful* re-entry of
*fixed* bytes, while variant families are governed by the per-epoch rate
and calibration clauses, not by this ceiling.

###### Remark S5.30 (Weighted form).

With endorsement weights, replace the exponent $`N-f`$ by
$`(W-W_{\mathrm{adv}})/w_{\max}`$. With seat weights in
$`[w_{\mathrm{seat}},w_{\max}]`$ and a vindication weight bar $`W_{m}`$,
honest accepting weight at least $`W_{m}-f_{\mathrm{s}}w_{\max}`$ is
required; seat weights are attestation-layer constants fixed at verdict
time, hence predictable in the sense of
Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
second clause, and Hoeffding for weighted sums
(Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
gives $`\exp(-2t^{2}/((k-f_{\mathrm{s}})w_{\max}^{2}))`$ with $`t`$ the
weight margin: constants change, exponents do not, and the bound remains
reach-free.

###### Remark S5.31 (Per-source-class thresholds).

Promotion thresholds may be set per *source* class of the underlying
content (authentication is not trust: a signed phishing message is still
an attack; so source identity only tunes the threshold, never bypasses
the quorum, and never widens a tool scope). All bounds hold with $`W`$,
$`N`$, $`m`$, $`k`$ read as the minimum over source classes;
Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
requires $`\min_{\mathrm{class}}W>W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$ and
$`\min_{\mathrm{class}}m>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$.

### Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget

###### Scope.

All results in this appendix count confirmations attached to *reusable
memory content*, per (value, tool) pair: a one-time personal cap of
private values, and the stream of shareable Confirmed items. Per-task
confirmations (for freshly composed sensitive arguments and for
crystallizing ephemeral task content) are common to every gated design,
scale with usage rather than population, and are orthogonal to the
amortisation analysed here. PerMIT’s distinction is layered. Pathwise —
independent of every federated and demand assumption, persistence
exceptions per
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— no user’s required cost exceeds once per (value, tool) pair, ever, and
the epoch’s expected shared required load never exceeds the standalone
single-user mass $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ — the cost of having no community
at all
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii));
this cap is the appendix’s firmest guarantee: pathwise, consuming no
federated or demand assumption (its expected clauses read the reference
model’s masses), subject only to the stated first-party persistence
exceptions. On top of it, the *ledger-charged* shared stream is at most
the front-loading multiple $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}`$ of the
standalone mass, independently of item popularity
(Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Remark [S6.11](#A6.Thmtheorem11 "Remark S6.11 (Reading of Theorem ). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and the *ledger residual* — demand arriving outside every charged piece,
in particular handle-expressed arrivals of already-certified bytes,
which gate by design
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
[S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— has its benign, assumption-conforming component vanish under the full
vanishing conditions of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii):
the coverage-and-representation assumption
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
together with the product-rate condition $`D_{0}(M)V(M)=o(M)`$,
$`\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$ (under
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
from $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$; $`d_{\mathrm{good}}`$ per
Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and bounded tool spread
([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
these conditions are sufficient, not necessary, and demand on poisoned
or assumption-violating pairs remains in $`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$
(Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Under the measured corridor of
§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— whose front-loading rows describe deployments whose time geometry
changes with scale, not consequences of population growth alone
(Remark [S6.12](#A6.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S6.12 (Operational reading of the shrinking-front-loading rows). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— both shared components vanish; where the corridor or
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
fails, the universal fallback applies to the *required* component: the
epoch’s expected shared required load remains at most the standalone
mass $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
the once-per-pair cap binding throughout. Voluntary invitation
confirmations remain governed by the ledger rows of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
rejection and attention effort is accounted separately in
[N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
No standalone-mass ceiling is claimed for those additional resources.
Headline readings of this appendix elsewhere in the paper must carry
these conditions: “shared verification load vanishes” is asserted only
under measured saturation, smoothness, coverage, juror-supply, and
bounded-mass hypotheses
([A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
never from population growth alone
(Remark [S6.12](#A6.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S6.12 (Operational reading of the shrinking-front-loading rows). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the firmest statements are the pathwise once-per-pair cap and the
reference-model standalone-mass ceiling
````
