````math
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

#### S6.1 Model

- •
  A population of $`M`$ users; a universe $`\mathcal{V}`$ of shareable
  Confirmed items. The accounting unit is the *(value, tool) pair* (the
  endorsement unit,
  §[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
  a user’s demand, required cost, and local coverage are all per pair.
  Personal and context-dependent values lie outside $`\mathcal{V}`$
  (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  Lemma [S5.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S5.2 (Type-level sharing exclusion). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
  $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$ is the expected number of distinct personal
  *(value, tool) pairs* a user ever confirms, once each over the
  deployment’s lifetime (the pair is the endorsement unit,
  §[S2.1](#A2.SS1a "S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  a personal value used at $`j`$ tools contributes $`j`$ pairs).
  $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$ is a *lifetime* quantity; where it appears
  alongside single-epoch masses
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
  the sum is read as a lifetime personal term plus a per-epoch shareable
  term, each bounding its own component.
- •
  The independent reference model (IRM) [Fagin (1977)](#bib.bib18), per
  pair and per user: user $`u`$ demands the pair $`(v,t)`$ within the
  epoch with probability $`p_{u,v,t}`$, independently across users; the
  model is heterogeneous, and $`p_{v,t}:=M^{-1}\sum_{u}p_{u,v,t}`$,
  $`p_{v}:=M^{-1}\sum_{u}\mathbb{P}[\text{$u$ demands $v$ at some tool}]`$
  denote the population-average marginals, so $`p_{v,t}\leq p_{v}`$ and
  $`\mathbb{E}[n_{v,t}]=Mp_{v,t}`$. Every expected-count argument in
  this appendix consumes only cross-user independence and this identity,
  never identical distribution across users (the owner’s degenerate
  indicator, next bullet, is the one systematic heterogeneity). The
  single-epoch masses are $`d:=\sum_{v}p_{v}`$ and
  $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}:=\sum_{v,t}p_{v,t}`$, both finite, owner coupling
  folded in (next bullet), with
  $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$ under
  [A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
  Under this model $`n_{v}`$ and $`n_{v,t}`$ denote the *latent* counts
  $`\sum_{u}D_{u,v,t}`$; the log-defined realized counts satisfy
  $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$ pathwise
  (§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  so every expected bound stated against $`Mp_{v,t}`$ covers the
  realized events the ledger charges.
- •
  *Owner coupling.* The owner’s publication schedule for each item — the
  epochs in which the owner submits or resubmits $`v`$
  (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  — is carried in the exogenous demand factor alongside the demand
  indicators
  (§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
  it is owner behaviour, exogenous to the protocol and the attacker
  exactly as the typed stream is
  ([A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  In every scheduled epoch the owner’s own demand indicator for $`v`$ is
  set to one, at the owner’s creating tool (formally, the owner’s
  marginal $`p_{u,v,t}`$ is degenerate at one in scheduled epochs; other
  users’ indicators and the cross-user independence are untouched — the
  heterogeneous form of the previous bullet): submission is modelled as
  demand-driven, latently mirroring
  Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
  clause that the owner’s publish confirmation is a realized demand
  event. Consequently every epoch containing a submission or re-entry of
  $`v`$ has $`n_{v}\geq 1`$, and every realized demander is a latent
  demander, so $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}\leq n_{v}`$ pathwise. A
  shared-tier presence can, by contrast, be *carried* into an epoch with
  no current-epoch owner activity (a dormant candidate short of its
  retirement clock, a live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ entry, or the one carry-in
  freeze of
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
  the vanishing clause of
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)–(iv)
  therefore rests on the absence of *events*, not of presence: on
  $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$ there is no entry (an entry requires a current-epoch
  submission, hence owner demand), no dispute or review opening (each
  opens at a *latent* demander’s protocol-bearing gate decision —
  attempted use realizes the latent indicator, required-approval clause;
  the opener need not be a realized log-demander, e.g. at a cache gate’s
  rejecting branch,
  Definitions [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii), [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  no freeze-bucket arrival, no invitation (a re-entry notification
  requires an entry, and a carried-in review issues no new prompts,
  Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),

  Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

  which quantifies over adaptive strategies.

  Promotion threshold $`N`$ per tool (weighted: distinct endorsers in
  $`[W/w_{\max},W/w_{\min}]`$, changing constants not exponents); panel
  cap $`k`$; credited endorsements per (entry, tool) are capped at
  $`N^{+}=\Theta(N)`$
  (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)).
- •
  A *confirmation* is an accepting gate decision
  (convention ([C6](#A1.I2.i6 "Item C6 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
  rejection effort is bounded separately
  ([N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Accepting decisions fall into three exhaustive classes. A confirmation
  of the pair $`(v,t)`$ is *required* if the gate fires for the user’s
  own use of $`v`$ at $`t`$ and the user holds no local endorsed copy of
  $`v`$ whose scope admits $`t`$ (for the pseudo-target: no local
  readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-level copy of $`v`$ at all — reasoning
  coverage,
  Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
  *Required-approval clause (a reference-model coupling).* The reference
  model is read with attempted use coupled to latent demand: a user’s
  own attempted use of $`v`$ at $`t`$ within the epoch — any event
  firing a gate for it, inside or outside a shared-tier presence,
  covered and cache gates included — occurs only on $`\{D_{u,v,t}=1\}`$;
  equivalently, every such event realizes the user’s latent indicator
  for the epoch. This is a modeling stipulation on the demand factor
  (§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  not a consequence of independent sampling: it is the natural extension
  of the existing convention that a realized shared-tier demand
  presupposes attempted use. Every user making a required approval of a
  pair is therefore a latent demander of it; the log-defined shared-tier
  demand of
  Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  ($`n^{\mathrm{log}}`$) remains the subclass realized during a
  shared-tier presence, with $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$
  pathwise. It is *voluntary* if it is recorded at an interpreter-issued
  invitation surface (a re-entry notification or suspension prompt,
  Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),
  declinable at zero required cost; voluntary confirmations exist *only*
  through such surfaces, deduplicated jointly at one invitation per
  identity per item per epoch. It is *redundant* if the gate fires for
  the user’s own use while an in-scope local copy is held — possible
  only through handle-expressed reuse
  (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
  or a reasoning-target confirmation of locally readable bytes
  (reasoning coverage,
  Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
  a *covered gate* — in which case the decision is protocol-inert on
  both branches
  (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)):
  no promotion weight, no freshness consumption, no dispute initiation,
  no verdict. Redundant confirmations are excluded from every count
  below and disclosed as attention cost in
  [N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
  $`C_{u}`$ counts user $`u`$’s required and voluntary shareable
  confirmations; $`\bar{C}_{M}=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{u}C_{u}`$. The cap
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  is stated over required confirmations; the ledger
  (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
  over required and voluntary.
- •
  *Epoch vs. lifetime masses.* $`p_{v,t}`$ is a per-epoch probability.
  The lifetime mass is
  $`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}:=\sum_{v,t}p^{\infty}_{v,t}`$ with
  $`p^{\infty}_{v,t}`$ the probability that a user *ever* demands the
  pair; single-epoch and lifetime expected bounds are stated against the
  matching mass and never conflated
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)–(iii)).
  Disputes add the ledger rows of
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  revocation adds
  Corollary [S6.5](#A6.Thmtheorem5 "Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  (re-verification mechanics:
  [N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
- •
  Saturation: $`V(M):=\mathbb{E}|\{v:n_{v}\geq 1\}|=o(M)`$; concretely
  Heaps’ form $`V(M)=\Theta(M^{\beta})`$, $`\beta\in(0,1)`$ [Newman
  (2005)](#bib.bib34).

###### Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form).

There are a constant $`s_{0}\geq 1`$ and a front-loading bound
$`\bar{\gamma}=\bar{\gamma}(M)\in(0,1]`$ such that, for every pair
$`(v,t)`$ demanded in the epoch: the number of distinct demanders of
$`(v,t)`$ whose first demand of the pair falls within any single
finalisation window (length $`T_{\mathrm{win}}`$) or any single
*candidate-dormancy* interval (an inter-window span carrying no live
community entry, of length $`\leq T_{\mathrm{exp}}`$ by the retirement
clock; *stable promoted intervals* — a live, unsuspended $`\mathsf{CC}`$
presence with no open window — are exempt from both clauses: demand
there is fast-pathed or ledger-residual, never bucketed,
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is at most $`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0}`$; and likewise the number of
distinct identities whose *first audit-recorded decision on the pair*
$`(v,t)`$ in the epoch
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
display-transcript decisions at non-covered gates, cache gates on *both*
branches included — the accepting branch is audit-recorded though never
federation-logged,
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
falls within any single such window or interval is at most
$`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0}`$ (the *first-pair-decision clause*).
Demander counts are *realized* shared-tier demand events
($`n^{\mathrm{log}}`$,
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
decider counts are audit-recorded first pair-decisions (a class
containing every federation-logged first pair-decision), whose deciders
are latent demanders (required-approval clause,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
but need not be realized log-demanders. Both are capped against the
item’s *latent* demand $`n_{v}`$ — the weaker denominator, since
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}\leq n_{v}`$ and every decider is a latent
demander.

- Commentary (non-normative; reading and validation of
  [A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). The
  cap is relative to the item’s own demand, never an absolute count: it
  forbids *front-loading* (demand concentrating inside one window), not
  popularity. For demand arriving steadily over an epoch of length
  $`L`$, $`\bar{\gamma}\approx T_{\mathrm{win}}/L`$ for every item,
  independently of $`n_{v}`$ and of $`M`$; the additive $`s_{0}`$ makes
  the cap satisfiable for items of tiny demand.
  [A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is a hindsight property of completed epochs, used only in the
  analysis: no protocol rule reads, estimates, or depends on
  $`\bar{\gamma}`$. Its violation is item-local and graceful: an item
  whose demand spikes into one window ($`\gamma_{v}\approx 1`$) simply
  fails to amortise: each of its demanders pays the one required
  confirmation the pathwise cap
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
  already bounds, while every other item’s accounting is untouched
  ([S17](#Thmobjx17 "Analysis S17 (Release-day demand spikes). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Demand-paced panels need no such cap: panels accumulate verdicts
  across windows, so
  [A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  constrains promotion finalisation windows and dormant intervals only;
  the dormant-interval clause is the stronger half
  ($`T_{\mathrm{exp}}\gg T_{\mathrm{win}}`$ typically), kept plausible
  by the dormancy-retirement clock of
  Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
  and by its restriction to *candidate* dormancy: a promoted item’s
  demand, however concentrated, is exempt from both clauses (its cost is
  fast-pathed or ledger-residual,
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Validation: per-item realised fractions $`\gamma_{v}`$, checked
  specifically on the most-demanded items
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  The first-pair-decision clause has the same character and the same
  validation path: for demand arriving steadily, first pair-decisions
  track first pair-demands; both realised fractions are logged per item
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  The audit-recorded class is validated the same way, directly from
  display-transcript logs: both branches of every gate, cache gates
  included, are recorded there
  (Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e)),
  so realised first-pair-decision fractions are observable without
  reference to the federation log. Its pair-level indexing is
  load-bearing: it is what makes the dispute-initiation classification
  of
  Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  exhaustive, since a cross-tool repeat decision (a prior acceptance at
  another pair) and a decision postponed past an abandoned dialog are
  each the identity’s *first* decision at their own pair, counted where
  they fall. The pair-level form is the item-level cap read tool by
  tool, still stated against the item’s *total* demand $`n_{v}`$, the
  weaker and more plausible denominator; steady demand gives
  $`\bar{\gamma}\approx T_{\mathrm{win}}/L`$ per pair exactly as per
  item, and the same per-item logging of realised fractions
  $`\gamma_{v}`$ validates it
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form).

Adopt the presence taxonomy and charging convention of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
within an epoch, an item’s shared-tier presence partitions into entry
windows, candidate-dormancy intervals, and freeze/suspension intervals
(the *ledger-charged* pieces), and *stable promoted intervals* (a live,
unsuspended community entry with no open entry window). For a pair
$`(v,t)`$ and an epoch, let $`U_{v,t}`$ count the epoch’s *residual*
required pair-approvals of $`(v,t)`$: those charged to no ledger row
(option-induced cache confirmations excluded: floor-charged,
Corollary [S6.6](#A6.Thmtheorem6 "Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options –). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— a subclass of the required confirmations by demanders whose
epoch-first demand of the item falls in a stable promoted interval or
outside every shared-tier presence (a credited such decision is
weight-row-charged instead,
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
only shrinking the residual) (before first publication, after
retirement, or after demotion; gates fired during a suspension are
freeze-bucket events, ledger-charged, never residual). Each belongs to a
distinct demander of the pair
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so $`U_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$ pathwise. The residual class is
*operational*, keyed to gate behaviour, never to certificate existence:
a live $`\mathsf{CC}`$ entry naming $`(v,t)`$ fast-paths only
*literal*-expressed use
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a));
a handle-expressed use of the same pair gates at every tool
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
and, absent a local in-scope copy, is required — and, in a stable
promoted interval, residual. There are $`D_{0}(M)\geq 0`$ and
$`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$ such that, for every *benign*
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
shareable item $`v\in\mathcal{V}`$, every target $`t`$, and every
$`n\geq 1`$, conditional on $`n_{v,t}=n`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\big[U_{v,t}\mid n_{v,t}=n\big]\ \leq\ D_{0}(M)+\varepsilon(M)\,n.
``` |  |

Like
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
this is a hindsight property of completed epochs, read against latent
demand
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
no protocol rule reads, estimates, or depends on it, and it is trivially
satisfied whenever $`n\leq D_{0}(M)`$ (since $`U_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$).
The growth of $`D_{0}`$ is consumed only through the *product condition*
$`D_{0}(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$ of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
a joint property of the coverage threshold and the saturation law, never
of either alone; under the Heaps form $`V(M)=\Theta(M^{\beta})`$
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the sufficient rate is $`D_{0}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$, the form used in the
corridor
(§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and in the sufficiency sketch below. It bounds jointly: (i) *publication
coverage* — a demanded benign item its owner never publishes has every
gate-firing accepting demand residual, and satisfies the bound only if
that demand is small; (ii) *promotion coverage* — demand at
not-yet-promoted pairs arriving outside every ledger-charged piece; and
(iii) *representation coverage* — demand for live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$ pairs
arriving handle-expressed (untrusted-channel arrival of
already-certified bytes), which gates and pays despite the certificate
([S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
An item or arrival pattern violating it never amortises: each residual
demander pays the one required confirmation the pathwise cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
already bounds, item-locally and gracefully, entering the residual
$`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$ of
Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility.

The following sufficiency sketch is heuristic — a plausibility argument,
not a derivation: it does not formally compose intervening freezes,
wrongful evictions, the entry cap, the pool-composition requirements, or
the arrival-representation mix into a proof of
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which remains an assumption; the compatibility calculation closing the
paragraph is exact. Heuristically sufficient, for a benign item and any
fixed $`\eta>0`$: the owner publishes the item before more than an
$`\varepsilon`$-fraction of each demanded pair’s demand arrives and
resubmits promptly after each unpromoted window (dormant intervals short
of the retirement clock, within the per-epoch entry cap of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i));
some entry, counting the banked credits of its preceding interval
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
accrues at least $`(1+\eta)N/p_{b}`$ fresh byte-first demanders (a
positive byte-first fraction per demanded tool — enough demanders whose
first decision on the bytes occurs at that tool — is one empirical
mechanism supporting this cohort’s existence; it is a heuristic
diagnostic for
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
not a hypothesis of any theorem) whose demand spans at least
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ pools with at least
$`\lceil N/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ accepting demanders available per
pool (so the per-pool credit caps of
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)
do not bind below $`N`$), almost all of them authority-active
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a):
honest identities are authority-inactive only in the rare calibrated
states of
[Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
folded into the same $`\varepsilon`$) — a demand-composition property of
the same character as
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
structural half, validated by the same pool-stratified logging
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and demotion of promoted benign entries is exponentially rare
(Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so promoted status, once reached, persists; and, for the representation
clause, demand for promoted pairs predominantly arrives
fast-path-expressed — through trusted retrieval of the live entry
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii))
or reuse of local readable copies — with the handle-arrival fraction
([S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
folded into the same $`\varepsilon`$: an arrival-channel property of the
demand stream, logged directly
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
never derived from the protocol. For schedules with $`N(M)\to\infty`$ —
every corridor schedule,
§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— the accepting count then crosses $`N`$ except with probability
$`e^{-2\eta^{\prime 2}N(M)/(1+\eta)^{2}}\to 0`$ by Hoeffding’s lower
tail, for a margin $`\eta^{\prime}`$ depending on $`\eta`$ and
$`p_{b}`$, giving $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$; at *fixed* $`N`$ the same
cohort yields only a fixed failure probability, so
$`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$ under fixed protocol constants requires instead
that available cohorts grow beyond a fixed multiple of $`N`$, which
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
then asserts rather than derives; intervening disputes are absorbed by
the vindication exemption of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)(b)
([N15](#Thmnotex15 "Note N15 (The vindication exemption). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and resolve at the item’s own demand rate, freezes excluding themselves
from the window clock
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)).
*Consistency with
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")*:
under the fractional cap the two assumptions do not constrain one
quantity from opposite sides. A crossing window is permitted to contain
$`(1+\eta)N/p_{b}`$ demanders whenever
$`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0}\geq(1+\eta)N/p_{b}`$, i.e. whenever
$`n_{v}\geq\big((1+\eta)N/p_{b}-s_{0}\big)/\bar{\gamma}`$; $`D_{0}(M)`$
may therefore be taken of order $`N(M)/\bar{\gamma}(M)`$, and the
product condition’s Heaps form $`D_{0}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$
(Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
becomes $`N(M)/\bar{\gamma}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$, satisfied by every
corridor schedule
(§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

- Commentary (non-normative; scoping, representation dependence, and
  validation of
  [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). *Benign
  scoping is deliberate*: poisoned items are excluded; their promotion
  probability is bounded above by
  Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  and their residual demand is charged at the single-user cap by design,
  each such confirmation being a personal gate inspection of an
  unpromoted or flagged item, exactly the inspection the design intends.
  *The operational (no-row) form is load-bearing*: an earlier draft
  keyed coverage to certificate existence, under which a
  handle-expressed use of a live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$ pair counted as covered
  while its gate — required under
  Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
  — was charged to no row and to no residual; the operational form
  charges every required confirmation somewhere by construction
  (Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  charging convention), and names exactly the demand the amortisation
  story must cover. *Representation dependence is the disclosed price*:
  community certification amortises the flows that can take the fast
  path — literal-expressed reuse of promoted bytes, in particular bytes
  obtained through trusted retrieval (Retrieve returns live entries as
  readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes,
  Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
  which then byte-match the live entry,
  Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a))
  — and never the handle-expressed arrivals, which gate by design
  ([S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
  $`\varepsilon(M)`$ must absorb the handle-arrival fraction of
  certified demand, so the vanishing of the residual is a joint property
  of publication timing, promotion speed, *and* arrival representation.
  Failure is graceful and item-local: residual demand is priced at the
  cap
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
  and the epoch’s shared required load never exceeds the standalone mass
  $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ in any case
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
  Incentive sensitivity is the disclosed residual
  [S16](#Thmobjx16 "Analysis S16 (Incentive feedback on publication). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
  Under permanent freshness the condition weakens in one direction and
  is explicitly priced in the other: banked credits accumulate across
  epoch boundaries toward the next entry, so qualifying demand need not
  concentrate within one epoch; conversely, endorsers consumed by a
  failed entry never renew, which the identity-disjoint counting already
  prices
  (Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  Validation: log each item’s realized residual fraction
  $`U_{v,t}/n_{v,t}`$ *and* the fast-path-vs-gate split of
  live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$ demand (the handle-arrival fraction), stratified
  on the most-demanded items, together with per-item time-to-promotion
  against accumulated demand and the per-epoch demanded-but-unpublished
  mass
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread).

Each shareable item is demanded at no more than
$`c_{\mathrm{tool}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ distinct tools over the epoch: at
most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ tools have $`n_{v,t}\geq 1`$, and hence
$`\sum_{t}n_{v,t}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,n_{v}`$ (latent reference-model
counts,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the realized counts of
Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
inherit the bound pathwise: $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$
places the realized tool support inside the latent tool support, so at
most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ tools have $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\geq 1`$,
and every realized pair-demander is a realized item-demander, so
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}`$
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
hence
$`\sum_{t}n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v}`$
pathwise). In particular each user demands at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$
pairs per item, and $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$ (the
$`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ demanded targets per item include
$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ where demanded; constants unchanged).

- Commentary (non-normative; reading and validation of
  [A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). The
  bound formalises the observation that a published item typically
  addresses the scenario its owner used it in: endorsement, promotion,
  and scope are all per (value, tool); it licenses the per-tool split in
  Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii).
  Validation: per-item distinct-tool counts
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  The *byte-first density* of a demanded tool’s stream — the fraction of
  its demanders whose first decision on the bytes occurs at that tool —
  is deliberately *not* part of this assumption: no proof consumes it,
  and its role is heuristic support for the promotion-coverage clause of
  [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  (see the heuristic-sufficiency paragraph there).

###### Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass).

Along the population scaling, the single-epoch per-user demand mass is
uniformly bounded: $`\sup_{M}d(M)<\infty`$, where
$`d(M)=\sum_{v}p_{v}=M^{-1}\sum_{u}\sum_{v}\mathbb{P}[\text{$u$ demands $v$}]`$
is the population-average number of distinct shareable items one user
demands per epoch
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
hence $`\sup_{M}d_{\mathrm{tool}}(M)<\infty`$ under
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and $`d_{\mathrm{good}}\leq d`$ throughout. Where
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is not adopted, every vanishing ($`\to 0`$) budget conclusion below
holds verbatim with its rate condition read against the mass:
$`\bar{\gamma}(M)\,(1+\kappa(M))\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$ in
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)
and
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
and $`\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$ in
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
(whose $`D_{0}(M)V(M)/M`$ term is independent of the per-user mass and
unchanged). The relative bounds (cost at most the front-loading multiple
$`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}`$ of the standalone mass,
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
first clause) and the cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
consume no bound on $`d`$ in any case.

- Commentary (non-normative; reading and validation of
  [A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")). The
  assumption is load-bearing and deliberately explicit: without it, the
  vanishing conclusions would fail — a population-indexed demand law
  with $`d(M)\to\infty`$ (each user demanding ever more distinct shared
  items as the community grows) satisfies every remaining hypothesis
  while the front-loading term $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d`$
  grows — and pointwise finiteness of $`d`$ at each $`M`$ does not
  supply the uniform bound the limits consume. It is an individual-usage
  property, not a population property: under any fixed per-user demand
  law the masses are constants in $`M`$ and
  [A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is automatic (the Zipf law of
  §[S8.5](#A8.SS5 "S8.5 Zipf case study for the budget ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  has $`d=\sum_{r}p_{r}=1`$ identically), and the Heaps form is
  standardly read over a corpus accumulated from bounded individual
  streams [Lü et al. (2010)](#bib.bib29), so the saturation hypothesis
  already carries this reading. The owner-coupling convention cannot
  violate it: coupled indicators number at most $`\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}`$
  per user per epoch
  (Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  The disclosed failure mode is demand growth induced by the shared tier
  itself — a richer library drawing each user to more shared items per
  epoch — a network effect of the same character as the incentive
  feedback of
  [S16](#Thmobjx16 "Analysis S16 (Incentive feedback on publication). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  violation is graceful: the relative bounds and the pathwise cap
  (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
  are unaffected, and the general-form rate conditions of
  [A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  price the growth explicitly. Validation: log per-user distinct
  shareable-item demand per epoch across deployment growth
  ([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

#### S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap

The cap’s core is a counting identity. Its pathwise clause,
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
rests on the harness rules and
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
alone: no ledger row, no behavioural parameter, no demand model, and no
assumption of this appendix. Its expected clauses restate that identity
against the reference demand model’s masses
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
still using no assumption; the single assumption-bearing statement in
this subsection is the mass comparison of
Corollary [S6.3](#A6.Thmtheorem3 "Corollary S6.3 (The cap under bounded tool-spread). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The cap is therefore stated first. Its dependency chain is
Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
$`\to`$
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
$`\to`$
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
$`\to`$
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
strictly in that order.

###### Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence).

Fix a user $`u`$, a value $`v`$, and a tool $`t`$, and suppose $`u`$’s
own accepting review of $`(v,t)`$ has occurred at any gate transaction —
including a transaction another of whose reviews aborted the enclosing
invocation
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
endorsement is durable). Then in every later configuration, unless
$`u`$’s own agent has evicted the block
([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
$`u`$’s store contains a $`\mathsf{C}`$-block with bytes $`v`$ and
$`t\in\mathsf{scope}`$, and every use of $`v`$ at $`t`$ by $`u`$
expressed as a readable literal takes the fast path of
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a);
a use expressed through a handle gates
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
as a covered gate, protocol-inert and redundant
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
In particular no later gate event of $`u`$ for $`(v,t)`$ is *required*.
(Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is requirements-level and absent from the formal semantics; a conforming
instantiation would leave the block in place and read the authorization
and coverage tests over currently authorizing witnesses,
[O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),(c)–(d).)
For the pseudo-target: once $`u`$ holds *any* local readable
$`\mathbb{E}`$-level copy of the bytes (via Recall-E,
Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
a later $`\mathsf{confirm}`$ on those bytes at $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ is
a covered gate by the reasoning-coverage clause of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
protocol-inert and redundant; hence no later gate event of $`u`$ for
$`(v,\mathsf{reasoning})`$ is required.

###### Proof.

By
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
every accepting review of $`(v,t)`$ writes a fresh $`\mathsf{C}`$-block
with bytes $`v`$ and $`t\in\mathsf{scope}`$ at the close of its atomic
transaction, on the executing and the aborting branch alike (Conf-Acc,
Tool-Gate-Acc, Tool-Gate-Rej;
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(vii)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
By
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
blocks are immutable once written, so neither this block’s label nor its
scope ever changes; local stores mutate only through owner-invoked
$`\Sigma`$-operations and owner confirmations, and no protocol event
initiated by any other identity alters or removes any block in $`u`$’s
local store
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The only removal path is first-party eviction
([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
then byte-matches $`v`$ against the stored block with
$`t\in\mathsf{scope}`$. For the pseudo-target: any local
$`\mathbb{E}`$-level copy of the bytes is readable (Recall-E,
Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and persists by
[A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A2](#Thmassumptionx2 "Assumption A2 (Label persistence and block immutability). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the first-party eviction exception aside; the reasoning-coverage clause
of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
then classifies every later reasoning-target gate on those bytes as
covered. Its owner-side test reads exactly the readability fact
Rule [R5](#Thmrulex5 "Rule R5 (Readable local endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
establishes: readability is the entirety of what an accepting reasoning
confirmation buys, so the clause covers precisely the gates whose
acceptance would change nothing locally. ∎

###### Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap).
````
