````math
The cap counts *required user approvals* — first authorizations of
reusable (value, tool) pairs — and nothing else: not rejecting
decisions, abandoned or repeated dialogs, covered-gate (redundant)
acceptances, batch-page attention, or per-task confirmations (classes:
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
effort account:
[N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The superscript $`\mathrm{forced}`$ below denotes this required-approval
count. Suppose the owner’s agent does not evict the relevant local
blocks (the disclosed first-party exception of
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is requirements-level and absent from the formal semantics
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so no lease expiry exists in the proved system.

1.  (i)
    *(Pathwise lifetime invariant.)* Pathwise and independent of every
    federated and demand-model assumption, subject to the stated
    first-party persistence exceptions: under any dispute, rejection,
    revocation, or availability campaign whatsoever, no user is required
    to confirm any given (value, tool) pair more than once over the
    deployment’s lifetime: $`C^{\mathrm{forced}}_{u,v,t}\leq 1`$
    pathwise, counting required pair-approvals
    (Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    counting unit). This is
    [INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    established by
    Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
    Rejecting decisions, abandoned dialogs, repeated within-transaction
    reviews, redundant confirmations
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and inspection time are a distinct resource, disclosed and partially
    bounded in
    [N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    and are not bounded by this clause.
2.  (ii)
    *(Expected cap, single epoch, reference model.)* In the independent
    reference model
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    the two components are bounded on their own horizons:
    $`\mathbb{E}[C^{\mathrm{forced},\infty}_{\mathrm{personal}}]\leq d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$
    (lifetime) and
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{forced},(e)}_{\mathrm{share}}]\leq d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$
    (per epoch $`e`$); the componentwise sum
    $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}+d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ is a valid upper bound for
    their sum on any single epoch read jointly with the lifetime
    personal term, not a homogeneous single-horizon cost. The bound
    $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ is exactly the expected shareable cost a
    single user incurs in isolation, where every gate necessarily fires:
    no user is ever pushed above the single-user cost. The comparison to
    the item-level mass, $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$,
    is
    Corollary [S6.3](#A6.Thmtheorem3 "Corollary S6.3 (The cap under bounded tool-spread). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and is this theorem’s only assumption-bearing companion.
3.  (iii)
    *(Expected cap, lifetime.)* Over the deployment’s lifetime, expected
    required shareable cost is at most
    $`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}=\sum_{v,t}p^{\infty}_{v,t}`$; the
    single-epoch mass bounds the lifetime cost only when it is itself
    read as the lifetime mass
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
4.  (iv)
    *(Monotonicity.)* At a fixed realised workload with no disputes,
    adding users never increases any individual’s required count:
    promotions only advance, and a promotion of $`(v,t)`$ removes the
    gate for every later demander of that pair
    (Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    With disputes, an added identity can suspend amortisation, forcing
    later demanders to confirm personally; the pathwise invariant (i)
    still caps every user at once per pair.

###### Proof.

(i) By
Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
$`u`$’s first accepting review of $`(v,t)`$ writes the covering local
copy durably, whatever the enclosing transaction’s outcome, so no later
gate event of $`u`$ for $`(v,t)`$ is required (a literal-expressed use
fast-paths; a handle-expressed use is a covered gate, redundant by
definition); within that first transaction the pair is counted once
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
declining voluntary invitations costs nothing
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(ii) By (i), each required confirmation of $`(v,t)`$ belongs to a
distinct demander of the pair (realized, hence latent,
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so the population’s required total for $`(v,t)`$ is at most $`n_{v,t}`$,
with $`\mathbb{E}[n_{v,t}]=Mp_{v,t}`$ in the reference model; summing
over pairs and dividing by $`M`$ gives $`d_{\mathrm{tool}}`$; personal
pairs add $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$, once each
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(iii) The pathwise clause (i) is lifetime; taking expectations over
lifetime pair-demand indicators gives $`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}`$.
(iv) Immediate from
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and (i). ∎

###### Corollary S6.3 (The cap under bounded tool-spread).

Under
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
$`d_{\mathrm{tool}}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$; hence the shareable cap
of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
is at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$ per epoch (componentwise sum
$`d_{\mathrm{priv}}+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d`$, horizons per
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
The lifetime analogue,
$`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,d^{\infty}`$ with
$`d^{\infty}:=\sum_{v}p^{\infty}_{v}`$, holds when
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is read over lifetime demand (at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ distinct
tools per item ever), a strictly stronger reading than the per-epoch
form and asserted only here. This corollary restates the cap against the
coarser item-level mass; no other result consumes it.

###### Proof.

A user demanding the pair $`(v,t)`$ demands the item $`v`$
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and under
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ tools per item carry demand, so
$`\sum_{t}p_{v,t}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,p_{v}`$ per item; sum over
items. The lifetime form is identical under the lifetime reading. ∎

###### Remark S6.4 (Voluntary effort and the cap).

The cap is stated over required confirmations. Voluntary community
effort (a repeat re-inspection after a dispute or re-entry notification)
is declinable at zero personal cost, carries no promotion weight
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and is counted in the budget
(Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
never in the cap.

###### Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation).

Post-promotion suspensions and re-verification
([N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
do not multiply required cost: a user who relied on ungated
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ status at $`t`$ and loses it on demotion or suspension
owes at most their first-ever confirmation of $`(v,t)`$, already counted
inside $`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}`$, after which their local
$`\mathsf{C}`$ copy covers all reuse at $`t`$ for the deployment’s
lifetime
(Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Hence expected total required cost is at most
$`d_{\mathrm{priv}}+d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}`$, lifetime, independent
of the number of epochs. A multiplicative factor $`E_{\mathrm{lease}}`$
would arise only under a conforming instantiation of the
requirements-level
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— an extension-level claim, stated and to be proved with that extension
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e)),
outside this corollary.

###### Proof.

Immediate from
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(iii):
required confirmations are once per (user, value, tool) over the
lifetime; demotion, suspension, and re-verification never touch local
$`\mathsf{C}`$ copies
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is absent from the formal semantics
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
∎

###### Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Option-induced cache confirmations
(Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
belong to no pipeline ledger row and to no residual
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
exclusions): they are accept-inert for the shared tier
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
and are accounted in two classes. *(Per-task.)*
[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
confirmations of freshly composed data-tool arguments lie in the
per-task stream, outside the reusable-memory accounting entirely, by the
scope hypothesis of
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
*(Floor-charged.)* All remaining option-induced cache confirmations —
[O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
first-use sensitive-sink confirmations of $`\mathsf{T}`$-values and
[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
confirmations of endorsed-value reuse at data tools — are required
pair-confirmations of the confirming user, charged to the floor
component: each is at most one per (user, value, sensitive sink) resp.
(user, value, data tool) (scope-caching,
Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
an $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$ enlargement of the per-item pair count under the
sink-spread and data-tool-spread hypotheses of
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— folded exactly as
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
folds tool pairs. The exhaustiveness of the charging convention
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
is unaffected: option-induced confirmations are charged to the per-task
stream or the floor, never to any pipeline row or residual.

###### Proof.

Immediate from
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
and
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the fresh cache copy scope-caches
(Lemma [S6.1](#A6.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S6.1 (Local scope persistence). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so each (user, value, target) triple is required at most once; the
spread hypotheses bound the targets per value by $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$; and
the freshly-composed class is per-task by hypothesis. ∎

#### S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger

###### Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, $`\mathcal{O}`$-form).

Fix an item $`v`$ and an epoch; adopt the default bars of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and, for the bucket rows, that each honest inspection, fresh or repeat,
accepts a benign item with conditional probability at least $`p_{b}`$
given all prior protocol events (for a repeat inspection of bytes the
inspector previously accepted, the bound is if anything the more
plausible). Adopt also the standing exception of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(no owner eviction of the relevant local blocks;
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is requirements-level and absent from the formal semantics,
[O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Option-induced cache confirmations
(Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are excluded throughout — from $`C^{\mathrm{pipe}}_{v}`$, from the
residual of
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and from the pathwise count $`C_{v}`$ of clause (iv): they are charged
to the floor component, with the $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$ spread factors of
Corollary [S6.6](#A6.Thmtheorem6 "Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options –). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Let $`E_{\star}:=E_{\max}+1`$. *Presence taxonomy.* Within the epoch,
the item’s shared-tier presence partitions into four classes of pieces:
*entry windows* (at most $`E_{\max}`$, by the per-item entry cap of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
counting promoted, evicted, and unpromoted entries alike; windows are
epoch-contained,
convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
*freeze/suspension intervals* (the current-epoch disputes and fast-track
reviews, plus at most one carry-in instance — the byte-level freeze is
exclusive,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii);
a carried-in instance is counted toward
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
in its opening epoch,
convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
but its current-epoch demanders are charged here, via the carry-in term
of $`\bar{D}_{v}`$, and it issues no new prompts,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi));
*candidate-dormancy intervals* (no open window, no live promotion at any
tool, unfrozen); and *stable promoted intervals* (a live, unsuspended
community entry at some tool, no open window, unfrozen). Inter-window
spans — each entry is followed by at most one, ending at the next entry,
retirement, or the epoch boundary, so at most $`E_{\star}`$ begin in or
carry into the epoch — have promotion status fixed at the preceding
window’s close, so each span is candidate-dormant or stable-promoted
throughout, with its freeze/suspension pieces carved out;
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
dormant-interval clause is applied per candidate-dormancy span,
freeze-time demanders within a span being charged to the freeze bucket.
The first three classes are the *ledger-charged* pieces; stable promoted
intervals are deliberately *not* bucketed: a matching literal fast-paths
there at the promoted tool
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a))
at zero cost, while the gates that do fire there — handle-expressed uses
of the certified pair
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
and uses at unpromoted tools — are charged to the *ledger residual*
below, bounded by
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
under
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(A stable promoted interval is “window closed, not yet resubmitted or
retired” in the sense of
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b):
first decisions logged there bank toward the item’s next entry exactly
as in candidate dormancy; the taxonomy separates the classes for cost
attribution only and changes no protocol rule.) We use the common
conservative bound $`E_{\star}`$ for the window- and dormancy-bucket
piece counts. (The attempt structure of
Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
partitions the same presence; the ledger’s buckets and bounds are
unchanged by it.) Write

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bar{D}_{v}\ :=\ 2(1-p_{b})\,E_{\star}\,c_{\mathrm{tool}}\big(\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0}\big)\;+\;(1-p_{b})\,E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}\;+\;c_{\mathrm{acc}}f\;+\;2E_{\max}\;+\;1\,,
``` |  |

the final $`+1`$ is the carry-in instance; the invited-reconsideration
term keeps $`E_{\max}`$ because invitations are epoch-scoped
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
$`\bar{D}_{v}`$ is a function of the realised demand $`n_{v}`$: the
bucket rows bound conditional expectations given the demand realisation,
and the split in (iii) follows by taking the expectation over demand
last, licensed by the demand construction of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the behavioural bounds are asserted uniformly over demand realisations,
so
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
applies under the demand-conditional measure. For poisoned items no
$`p_{b}`$ bound is asserted: their entries are counted by
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and their residual demand is charged at the single-user cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

*Pipeline component and ledger residual.* The rows cover the *pipeline
component* $`C^{\mathrm{pipe}}_{v}`$: every confirmation of a pair of
$`v`$ charged to a ledger row under the convention below — credited
weight-bearing endorsements, bucketed required confirmations (window,
candidate-dormancy, and freeze/suspension time, carry-in included), and
all invited-repeat, prompt, and publish confirmations of $`v`$. Required
confirmations charged to *no* row are the *ledger residual*: those of
demanders whose epoch-first item-demand falls in a stable promoted
interval (in particular handle-expressed uses of a live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$
pair, which gate under
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
despite the certificate) or outside every shared-tier presence (before
first publication, after retirement, or after demotion). The residual is
bounded by
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
under
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
any overlap between the two accountings only over-counts.

*Charging convention (retrospective).* At the close of the logging epoch
every confirmation of $`v`$ — a durable accepting pair-confirmation,
counted once per pair per transaction
(Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— is assigned to exactly one row or to the ledger residual; the ledger
is a hindsight accounting device, like
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
never protocol state. The ledger *rows* charge protocol-bearing
decisions and invited and publish events
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the *residual* is defined over all required confirmations of the bytes,
protocol-bearing or not — in particular outside-presence confirmations,
which are unlogged as candidate decisions — so that every required
confirmation in this lemma’s accounting universe (option-induced cache
confirmations excluded, above) is charged somewhere, to a row or to the
residual, by construction.
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
retirement clause governs *demand counting*, not the confirmation
universe of this convention.) Non-covered reasoning-target confirmations
satisfying
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are protocol-bearing
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and are charged to the pair $`(v,\mathsf{reasoning})`$ exactly as tool
pairs are; covered reasoning gates are inert
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
and excluded like any redundant confirmation. *Credited* weight-bearing
endorsements (in-entry, banked-and-credited within the epoch, or
vindication-credited; required or invited alike) are assigned to the
weight row — including a banked first decision taken in a stable
promoted interval, so a residual-class demander’s credited acceptance is
weight-row-charged, only shrinking the residual; *uncredited invited*
confirmations to their invitation row (re-entry or prompt; invitations
are epoch-scoped, so no invitation row carries over); *publish*
confirmations to the publish row; every other *required* confirmation to
the ledger-charged piece (window, candidate-dormancy, or
freeze/suspension — current-epoch instances and the at most one carry-in
instance) containing its demander’s *first demand of the item* in the
epoch, at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ confirmations per demander (one per
pair,
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
when that first item-demand falls in a ledger-charged piece, and to the
*ledger residual* otherwise (first item-demand in a stable promoted
interval or outside every presence). Cross-epoch crediting of an
already-logged event
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv))
relabels a prior epoch’s event and adds nothing to any epoch. The four
presence classes partition the item’s shared-tier presence within the
epoch, so every demander’s epoch-first item-demand falls in exactly one
piece or outside every presence; the assignment classes are disjoint and
exhaustive over required, voluntary, and publish confirmations
(redundant confirmations excluded throughout,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— in particular *every required confirmation is charged somewhere, to a
bucket row or to the residual, by construction* — and each row bound is
an upper bound for its assigned class. Then:

1.  (i)
    *(Once, ever, per pair.)* No user’s required count for any pair
    $`(v,t)`$ exceeds one over the deployment’s lifetime
    ([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    exceptions per
    Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    a fortiori one per epoch; required confirmations of $`(v,t)`$ belong
    to distinct demanders of the pair.
2.  (ii)
    *(Row bounds.)* Every pipeline-component confirmation is assigned to
    exactly one row of
    Table [S2](#A6.T2 "Table S2 ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    under the retrospective charging convention above, with the stated
    per-epoch bounds; cross-epoch crediting of an already-logged event
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
    Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b))
    is a relabel adding no event to any epoch.
3.  (iii)
    *(Split.)* Summing rows, there are $`A(M)`$ and $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$
    depending only on protocol constants, with

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    A(M)=\mathcal{O}\!\big(E_{\max}\,c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}\,(N+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f)(1+\kappa)\big)\ \text{(via $N^{+}<N+D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq 2N$)},
    ``` |  |

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    B_{\mathrm{fl}}=\mathcal{O}\!\big(E_{\max}\,c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(1+(1-p_{b})\,\kappa)\big),
    ``` |  |

    such that
    $`\mathbb{E}[C^{\mathrm{pipe}}_{v}]\ \leq\ A(M)\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]\;+\;B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]`$;
    the pipeline required total obeys the same bound. Explicit
    constants:
    Lemma [S8.18](#A8.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S8.18 (Explicit forms of 𝐴(𝑀) and 𝐵_fl). ‣ S8.3 Explicit ledger constants ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (§[S8.3](#A8.SS3 "S8.3 Explicit ledger constants ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
4.  (iv)
    *(Pathwise, all baseline-counted confirmations.)* Let $`C_{v}`$
    count all required, voluntary, and publish confirmations of $`v`$’s
    exact bytes in the epoch, wherever they fall — ledger-charged and
    residual alike; redundant confirmations and option-induced cache
    confirmations excluded
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    Corollary [S6.6](#A6.Thmtheorem6 "Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options –). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    In the single-epoch model, with
    $`K:=E_{\max}(c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{p}}k+1)`$,

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    C_{v}\ \leq\ c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,n_{v}+K\,\mathbf{1}\{n_{v}\geq 1\}:
    ``` |  |

    every required confirmation of a pair of $`v`$ belongs to a demander
    of the pair — its confirmer’s own attempted use fires the gate,
    hence realizes the latent indicator (required-approval clause,
    §[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    inside or outside any shared-tier presence — at most
    $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ pairs per demander (one per pair,
    [INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    voluntary confirmations exist only at invitation surfaces, by
    definition
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    and invitations per epoch are deterministically capped at
    $`E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}`$ re-entry notifications plus
    $`E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ suspension prompts, *independently of
    current-epoch demand* — notified endorsers and prompted adopters
    need not be current-epoch demanders — with joint deduplication
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi));
    the owner contributes at most $`E_{\max}`$ publish confirmations
    (one accepting publish per opened entry: a cap-exhausted submission
    is ineligible and records no accepting confirmation;
    Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
    Every term vanishes on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$, by the event-based vanishing
    clause of the owner-coupling convention and the required-approval
    clause
    (§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
    no latent demander means no attempted use, hence no required
    confirmation, and no entry, review, invitation, or publish
    confirmation occurs in the epoch, whatever presence is carried in.

|  Row |  Kind |  Bound per item per epoch |
|----|----|----|

credited by the close of the logging epoch, within-epoch banked credits included; cross-epoch crediting relabels a prior epoch’s event and adds nothing), credited $`\Rightarrow`$ authority-active (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)); $`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ demanded tools ([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")), entries $`\leq E_{\max}`$ deterministically (entry cap, Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)), credited sets identity-disjoint across entries (Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")); vindication-credited prompted acceptances included, required or invited alike. |

Stable promoted intervals are charged to no row: their required gates are ledger residual (Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)). |
|  Freeze-bucket confirmations |  required |  expected current-epoch disputes and reviews, plus the at most one carry-in instance, $`\leq\bar{D}_{v}`$; each admits $`\leq\kappa`$ arriving demanders in expectation while unresolved (Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")) — item-arrivals during the freeze or suspension, exactly what Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust") counts; each such demander (including every demander gating during a suspension, Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)) is charged $`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ confirmations; total $`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\bar{D}_{v}\,\kappa`$ in expectation. Each is owed on any unpromoted pair regardless (Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)). |

Bucket rows use the conservative $`E_{\star}=E_{\max}+1`$

windows need only $`E_{\max}`$. Stable promoted intervals are charged to

under

and no third party can disturb it

this is

*(ii)* *Weight-bearing:* within an entry, credited endorsements per tool
number at most $`N^{+}`$ by the credit caps
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)),
banked credits filling slots the same caps govern; each credited

(Lemma [S5.3](#A5.Thmtheorem3 "Lemma S5.3 (Entry disjointness). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
entries per epoch at most $`E_{\max}`$ (the entry cap of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
republications and post-eviction republications included). *Buckets:*
within the epoch, the item’s shared-tier presence partitions into the

$`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ pairs, so
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
demand clause (scoped to exactly these two piece types) bounds
window/candidate-dormancy occupancy by
$`c_{\mathrm{tool}}(\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0})`$ per piece; each such
demander is charged at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ required
pair-confirmations (once per pair per transaction,
Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");

[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
giving the two bucket rows with the factor $`E_{\star}`$.

bounds each freeze or review’s arriving demanders by $`\kappa`$ in

under

counted below within the review cap) — hence only during window or

An honest identity’s initiating rejection is the rejecting branch of its

with tool or reasoning target while $`v`$ is unfrozen (an earlier

making the gate covered, hence inert; an earlier rejecting decision —

— would make the present one non-initiating; abandonment records
nothing). The trial is indexed at the pre-outcome header atom of an
audit-recorded first pair-decision, so its occurrence never selects the
outcome, and the occurrences are capped by
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
first-pair-decision clause: at most $`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0}`$ per
pair per piece, $`\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ pairs, over at most
$`E_{\star}`$ window pieces and $`E_{\star}`$ candidate-dormancy pieces
— conservatively
$`2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}(\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0})`$ candidate
occurrences, each rejecting a benign item with conditional probability

Lemma [S8.1](#A8.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S8.1 (Decision-conditioned content bounds). ‣ Dispositions. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)),
contributing the first term. *Invited reconsiderations* are epoch-scoped
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):

$`\leq c_{\mathrm{acc}}f`$ in total; or terminal (eviction or expiry),

The carry-in instance adds $`1`$. Summing gives $`\bar{D}_{v}`$.
*Voluntary and publish rows:*
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

*(iii)* Summing the row bounds (with $`E_{\star}`$ in the bucket rows
and the carry-in term of $`\bar{D}_{v}`$) and collecting the coefficient
of $`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}`$ gives the split; every row’s pathwise count
vanishes on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$ (the event-based vanishing clause of the
owner-coupling convention,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
no entries, reviews, invitations, or demanders on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$,
whatever presence is carried in), so each demand-free term is carried

applied to the indicator-stopped counts), multiplying it by
$`\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]`$; the explicit algebra, with the stated

Each required confirmation belongs to a distinct demander, so the

*(iv)* With
$`K:=E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{p}}k+E_{\max}`$:

|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
C_{v}\ \leq\ c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,n_{v}+K\,\mathbf{1}\{n_{v}\geq 1\}.

Required: by the required-approval clause
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
every user making a required approval of a pair of $`v`$ is a latent
demander of $`v`$, contributing at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$
pair-confirmations, once per pair per transaction and once ever required
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));

(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
which are epoch-scoped and deterministically capped at
$`E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}`$ re-entry notifications plus
$`E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ suspension prompts, with joint deduplication
and boundary expiry
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),
independently of current-epoch demand; publish: at most $`E_{\max}`$
(one per opened entry;
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
Every term vanishes on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$: no latent demander means no
attempted use, hence no required confirmation (required-approval
clause); an entry requires a current-epoch submission (owner demand); a
review or dispute opens at a latent demander’s protocol-bearing
````
