````math
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi));
a carried-in freeze with no current-epoch arrivals charges nothing. ∎

#### S6.4 Saturation

###### Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form).

Let $`\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}\subseteq\mathcal{V}`$ be the benign
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
assumption-conforming items — those to which the $`p_{b}`$,
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
hypotheses of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
apply — and write
$`V_{\mathrm{good}}(M):=\mathbb{E}|\{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}:n_{v}\geq 1\}|\leq V(M)`$
and
$`d_{\mathrm{good}}:=\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}}p_{v}\leq d`$.
Then Under
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the competence bound of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with $`A(M)`$, $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$, $`\kappa`$ as there,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}]\ \leq\ A(M)\,\frac{V_{\mathrm{good}}(M)}{M}\;+\;B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d_{\mathrm{good}},
``` |  |

where $`\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}`$ counts all pipeline-component
shareable confirmations, required and voluntary
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
over $`\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}`$; the ledger residual
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
charging convention) is bounded separately by
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
and added in
Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The first term is carried by the number of distinct demanded items and
vanishes under saturation; the second is the *front-loading term*: item
popularity has cancelled out of it, leaving only the front-loading
multiple $`\bar{\gamma}`$ against the standalone single-user shareable
mass $`d`$. Demand on the complement is charged at the single-user cap
and enters the residual $`r_{\mathrm{bad}}`$ of
Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Proof.

By
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
$`\mathbb{E}[C^{\mathrm{pipe}}_{v}]\leq A(M)\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]`$.
Summing over $`v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}`$:
$`\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}}\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]=\mathbb{E}|\{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}:n_{v}\geq 1\}|=V_{\mathrm{good}}(M)`$
and
$`\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}}\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]=Md_{\mathrm{good}}`$;
divide by $`M`$. ($`E_{\max}`$ inside $`A(M)`$ is a deterministic
per-epoch entry bound,
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i);
no expectation over entry counts is needed.) ∎

###### Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation).

Under
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the competence bound of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and — consumed only by the limit ($`\to 0`$) clauses below —
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):

1.  (i)
    if $`V(M)=o(M)`$ and $`A(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$, then
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}]\leq o(1)+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d_{\mathrm{good}}`$:
    the ledger-counted shareable cost falls to at most the front-loading
    multiple $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}`$ of the standalone
    single-user shareable mass, independently of item popularity; if in
    addition $`\bar{\gamma}(M)(1+\kappa(M))\to 0`$, then
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}]\to 0`$ (an
    upper-bound statement: the displayed bounds vanish);
2.  (ii)
    with $`V(M)=\Theta(M^{\beta})`$, $`\beta\in(0,1)`$, the protocol
    constants fixed, and additionally $`f(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ and
    $`\inf_{M}\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}(M)>0`$ — hence
    $`\kappa(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$, so $`A(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ and
    $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$; the added hypotheses are not
    implied by fixing the protocol constants, $`f`$ being an adversary
    resource and $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ a behavioural parameter —
    (i)’s hypothesis holds automatically:
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}]\leq\mathcal{O}(M^{\beta-1})+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d_{\mathrm{good}}`$,
    vanishing whenever $`\bar{\gamma}(M)\to 0`$ (under these hypotheses
    equivalent to (i)’s condition
    $`\bar{\gamma}(M)(1+\kappa(M))\to 0`$). This is the fixed-adversary,
    fixed-constants regime; the growing-adversary regime is the corridor
    (§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
3.  (iii)
    *(Ledger residual, benign conforming component.)* under
    [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and
    [A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    the expected per-user required cost charged to no ledger row *over
    the benign,
    [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-conforming
    items* — the ledger residual of
    Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
    required confirmations of demanders whose epoch-first item-demand
    falls in a stable promoted interval (in particular handle-expressed
    use of a live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$ pair, which gates under
    Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
    or outside every shared-tier presence (before first publication,
    after retirement, or after demotion); residual demand on poisoned or
    [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-violating
    pairs enters $`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$
    (Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    instead — is at most
    $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\big(D_{0}(M)\,V(M)/M+\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\big)`$
    ($`d_{\mathrm{good}}\leq d`$, $`V_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\leq V(M)`$ as
    in
    Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    This bound vanishes if, in addition, $`D_{0}(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$ and
    $`\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$; under
    [A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    the latter follows from $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$. In particular,
    under the Heaps form $`V(M)=\Theta(M^{\beta})`$ of clause (ii),
    $`D_{0}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ supplies the product condition. The
    product condition is an additional rate hypothesis of this vanishing
    conclusion: neither
    [A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    nor clause (i)’s hypotheses alone implies it.

###### Proof.

(i)–(ii) Immediate from
Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
$`A(M)V(M)/M=o(1)`$ by hypothesis (under Heaps’ form with the hypotheses
of (ii) — protocol constants fixed, $`f(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$,
$`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ bounded below — $`A(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$,
$`\kappa(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$, and $`V(M)/M=\mathcal{O}(M^{\beta-1})`$),
and
$`B_{\mathrm{fl}}=\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(1+\kappa))=\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}(1+\kappa))`$
($`c_{\mathrm{tool}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ absorbed), so the second term is
$`\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}(1+\kappa)\bar{\gamma})\,d_{\mathrm{good}}`$,
vanishing whenever $`\bar{\gamma}(M)(1+\kappa(M))\to 0`$, the mass
factor being uniformly bounded ($`d_{\mathrm{good}}\leq d`$,
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
(a sufficient condition: the displayed bound is an upper bound, and
degenerate parameter regimes, e.g. $`p_{b}=1`$, can shrink it further).
(iii) Fix a benign,
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-conforming
item $`v`$ and a target $`t`$. Every required confirmation of $`(v,t)`$
belongs to a distinct demander of the pair
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Under the charging convention of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
each is charged to a bucket row (its demander’s epoch-first item-demand
lying in a ledger-charged piece), to the weight row (credited), or to
the ledger residual; nothing is uncharged. The residual required
confirmations of $`(v,t)`$ number exactly $`U_{v,t}`$
([A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
with $`U_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$ pathwise; conditioning on $`n_{v,t}`$ and
applying
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(whose bound holds trivially on $`\{n_{v,t}=0\}`$, where $`U_{v,t}=0`$),

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[U_{v,t}]\ \leq\ D_{0}(M)\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v,t}\geq 1]+\varepsilon(M)\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v,t}].
``` |  |

Now sum over *all* targets $`t`$, using
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
pathwise on each term:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{t}\mathbb{P}[n_{v,t}\geq 1]=\mathbb{E}\big[\#\{t:n_{v,t}\geq 1\}\big]\ \leq\ c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1],
``` |  |

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{t}\mathbb{E}[n_{v,t}]=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t}n_{v,t}\Big]\ \leq\ c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v}],
``` |  |

the first because at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ tools carry demand and
none does on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$ ($`n_{v,t}\leq n_{v}`$), so
$`\#\{t:n_{v,t}\geq 1\}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\mathbf{1}\{n_{v}\geq 1\}`$
pathwise; the second by
$`\sum_{t}n_{v,t}\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,n_{v}`$. Summing over the
benign,
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-conforming
items
($`\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}}\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]=V_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\leq V(M)`$,
$`\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{good}}}\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]=M\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)`$,
Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and dividing by $`M`$ gives
$`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\big(D_{0}(M)V(M)/M+\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\big)`$,
which vanishes under the additional rate hypotheses of the statement
($`D_{0}(M)V(M)=o(M)`$; $`\varepsilon(M)d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$,
supplied under
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
by $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$), with $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$;
under the Heaps form of clause (ii), $`D_{0}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$
supplies the product condition. (Beyond
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the pair-to-item aggregation consumes only the bounded tool-spread of
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the vanishing limit additionally consumes the stated rate hypotheses
and, where $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$ is invoked,
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Demand at pairs where
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
fails enters $`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$,
Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
∎

###### Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading).

Fix an analyzed epoch $`e`$ satisfying the hypotheses of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(iii)
*including the additional rate conditions of clause (iii), read per
epoch*: $`D_{0,e}(M)\,V_{e}(M)=o(M)`$ and
$`\varepsilon_{e}(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good},e}(M)\to 0`$ (under
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
from $`\varepsilon_{e}(M)\to 0`$); let
$`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}=r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}(M)`$ be the expected
per-user demand mass in epoch $`e`$ on $`\mathsf{Bad}`$
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
or
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")-violating
pairs (each such pair charged at most once ever,
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
Then

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\limsup_{M\to\infty}\ \mathbb{E}\big[\bar{C}^{(e)}_{M,\mathrm{share}}\big]\;\leq\;\limsup_{M\to\infty}\Big(B_{\mathrm{fl}}(M)\,\bar{\gamma}(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}\;+\;r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}(M)\Big),
``` |  |

and under a shrinking-front-loading schedule with bounded mass
(§[S6.5](#A6.SS5 "S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
the first term vanishes. The personal component is a *lifetime*
inventory: at most $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$ expected required
pair-confirmations over the deployment’s life
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
The headline reading “lifetime personal inventory plus current-epoch
shared load” therefore satisfies
$`\limsup_{M\to\infty}\big(\text{lifetime personal}+\text{epoch-$e$ shared}\big)\leq d_{\mathrm{priv}}+\limsup_{M\to\infty}r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}(M)`$.
This is *not* a bound on the sum of shared costs over an unbounded
number of epochs: the present accounting yields a lifetime shared *upper
bound* whenever the following series of per-epoch upper bounds is
summable — a sufficient condition only: the terms are loose upper
bounds, so divergence of this series implies nothing about the true
lifetime cost — with the coverage parameters read per epoch
($`D_{0,e},\varepsilon_{e}`$; a deployment asserting
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with epoch-uniform parameters drops the subscripts),

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{e}\Big(A_{e}(M)\,\tfrac{V_{e}(M)}{M}+B_{\mathrm{fl}}^{(e)}(M)\,\bar{\gamma}_{e}(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good},e}\\
+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\big(D_{0,e}(M)\tfrac{V_{e}(M)}{M}+\varepsilon_{e}(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good},e}\big)+r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}\Big)<\infty,
``` |  |

in which case lifetime expected total cost is at most
$`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$ plus that sum; the lifetime shareable mass
comparison of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
($`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}`$) bounds the required component
unconditionally in any case. These are upper bounds; no matching lower
bound is claimed.

###### Proof.

Combine
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(iii)
over epoch $`e`$ with
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(iii);
the summable case is termwise. ∎

###### Remark S6.11 (Reading of Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

Four observations govern the interpretation of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
First, the residual charges are the design operating as intended: each
residual poisoned-demand confirmation is a personal gate inspection of
an unpromoted or flagged item, and each residual handle-arrival
confirmation is a personal gate inspection of bytes that reached this
user through an untrusted channel — the certificate amortises
trusted-channel reuse, never untrusted-channel arrival
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
[S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
both are exactly the inspections the design intends (cf.
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Second, the front-loading term is the price of certifying popular items
rather than an overhead: each within-window confirmation is a fresh
honest inspection *before finalisation*: exactly the pre-promotion
scrutiny the exponent $`N-f`$ of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
counts. Third, the bound is informative when
$`\bar{\gamma}\lesssim 1/B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$; for larger $`\bar{\gamma}`$
it remains valid but loose, a bounded multiple of $`d`$, with
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
the binding guarantee throughout. Fourth, these are conditional
*accounting* statements. Clauses (i)–(ii) consume the ledger,
smoothness, competence, juror-supply, and demand-shape hypotheses;
clause (iii) additionally consumes
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— the assumption carrying publication, promotion, and
arrival-representation coverage jointly — together with the product
condition $`D_{0}(M)V(M)=o(M)`$ and the remaining vanishing conditions
of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii).
The shrinking-front-loading conditions describe changing time geometry,
never a consequence of population growth alone
(Remark [S6.12](#A6.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S6.12 (Operational reading of the shrinking-front-loading rows). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
no clause derives coverage or shrinking front-loading from the protocol.
The assumption-free protocol guarantee is the pathwise cap of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),
with clause (ii) giving its reference-model standalone-mass ceiling.

#### S6.5 Conditional co-scaling

###### Status of the corridor.

The corridor collects, in one place, every constraint the co-scaling
result uses; each row exists elsewhere and none is new. Two of its rows
are *schedules* of protocol constants ($`g_{N},g_{k}`$), which a
deployment controls; the rest are empirical or behavioural properties
($`\beta`$, $`\bar{\gamma}`$, $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, $`q+p_{b}`$,
$`d`$, the coverage law $`(D_{0},\varepsilon)`$ of
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the Sybil bounds), which a deployment *measures*
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and cannot set. The co-scaling theorem is therefore a compatibility
statement: *if* the measured environment satisfies its rows, *then*
schedules exist under which security, resolution correctness, and budget
improve together; and the floor of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds outside the corridor unconditionally.

###### Remark S6.12 (Operational reading of the shrinking-front-loading rows).

For steady demand over an epoch of length $`L`$ with fixed window
$`T_{\mathrm{win}}`$, $`\bar{\gamma}\approx T_{\mathrm{win}}/L`$
*independently of $`M`$*
([A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
commentary): population growth alone does not shrink $`\bar{\gamma}`$.
The rows $`\bar{\gamma}(M)(1+\kappa(M))=o(1)`$ and
$`\bar{\gamma}(M)k(M)\to 0`$ therefore describe deployments whose *time
geometry* changes with scale — finalisation windows shrinking relative
to the epoch, or demand growing more diffuse as the population grows —
and are to be read as measured properties of that geometry, not
consequences of $`M\to\infty`$. Where they fail, the
fixed-$`\bar{\gamma}`$ reading of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the operating point: pipeline cost falls to the front-loading
multiple $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d_{\mathrm{good}}`$ of the
standalone single-user shareable mass, with
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
binding throughout
(Remark [S6.11](#A6.Thmtheorem11 "Remark S6.11 (Reading of Theorem ). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

A concrete schedule satisfying every row simultaneously:
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$, $`f(M)=\log M`$, $`N(M)=2\log M`$,
$`k(M)=f_{\mathrm{s}}+\log^{2}M`$, against measured
$`\bar{\gamma}(M)=\log^{-3}M`$ and bounded measured $`d`$
([A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
then with $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ bounded below,
$`\kappa=\Theta(\log^{2}M)`$, so
$`\bar{\gamma}(1+\kappa)=\Theta(\log^{-1}M)\to 0`$; for an illustrative
measured coverage law with
$`D_{0}\asymp N/\bar{\gamma}=\Theta(\log^{4}M)`$ and empirically
validated $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$,
$`D_{0}V=\Theta(M^{\beta}\log^{4}M)=o(M)`$; and
$`Nk=\Theta(\log^{3}M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$.

###### Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost).

Adopt
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with the default bars,
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and saturation $`V(M)=\Theta(M^{\beta})`$, $`\beta\in(0,1)`$. Assume
also the coverage-rate condition of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
$`D_{0}(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$ (under the Heaps form, equivalently
$`D_{0}(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$; $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$ per
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Suppose $`f(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ and $`q+p_{b}>1`$; fix
$`\gamma_{0}\in(0,q+p_{b}-1)`$. Choose margin schedules
$`g_{N}(M),g_{k}(M)\to\infty`$ with $`g_{N},g_{k}=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ and
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}(M)=o(g_{k}(M))`$, and set $`N(M)=f(M)+g_{N}(M)`$,
$`k(M)=f_{\mathrm{s}}(M)+g_{k}(M)`$,
$`m(M)=f_{\mathrm{s}}(M)+\lceil(1-q+\gamma_{0})g_{k}(M)\rceil`$,
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}(M)=k(M)+1-m(M)`$ (so every panel that gathers $`k`$
verdicts resolves decisively and $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}>f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ for
all large $`M`$). All protocol caps and multiplicity parameters not
explicitly scheduled here are uniformly $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$ in $`M`$
(fixed TCB configuration along the scaling,
convention ([C8](#A1.I2.i8 "Item C8 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
in particular
$`E_{\max},\rho_{\mathrm{sub}},r_{\max},c_{\mathrm{ceil}},c_{\mathrm{p}},s_{0},D_{\mathrm{pool}},c_{\mathrm{batch}},c_{\mathrm{cand}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$,
hence $`c_{\mathrm{acc}}=c_{\mathrm{ceil}}+r_{\max}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$,
while $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ by
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
This is load-bearing: the conclusions
$`A(M)=\mathcal{O}\!\big(E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(N+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f)(1+\kappa)\big)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$
and $`K(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ consume it. Assume further the cross-term
condition $`N(M)\,k(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ (which, since $`N>f`$, implies
$`f(M)k(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$) and the shrinking front-loading condition
$`\bar{\gamma}(M)\,k(M)\to 0`$ ($`\kappa=\Theta(k)`$ for
$`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ bounded below); both are achievable by choosing
$`g_{k}`$ to grow slowly against the measured front-loading of the
demand stream. Then:

1.  (i)
    *(Safety, per poisoned entry.)*
    $`\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion of a fixed poisoned entry}]\leq(1-q)^{g_{N}(M)}+e^{-2\gamma_{0}^{2}g_{k}(M)}\to 0`$
    (Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
    against adaptive presentation and at any reach
    ([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    *(System-wide, per anchor epoch.)* If additionally
    $`2f(M)\,\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}\big((1-q)^{g_{N}(M)}+e^{-2\gamma_{0}^{2}g_{k}(M)}\big)\to 0`$,
    the per-anchor-epoch bound of
    Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    over all adversary-published attempts anchored in the epoch also
    vanishes; the example schedule satisfies this: with $`f=\log M`$,
    $`g_{N}=\log M`$ (natural logarithm throughout; a fixed change of
    logarithm base only rescales the schedule by a constant and leaves
    every limit below unaffected),
    $`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}(1-q)^{g_{N}}=2\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}\log M\cdot M^{\ln(1-q)}\to 0`$,
    and $`2f\rho_{\mathrm{sub}}\,e^{-2\gamma_{0}^{2}\log^{2}M}\to 0`$ a
    fortiori;
2.  (ii)
    *(Wrongful eviction.)* with
    $`\delta_{b}:=\tfrac{q+p_{b}-1-\gamma_{0}}{2}>0`$, for all
    sufficiently large $`M`$ a benign item is evicted, penalising its
    publisher, with probability at most
    $`e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}g_{k}(M)}\to 0`$
    (Propositions [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    equivalently
    $`\mathbb{P}[\text{vindication}]\geq\mathbb{P}[\text{resolution}]-e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}g_{k}(M)}`$,
    resolution being the demand-side event of
    Remark [S5.21](#A5.Thmtheorem21 "Remark S5.21 (Resolution as a demand-side event). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
3.  (iii)
    *(Budget, per analyzed epoch.)* with $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$
    bounded below,
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}^{\mathrm{pipe,good}}_{M}]\leq A(M)\,\mathcal{O}(M^{\beta-1})+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}=o(1)`$,
    and the benign ledger residual is $`o(1)`$
    (Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)):
    the analyzed epoch’s shared confirmation load vanishes, while the
    lifetime personal inventory remains at most $`d_{\mathrm{priv}}`$
    (Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
    and demand on $`\mathsf{Bad}`$ or assumption-violating pairs adds
    that epoch’s residual $`r^{(e)}_{\mathrm{bad}}`$, bounded pathwise
    by
    Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i).
    No claim is made about the sum over an unbounded number of epochs
    without the summability condition of
    Corollary [S6.10](#A6.Thmtheorem10 "Corollary S6.10 (Per-epoch shared cost; lifetime reading). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

All three hold with no assumption on how widely a poison spreads.

###### Proof.

(i) $`N-f=g_{N}`$, and
$`\delta=\frac{m-f_{\mathrm{s}}}{k-f_{\mathrm{s}}}-(1-q)\geq\gamma_{0}`$
by the choice of $`m`$, so
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives the bound with exponents $`g_{N}`$ and $`2\gamma_{0}^{2}g_{k}`$.
(ii)
$`m/(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})\leq(1-q+\gamma_{0})+(f_{\mathrm{s}}+1)/g_{k}(M)`$;
since $`1-q+\gamma_{0}=p_{b}-2\delta_{b}`$ by the definition of
$`\delta_{b}`$ (using $`\gamma_{0}<q+p_{b}-1`$, so $`\delta_{b}>0`$),
and $`(f_{\mathrm{s}}+1)/g_{k}(M)\to 0`$ is eventually at most
$`\delta_{b}`$, we get $`m/(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})\leq p_{b}-\delta_{b}`$ for
all large $`M`$, and
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
applies;
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
restates the same event as the publisher penalty. (iii) By
Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
$`A(M)=\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(N(M)+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f(M))(1+\kappa(M)))=o(M^{1-\beta})`$
by the margin schedules, the cross-term condition, and
$`\kappa=\Theta(k)`$, so the first term is
$`o(M^{1-\beta})\cdot\mathcal{O}(M^{\beta-1})=o(1)`$; the second term is
$`\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}\,\kappa(M)\,\bar{\gamma}(M))\,d=o(1)`$ by the
shrinking front-loading condition and the bounded mass
([A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the residual clause of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
applies by the coverage-rate hypothesis $`D_{0}(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$ assumed
in the statement, with $`\varepsilon(M)\,d_{\mathrm{good}}(M)\to 0`$
from $`\varepsilon(M)\to 0`$
([A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and
[A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
∎

###### Remark S6.14 (Role of the saturation exponent).

Smaller $`\beta`$ is uniformly favourable: faster budget decay
$`M^{-(1-\beta)}`$ *and* a weaker Sybil requirement
$`f(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$. There is no design trade-off along $`\beta`$:
it is not a design parameter but an empirical property of the
community’s demand stream, to be measured
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
which references neither $`\beta`$ nor the demand model, remains
available at any $`\beta`$ under its own hypotheses

#### S7.2 Design rationale

Four rationale remarks whose content adjoins specific formal results
(the freshness asymmetry, the reading of $`q`$, the accountability
calibration, and the roles of the protocol clocks) are set as numbered
Remarks adjacent to their points of use
(Remarks [S4.7](#A4.Thmtheorem7 "Remark S4.7 (Why the freshness asymmetry is safe). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S5.26](#A5.Thmtheorem26 "Remark S5.26 (Roles of 𝑇_win, 𝑇_pan, 𝑇_exp; the demand-paced design). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and are indexed here for completeness. The notes below record the
remaining design rationale.

###### Note N1 (Model lineage).

The target property is an integrity property: content from an untrusted
source must not drive a sensitive action unless the user explicitly
authorised the exact value involved. Integrity is the lattice dual of
Denning’s confidentiality flow [Denning (1976)](#bib.bib13); [Denning &
Denning (1977)](#bib.bib14), made precise by Biba [Biba
(1977)](#bib.bib5); the behavioural definition is noninterference
[Goguen & Meseguer (1982)](#bib.bib19), proved by the unwinding method
[Goguen & Meseguer (1984)](#bib.bib20) transported to a small-step
operational semantics [Volpano et al. (1996)](#bib.bib44); [Sabelfeld &
Myers (2003)](#bib.bib38). Two refinements distinguish PerMIT. First,
PerMIT *does* permit untrusted-derived values to reach sensitive
actions, but only after a user confirmation; a confirmation is an
*endorsement* [Myers et al. (2006)](#bib.bib33), and the danger that an
attacker controls *what* is endorsed is ruled out by robustness
[Zdancewic & Myers (2005)](#bib.bib53); [Myers et al.
(2006)](#bib.bib33). Second, PerMIT lets verified crystallized knowledge
inform the Protected LLM’s reasoning; the right noninterference
statement is therefore one modulo the release history, in the delimited-
and gradual-release tradition [Sabelfeld & Sands (2009)](#bib.bib40);
[Sabelfeld & Myers (2004)](#bib.bib39); [Askarov & Sabelfeld
(2007)](#bib.bib3), with the display transcript playing the role of the
release-event history. The carve-out is the *full* transcript: candidate
previews as well as decision-pane displays, rejections as well as
acceptances
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The substrate, including the provenance-tracking interpreter and the
separation of a trusted orchestrating model from a quarantined reader,
is CaMeL [Debenedetti et al. (2025)](#bib.bib12); we name these the
Protected LLM ($`P`$) and the Quarantined Reader LLM ($`Q`$), realizing
$`Q`$ as a Recursive Language Model [Zhang et al. (2025)](#bib.bib54).
Related efforts: AgentDojo [Debenedetti et al. (2024)](#bib.bib11),
information-flow control for agents [Costa et al. (2025)](#bib.bib9),
memory-poisoning defenses [Wei et al. (2025)](#bib.bib46), collaborative
memory [Rezazadeh et al. (2025)](#bib.bib37). CaMeL leaves formal
verification as future work ([Debenedetti et al., 2025](#bib.bib12),
§10). PerMIT leaves planning and tool choice to the agent while bounding
its observations and data flows through the finite interface of
Figures [S2](#A2.F2 "Figure S2 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
including tool-output capture and argument mediation. The channel
analysis
(Lemmas [S3.17](#A3.Thmtheorem17 "Lemma S3.17 (Interface completeness). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
checks this written specification clause by clause.

###### Note N2 (The endorsement unit).

Endorsement is per (value, tool) and cached indefinitely while the
relevant local copy is retained. A conforming instantiation of the
requirements-level
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
would bound its scope-checked tool-authorization lifetime, but is
outside the proved model. Combinations, orderings, and timings of
separately endorsed values are ungated. The policy does not bind
argument position, task, purpose, or the complete argument tuple.
Reasoning Integrity excludes additional hidden influence when the
complete display transcript is fixed; it does not certify the safety of
later combinations
([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
refine tool-scoped checks, not complete-transaction approval.

###### Note N3 (The reader asymmetry).

$`Q`$ may read the whole store because its output is always untrusted or
handle-hidden; $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ may read only the endorsed store
because its output flows to $`P`$ as readable endorsed bytes. Neither
can be relaxed without breaking a theorem: a $`\mathsf{U}`$-reading
$`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ violates
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
an $`\mathbb{E}`$-emitting $`Q`$ violates
Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Note N4 (Failure indistinguishability, operationally).

Under
Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the agent cannot distinguish “the untrusted store contained nothing
useful” from “the reader failed while looking”: both worlds return the
same operation-determined handle, so neither the contents nor the volume
of untrusted memory can signal through the failure path. Likewise,
whether an identifier is occupied by a $`\mathsf{U}`$-block is a fact
the attacker influences through the number of blocks captured per call,
which is why occupancy is never observable
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
The store-quota policy of
convention ([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
exists because a volume-dependent error would reopen exactly this
channel
([S7](#Thmobjx7 "Analysis S7 (Store-exhaustion side channel). ‣ S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N5 (The human channel).

[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
idealizes the user’s typing as exogenous. In reality, displayed content
can steer what the user subsequently types, which enters as trusted
input. Influence of displayed content on typing is accounted for exactly
insofar as that content appears in the display transcript, which, by
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e),
records *every* attacker-influenceable rendering the user sees, on both
surfaces. The design therefore discharges the idealization’s practical
content by logging both surfaces: the release history covers every
surface through which such influence can pass, so
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
[N7](#Thmnotex7 "Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
remain faithful even where
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
frays. The residual is disclosed at
[S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

###### Note N6 (The batch gate is all-or-nothing).

The selected batch design is all-or-nothing: a per-page decision
returned to $`P`$ would leak the attacker-influenceable page count
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)),
and the aggregate decision avoids that channel at the cost that one
poisoned element forces rejection of the whole batch — an availability
and attention cost, not a safety gap. Sufficiency of this design is what
is established; no impossibility of alternative fixed-shape or padded
designs is claimed. The user may reject at any page, aborting the
remainder
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d)),
so attacker-imposed attention is bounded by the user’s own patience,
never compelled. Both facts argue for sizing $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$
conservatively
([S12](#Thmobjx12 "Analysis S12 (Batch-gate attention). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented).

The harness records every display event, selection renderings included,
in a hash-chained audit log, a tamper-evident materialization of
$`\mathsf{DT}`$.
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
therefore has operational force: the transcript supplies a complete
record of the modeled release surfaces relevant to the protected
behaviours — ungated sinks, Protected-LLM operations, tool invocations
(Definition [S3.11](#A3.Thmtheorem11 "Definition S3.11 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— missing no surface on which attacker-shaped content was ever rendered;
it does not by itself reconstruct causation, timing, unreleased tool
outputs, or attacker identity. This is not a proof that the user cannot
be manipulated; it is a proof that any attacker influence on those
behaviours must pass through the logged display transcript or an
explicitly accepted endorsement. Logging makes influence visible and
attributable after the fact — attributable to a recorded release or
decision, not necessarily to an attacker identity; the prevention half
of the design is
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
gate, which stops any value that is neither user-typed nor endorsed
(personally, or, under delegation, by a qualifying community quorum) for
the exact sensitive tool from ever crossing that boundary
(argument-value integrity: the decision to invoke a tool, and
zero-argument sensitive calls, are scoped at
§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(X)).

###### Note N8 (What previews can and cannot do).

An adversarial reader can decorate a malicious candidate with a
benign-looking preview. Within the formal model, previews are inert:
they never enter $`\sigma_{P}`$
(Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and endorsement binds to the true resolved bytes on the decision pane
([A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so a preview can never forge an endorsement. Outside the formal model, a
preview can influence the human: what the user chooses to examine, and,
through
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
idealization, what the user subsequently types. This is precisely why
previews are included in the display transcript and the audit log
([S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N9 (What the gate does to the detection task).

The confirmation gate reshapes the detection task an honest inspector
faces, in three architectural ways. First, stealth is eliminated by
construction:
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
renders the exact bytes that will flow, in full, on every gated
invocation, so no gated content can reach a sensitive action unseen —
there is no channel by which poison avoids display altogether. Second,
hijacking-style content — bytes written to be read as instructions
rather than data — is surfaced on the decision pane out of the narrative
context it was designed to exploit, isolated against a fixed provenance
zone
([A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
this plausibly raises $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ for that class of poison, but
it is offered as motivation for the parameter, never as a proof of it:
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ remains an empirical, weakest-target quantity
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
estimated by logging, not derived from the display design. Third,
because every gate decision is logged
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
$`q`$ is made log-measurable rather than merely posited: the validation
protocol of
[N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is only possible because the architecture records the events it needs.
None of this touches *semantic* poison — content that is simply false or
misleading, with no injection mechanism for display to expose — which
gains nothing from being shown out of context and remains exactly the
disclosed residual of
[S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
consumed by no proof in this document.

###### Note N10 (Federated lineage).

The federated tier is built on machinery network security has already
made rigorous: threshold endorsement from the PGP web of trust [Maurer
(1996)](#bib.bib31); transparency and revocation from Certificate
Transparency [Laurie et al. (2013)](#bib.bib24); [Laurie et al.
````
