(2021)](#bib.bib25); the identity-cost requirement of the Sybil
literature [Douceur (2002)](#bib.bib16); [Dwork & Naor
(2007)](#bib.bib17) , the precise reason the scaling results are
conditional on an attested or cost-bounded setting. The panel’s
competence condition is the classical jury condition [Grofman et al.
(1983)](#bib.bib21); [Allen et al. (2021)](#bib.bib2); [Martel et al.
(2024)](#bib.bib30).

###### Note N11 (What pool diversity buys).

The requirement $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ caps per-pool verdicts and mixes
the fresh-inspector population, attacking correlated blind spots and
demand-side selection bias among panelists. Diversity bounds
*correlation*, not the *minimum*: since the adversary chooses whom to
present the item to
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
$`q`$ remains a uniform lower bound over the honest identities the
adversary can target, and the pool caps of
Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
force those targets to span $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ pools rather than one
cluster, raising the effective bound from the most fallible cluster
toward the most fallible identity per pool, never to a population
average. The per-person correlation across *logged* re-inspections is
discharged structurally by fresh-inspection counting
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the residual across unlogged personal inspections is a calibration
matter
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S13](#Thmobjx13 "Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N12 (Reputation farming).

$`f`$, $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$, and $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are lifetime totals
over every identity the adversary ever controls
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
capped by the attestation layer’s issuance; farming weight before
spending it changes *when* the capacity exists, never its total, so no
bound stated against the lifetime totals can be outrun. Publisher
penalties
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii))
only shrink the adversary’s capacity below these totals, so every bound
stated against them remains valid. The economic deterrent of burning
accrued reputation is real but deliberately unused in any proof: the
proofs assume the attacker spends everything
([S3](#Thmobjx3 "Analysis S3 (Reputation farming). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N13 (The $`\mathsf{evict}`$ residual).

$`\mathsf{evict}`$ is owner-scoped but $`P`$-invocable and ungated, so
an *erring* (not attacker-steered, which
Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
exclude) Protected LLM can remove its owner’s endorsed blocks without a
confirmation; the no-deletion guarantee of
Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is a third-party guarantee only. Deployments wanting first-party cover
may gate $`\mathsf{evict}`$ on $`\mathbb{E}`$-labelled blocks like any
sensitive call, a further monotone hardening in the sense of
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The uniform-$`\mathsf{ack}`$ totalisation of $`\mathsf{evict}`$
(Figure [S3](#A2.F3 "Figure S3 ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
convention [(v)](#A2.SS2a "S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
changes only the reply surface, never this capability: the residual is
unchanged, and the realised outcome remains visible to the owner in the
audit log. The residual includes evictions $`P`$ performs *in reaction
to* legitimate federation events (notifications are $`\mathbb{E}`$-level
log data): a third party can occasion such a reaction but not steer it —
Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
exclude any $`\mathsf{U}`$-derived influence on the choice — so this is
erring-agent behaviour, outside the threat model
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(V)),
not an attacker channel.

###### Note N14 (Availability degrades gracefully, never destructively).

All federated guarantees are safety guarantees; availability is
explicitly not guaranteed, but its loss is bounded *in harm* (in
required confirmations) per dispute: under
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
at most $`\kappa=(k{+}1)/\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ affected demander
arrivals in expectation, with exponential tail
(Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
if
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is additionally read over the entire unresolved-dispute demand horizon,
at most $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\kappa`$ additional required confirmations
in expectation, with the corresponding tail at thresholds scaled by
$`c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$; under the stated per-epoch reading of
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
only the corresponding per-epoch conversion is asserted, while the
pathwise per-user cap remains valid for a freeze of any duration
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii));
pathwise, independent of every federated and demand assumption
(persistence exceptions per
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
no affected user exceeds the single-user cap, regardless of the freeze’s
duration
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii));
recoverable (low wrongful-eviction risk,
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
accountable on both sides
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v),(vii));
and never destructive
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
in the worst case the shared tier contributes nothing and each user
verifies personally, within the single-user cap of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
The per-epoch free charge renews, so the adversary retains a per-epoch
throughput bounded in the three currencies of
Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv);
what it buys is bounded required-confirmation harm and bounded per-epoch
harassment throughput
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),(iv)),
never deletion — the *wall-clock duration* of an unresolved freeze is
deliberately unbounded, resolution being demand-paced with no deadline
(Remark [S5.21](#A5.Thmtheorem21 "Remark S5.21 (Resolution as a demand-side event). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
its harm, not its duration, is what is capped. A promoted benign item
can be harassed only through Suspended-state fast-track panels, at most
$`E_{\max}`$ per item per epoch
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi))
and penalty-escalating. An unpromoted benign candidate cannot be retired
by sequential vindicated disputes
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)(b)
exempts them,
[N15](#Thmnotex15 "Note N15 (The vindication exemption). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
each adversarial rejection buys one freeze, resolved at the item’s own
demand rate, while occupying a rejection slot and, beyond the first per
identity per epoch, escalating the rejecter’s accountability; the
adversary’s per-epoch freeze throughput against any item being bounded
(Lem. [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)),
what it buys is bounded required-confirmation harm within the
single-user cap — of unbounded wall-clock duration, the freeze being
demand-paced — never retirement, and the single-initiation clause caps
any identity, adversarial or honest, at one freeze per item per epoch,
so per-item harassment throughput is at most $`f`$ freezes per epoch
deterministically. The entry cap of
Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
is likewise availability-only: an item whose per-epoch entries are
exhausted (e.g. through repeated wrongful evictions, each already
exponentially rare,
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
waits for the epoch boundary with its banked credits and any live
promotion status intact
(convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
each demander meanwhile paying at most the cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
Under this invalidating semantics, a suspension additionally converts
its demanders’ ungated reuse into at most one required confirmation each
— the cap confirmation they would in any case owe on demotion
(Corollary [S6.5](#A6.Thmtheorem5 "Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— after which the pair is permanently covered by a local $`\mathsf{C}`$
copy; this is priced once per demander and never renewed.

###### Note N15 (The vindication exemption).

Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)(b)
counts only *non-vindicated* disputes toward expiry. The exemption is
what prevents both an adversary’s wrongful rejections (each vindicated,
each feeding the accountability schedule of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v))
and the honest wrongful-rejection noise, which arrives at rate
$`1-p_{b}`$ per benign fresh inspection and would otherwise, at the
co-scaling thresholds $`N(M)\to\infty`$ of
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
retire *every* item before promotion became arithmetically reachable,
from terminating a benign item. Under the default bars every resolved
dispute ends in vindication or eviction and every unresolved one ends in
expiry, so this trigger fires only through the optional neither-bar
outcome of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv);
it remains availability-only and conservative
(Lemma [S5.9](#A5.Thmtheorem9 "Lemma S5.9 (Hygiene preserves safety through bound uniformity). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering).

Post-promotion suspensions and re-verification add panel and
re-inspection events but never multiply any user’s required cost
(Corollary [S6.5](#A6.Thmtheorem5 "Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
local endorsements are permanent, so revocation campaigns tax the shared
tier’s voluntary and verdict effort, bounded per suspension by
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)
and the rate limits; a prior $`\mathsf{CC}`$-only user additionally owes
their first-ever required confirmation of the pair — a cost *within* the
cap, already counted inside $`d^{\infty}_{\mathrm{tool}}`$
(Corollary [S6.5](#A6.Thmtheorem5 "Corollary S6.5 (The cap under revocation). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
never beyond it. Re-verification draws its inspectors from identities
with no prior *logged* decision on the bytes (log-fresh,
Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
a cohort that can include previously exposed but never-logged
inspectors,
[Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so the probability of a uniformly convincing poison remaining uncaught
across $`E_{\mathrm{rv}}`$ re-verification rounds, each reaching a
cohort of new inspectors, is at most
$`(1-q_{c})^{E_{\mathrm{rv}}}\to 0`$, with $`q_{c}`$ the correlated
catch rate of
[S13](#Thmobjx13 "Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the mechanism’s strength scales with the supply of never-decided
inspectors (population growth and new demand), not with epoch renewal.
Grandfathering: items promoted at lower historical thresholds retain
$`\mathsf{CC}`$ but enter the re-verification queue until their
endorsement meets the current bar. Within the formal semantics,
first-party eviction aside
([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
nothing re-forces a confirmed pair’s authorization; a conforming
instantiation of the requirements-level
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
would re-force exactly the scope-checked tool authorization on lease
expiry — never reasoning readability — an explicit trade stated and to
be priced with that extension
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Note N17 (Validation without a user study).

Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the counting cores of
Lemmas [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"), [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are identities. Saturation ($`V(M)=o(M)`$), fractional temporal
smoothness
([A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
log each item’s realised front-loading fraction $`\gamma_{v}`$,
validated specifically on the most-demanded items, where population
averages would hide spikes), coverage sufficiency
([A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
log each item’s realized residual fraction $`U_{v,t}/n_{v,t}`$ *and* the
fast-path-vs-gate split of live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$ demand — the
handle-arrival fraction,
[S18](#Thmobjx18 "Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content). ‣ S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— stratified on the most-demanded items, with per-item time-to-promotion
against accumulated demand), tool-spread
([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
log per-item distinct-tool counts), bounded demand mass
([A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
log per-user distinct shareable-item demand per epoch across deployment
growth), and the verdict rate
([A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
log verdict-eligibility rates on disputed items) are modelling
assumptions checked by logging in the prototype and by replaying the
promotion and demand-paced panel mechanics in simulation while sweeping
the growth exponent, a replay of an algorithm, not an experiment on
people. The replay’s own fidelity is checked independently of any
behavioural parameter by the closed form of
§[S8.2](#A8.SS2 "S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
whose support-level consequences are byte-identity properties of the
implementation rather than statistical agreements. One caveat governs
the behavioural parameters specifically: $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$,
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, $`p_{b}`$, and $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ are
*uniform conditional* lower bounds, each validated on its own stratum
(gate inspections vs. eligible verdicts), on the prior-atom
$`\sigma`$-algebras of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
aggregate log rates do not directly estimate such bounds. Their
validation therefore reports stratified rates (by identity class,
presentation context, and flag state) rather than population averages,
uses lower confidence bounds rather than point estimates, corrects for
adaptive selection of inspection targets, and monitors nonstationarity
across epochs; the estimand is the infimum over strata, and the deployed
constants ($`N,k,m`$ margins, $`\theta_{\mathrm{acc}}`$,
$`c_{\mathrm{ceil}}`$) are set against that infimum with margin, never
against a mean. These stratified, lower-confidence-bound estimates are
*falsification and calibration* evidence: they can refute an assumed cap
— a stratum whose observed rate falls below the claimed bound — and can
inform recalibration, but they do not *certify* the uniform
infimum-over-history bounds $`q_{\mathrm{pre}},q_{\mathrm{pan}},p_{b}`$
require. Sparse or unobserved strata (rare identity classes, rare
presentation contexts) are not covered by any finite sample, and the
uniform bounds remain modelling hypotheses, not measured quantities. One
further caveat: the classification $`\mathsf{Bad}`$ is exogenous
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so the log alone cannot label a trial as poisoned or benign; estimating
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$, $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, and $`p_{b}`$ therefore
requires an exogenously labeled corpus — red-team–injected known-poison
items and expert-adjudicated benign samples — with the stratified
lower-confidence-bound machinery applied to the labeled trials.
Unlabeled log rates validate the protocol mechanics only
($`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, realised $`\gamma_{v}`$, $`U_{v,t}/n_{v,t}`$,
tool spread, demand mass).

###### Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections).

The ledger of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
covers every *counted* (required or voluntary) durable accepting
pair-confirmation of shareable items, redundant covered-gate acceptances
and the personal, per-task, and option-induced streams excluded or
separately charged
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S6.6](#A6.Thmtheorem6 "Corollary S6.6 (Budget under Options –). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
rejection and attention effort is a distinct resource with a two-sided
account. Under the durable semantics of
Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
there are no accepted-but-uncommitted confirmations: every accepting
review commits its copy. What remains uncounted is attention: rejected
dialogs, abandonment, batch-page review, repeated reviews of an
already-accepted pair within one transaction (counted once,
Definition [S2.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S2.5 (Sensitive sinks, gate transactions, and confirmations). ‣ Two scopes and one selector. ‣ S2.1 Configurations, labels, and roles ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and redundant covered-gate decisions. *Protocol-effective rejections*
are tightly capped: one dispute-initiation per identity per byte string
per epoch
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
at most $`r_{\max}`$ open slots, and the accountability schedule of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v).
*Rejection dialogs*, by contrast, recur: a user who rejects an uncovered
pair holds no local $`\mathsf{C}`$ copy, so each later attempted use of
that pair fires the gate again, and the later rejections are logged as
corroboration or advisory flags
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
— the *protocol* does not bound a user’s total rejection dialogs on one
value. What bounds them is the user’s own use stream and the exposure
caps: per retrieval at most $`c_{\mathrm{cand}}`$ candidates are
surfaced
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
disputed items are flagged and ordered last, paraphrase spam consumes
the submitter’s rate limit per byte-distinct variant
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and a $`P`$-emitted $`\mathsf{confirm}`$ or handle-expressed tool call
on a *covered* pair fires a covered gate, protocol-inert on both
branches
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
reasoning-target repetition on locally readable bytes included
(reasoning coverage,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)):
the resulting redundant confirmations and rejections have no shared-tier
effect and are excluded from every ledger count
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so agent repetition on covered values costs the user attention only,
disclosed here — and $`P`$ *can* re-emit $`\mathsf{confirm}`$ on a
repeatedly-rejected, *uncovered* handle every step: covered-gate
inertness neutralises covered values only, by design. Repeated dialogs
arising from the user’s own repeated attempts at an *uncovered* pair are
a first-party cost of declining, of the same character as the
$`\mathsf{evict}`$ residual
([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
attacker-steered repetition is excluded
(Lemmas [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
but the model places no constant on it. Accordingly, every
“bounded-harm” statement in this document is a statement about *required
user approvals*
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
with inspection effort disclosed here. One deployment device reduces
this attention cost without touching the semantics: the decision pane
may visibly badge a covered gate — the resolved bytes byte-match a local
in-scope copy, an owner-side deterministic fact
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
— and offer a one-tap accept; the gate, its display, and its logged
decision are unchanged. Interpreter-level rate-limiting of repeated
uncovered gate requests is a candidate further hardening, monotone in
the sense of
Proposition [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
it is an operational-semantics change requiring its own transition,
transcript, and two-run treatment, and is not specified in this
document.

#### S7.3 Security and robustness analysis

Each entry states an attack vector or failure mode in its strongest form
(*Vector*), the facts that govern it (*Disposition*), and its *Status*
per
§[S7.1](#A7.SS1 "S7.1 Attack and limitation index ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Entries are grouped by attack surface.

##### S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism

###### Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families).

*Vector.* Freshness is byte-keyed
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
An adversary submits paraphrase variants of the same poison as distinct
byte strings; every inspector, including one already fooled by a sibling
variant, is fresh again on each variant, so the per-person discharge of
correlation is byte-scoped, not content-scoped. *Disposition.* The
discharge of per-person correlation is indeed *per byte identity*
(convention ([C5](#A1.I2.i5 "Item C5 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
and the arithmetic is unchanged: each variant is a distinct item
consuming the submitter’s rate limit and its own union-bound term
(Rule [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and per-retrieval exposure is capped at $`c_{\mathrm{cand}}`$
(Rule [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
[N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
What survives is an *interpretation* obligation on the deployer: $`q`$
inside each union-bound term must be calibrated as the catch rate
against the *variant family*, not against a single presentation; an
inspector fooled by one variant is plausibly likelier to be fooled by
its siblings. Deployments may additionally surface an advisory-only
similarity flag (“similar disputed or evicted items exist”) alongside
disputed items, of the zero-authority advisory class of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i):
it informs inspectors without granting the model computing similarity
any protocol effect. *Status.* Mechanism disposed; calibration duty
disclosed. Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S2 (Self-dispute).

*Vector.* Reject one’s own item; fill the panel with one’s own verdicts;
sustain the dispute across epochs via one’s own demand events.
*Disposition.* The case-(b) bound of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
does not condition on the rejecter’s identity, so self-dispute gains
only the panel term already counted, while consuming a rejection slot
and accountability exposure; verdict capacity never renews
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
capping the adversary’s tally at $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ for the dispute’s
life; self-initiations are capped at one per identity per item per epoch
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
*Status.* Disposed (under stated assumptions;
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S3 (Reputation farming).

*Vector.* Farm attestation weight and reputation over time; spend it in
one campaign. *Disposition.* $`f`$, $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}`$,
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ are lifetime totals over every identity the adversary
ever controls
(§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
every bound is stated against the totals, so farming shifts timing,
never capacity
([N12](#Thmnotex12 "Note N12 (Reputation farming). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The economic deterrent of burning reputation is real but deliberately
unused: the proofs assume the attacker spends everything. *Status.*
Disposed (under stated assumptions; lifetime-total definition). Not used
in any proof.

###### Analysis S4 (Tool-targeted poison).

*Vector.* Disputes are byte-level but harm is tool-level: a poison
dangerous at tool $`A`$ and innocuous at tool $`B`$ is sincerely
vindicated by a panel drawn from $`B`$-demanders, contradicting honest
$`A`$-rejecters; the freeze lifts and the interrupted entry resumes.
*Disposition.* The two promotion paths behave differently. *Ordinary
path at $`A`$: disposed.* Promotion at $`A`$ still requires $`N`$
credited fresh endorsements at $`A`$ itself
(Lemma [S3.14](#A3.Thmtheorem14 "Lemma S3.14 (Endorsement is the only trust raise). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
where inspectors face the harmful use, so the case-(a) term of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
applies with $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ read at $`A`$. *Panel path: residual.*
The panel term is *not* bounded by $`A`$-context competence:
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is uniform over the jurors’ own tool contexts
(Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)),
and for $`A`$-targeted, $`B`$-benign poison it may be near zero —
sincere $`B`$-juror vindication is then likely, the freeze lifts, and
the entry resumes toward its $`A`$-threshold. What remains against
$`A`$-promotion is the ordinary-path term, plus renewable re-freezes:
each epoch, each honest identity’s first rejecting decision on the bytes
— in particular each new $`A`$-context detection — re-freezes promotion
at every tool
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)).
*Accountability erosion.* Honest $`A`$-rejecters contradicted by
$`B`$-vindications feed
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v);
mitigation is threefold: the free first charge per epoch, the
per-fresh-inspection rate trigger calibrated above the honest baseline
([Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and conversion to zero-authority advisory flags at the ceiling. We
deliberately do *not* exempt rejecters whose vindicating jurors sat at a
different tool: because a rejection at any tool freezes all tools
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
such an exemption would let an adversary file every rejection “at” an
obscure tool no juror will ever demand, harvesting freezes with zero
accountability exposure and breaking the throughput bounds of
Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv).
The per-pair scoping variant of
Remark [S4.9](#A4.Thmtheorem9 "Remark S4.9 (Per-pair dispute scoping (deployment variant)). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
removes this residual; it is a deployment choice, consumed by no
theorem. *Status.* Ordinary-path promotion at the targeted tool
disposed; panel-path vindication under cross-tool juries residual,
disclosed; accountability erosion residual, mitigated,
availability-only. Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S5 (Panel-lapse exploitation and slot economics).

*Vector.* Reject a low-demand benign item; let the panel lapse; tax the
owner’s rate limit on each forced re-entry. *Disposition.* The attack
presupposes a deadline-based design; there is no panel lapse and no
forced re-entry
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)):
the only re-entry paths are owner-initiated, and slots free on
resolution or expiry. Roles of the clocks:
[Remark S5.26](#A5.Thmtheorem26 "Remark S5.26 (Roles of 𝑇_win, 𝑇_pan, 𝑇_exp; the demand-paced design). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
*Status.* Disposed (under stated assumptions;
Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S6 (Juror exhaustion by wide pre-exposure).

*Vector.* Pre-expose the poison so widely that few verdict-eligible
(fresh, seat-weighted) demanders remain; the panel never fills.
*Disposition.* The item stalls *frozen*: promotion is blocked at every
tool with no deadline to exploit
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)–(iii));
the cost is availability, never safety, borne by the adversary’s own
submission, and the benign-item variant is bounded at the cap
(Remark [S5.25](#A5.Thmtheorem25 "Remark S5.25 (Wide pre-exposure). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
Pre-exposure also feeds the defence: each additional honest *rejection*
opportunity can freeze promotion
([INV-2](#Thminvx2 "Invariant INV-2 (Rejection asymmetry). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and consumed honest identities are never re-usable for later entries of
the same bytes
(Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Safety disposed $`+`$ availability residual (under
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
hypotheses; deterministic failure mode of
[A9](#Thmassumptionx9 "Assumption A9 (Verdict rate). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
disclosed at its commentary). Not used in any proof.

##### S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels

###### Analysis S7 (Store-exhaustion side channel).

*Vector.* The store is idealized as unbounded; a real deployment has
quotas, and quota errors visible to $`P`$ leak the attacker-chosen
volume of captured blocks. *Disposition.* Correct, which is why the
quota policy is a stated convention rather than an afterthought:
deployments must apply quotas to the untrusted tier by silent eviction,
never by an error visible to $`P`$
(convention ([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
otherwise store exhaustion reopens exactly the channel
Rule [R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
closes
([N4](#Thmnotex4 "Note N4 (Failure indistinguishability, operationally). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Under the convention, no operation’s defined behaviour depends on
aggregate store volume, and
Lemma [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)
stands. *Status.* Disposed (under stated assumptions), conditional on
the stated deployment policy
([C7](#A1.I2.i7 "Item C7 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S8 (Timing channels).

*Vector.* The bisimulation matches $`P`$-operations; wall-clock timing
of the harness is unmodelled and could leak. *Disposition.* Conceded:
timing and termination are out of scope
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The interface returns no clock or step-count value, so no timing value
exists in $`\sigma_{P}`$ to branch on
(Lemma [S3.18](#A3.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S3.18 (Control-flow confinement to trusted data and releases). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e));
a clock consulted *through a tool* is already inside the model: its
reading is captured to $`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$ like any tool output
(Rule [R3](#Thmrulex3 "Rule R3 (Ingress: all tool outputs captured). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and never reaches $`\sigma_{P}`$. The exclusion concerns only implicit
timing: wall-clock latency of the harness observed by an outside party.
*Status.* Residual, precisely scoped
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(IV)).
Not used in any proof.

##### S7.3.3 The human factor

###### Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation).

*Vector.* An adversarial reader decorates a malicious candidate with a
benign-looking preview and steers the user. *Disposition.* Within the
formal model, previews are inert: they never enter $`\sigma_{P}`$
(Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and endorsement binds to the true resolved bytes on the decision pane
([A3](#Thmassumptionx3 "Assumption A3 (Faithful, zoned display). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so a preview can never forge an endorsement: the wrong value is
displayed truthfully and rejected under
[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Outside the formal model, a preview can influence what the user chooses
to examine and, through
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
idealization, what the user subsequently types. That residual is covered
by design rather than assumed away: previews are part of the display
transcript and the audit log
(Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e)),
so the release history covers every surface through which such influence
can pass, and
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
remains faithful even where
[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
frays
([N5](#Thmnotex5 "Note N5 (The human channel). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[N8](#Thmnotex8 "Note N8 (What previews can and cannot do). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Disposed (under stated assumptions) within the model; residual
at the human channel, disclosed. Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel).

*Vector.* After one careless narrative confirmation (a false acceptance
in the sense of
Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
a failure of
[A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the endorsed summary’s bytes are readable and flow, literal-expressed,
to data tools ungated (handle-expressed use gates regardless,
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c));
a poisoned summary can both mislead reasoning and direct data-tool
egress. *Disposition.* Correct, and no theorem is violated: the
influence entered through a transcript event the user accepted. The
compound shape is: one careless narrative endorsement (a failure of
[A5](#Thmassumptionx5 "Assumption A5 (Sound narrative endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
simultaneously (i) admits attacker-shaped content into $`P`$’s readable
state and (ii) opens ungated *literal-expressed* data-tool egress of
endorsed and typed bytes
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b);
handle-expressed use gates regardless,
Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c));
the misled $`P`$ may then recombine separately endorsed values at
sensitive tools without further gates
([S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Containment is threefold: the influence never crosses a sensitive
boundary with bytes neither user-typed nor endorsed for that tool
(Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
its triggering endorsement is a logged transcript event, and any
divergence it induces in the protected behaviours is transcript-carried
(Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and the community mechanism reduces the frequency of the triggering
endorsement for shareable content
(Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
In the federated tier the residual carries a further, deliberate cost:
an honest user who carelessly confirms and then *publishes*
attacker-crafted content will, on that item’s panel eviction, incur the
publisher penalty of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vii),
a corrective on the publish gate; the penalty never touches any local
store
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
removes the *ungated* data-tool egress of out-of-scope endorsed bytes
(each such flow then gates once per pair,
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b));
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
if instantiated conformingly, would limit only scope-checked local tool
authorization; data-tool enforcement requires
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and readable reasoning state is unaffected
([O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Residual, disclosed, contained, and priced. Not used in any
proof.

###### Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values).

*Vector.* Individually authorized values can form a harmful transaction
without violating Action Integrity: approval of a recipient and a body
separately for an email tool does not record approval of sending that
body to that recipient. Order, timing, and task context can also change
the meaning of reuse. *Disposition.* Recombination is ungated by design.
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
excludes additional hidden influence for matched runs with equal
complete display transcripts. It does not exclude influence through
changed displays, incorrect endorsements, or inappropriate reuse in a
later context.
Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
narrows typed-value authority by sensitive tool, and
Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
extends exact-tool checks to data tools; neither binds the complete
transaction. Human or agent memory managers could review combined
content and seek fresh endorsements before it becomes trusted, as
proposed in the main paper
(Appendix [D.2.1](#A4.SS2.SSS1 "D.2.1 Action Integrity ‣ D.2 Integrity Proofs ‣ Appendix D Formal Guarantees and Proof Sketches ‣ Part II Empirical and Explanatory Appendices ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
This is untested future work, not a guarantee for all later
combinations. Context-bound or transaction-level authorization would
require extended semantics and revised confirmation-cost accounting.
*Status.* Policy boundary and endorsement residual disclosed. Not used
in any proof.

###### Analysis S12 (Batch-gate attention).

*Vector.* The batch gate displays every element’s bytes, but
displayed-in-full is not reviewed-in-full;
