[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is weakest here. *Disposition.* Conceded:
Definition [S3.10](#A3.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds literally at the batch gate (every element’s bytes are displayed,
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
but the human premise
[A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is at its weakest, and deployments should size $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$
conservatively. The selected batch design is all-or-nothing: a per-page
decision returned to $`P`$ would leak the attacker-influenceable page
count, and the aggregate decision avoids that channel at the cost that
one poisoned element forces rejection of the whole batch: an
availability and attention cost, not a safety gap (no impossibility of
alternative fixed-shape or padded designs is claimed); and the user may
reject at any page, aborting the remainder, so attacker-imposed
attention is bounded by the user’s own patience, never compelled
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),(d),
[N6](#Thmnotex6 "Note N6 (The batch gate is all-or-nothing). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Deployments may additionally cap total batch cardinality
(Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),
converting oversize collections into a fixed, decision-free reject; the
cap lies outside the mechanized batch layer
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Mechanism disposed; residual at the human premise, disclosed.
Not used in any proof.

##### S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes

###### Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness).

*Vector.* A uniformly convincing poison lowers every fresh inspector’s
catch rate together; the exponential bounds assume independently varying
carelessness and collapse toward $`1-q_{c}`$ under engineered
correlation. *Disposition.* The premise of the vector is corrected
first: the bounds of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
assume *no* independence across inspectors; they assume a uniform
*conditional* lower bound $`q`$ on each fresh inspection given the
entire past
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
What engineered cross-person correlation attacks is that bound itself: a
uniformly convincing poison is one for which the honest conditional
catch rate, *after conditioning on earlier misses*, is some $`q_{c}<q`$.
Three facts limit the damage: the theorem remains valid with $`q`$ read
as $`q_{c}`$, the bound degrading toward $`1-q_{c}`$ transparently,
never silently; the diversity requirement $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ mixes
fresh-inspector pools, raising $`q_{c}`$
([N11](#Thmnotex11 "Note N11 (What pool diversity buys). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and periodic re-verification re-presents the bytes to inspectors with no
prior decision, so the probability of remaining uncaught across
$`E_{\mathrm{rv}}`$ rounds is at most $`(1-q_{c})^{E_{\mathrm{rv}}}`$,
scaling with the supply of never-decided inspectors, not with epoch
renewal
([N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The worst-case fallback as $`q_{c}\to 0`$ is the local layer of
Remark [S5.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S5.12 (Scope of Theorem ). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
not
Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
whose $`q=1`$ hypothesis engineered correlation directly attacks. The
*per-person* half of the correlation concern (re-inspection of the same
bytes is not re-randomisation) is discharged structurally for *logged*
inspections: no logged repeat carries weight or a verdict
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
across unlogged personal inspections
(Definition [S4.5](#A4.Thmtheorem5a "Definition S4.5 (Shared-presence freshness). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
it survives as a calibration obligation inside the log-fresh class
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Residual with a three-layer cap, disclosed. Not used in any
proof.

###### Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, $`q\to 0`$).

*Vector.* If no honest reviewer can recognize the poison, the
probabilistic bounds are vacuous. *Disposition.* Conceded, and the
guarantee is calibrated to what a human-verification design can
coherently mean by “safe”: content is treated as safe when the
qualifying community, inspecting the exact bytes at the exact tool,
accepts it. Content that fools *every* honest inspector is, within this
paradigm, indistinguishable from truth, and no design that routes trust
through human judgment can promise otherwise. What the design does
promise is one-sided and strong: it takes only one honest *effective
qualifying rejection* — a rejecting decision at a protocol-bearing gate
by an identity currently holding dispute-initiation authority
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(v))
— to freeze promotion immediately; detections by authority-inactive
identities are advisory flags, but the same identities’ acceptances
carry no promotion weight
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so silencing states never trade a lost rejection for a harvestable
acceptance; shared-presence freshness ensures the attacker can never
harvest a second *weight-bearing* acceptance from any identity that has
already logged a decision on the bytes
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
and the moment a refuting inspection arrives, however late, it takes
protocol-level effect immediately. What survives this regime is the
local layer of
Remark [S5.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S5.12 (Scope of Theorem ). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the one-sided freeze clause above, and re-verification
([N16](#Thmnotex16 "Note N16 (Revocation, re-verification, and grandfathering). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
does *not* apply, its $`q=1`$ hypothesis being the exact negation of
this regime. Safety alone can additionally be forced for any $`q>0`$ by
raising $`m`$ toward $`k`$, at the price of a weaker wrongful-eviction
bound
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Residual; the paradigm’s boundary disclosed
(§[S7.4](#A7.SS4 "S7.4 Scope and residuals ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(VI)).
Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S15 (Accountability mis-calibration).

*Vector.* The rate trigger and ceiling require estimating the honest
baseline $`1-p_{b}`$; mis-calibration can suppress honest
dispute-initiation and crediting, reducing availability — and, absent
authority-gated crediting
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
it would also invalidate the uniform $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$
interpretation. *Disposition.* The exposure is availability-only, never
safety, and is bounded as follows. (i) Panel verdicts are never
penalised and never charged
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(a)),
and verdict-eligible rejections are cast regardless of accountability
state
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(e)),
so the panel arithmetic of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
Proposition [S5.20](#A5.Thmtheorem20 "Proposition S5.20 (Wrongful-eviction bound). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is independent of calibration. (ii) A capped or suspended honest
identity retains advisory flags and ordinary use — though its
acceptances are authority-inert for the duration
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— loses nothing permanent, and is restored at the epoch boundary
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(d),
[Remark S5.5](#A5.Thmtheorem5 "Remark S5.5 (Calibration of rejecter accountability). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
(iii) Its ordinary, non-verdict gate inspections while
dispute-initiation and crediting authority are inactive are *excluded
trials*, not silenced misses: neither branch enters the
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ trial class — the acceptance carries no promotion
weight and the rejection no initiation
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— so these inspections do not enter $`1-q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$. Eligible
panel verdicts are different: verdict capacity is never authority-gated,
and every cast eligible verdict remains a $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ trial
regardless of accountability state
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v)(a),(e),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)).
Mis-calibration may change the composition of the authority-active
ordinary class, so the deployment must continue to validate the
weakest-target $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$ bound over that class
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
it does not convert excluded inspections into misses. The remaining cost
is availability: throttled honest dispute-initiation and delayed
crediting. (iv) The calibration enters only the budget constants,
through the deterministic bound $`c_{\mathrm{acc}}`$
(Lemma [S5.4](#A5.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma S5.4 (Deterministic accountability bound). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Figure [S1](#A1.F1 "Figure S1 ‣ S1.1 Organisation and register conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
no safety theorem depends on it. (v) Under authority-gated crediting
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a),
Remark [S5.18](#A5.Thmtheorem18 "Remark S5.18 (Authority-gated crediting: soundness and cost). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
mis-calibration cannot be exploited to harvest promotion weight from
silenced honest identities — a silenced identity’s acceptance is
authority-inert — so the exposure remains throttled honest
dispute-initiation, with correspondingly delayed crediting,
availability-only. What mis-calibration buys an adversary is therefore
throttled honest dispute-initiation: bounded required-confirmation harm
and bounded per-epoch throughput
(Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
wall-clock delay unbounded, resolution being demand-paced,
Remark [S5.21](#A5.Thmtheorem21 "Remark S5.21 (Resolution as a demand-side event). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
no third-party alteration of any local store
(Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and required cost within the single-user cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Safety disposed; availability exposure residual, disclosed.
Enters budget constants only.

##### S7.3.5 Modelling-boundary effects

###### Analysis S16 (Incentive feedback on publication).

*Vector.* Publisher penalties, though provably rare for benign items,
depress publication; a thinner shared tier raises the effective
$`\beta`$ and weakens
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
directly at its coverage clause (late or absent publication inflates
$`U_{v,t}`$). *Disposition.* Conceded and unmodelled: the incentive
feedback between the accountability layer and the demand model of
Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is outside the formal development. Its impact is confined to the budget
*asymptotics*: the cap of
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is unaffected by it (it is an identity over required confirmations), the
safety theorems are unaffected (they do not reference $`\beta`$), and
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
bounds the penalty’s probability for benign publishers at
$`e^{-2\delta_{b}^{2}(k-f_{\mathrm{s}})}`$ per panel, with expected
counts per epoch bounded by the dispute ledger
(Prop. [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
linear tier). *Status.* Residual, confined to budget asymptotics. Not
used in any proof.

###### Analysis S17 (Release-day demand spikes).

*Vector.* A popular item’s demand arrives in one burst;
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
fails, and the amortisation claims fall with it. *Disposition.* A
release-day spike is precisely a violation of
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
*for that item* ($`\gamma_{v}\approx 1`$): its cost is at most the
item’s own demand, once: each affected demander pays the required
confirmations (at most one per demanded pair,
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
that the pathwise cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i))
already bounds (whose counting identities never use
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and every other item’s accounting is untouched, since the ledger of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is per-item. Degradation under spikes is therefore item-local, bounded
by
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and transient; the window- and dormancy-bucket rows of the ledger are
exactly where within-window demand, diversity wait, propagation delay,
and dormant intervals are collected, and
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
caps them at the fraction $`\bar{\gamma}`$ of each item’s own demand, so
popularity never enters the per-user bound
(Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
A pre-publication demand burst is likewise an
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
violation for that item (its early demanders are residual), priced
identically at the cap. *Status.* Disposed (under stated assumptions):
the failure mode is priced by the pathwise cap
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)).
Not used in any proof.

###### Analysis S18 (Handle-mediated arrival of certified content).

*Vector.* Not an attack but a representation effect: a pair $`(v,t)`$ is
live-$`\mathsf{CC}`$, yet a user’s copy of $`v`$ arrives through an
untrusted channel (a message, a tool output) and is therefore held only
as an opaque handle
(Lemma [S3.12](#A3.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma S3.12 (Protected-LLM isolation / provenance preservation). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
passing the handle to $`t`$ gates
(Rule [R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
despite the certificate, and, absent a local in-scope copy, the
confirmation is required. A demand stream arriving predominantly
handle-expressed can drive the shared *required* load toward the
standalone mass, community certification notwithstanding. *Disposition.*
Deliberate and structural: exempting certificate-matching handle
resolutions from the gate would make the gate-vs-no-gate behaviour a
function of hidden $`\mathsf{U}`$-resolution, reopening the channel
Rules [R6](#Thmrulex6 "Rule R6 (Null handle). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")/[R7](#Thmrulex7 "Rule R7 (Failure indistinguishability). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
close and breaking
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(two runs whose handles resolve to different $`\mathsf{CC}`$-matching
byte strings would flow ungated under equal transcripts with different
sink projections); the gate on untrusted-channel arrivals is the
inspection the design intends
(Remark [S6.11](#A6.Thmtheorem11 "Remark S6.11 (Reading of Theorem ). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
The cost is bounded on both sides: each such confirmation is once ever
per (user, pair)
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the epoch’s shared required load never exceeds the standalone mass
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)),
and the accepting user thereafter holds a local in-scope copy,
fast-pathing all literal reuse. Amortisation applies to the
fast-path-expressed share of certified demand — notably trusted
retrieval, which returns live entries as readable $`\mathbb{E}`$-bytes
byte-matching the entry
(Definition [S4.1](#A4.Thmtheorem1a "Definition S4.1 (Federated product configuration; live endorsed view). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rules [R14](#Thmrulex14 "Rule R14 (Candidate hygiene). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
[R4](#Thmrulex4 "Rule R4 (Whitelist mediation at every tool boundary). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a));
the handle-arrival fraction is priced inside $`\varepsilon(M)`$ of
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and logged directly
([N17](#Thmnotex17 "Note N17 (Validation without a user study). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
*Status.* Residual, disclosed, priced in
[A11](#Thmassumptionx11 "Assumption A11 (Coverage sufficiency, operational form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
bounded pathwise by
Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
(persistence exceptions per
[INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Not used in any safety proof; enters budget assumptions only.

#### S7.4 Scope and residuals

The guarantees’ boundaries, collected in one place.

1.  (I)
    *Per-execution, per-(value, tool).* Action Integrity is per
    execution; endorsement is per (value, tool) and cached indefinitely
    (a conforming instantiation of the requirements-level
    Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    would bound the scope-checked tool-authorization lifetime;
    [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    recombination of separately endorsed values is ungated by design
    ([N2](#Thmnotex2 "Note N2 (The endorsement unit). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
2.  (II)
    *The human channel.*
    [A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    idealizes typing as exogenous; influence through displayed content
    is recorded, not prevented
    ([N5](#Thmnotex5 "Note N5 (The human channel). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [N7](#Thmnotex7 "Note N7 (The transcript is recorded, not prevented). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S9](#Thmobjx9 "Analysis S9 (Preview manipulation). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    Reasoning Integrity is modulo the transcript, and the compound
    residual is
    [S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
3.  (III)
    *The batch gate.* Every element’s bytes are displayed, so
    Definition [S3.10](#A3.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S3.10 (Action Integrity, personal and delegated). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    holds literally; but displayed-in-full is not reviewed-in-full:
    [A4](#Thmassumptionx4 "Assumption A4 (Sound atomic endorsement). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    is weakest here, and $`c_{\mathrm{batch}}`$ should be sized
    accordingly
    ([N6](#Thmnotex6 "Note N6 (The batch gate is all-or-nothing). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S12](#Thmobjx12 "Analysis S12 (Batch-gate attention). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
4.  (IV)
    *Timing and termination* are out of scope; the exclusion concerns
    only implicit wall-clock channels observed from outside
    ([S8](#Thmobjx8 "Analysis S8 (Timing channels). ‣ S7.3.2 Side channels and covert channels ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
5.  (V)
    *Model intent.* Isolation restricts hidden untrusted influence; it
    does not certify $`P`$ or $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$ as benign or guarantee
    that a later combination of typed or endorsed values is appropriate.
    Influence through changed displays and incorrect endorsements
    remains possible
    ([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    [S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
    The baseline’s extensional, tool-blind trust of typed literals is
    Remark [S3.22](#A3.Thmtheorem22 "Remark S3.22 (Extensional trust of typed values). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    Option [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    narrows that authority by sensitive tool without approving a whole
    transaction. One first-party residual: $`\mathsf{evict}`$ is
    owner-scoped but $`P`$-invocable and ungated, so an erring Protected
    LLM can remove its owner’s endorsed blocks; the no-deletion
    guarantee is third-party only, and gating $`\mathsf{evict}`$ on
    $`\mathbb{E}`$-blocks is a further monotone hardening
    ([N13](#Thmnotex13 "Note N13 (The 𝖾𝗏𝗂𝖼𝗍 residual). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
6.  (VI)
    *Unrecognizable poison* ($`q\to 0`$): no community-truthfulness
    guarantee survives this regime within a human-judgment design
    (Remark [S5.12](#A5.Thmtheorem12 "Remark S5.12 (Scope of Theorem ). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    what survives is the local layer, the one-sided freeze on any single
    honest recognition, and re-verification against never-decided
    inspectors
    ([S14](#Thmobjx14 "Analysis S14 (Unrecognizable poison, 𝑞→0). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    degradation under engineered correlation is to the rate $`q_{c}`$,
    transparently
    ([S13](#Thmobjx13 "Analysis S13 (Cross-person correlated carelessness). ‣ S7.3.4 Adverse parameter regimes ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
7.  (VII)
    *Federated influence through legitimate log activity* is held fixed
    by
    [A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    in the noninterference statement and is bounded instead by
    Theorems [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
8.  (VIII)
    *Availability* is not guaranteed; a dispute’s harm *in required
    confirmations* is bounded per
    Lemma [S5.24](#A5.Thmtheorem24 "Lemma S5.24 (Bounds on rejection-based denial of service). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    and
    [N14](#Thmnotex14 "Note N14 (Availability degrades gracefully, never destructively). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (including the suspension-induced, once-per-demander confirmation,
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi)),
    inspection effort disclosed separately
    ([N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    degradation is never destructive
    (Lemma [S5.8](#A5.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S5.8 (Third-party immutability of local stores). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
9.  (IX)
    *Confidentiality.* Only the type-level exclusion is proved
    (Lemma [S5.2](#A5.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S5.2 (Type-level sharing exclusion). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
    semantic confidentiality of published content rests on the publish
    gate
    ([A7](#Thmassumptionx7 "Assumption A7 (Federated endorsement transfer). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
10. (X)
    *Tool choice and zero-argument actions.* Action Integrity constrains
    the values crossing sensitive tool boundaries; it does not authorize
    the invocation itself, and a sensitive tool with no gated arguments
    satisfies the value-flow property vacuously. Deployments requiring
    authorization of the act itself gate the capability (a monotone
    hardening in the sense of
    Prop. [S3.28](#A3.Thmtheorem28 "Proposition S3.28 (Hardening is monotone). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
11. (XI)
    *The reasoning pseudo-target.* Shared-tier accounting treats
    $`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ as a canonical pseudo-target
    (§[S4.1](#A4.SS1a "S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
    knowledge items amortise and are defended at it, and
    $`\mathsf{CC}`$-at-$`\mathsf{reasoning}`$ status buys community-wide
    readability only, never any tool flow.

#### S7.5 Summary of composed guarantees

###### (A) One user, deployment lifetime (trust axioms [A1](#Thmassumptionx1 "Assumption A1 (Deterministic source labelling). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust") alone).

Mechanization boundary, wherever machine-checking is advertised:
kernel-checked are Personal Action Integrity from the empty
configuration and from arbitrary mechanized well-formed configurations;
the map-free Reasoning Integrity core from empty stores and from the
canonical shared-endorsed seed class; and the standalone
batch-confirmation layer
(§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Paper-only are the run-level $`\mathsf{map}`$ integration, the batch
cardinality cap,
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(requirements-level), arbitrary matched *mid-run* pairs, the
index-oracle reduction
(Prop. [S3.29](#A3.Thmtheorem29 "Proposition S3.29 (Index-oracle coverage of display-reactive behaviour). ‣ Mechanization. ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the federated product system, and every probabilistic and budget result.
Gating where influence acts:
Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a).
Recording where it persuades:
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Corollary [S3.26](#A3.Thmtheorem26 "Corollary S3.26 (Attack-surface confinement). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(Phrasing discipline, here and in any summary elsewhere: Reasoning
Integrity is a fixed-horizon, termination-insensitive equivalence
*modulo the full display transcript*, under coupled typed input — and,
federated, a coupled log
([A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— never an unconditional noninterference or inertness claim;
Definition [S3.11](#A3.Thmtheorem11 "Definition S3.11 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Remark [S3.9](#A3.Thmtheorem9 "Remark S3.9 (Coverage of the display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").)
Residuals: the user’s own false endorsement
([S10](#Thmobjx10 "Analysis S10 (Careless endorsement and the post-endorsement channel). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the post-endorsement boundary
(Corollary [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
recombination
([S11](#Thmobjx11 "Analysis S11 (Recombination of endorsed values). ‣ S7.3.3 The human factor ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Deployments whose threat model emphasises data-tool exfiltration should
select

as the default profile: it closes the baseline post-endorsement channel
(Cor. [S3.23](#A3.Thmtheorem23 "Corollary S3.23 (No silent resolution; the post-endorsement boundary). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)),

and costs $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$ per reusable endorsed-value pair, freshly

relied on
(Theorem [S6.2](#A6.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem S6.2 (Single-user first-authorization cap). ‣ S6.2 The single-user first-authorization cap ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

effort scope per
[N18](#Thmnotex18 "Note N18 (Total effort, including rejections). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

Theorem [S5.11](#A5.Thmtheorem11 "Theorem S5.11 (Deterministic safety under perfect honest detection). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),

*Probabilistic, per poisoned attempt
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))*
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):

reach-free
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
per-anchor-epoch and lifetime exposure
Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(attempts keyed to anchor epochs,

Scoping caveats:
[S1](#Thmobjx1 "Analysis S1 (Paraphrase-variant families). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[S4](#Thmobjx4 "Analysis S4 (Tool-targeted poison). ‣ S7.3.1 Attacks on the endorsement mechanism ‣ S7.3 Security and robustness analysis ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
and one explicitly: the numeric system-wide bound covers
*adversary-published* attempts, counted by the rate limit at their

(third-party transitions; first-party residual

convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
not integrated into the single-user small-step relation
(§[S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

### Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results

#### S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline

###### The adaptive-adversary framework.

Fix an epoch. All protocol events (submissions, presentations, gate
decisions, verdicts, promotions) form a discrete sequence; let
$`(\mathcal{F}_{s})_{s\geq 0}`$ be the filtration generated by all
logged protocol events and all display events up to step $`s`$. The
adversary’s strategy (whom to present the item to next, when to submit,
re-enter, self-dispute, or stop) is *predictable* with respect to
$`(\mathcal{F}_{s})`$: its action at step $`s`$ is
$`\mathcal{F}_{s-1}`$-measurable
(convention ([C2](#A1.I2.i2 "Item C2 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
Two structural facts constrain the adversary’s adaptivity. First, an
entry’s bytes are immutable once submitted (the log is append-only and
the gate displays exact bytes), so within an entry the adversary adapts
*presentation and stopping* only, never the inspected content. Second,
because the adversary chooses whom to present the item to, the
inspection parameter $`q`$ must be read as a *uniform* lower bound over
all honest identities and presentation contexts, the catch rate of the
most fallible honest user the adversary can target, with flagged
scrutiny only raising it
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
[N11](#Thmnotex11 "Note N11 (What pool diversity buys). ‣ S7.2 Design rationale ‣ Appendix S7 Design Rationale, Security Analysis, and Scope (informative) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Atomic gate events; log order.

Gate events are atomic federated-wide, exactly as at the interface
(Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
a presentation and its disposition (an accepting decision, a rejecting
decision, or abandonment) occupy a *single* position of the linearizable
log
(convention ([C3](#A1.I2.i3 "Item C3 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")));
no dialog is ever pending, and dispositions never resolve out of log
order. The analysis reads each such position as up to three consecutive
*atoms*: the *rendering atom* (item, tool, presenting identity, dispute
flag, both provenance zones — recorded in the display transcript whether
or not a decision follows,
Rule [R8](#Thmrulex8 "Rule R8 (Faithful display on a split, zoned surface). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(e));
if and only if the user records a decision, the *header atom* (the fact
that a decision by this identity on these bytes at this gate is being
appended, together with its verdict eligibility, a deterministic
predicate of the prior log and the identity,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(a)–(e));
and the *content atom* (the decision
$`z\in\{\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\}`$). Abandonment appends no
decision record and contributes no decision trial. Cache gates
(Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are the one asymmetrically recorded class: both branches occupy a
decision-pane position of the display transcript — rendering, header,
and content atoms exactly as above, all inside the filtration, which is
generated by display events as well as logged protocol events — while
only the rejecting branch additionally appends a federation-log
candidate record
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
We say a decision is *audit-recorded* if its atoms lie on the display
transcript (every recorded gate decision, cache acceptances included)
and *federation-logged* if it is appended to the federation log as a
candidate decision (protocol-bearing decisions only). Trials at cache
gates are indexed by their audit-recorded atoms: their occurrence is
pre-outcome, never selected by the rejecting branch’s federation-log
append. No protocol event, and no adversary action, interleaves between
the atoms of one position; the discrete step index totally orders all
atoms, and every trial sequence in this document is indexed by these
log-ordered atoms: inspection and arrival trials by rendering atoms,
decision and verdict trials by header atoms. In particular, every
earlier trial’s content atom precedes every later trial’s occurrence
atom. The adversary’s strategy, predictable with respect to the
record-level filtration, remains predictable with respect to this
refinement: the refinement inserts atoms inside single records and
reveals nothing between records on which a strategy could act.

###### Conditioning convention.

The conditioning $`\sigma`$-algebra depends on the trial type. For an
*arrival or inspection-occurrence* trial, $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$ is
generated by all atoms strictly prior to the trial’s rendering atom. For
a *decision- or verdict-content* trial, $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$ is generated
by all atoms strictly prior to the trial’s header atom *together with
that header atom itself* — the fact that a decision by this identity on
these bytes at this gate is being recorded, and its deterministic
eligibility facts
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii))
— but not the trial’s content atom. Thus the occurrence event $`O_{i}`$
(a decision is recorded) is $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurable in every
application. Every behavioural lower bound ($`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$,
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$, $`p_{b}`$, $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$) is a
conditional bound given the corresponding $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$, further
enlarged by the exogenous demand factor below (uniformly over demand
realisations). Under the atomic reading above, these $`\sigma`$-algebras
already contain the disposition of every earlier presentation — there
are no latent or pending dispositions — so the occurrence,
measurability, and independence conditions of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
hold at them directly. Where a behavioural parameter is stated at the
disposition level ($`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$, $`p_{b}`$),
Lemma [S8.1](#A8.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma S8.1 (Decision-conditioned content bounds). ‣ Dispositions. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
transports it to the header-inclusive $`\sigma`$-algebra. For a
per-attempt bound
(Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the conditioning $`\sigma`$-algebra is generated by all atoms up to and
including the attempt’s anchor atom
(Definition [S5.1](#A5.Thmtheorem1 "Definition S5.1 (Promotion attempt). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the anchor preceding every decision creditable to the attempt; the trial
$`\sigma`$-algebras above refine it, and the behavioural bounds,
asserted uniformly over histories, hold under the anchor-conditional
measure.

###### Dispositions.

An honest inspection presented at a gate has three possible
dispositions, realized at that gate’s log position: an accepting
decision, a rejecting decision, or abandonment. Only decisions are
logged; abandonment leaves no record and has no protocol effect
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i),(iii)).
The conditional decision probabilities therefore satisfy
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1`$, abandonment carrying the
remaining mass, and every behavioural parameter ($`q`$, $`p_{b}`$,
$`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$) is stated over dispositions: abandonment
counts as a miss inside $`1-q`$ and as a non-verdict inside
$`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$
([Remark S5.19](#A5.Thmtheorem19 "Remark S5.19 (Interpretation of the parameter 𝑞). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Lemma S8.1 (Decision-conditioned content bounds).

Consider a gate presentation with rendering-atom $`\sigma`$-algebra
$`\mathcal{G}`$ and conditional disposition probabilities
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}},p_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ given $`\mathcal{G}`$, with
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1`$ (abandonment carrying the
remaining mass). On the event that a decision is recorded, and given
$`\mathcal{G}`$ together with the header atom: (i) if
$`p_{\mathrm{rej}}\geq q`$, the conditional probability of
$`\mathrm{accept}`$ is at most $`1-q`$; (ii) if
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}\geq p_{b}`$, the conditional probability of
$`\mathrm{reject}`$ is at most $`1-p_{b}`$; (iii) symmetrically, let a
designated sub-branch of the rejecting disposition (e.g. the *effective*
qualifying rejection of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c))
have conditional probability $`p_{\mathrm{eff}}\leq p_{\mathrm{rej}}`$
given $`\mathcal{G}`$; if $`p_{\mathrm{eff}}\geq q`$ for some
$`q\in(0,1]`$, then, on the event that a decision is recorded, the
conditional probability of that sub-branch at the header atom is at
least $`q`$:
$`p_{\mathrm{eff}}/(p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}})\geq p_{\mathrm{eff}}\geq q`$,
since $`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1`$. The header atom adds
no randomness beyond the fact that a decision is recorded: verdict
eligibility is a deterministic function of the prior log and the
identity
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)).
(Part (i), the accept-side special case of (iii), is retained for
reference; part (iii) serves $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$’s lower-bound
direction as used in
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
case (a); part (ii) serves $`p_{b}`$; the verdict parameter
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is defined at the header atom directly,
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
and needs no bridge.)

###### Proof.

The decision-recorded event has conditional probability
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ given $`\mathcal{G}`$, so the
conditional accept probability given a recorded decision is
$`p_{\mathrm{acc}}/(p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}})=1-p_{\mathrm{rej}}/(p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}})\leq 1-p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1-q`$,
using $`p_{\mathrm{acc}}+p_{\mathrm{rej}}\leq 1`$; (ii) is symmetric.
Eligibility being measurable in $`\mathcal{G}`$ and the prior log,
conditioning on it changes nothing. ∎

###### Demand randomness, formally.

The underlying space is a product
$`\Omega_{\mathrm{prot}}\times\Omega_{\mathrm{dem}}`$. The factor
$`\Omega_{\mathrm{dem}}`$ carries the exogenous *demand indicators* of
