````math
the reference model
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— Bernoulli variables $`D_{u,v,t}`$ ($`u`$ demands the pair $`(v,t)`$
within the epoch, with per-user probability $`p_{u,v,t}`$
($`p_{v,t}=M^{-1}\sum_{u}p_{u,v,t}`$,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))),
independent across users and of every
$`\Omega_{\mathrm{prot}}`$-coordinate — together with each owner’s
publication schedule, coupled to the owner’s own indicators per the
owner-coupling convention
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
the counts $`n_{v,t}=\sum_{u}D_{u,v,t}`$ and $`n_{v}`$ are measurable in
this factor alone, and every epoch containing a submission or re-entry
of $`v`$ has $`n_{v}\geq 1`$ (owner coupling; the ledger’s vanishing
clause on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$ is event-based,
§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
Three demand quantities must be distinguished. *Latent demand*
$`D_{u,v,t}`$ is the exogenous indicator above. *Realized shared-tier
demand* is the log-defined event of
Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
the first interpreter event at which $`u`$’s use of the pair fires a
gate or dereferences a shared entry, per
Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
exclusions (covered and cache gates are not demand events on either
branch), occurring only while $`v`$ has a shared-tier presence; its
count is denoted $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}`$. *Reclassified personal
demand* is a latent demander’s post-retirement encounter, charged to the
single-user stream
(Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
retirement clause). Realized shared-tier demand is dominated pathwise by
latent demand: every realized demander is a latent demander — for third
parties by
Definition [S4.4](#A4.Thmtheorem4a "Definition S4.4 (Demand). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
(a realized demand presupposes attempted use), for the owner by the
owner-coupling convention
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
— so $`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$ pointwise; and by the
required-approval clause
(§[S6.1](#A6.SS1 "S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
a reference-model coupling, any epoch event at which a user’s attempted
use fires a gate realizes the user’s latent indicator, so every required
confirmation in the epoch belongs to a latent demander, wherever the
event falls; hence every ledger bound stated against $`n_{v,t}`$ or
$`\mathbb{E}[n_{v,t}]=Mp_{v,t}`$ is an upper bound for the realized
counts the rows charge. Which class a latent demander lands in (realized
vs. reclassified) is protocol-dependent; the *total* per-pair required
cost across both classes is nonetheless at most one per (user, pair)
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
which is why the floor never consults the split. The arrival *times* of
realized demand are protocol-endogenous, measurable in
$`(\mathcal{F}_{s})`$, revealing the corresponding indicator at that
event; no independence between arrival times and the protocol is
asserted, and
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
— both its demand clause (used for bucket attribution,
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and its first-pair-decision clause (used only for the $`\bar{D}_{v}`$
derivation) — is a hindsight cap on the realised arrival and decision
schedules respectively, per item, read pathwise on completed epochs. The
behavioural lower bounds $`q`$, $`p_{b}`$, $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ are
asserted conditionally per the conditioning convention of this section,
further enlarged by the entire demand factor: uniformly over demand
realisations. This licenses the ledger’s two-stage argument
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")):
the freeze rows bound conditional expectations given the demand
coordinates, by
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
under the demand-conditional measure, whose hypotheses hold there by the
uniform reading; the expectation over demand is taken last, by the tower
property, and the pathwise domination
$`n^{\mathrm{log}}_{v,t}\leq n_{v,t}`$ carries every realized-count row
under the latent masses.

###### Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination).

Let $`(\mathcal{F}_{s})`$ be a filtration and let
$`Z_{1},Z_{2},\dots\in\{0,1\}`$ be decision indicators observed at
strictly increasing stopping times $`\tau_{1}<\tau_{2}<\cdots`$. Write
$`O_{i}`$ for the event that the $`i`$-th observation occurs, so that
$`O_{1}\supseteq O_{2}\supseteq\cdots`$ and
$`O_{i}\in\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{i}^{-}}`$; unrealised observations are read
as $`Z_{i}:=0`$ off $`O_{i}`$. Fix $`p\in[0,1]`$ and $`n`$. There is an
enlargement of the probability space carrying i.i.d.
$`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)`$ variables $`Y_{1},Y_{2},\dots`$ such that:

1.  (i)
    *(Majorant.)* If
    $`\mathbb{P}[Z_{i}=1\mid\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{i}^{-}}]\leq p`$ on
    $`O_{i}`$ for every $`i\leq n`$, then $`Z_{i}\leq Y_{i}`$ pointwise
    for every $`i\leq n`$; hence for every $`x`$,
    $`\mathbb{P}[\sum_{i\leq n}Z_{i}\geq x]\leq\mathbb{P}[\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\geq x]`$,
    and the same bound holds for any sum truncated by a predictable
    stopping rule, truncation removing only nonnegative terms.
2.  (ii)
    *(Minorant, joint form.)* If
    $`\mathbb{P}[Z_{i}=1\mid\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{i}^{-}}]\geq p`$ on
    $`O_{i}`$ for every $`i\leq n`$, then $`Y_{i}\leq Z_{i}`$ pointwise
    on $`O_{i}`$ for every $`i\leq n`$; hence for every $`x`$,

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\Big[O_{n}\cap\Big\{\sum_{i\leq n}Z_{i}\leq x\Big\}\Big]\ \leq\ \mathbb{P}[\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\leq x],\qquad\text{in particular}
    ``` |  |
    |  |
    ``` math
    \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\big[O_{n}\cap\{Z_{1}=\cdots=Z_{n}=0\}\big]\ \leq\ (1-p)^{n}.
    ``` |  |

    No claim is made about the conditional law of
    $`\sum_{i\leq n}Z_{i}`$ given $`O_{n}`$: the occurrence events may
    depend on the realised $`Z_{i}`$, so only joint-event bounds are
    asserted.
3.  (iii)
    *(Counting.)* If the hypothesis of (i) holds for every $`i`$, then
    for the total count $`T`$ of realised observations,
    $`\mathbb{E}\big[\sum_{i\leq T}Z_{i}\big]\leq p\,\mathbb{E}[T]`$.

###### Proof.

*Construction.* All protocol randomness lives on a standard Borel space:
the event alphabet of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is countable and the filtration is generated by a discrete event
sequence $`(\xi_{s})_{s\geq 0}`$, so regular conditional distributions
exist, and the process admits a *sequential quantile representation*:
there are measurable maps $`(\phi_{s})`$ and i.i.d.
$`\mathrm{Uniform}[0,1]`$ variables $`(V_{s})`$, adjoined by the
Ionescu–Tulcea extension, with
$`\tilde{\xi}_{s}:=\phi_{s}(\tilde{\xi}_{0},\dots,\tilde{\xi}_{s-1},V_{s})`$
reproducing the joint law of $`(\xi_{s})`$ coordinate by coordinate
(each $`\phi_{s}(\,\cdot\,,V_{s})`$ realising the regular conditional
law of $`\xi_{s}`$ given the past by quantile inversion). We choose the
representation so that, for each $`i`$, the coordinate deciding the
$`i`$-th observation’s value uses a dedicated uniform $`U_{i}`$, with
the decision indicator realised as
$`\tilde{Z}_{i}=\mathbf{1}\{U_{i}\leq p_{i}\}`$ on $`\tilde{O}_{i}`$,
where $`p_{i}:=\mathbb{P}[Z_{i}{=}1\mid\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{i}^{-}}]`$
evaluated along the *redefined* history. Because the whole trajectory is
rebuilt recursively, the stopping times, occurrence events, and every
other coordinate are measurable functions of the redefined past, and the
redefined process has the same joint law as the original; every
conclusion below is a property of that joint law, so we argue on the
redefined process and drop the tildes. Set
$`Y_{i}:=\mathbf{1}\{U_{i}\leq p\}`$; the $`Y_{i}`$ are i.i.d.
$`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)`$, each $`U_{i}`$ independent of the past at its
use.

*(i) Majorant.* On $`O_{i}`$, $`p_{i}\leq p`$, so $`Z_{i}=1`$ entails
$`U_{i}\leq p_{i}\leq p`$, hence $`Y_{i}=1`$; off $`O_{i}`$,
$`Z_{i}=0`$. So $`Z_{i}\leq Y_{i}`$ everywhere. Pointwise domination of
each term transfers superlevel events of the sums, and dropping terms of
a $`\{0,1\}`$-valued sum only lowers it, giving the truncated form.

*(ii) Minorant, joint form.* On $`O_{i}`$, $`p_{i}\geq p`$, so
$`Y_{i}=1`$ entails $`U_{i}\leq p\leq p_{i}`$, hence $`Z_{i}=1`$; on
$`O_{n}`$ every $`O_{i}`$ with $`i\leq n`$ holds, so
$`O_{n}\cap\{\sum_{i\leq n}Z_{i}\leq x\}\subseteq\{\sum_{i\leq n}Y_{i}\leq x\}`$,
an event of unconditional binomial law; $`x=0`$ gives the all-zeros
bound.

*(iii) Counting.* Iterated conditioning:
$`\mathbb{E}[\sum_{i}\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}Z_{i}]=\sum_{i}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}\,p_{i}\big]\leq p\sum_{i}\mathbb{P}[O_{i}]=p\,\mathbb{E}[T]`$.
∎

###### Remark S8.3 (Alternatives to pathwise coupling).

Readers preferring to avoid the sequential quantile construction may
replace parts (i)–(ii) by exponential supermartingale bounds, at the
cost of the pointwise dominations; the pathwise form is kept because the
truncation and joint-event arguments of
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
and
Lemma [S5.6](#A5.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma S5.6 (Verdict pacing under ). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
consume domination, not merely tail bounds.

###### Remark S8.4 ($`\sigma`$-algebra form).

Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
holds verbatim with the pre-stopping-time $`\sigma`$-algebras
$`\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{i}^{-}}`$ replaced by any increasing
$`\sigma`$-algebras
$`\mathcal{G}_{1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{2}\subseteq\cdots`$ such that,
for each $`i`$: $`O_{i}\in\mathcal{G}_{i}`$; $`Z_{j}`$ is
$`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurable for every $`j<i`$; and the coupling
variable $`U_{i}`$ is independent of $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$. The proof is
unchanged: the conditional-quantile construction and the pointwise
dominations use only these three properties. The applications take
$`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$ per the conditioning convention of
§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):
for arrival and inspection trials, all atoms strictly prior to the
rendering atom; for decision and verdict trials, all prior atoms *plus*
the trial’s own header atom (content atom excluded), so that
$`O_{i}\in\mathcal{G}_{i}`$; both enlarged by the demand factor. All
trials being log-ordered with earlier contents preceding later
occurrence atoms, the three conditions hold at these $`\sigma`$-algebras
directly.

###### Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks).

Let $`\mathcal{G}_{1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{2}\subseteq\cdots`$ be
$`\sigma`$-algebras, $`O_{i}\in\mathcal{G}_{i}`$ occurrence events, and
let $`X_{i}`$ be $`[0,1]`$-valued random variables with
$`\mathbb{E}[X_{i}\mid\mathcal{G}_{i}]\leq p`$ on $`O_{i}`$ for every
$`i`$. Then, with $`N:=\sum_{i}\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}`$ finite almost
surely,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{i}\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}X_{i}\Big]\ \leq\ p\,\mathbb{E}[N].
``` |  |

No ordering of the times at which the $`X_{i}`$ resolve, no
measurability of any $`X_{i}`$ with respect to any $`\mathcal{G}_{j}`$,
and no independence is required: each $`X_{i}`$ may resolve arbitrarily
later than its occurrence event, interleaved with other trials’
occurrences and resolutions.

###### Proof.

$`\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}X_{i}]=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbf{1}_{O_{i}}\,\mathbb{E}[X_{i}\mid\mathcal{G}_{i}]\big]\leq p\,\mathbb{P}[O_{i}]`$
by the tower property; sum over $`i`$. ∎

###### Remark S8.6 (Realised-at-time vs. delayed marks).

Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
is the special case in which $`X_{i}`$ is a decision indicator realised
at its own stopping time.
Lemma [S8.5](#A8.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma S8.5 (Delayed marks). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is the form consumed by trials whose *outcome* resolves only later —
anchor-indexed promotion attempts
(Corollary [S5.27](#A5.Thmtheorem27 "Corollary S5.27 (Submission budget and publisher accountability). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and opening-indexed panel instances
(Proposition [S5.22](#A5.Thmtheorem22 "Proposition S5.22 (Publisher accountability is safe for benign items). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii),
linear tier) — where later trials may open before earlier outcomes
resolve, so outcome order need not equal occurrence order. The coupling
machinery of
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is neither needed nor invoked there.

###### Lemma S8.7 (Predictable cell allocation).

In the setting of
Remark [S8.4](#A8.Thmtheorem4 "Remark S8.4 (𝜎-algebra form). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
fix finitely many cells $`(j,\ell)`$, $`j\leq r`$, $`\ell\leq K`$.
Suppose each realised trial $`i`$ is assigned to at most one cell,
injectively across trials, by an assignment that is
$`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurable (decided at the trial’s occurrence,
before its content). On the enlargement of
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
carrying the coupling variables $`Y_{i}=\mathbf{1}\{U_{i}\leq p\}`$,
define the cell-indexed array $`X_{j,\ell}:=Y_{i(j,\ell)}`$ where
$`i(j,\ell)`$ is the trial assigned to cell $`(j,\ell)`$, and
$`X_{j,\ell}:=\mathbf{1}\{U^{\prime}_{j,\ell}\leq p\}`$ with fresh
independent uniforms $`U^{\prime}_{j,\ell}`$ for never-filled cells.
Then $`(X_{j,\ell})_{j\leq r,\,\ell\leq K}`$ is i.i.d.
$`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)`$.

###### Proof.

This is optional skipping in the sense of Doob, extended to a
predictable partition. Order trials by occurrence. At trial $`i`$’s
occurrence its cell assignment is $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$-measurable, while
$`U_{i}`$ is independent of $`\mathcal{G}_{i}`$
(Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
construction) — in particular of all previously assigned cells and all
previously revealed coupling variables; the fresh
$`U^{\prime}_{j,\ell}`$ are independent of everything. Fix any
$`\varepsilon:\{(j,\ell)\}\to\{0,1\}`$ and reveal the array in
assignment order, completing with the fresh uniforms: at each
revelation, the conditional probability that the next revealed entry
equals its prescribed value is $`p^{\varepsilon}(1-p)^{1-\varepsilon}`$
for that entry, by the independence just stated. Induction along the
revelation order gives
$`\mathbb{P}[X_{j,\ell}=\varepsilon(j,\ell)\ \forall j,\ell]=\prod_{j,\ell}p^{\varepsilon(j,\ell)}(1-p)^{1-\varepsilon(j,\ell)}`$,
i.e. the array is i.i.d. $`\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)`$. ∎

###### Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms).

1.  (i)
    *(Independent, deterministic weights.)* Let $`X_{j}\in\{0,1\}`$ be
    independent with $`\mathbb{P}[X_{j}{=}1]\leq\varepsilon`$, and let
    $`w_{j}\in[0,w_{\max}]`$ be deterministic, $`j=1,\dots,n`$. Then for
    $`t>0`$,
    $`\mathbb{P}[\sum_{j}w_{j}X_{j}\geq\varepsilon\sum_{j}w_{j}+t]\leq\exp\!\big(-2t^{2}/(nw_{\max}^{2})\big)`$
    [Hoeffding (1963)](#bib.bib22); the unweighted case gives
    $`\mathbb{P}[\mathrm{Bin}(n,\varepsilon)\geq(\varepsilon+\delta)n]\leq e^{-2\delta^{2}n}`$.
2.  (ii)
    *(Predictable weights, conditional success bound.)* Let
    $`(\mathcal{H}_{j})_{j\geq 0}`$ be a filtration, $`X_{j}\in\{0,1\}`$
    adapted with
    $`\mathbb{P}[X_{j}{=}1\mid\mathcal{H}_{j-1}]\leq\varepsilon`$, and
    $`w_{j}\in[0,w_{\max}]`$ predictable (each $`w_{j}`$
    $`\mathcal{H}_{j-1}`$-measurable). Then the bound of (i) holds with
    the identical exponent.

###### Proof.

(ii) Set
$`D_{j}:=w_{j}\big(X_{j}-\mathbb{E}[X_{j}\mid\mathcal{H}_{j-1}]\big)`$,
a martingale-difference sequence whose $`j`$-th increment lies, given
$`\mathcal{H}_{j-1}`$, in an interval of predictable length
$`w_{j}\leq w_{\max}`$. The Hoeffding–Azuma inequality in its
conditional-range form (Hoeffding’s lemma applied conditionally to each
increment, then Markov on the exponential moment) gives
$`\mathbb{P}[\sum_{j}D_{j}\geq t]\leq\exp\!\big(-2t^{2}/\sum_{j}w_{j}^{2}\big)\leq\exp\!\big(-2t^{2}/(nw_{\max}^{2})\big)`$.
Since
$`\sum_{j}w_{j}\mathbb{E}[X_{j}\mid\mathcal{H}_{j-1}]\leq\varepsilon\sum_{j}w_{j}`$
pathwise, the event
$`\{\sum_{j}w_{j}X_{j}\geq\varepsilon\sum_{j}w_{j}+t\}`$ is contained in
$`\{\sum_{j}D_{j}\geq t\}`$. (The bounded-difference form of Azuma’s
inequality, with increments bounded in absolute value by $`w_{\max}`$,
would give only $`\exp(-t^{2}/(2nw_{\max}^{2}))`$; the range form is the
one used.) ∎

###### Theorem S8.9 (No-dispute baseline: reach-dependent).

Without
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with rejections protocol-inert and a poisoned item shown to at most
$`R`$ honest users each erroneously accepting with probability
$`\leq\varepsilon`$ independently: if
$`W>W_{\mathrm{adv}}+\varepsilon Rw_{\max}`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion}]\ \leq\ \exp\!\Big(-\frac{2(W-W_{\mathrm{adv}}-\varepsilon Rw_{\max})^{2}}{R\,w_{\max}^{2}}\Big).
``` |  |

###### Proof.

Accepting weight is at most $`W_{\mathrm{adv}}+S`$ with
$`S=\sum_{j}w_{j}X_{j}`$ over $`\leq R`$ honest users; apply
Lemma [S8.8](#A8.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S8.8 (Hoeffding tails: independent and predictable-weight forms). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with $`t=W-W_{\mathrm{adv}}-\varepsilon Rw_{\max}`$. ∎

###### Comparison with the no-dispute baseline.

The comparison isolates exactly what the panel and the
gate-rejection-as-report rule buy. In
Theorem [S8.9](#A8.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S8.9 (No-dispute baseline: reach-dependent). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
rejections are inert, so honest false acceptances accumulate with reach:
the sample size is the *attacker-chosen reach* $`R`$, the bound requires
$`W`$ to grow linearly with $`\varepsilon R`$ merely to stay
non-trivial, dragging the budget of
Appendix [S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with it, and spreading the poison farther helps the attacker: the bound
is not reach-free in the sense of
[INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
In
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
because every honest inspection carries its own report
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)),
the no-dispute event shrinks with every additional honest viewer, and
the false-accept mass that matters after a dispute is confined to a
bounded jury of $`k-f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ honest verdicts, a protocol
constant the attacker cannot multiply, and one the demand-paced
formation rule fills without any deadline the attacker could exploit.
Reach drops out of the bound entirely, and spreading the poison cannot
loosen the bound, while any single honest gate rejection freezes it. The
dispute log additionally makes wrongful rejection a costly, attributable
act, and panel eviction makes poisoned submission a costly, attributable
act
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(v),(vii)),
neither of which the inert-rejection baseline can express.

#### S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law

This subsection derives, in closed form, the promotion probability of
one *simulated* presentation schedule under one *simulated* model of
honest behaviour. It is an analysis tool for the empirical evaluation,
not a protocol guarantee: no rule, assumption, definition, or theorem of
Appendices [S2](#A2a "Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
cites it, and nothing in this document depends on it. Its purpose is to
turn the simulator’s output into a falsifiable prediction, so that
agreement is evidence the implementation realises the rules of
Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and disagreement localises a defect in one of the two.

###### Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin).

The *blast* schedule is the non-adaptive presentation strategy that
(i) submits a poisoned item
(Definition [S4.10](#A4.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S4.10 (Exogenous item classification). ‣ Adversary (federated). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
with all endorsement and all demand at a single tool, (ii) spends every
adversarial identity as a pre-dispute accepting endorser at that tool,
and (iii) then presents the item, once each, to $`R`$ honest identities
in a fixed order (the *reach*, as in
Theorem [S8.9](#A8.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S8.9 (No-dispute baseline: reach-dependent). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
continuing through every one of them whatever any of them decides. Four
stipulations fix the simulated setting.

1.  (a)
    *One window.* All $`R`$ presentations, and any panel the schedule
    induces, fall within a *single* finalisation window of one pipeline
    entry, with the freeze excluded from the window clock
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv))
    and no epoch boundary closing the window early
    (convention ([C4](#A1.I2.i4 "Item C4 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
    In particular the entry is open throughout, so no decision is banked
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b),
    which requires no open entry) and no re-entry occurs: every
    weight-bearing decision is credited to that one entry.
2.  (b)
    *Independent honest coin.* Each of the $`R`$ inspections is,
    independently of the others, a rejecting decision with probability
    $`q`$ and an accepting decision with probability $`1-q`$, with no
    abstention.
3.  (c)
    *Coupled reviewer quality.* The same $`q`$ governs pre-freeze gate
    inspections, panel verdicts, and post-resolution confirmations
    ($`q_{\mathrm{pre}}=q_{\mathrm{pan}}=q`$); the decoupled reading,
    under which those three classes may carry different parameters, is
    Remark [S8.17](#A8.Thmtheorem17 "Remark S8.17 (Decoupled reviewer quality). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
4.  (d)
    *Seat weight and eligibility.* Every identity carries attestation
    weight at least $`w_{\mathrm{seat}}`$, so a fresh decision on the
    item is verdict-eligible whenever a dispute is open
    (Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(a));
    every decision, the $`f`$ adversarial pre-dispute endorsements
    included, is authority-active
    (Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a))
    and taken at a non-covered, non-cache gate, so every accepting
    decision is creditable and every rejecting decision takes effect;
    and identities are assigned to the $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ pools
    round-robin.

Independence across inspections is a property of this simulation only:
no result of
Appendices [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[S6](#A6 "Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
assumes it, and
Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
explicitly does not
(§[S8.1](#A8.SS1 "S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Remark [S8.14](#A8.Thmtheorem14 "Remark S8.14 (𝜋_pan is not the theorem’s panel term). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proposition S8.11 (Blast promotion law).

Adopt
Rules [R12](#Thmrulex12 "Rule R12 (Sharing eligibility and the publish gate). ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
with the default bars of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
($`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=k+1-m`$, hence $`m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1=k`$), and the
blast schedule and independent honest coin of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
Suppose

|     |                                             |     |
|-----|---------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       N-f\;\leq\;m,\qquad N-f\;\leq\;R\;\leq\;2m,
       ```                                          |     |

and suppose the deployment’s constants and pool assignment leave the
credit caps of
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)
non-binding for promotion at every reach in that range (Step 1). Define

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S(J)\;:=\;\sum_{r=0}^{\min(J-m,\;m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1)}\binom{m-1+r}{r}\Big(\frac{q}{1-q}\Big)^{\!r}\quad(J\geq m),\qquad S(J):=0\quad(J<m).
``` |  |

Then the item is promoted to $`\mathsf{CC}`$ with probability
$`\pi_{\mathrm{blast}}(R)=\pi_{\mathrm{ord}}(R)+\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)`$,
where the two components — promotion with no dispute ever opened, and
promotion after a dispute — are disjoint and equal

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\pi_{\mathrm{ord}}(R)=(1-q)^{R},\qquad\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)=q\,(1-q)^{R-1}\sum_{J=m}^{R-1}S(J).
``` |  |

Neither expression contains $`k`$, $`f`$, $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$, or
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$.

###### Proof.

*Step 0 (no adversarial verdict).* Blast spends its $`f`$ identities as
pre-dispute accepting endorsers before any honest presentation. By
byte-permanence of freshness
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
each identity’s first logged decision on the bytes is its only
weight-bearing inspection, and verdict eligibility requires freshness
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(b));
so when the freeze lands no adversarial identity is verdict-eligible,
and every verdict is cast by an honest identity. Hence $`f`$ and
$`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$ do not appear.

*Step 1 (no capacity, verdict-pool, or credit cap binds).* Under the
default bars $`m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1=k`$, so at most $`k`$ verdicts are
cast before a bar is reached
(Lemma [S5.7](#A5.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S5.7 (Decisive resolution under the default bars). ‣ S5.1 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii))
and the capacity cap of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(e)
is never the binding constraint. Two further caps are properties of the
simulated population rather than consequences of the rules, and are
disclosed as such. With the round-robin assignment of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d),
no pool contributes more than $`\lceil k/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$
verdicts among any prefix of $`k`$ arrivals, so the per-pool verdict cap
of
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(d)
does not bind. Likewise the per-pool and total *credit* caps of
Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(f)
truncate crediting at $`\lceil N/D_{\mathrm{pool}}\rceil`$ per pool and
$`N^{+}`$ in total, and those caps are promotion-neutral in the sense
stated there — $`N^{+}\geq N`$, and a credited set meeting $`N`$ under
the per-pool cap necessarily spans at least $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ pools
— *provided* enough accepting identities are available in each pool at
the reach in question. That availability is a property of the constants
and the round-robin assignment, verified for the deployment studied here
and assumed in the statement; where it fails, the law does not apply and
$`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ re-enters. Hence, under the stated hypothesis,
$`k`$ and $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$ do not appear.

*Step 2 (the ordinary component).* Suppose no honest inspection rejects.
No dispute opens; the accepting decisions are all authority-active
(Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d)),
so credited accepting endorsements number $`\min(f+R,N^{+})\geq N`$,
using $`R\geq N-f`$ with Step 1; and the entry promotes at its window’s
close
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)).
Conversely, a rejecting decision at *any* point in the window is a
qualifying rejection that freezes promotion at every tool immediately
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)),
while finalisation occurs only at the window’s close, which by
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
lies after all $`R`$ presentations — so a single rejection, however
late, denies the ordinary path. The ordinary component is therefore
exactly the all-accept event, of probability $`(1-q)^{R}`$.

*Step 3 (the panel component; conditioning).* Condition on the first
rejection falling at honest position $`j`$, an event of probability
$`q(1-q)^{j-1}`$. The item is unpromoted and unfrozen at that moment, so
that rejection is dispute-initiating
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)–(ii)).
The remaining $`J:=R-j`$ inspections are, by Steps 0–1 and
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d),
honest, fresh and seat-weighted; each is an eligible verdict for as long
as the dispute is unresolved, and an ordinary accepting or rejecting
confirmation thereafter. Steps 4–5 treat the two segments separately.

*Step 4 (no rejection after the $`m`$-th acceptance).* Vindication
resumes the interrupted entry but never itself promotes: promotion
occurs only at the window’s close
(Definition [S4.6](#A4.Thmtheorem6a "Definition S4.6 (Endorsement counting and banking). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)).
A rejecting decision logged after vindication is therefore a fresh
qualifying rejection against an unpromoted entry, which re-imposes the
byte-level freeze
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)).
Verdict capacity is scoped to the dispute *instance*
([INV-5](#Thminvx5 "Invariant INV-5 (Verdict non-renewal). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and so is available afresh in the second instance; what is not available
is freshness, which is byte-permanent
([INV-1](#Thminvx1 "Invariant INV-1 (Byte-permanence of freshness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)(b)):
the second instance draws eligible jurors only from identities with no
prior logged decision on the bytes, of whom at most $`m-1`$ remain
(Step 7). It therefore cannot vindicate; its only other outcomes are
eviction, which ends the presence outright, and an unresolved instance,
under which the window clock does not run out at all because the freeze
is excluded from it
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)).
In either case the entry never reaches an unfrozen window end, so it
cannot finalise. Under blast every one of the $`J`$ post-freeze
identities decides, so the qualifying sequences are exactly those whose
tail after the $`m`$-th acceptance is unanimously accepting.

*Step 5 (the count, and the credited threshold).* Fix $`J`$ and index
the post-freeze inspections $`1,\dots,J`$. By Step 4, promotion
requires: the $`m`$-th accepting verdict at position $`m+r`$ for some
$`r`$, with exactly $`r`$ rejecting verdicts before it and
$`r\leq m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1`$ (otherwise the eviction bar is reached
first) and $`m+r\leq J`$; and every one of the remaining $`J-m-r`$
decisions accepting. The first $`m+r-1`$ positions hold $`m-1`$
acceptances and $`r`$ rejections in any order, $`\binom{m-1+r}{r}`$
ways, and every such sequence carries $`r`$ rejections and $`J-r`$
acceptances. *The credited count is sufficient on every such sequence*:
the accepting decisions credited to the entry are the $`f`$ pre-dispute
endorsements, the $`j-1`$ pre-freeze honest acceptances, the $`m`$
accepting verdicts (credited on vindication,
Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv))
and the $`J-m-r`$ post-resolution acceptances, all authority-active by
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d),
totalling $`f+R-1-r`$; since $`r\leq J-m=R-j-m`$ and $`j\geq 1`$, this
is at least $`f+m\geq N`$ by the hypothesis $`N-f\leq m`$, and Step 1
keeps the caps from truncating below $`N`$. Hence

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion}\mid J]=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(J-m,\,m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1)}\binom{m-1+r}{r}q^{r}(1-q)^{J-r}=(1-q)^{J}S(J),
``` |  |

which is $`0`$ for $`J<m`$, no arrangement of fewer than $`m`$ verdicts
reaching the $`m`$-bar.

*Step 6 (collapse).* Summing over $`j`$, and using
$`(1-q)^{j-1}(1-q)^{R-j}=(1-q)^{R-1}`$ with the substitution $`J=R-j`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)=\sum_{j=1}^{R-m}q(1-q)^{j-1}\,\Big[(1-q)^{J}S(J)\Big]_{J=R-j}=q(1-q)^{R-1}\sum_{J=m}^{R-1}S(J).
``` |  |

*Step 7 (validity, and exhaustiveness).* The hypothesis $`R\leq 2m`$ is
what makes Step 4’s tail requirement exactly right. At the $`m`$-th
accepting verdict, $`j+m+r`$ inspections have occurred, so at most
$`R-j-m-r\leq R-m-1\leq m-1<m`$ remain: too few for any second dispute
to reach its own $`m`$-bar, whatever its verdicts. The two cases — no
rejection anywhere, and a first rejection at some position — are
exhaustive and disjoint, so
$`\pi_{\mathrm{blast}}=\pi_{\mathrm{ord}}+\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$. ∎

###### Remark S8.12 (Where each hypothesis is consumed).

The proposition’s hypotheses and the stipulations of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
are not interchangeable, and each is used once. $`R\geq N-f`$ is
Step 2’s threshold. $`N-f\leq m`$ is Step 5’s, and it is not implied by
the others, since $`N-f\leq R\leq 2m`$ permits $`N-f=2m`$ — at which
reach a counted panel sequence can credit as few as $`f+m<N`$
acceptances and the formula would over-count; it is also what makes the
plateau identity of
Corollary [S8.13](#A8.Thmtheorem13 "Corollary S8.13 (Five structural consequences). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
meaningful, that identity evaluating $`\pi_{\mathrm{ord}}`$ at $`R=m`$,
which requires $`m\geq N-f`$. $`R\leq 2m`$ is Step 7. The credit-cap
non-bindingness is Steps 1, 2 and 5. The one-window stipulation of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(a)
is Step 2’s converse and Step 4’s re-freeze; the seat-weight and
authority stipulations of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(d)
are Step 3’s eligibility and Steps 2 and 5’s crediting. At the geometry
studied here ($`N=10`$, $`f=2`$, $`m=20`$, $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=12`$) the
first two hold with slack, $`N-f=8\leq\min(m,R)=\min(20,R)`$ for every
$`R\geq 8`$, and the binding hypothesis is $`R\leq 40`$.

###### Corollary S8.13 (Five structural consequences).

Under the hypotheses of
Proposition [S8.11](#A8.Thmtheorem11 "Proposition S8.11 (Blast promotion law). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"):

1.  (i)
    *(Structural zero and switch-on.)* $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)=0`$ for
    every $`R\leq m`$, and its first nonzero value is at $`R=m+1`$,
    where it equals exactly $`q(1-q)^{m}`$ (since $`S(m)=1`$). This is a
    support property, invariant under any change of measure.
2.  (ii)
    *(No $`k`$, $`f`$, $`f_{\mathrm{s}}`$, $`D_{\mathrm{pool}}`$.)* As
    stated, by Steps 0–1.
3.  (iii)
    *($`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ enters late.)* The cap in $`S(J)`$ first
    differs from $`J-m`$ at $`J=m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$, and
    $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)`$ reaches $`J=R-1`$; hence
    $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is independent of $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ for
    all $`R\leq m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ and first depends on it at
    $`R=m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}+1`$, where the difference between the capped
    and uncapped forms is exactly the single $`r=m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ term
    at $`J=m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$.
4.  (iv)
    *(Plateau identity.)*
    $`\pi_{\mathrm{blast}}(m)=\pi_{\mathrm{blast}}(m+1)=(1-q)^{m}`$
    exactly, since $`(1-q)^{m+1}+q(1-q)^{m}=(1-q)^{m}`$. The switch-on
    is therefore *invisible* in the total rate and visible only in the
    decomposition — which is why the figure that exhibits it plots the
    two components separately rather than their sum.
5.  (v)
    *(Peak and fall.)* $`S(J)`$ is constant in $`J`$ for
    $`J\geq m+m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1`$, so $`\sum_{J}S(J)`$ grows linearly
    in $`R`$ while $`(1-q)^{R-1}`$ decays geometrically:
    $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ rises, attains an interior maximum, and
    falls.

###### Remark S8.14 ($`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ is not the theorem’s panel term).

$`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)`$ and the panel term of $`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$
(Remark [S5.17](#A5.Thmtheorem17 "Remark S5.17 (The certified per-attempt ceiling 𝐵_att). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
are different objects and must not be conflated. The theorem’s term is a
reach-free *upper bound* over all adaptive presentation, stopping and
re-entry strategies, holding under a conditional lower bound on honest
behaviour alone and assuming no independence — the exact binomial tail
arises there from the coupling of
Lemma [S8.2](#A8.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma S8.2 (Adaptive conditional coupling and domination). ‣ Demand randomness, formally. ‣ S8.1 Probabilistic framework, coupling, and the no-dispute baseline ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
not from an independence hypothesis; $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(R)`$ is the
exact realised probability of one non-adaptive schedule under the
independence of
Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b).
A large gap between them is expected and is *not* evidence that the
bound is loose: tightness is a separate empirical question, addressed by
strategies that reserve seat-eligible identities and stop at the first
bar reached, which *empirically attain* the flat panel term — precisely
because they *can* stop, while blast cannot, which is why blast’s
realised rate peaks and falls where the theorem’s term is constant. Two
schedules, one mechanism, opposite consequences, both predicted.

###### Remark S8.15 (Validity, and the direction of failure beyond it).

The law holds in the single-dispute regime $`R\leq 2m`$, and Step 7 is
where that hypothesis is consumed. Beyond it a post-vindication
rejection can open a second dispute among still-unpresented, still-fresh
jurors, whose own $`m`$-bar is now reachable; the single-dispute form
therefore *under-counts*, and the direction of failure is fixed in
advance rather than discovered. Consequently no reading of the law
beyond $`2m`$ is a prediction: past that reach the schedule’s rate is a
measured quantity and the law is not a model of it. Nothing about the
failure bears on any bound: $`B_{\mathrm{att}}`$ is reach-free
([INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
and continues to hold at every reach, and
[INV-6](#Thminvx6 "Invariant INV-6 (Reach-freeness). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
disclaims monotonicity of the *realised* rate precisely so that a
plateau or a rise in a measured sweep is inside the theory rather than
against it.

- Commentary (non-normative; the validity boundary, measured). At the
  deployed geometry ($`q=0.6`$, $`N=10`$, $`f=2`$, $`k=31`$, $`m=20`$,
  $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=12`$, so $`2m=40`$) the boundary of
  Remark [S8.15](#A8.Thmtheorem15 "Remark S8.15 (Validity, and the direction of failure beyond it). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is measured, not merely asserted. At the last in-validity reach the
  law gives $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(40)=1.049\times 10^{-5}`$ against $`9`$
  promotions in $`10^{6}`$ trials. At $`R=64`$ the same schedule yields
  $`8`$ promotions in $`10^{6}`$ trials ($`8.0\times 10^{-6}`$,
  Clopper–Pearson $`95\%`$ $`[3.45,\,15.76]\times 10^{-6}`$) against an
  extrapolation of $`1.057\times 10^{-14}`$ — a factor
  $`7.57\times 10^{8}`$, i.e. $`8.88`$ orders of magnitude above it, in
  the disclosed under-counting direction. At equal trial count $`R=40`$
  and $`R=64`$ are statistically indistinguishable ($`z=0.243`$), so the
  realised rate plateaus rather than continuing its geometric decay. The
  plateau does not persist: at $`R=100`$ the rate is bounded above by
  $`3.69\times 10^{-6}`$, a bound that overlaps $`R=64`$’s lower
  confidence limit, so the claim is *no rise*, not *a fall*. Every
  measured cell of this sweep lies below
  $`B_{\mathrm{att}}=8.957\times 10^{-3}`$: the boundary cell $`R=40`$
  by $`3.00`$ decades and every cell beyond it by at least $`3.05`$. The
  generating experiment gates on that conformance, at every cell of
  every sweep, before writing its artifact. Inside the validity window
  the margin is far smaller — about $`0.58`$ decades at the panel-path
  peak $`R=32`$, where the measured rate is $`2.34\times 10^{-3}`$ —
  which is where the ceiling is informative rather than slack. No
  mechanism is proposed for the plateau’s magnitude: beyond $`2m`$ the
  sweep is *measured, not modelled*.

###### Remark S8.16 (Testability of the $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ entry).

Corollary [S8.13](#A8.Thmtheorem13 "Corollary S8.13 (Five structural consequences). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
is sharply testable only for small $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$. The entering
term is weighed against the partial sum $`\sum_{J=m}^{R-1}S(J)`$ that
$`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ carries at the entry reach, and that sum grows
with $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ far faster than the single entering term does,
so the relative effect shrinks sharply as the eviction bar rises. The
claim is therefore made where it is resolvable — at small
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$, for two values of $`m`$ — while for large
$`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ the testable statement is agreement with the
uncapped form below the entry reach. Two of the three confirmations
available are support properties rather than hypothesis tests: below the
entry reach the capped and uncapped forms are *equal*, so two panel
widths sharing one coin stream must produce byte-identical counts, which
cannot be passed by luck.

- Commentary (non-normative; the $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$ entry,
  measured). At $`m=20`$ and $`q=0.2`$: at $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=4`$, entry
  reach $`R=25`$, the entering term is $`34.59`$ against a partial sum
  of $`112.5`$, a $`+30.75\%`$ effect; at $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=12`$, entry
  reach $`R=33`$, it is $`8.411`$ against $`2003.05`$, a $`+0.42\%`$
  effect. The corresponding rates are $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(25)=0.10625`$
  capped against $`0.13892`$ uncapped, and
  $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}(33)=0.31740`$ against $`0.31873`$. Reading a
  five-sigma requirement as five standard errors of the difference
  between two arms of $`K`$ trials each, with the variance evaluated at
  the capped rate — $`K=25\cdot 2p(1-p)/\Delta^{2}`$ — those effects
  need $`4.5\times 10^{3}`$ and $`6.1\times 10^{6}`$ trials per arm
  respectively. The prediction is accordingly claimed at
  $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}=4`$, where it is confirmed three ways:
  byte-identical counts across two panel widths sharing one coin stream
  at every reach below the entry; a $`+13.6\sigma`$ divergence at the
  entry reach itself; and two $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ profiles whose
  maxima over the sampled reach grid fall where the law places them,
  $`R=26`$ with $`4{,}715`$ observed against $`4{,}705`$ predicted and
  $`R=30`$ with $`14{,}030`$ against $`14{,}001`$. One scope note on the
  maxima: the $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}{=}4`$ profile’s exact maximum lies at
  $`R=27`$, a reach that grid does not sample, so $`R=26`$ is a maximum
  over the sampled grid and not the argmax of $`\pi_{\mathrm{pan}}`$;
  the two differ by $`2.2\%`$ in value.

###### Remark S8.17 (Decoupled reviewer quality).

Definition [S8.10](#A8.Thmtheorem10 "Definition S8.10 (Blast schedule; independent honest coin). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(c)
couples three decision classes that the protocol distinguishes:
pre-freeze gate inspections, panel verdicts, and post-resolution
confirmations. Under a decoupled reading the first and third are
ordinary gate inspections, governed by $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$, while only
the second are verdicts, governed by $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$; Steps 0–5
then go through with

|     |                                                 |     |
|-----|-------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \pi_{\mathrm{ord}}(R)=(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{R},
       ```                                              |     |

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion}\mid J]=\sum_{r=0}^{\min(J-m,\,m_{\mathrm{rej}}-1)}\binom{m-1+r}{r}q_{\mathrm{pan}}^{\,r}(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})^{m}(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{J-m-r},
``` |  |

the $`m+r`$ verdicts charged at $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ and the unanimous
tail of $`J-m-r`$ post-resolution confirmations at $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}`$.
But Step 6’s collapse fails — the two geometric factors no longer share
a base — and the panel component remains the double sum
$`\sum_{j=1}^{R-m}q_{\mathrm{pre}}(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{j-1}\mathbb{P}[\text{promotion}\mid R-j]`$.
Setting $`q_{\mathrm{pre}}=q_{\mathrm{pan}}=q`$ recovers
Proposition [S8.11](#A8.Thmtheorem11 "Proposition S8.11 (Blast promotion law). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
exactly, which is why the closed form is specific to the coupled reading
and why the figures that exhibit the law run coupled reviewer quality
while the decoupled figures report ceilings only. A deployment or
simulator adopting the decoupled reading must additionally fix, and
disclose, which parameter governs the post-resolution tail: assigning it
to $`q_{\mathrm{pan}}`$ instead — a defensible modelling choice, since
those inspections occur under the dispute flag — replaces
$`(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{J-m-r}`$ by $`(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})^{J-m-r}`$ and
yields
$`q_{\mathrm{pre}}(1-q_{\mathrm{pre}})^{j-1}(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})^{J}S_{q_{\mathrm{pan}}}(J)`$
with $`S_{q_{\mathrm{pan}}}`$ the sum $`S`$ at ratio
$`q_{\mathrm{pan}}/(1-q_{\mathrm{pan}})`$. The two forms differ except
in the coupled case, and no result of this document distinguishes them.

- Commentary (non-normative; epistemic status of the blast law). Three
  things this law is not. It is not a safety claim: the safety statement
  is
  Theorem [S5.13](#A5.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S5.13 (Panel safety under adaptive presentation). ‣ S5.2 Main theorems ‣ Appendix S5 Federated Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  which assumes no independence and quantifies over all adaptive
  schedules, and this law’s exponential decay would not survive an
  adversary that stops at the first rejection — such an adversary is
  confined to the ordinary path and is measured separately. It is not a
  tightness claim
  (Remark [S8.14](#A8.Thmtheorem14 "Remark S8.14 (𝜋_pan is not the theorem’s panel term). ‣ S8.2 The blast-schedule promotion law ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
  And it is not an assumption of anything: no rule reads it, no proof
  cites it, and the protocol’s behaviour is identical whether or not it
  holds; it is accordingly absent from the assumptions ledger of
  §[S8.6](#A8.SS6 "S8.6 Assumptions ledger ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").

  What it is, is the instrument that makes the simulator falsifiable.
  Every one of its five consequences is a prediction the implementation
  could violate, three of them at the level of *support* rather than of
  a tail probability — the structural zero, the $`k`$-independence, and
  the $`m_{\mathrm{rej}}`$-independence below the entry reach are all
  byte-identity properties that cannot be passed by luck. Its own
  derivation is verified against two independent oracles: direct
  enumeration of every verdict sequence at small
  $`(m,m_{\mathrm{rej}})`$, applying the decision rule of Step 4 without
  reference to the closed form; and an uncollapsed exact-rational sum
  over the rejecter’s position, so that an algebra error in Step 6
  cannot cancel.

  These checks share an interpretive premise: Step 4 is a *reading* of
  Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  and the enumeration oracle shares that reading with the claim it
  checks, so the two are not independent on that point. Unlike the
  single-user core
  (§[S9](#A9 "Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
  none of this is machine-checked. An implementation that disagreed with
  the law would be either a simulator defect or a misreading of
  Appendix [S4](#A4a "Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
  and the law’s role is to make the difference cheap to find.

#### S8.3 Explicit ledger constants

###### Lemma S8.18 (Explicit forms of $`A(M)`$ and $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$).

Summing the rows of
Table [S2](#A6.T2 "Table S2 ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
under the charging convention of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
with $`\bar{D}_{v}`$ as there and
$`\kappa^{\prime}:=\kappa+c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[C^{\mathrm{pipe}}_{v}]\ \leq\ A(M)\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]\;+\;B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v}],
``` |  |

with

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle A(M)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}\big(N^{+}+1+s_{0}\big)`$ |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\big(2(1-p_{b})E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}s_{0}+(1-p_{b})E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f+2E_{\max}+1\big)\,\kappa^{\prime},`$ |  |

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
B_{\mathrm{fl}}\ :=\ 2\,E_{\star}\,c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}\Big[1+(1-p_{b})\,\kappa^{\prime}\Big],
``` |  |

where $`\kappa^{\prime}`$ folds at most $`c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ invited
re-inspections per fast-track review
(Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(vi))
into the freeze-bucket multiplier; the suspension-prompt row is
majorised by the $`c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ component of the freeze-bucket term
($`E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{p}}k\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\bar{D}_{v}\,c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$,
since $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\geq 1`$ and $`\bar{D}_{v}\geq 2E_{\max}+1`$),
a deliberate slackening: the prompt row is charged once in the ledger
and bounded once here, by a dominating expression. Using
$`1\leq D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq N`$
(Definition [S4.3](#A4.Thmtheorem3a "Definition S4.3 (Identity pools). ‣ Two-tier storage of community status. ‣ S4.1 Identities, pools, epochs, and demand ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
$`N\leq N^{+}<N+D_{\mathrm{pool}}\leq 2N`$ and
$`E_{\star}\leq 2E_{\max}`$, these satisfy
$`A(M)=\mathcal{O}\!\big(E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(N+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f)(1+\kappa)\big)`$
and
$`B_{\mathrm{fl}}=\mathcal{O}\!\big(E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(1+(1-p_{b})\kappa)\big)`$.
The forms are closed-form *upper bounds*, exact in structure and
monotone-slackened in constants; they are not claimed tight.

###### Proof.

Row sums under the charging convention of first item-arrival
attribution, splitting each $`(\bar{\gamma}n_{v}+s_{0})`$ term into its
$`\bar{\gamma}n_{v}`$ part (collected into $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$) and its
$`s_{0}`$ part (collected into $`A(M)`$):

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\underbrace{E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}}_{\text{weight}}+\underbrace{E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0})}_{\text{window bucket}}+\underbrace{E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}+s_{0})}_{\text{dormancy bucket}}\\
+\underbrace{c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\bar{D}_{v}\,\kappa^{\prime}}_{\text{freeze bucket (prompts
folded in)}}+\underbrace{E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}}_{\text{repeat}}+\underbrace{E_{\max}}_{\text{publish}}.
``` |  |

The former reversal accounting appears in no separate term: a prior
rejecter’s later acceptances are charged to that demander’s bucket
inside the per-demander $`\times c_{\mathrm{tool}}`$ factors of the
three bucket rows
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
charging convention), so no $`\bar{D}_{v}(1+\kappa)`$ reversal term
arises. The suspension-prompt row is majorised by, not identical to, the
$`c_{\mathrm{p}}k`$ component of the freeze-bucket term
($`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\geq 1`$, $`\bar{D}_{v}\geq 2E_{\max}+1`$), so its
events are charged once (to their row) and bounded once (by the
dominating freeze expression). Collecting the coefficient of
$`\bar{\gamma}n_{v}`$: $`2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}`$ from the
window and dormancy buckets, plus
$`2(1-p_{b})E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}\kappa^{\prime}`$ from the
freeze bucket through $`\bar{D}_{v}`$’s first term, giving
$`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$. Collecting the demand-free remainder:
$`2E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+E_{\max}+2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}s_{0}+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\kappa^{\prime}\big(2(1-p_{b})E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}s_{0}+(1-p_{b})E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f+2E_{\max}+1\big)\leq A(M)`$,
using
$`2E_{\max}c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+E_{\max}+2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}s_{0}\leq 2E_{\star}c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}(N^{+}+1+s_{0})`$
($`E_{\max}\leq E_{\star}`$, $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\geq 1`$,
[A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
$`E_{\star}\geq 1`$,
convention ([C8](#A1.I2.i8 "Item C8 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
Taking expectations over the demand, with the indicator carried per
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
(every row’s pathwise count vanishes on $`\{n_{v}=0\}`$), gives the
claim; the $`\mathcal{O}`$-forms follow since
$`c_{\mathrm{p}}k=\mathcal{O}(\kappa)`$ for $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$
````
