````math
bounded below, $`\kappa=(k{+}1)/\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}\geq k`$, and
$`E_{\star}=E_{\max}+1\leq 2E_{\max}`$ ($`E_{\max}\geq 1`$,
convention ([C8](#A1.I2.i8 "Item C8 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))).
∎

###### Remark S8.19 (Reading of the ledger constants).

\(i\) The bracketed
$`\big((1-p_{b})c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{acc}}f\big)\kappa^{\prime}`$
term is the *dispute cross-term*: honest reconsideration capacity and
adversarial dispute capacity multiplied by panel cost, with
suspension-prompt re-inspections folded into $`\kappa^{\prime}`$ inside
the freeze term, the prompt row majorised by the freeze term rather than
independently summed; it is what forces the cross-term condition
$`N(M)k(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$ of
Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(ii) The $`\kappa^{\prime}`$-part of $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$ is damped by
$`1-p_{b}`$, the honest wrongful-rejection rate: the front-loaded freeze
load scales with honest error, not with demand alone. (iii) The
front-loading coefficient $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}`$ multiplies only the
fraction $`\bar{\gamma}`$ of the item’s own demand: item popularity
enters the per-item cost solely through $`\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}`$ and
cancels against the population in
Lemma [S6.8](#A6.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma S6.8 (Distinct-demand bound, two-term form). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
(iv) The $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}^{2}`$ in both constants is the pair-level
discipline made explicit: one factor counts the pairs over which a
bucket’s demanders are enumerated
([A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")’s
demand clause, read per pair), the other the pairs each demander may
confirm
([INV-3](#Thminvx3 "Invariant INV-3 (Single-approval cap, per (user, value, tool)). ‣ S1.4 Named invariants and structural properties ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
both are $`\mathcal{O}(1)`$
([A12](#Thmassumptionx12 "Assumption A12 (Bounded tool-spread). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
so no asymptotic statement changes.

#### S8.4 Knowledge-based formulation of Reasoning Integrity

Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is trace-wise per coin sequence. It induces the following statement in
the knowledge-based style of gradual release [Askarov & Sabelfeld
(2007)](#bib.bib3), recorded to dispel the classical worry that
conditioning on release events can itself be secret-dependent.

###### Proposition S8.20 (Gradual release).

Fix the strategies $`P`$ and $`R_{\mathcal{E}}`$, the slot skeleton, a
coin sequence $`\omega`$, and a typed stream
([A6](#Thmassumptionx6 "Assumption A6 (Exogenous command stream). ‣ S2.4 Trust axioms ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
in the federated setting also a federation log,
[A8](#Thmassumptionx8 "Assumption A8 (Exogenous federation log). ‣ S4.3 Federated assumptions, adversary, and TCB additions ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
By
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
the entire behaviour of a run of horizon $`n`$ from a sorted
configuration (its Protected-LLM operations, tool invocations, reply
stream, and ungated sink events) is a function
$`F(c_{0}^{\approx},\mathsf{DT},\omega,n)`$ of the initial
matched-configuration class
(Definition [S3.6](#A3.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S3.6 (Matched configurations). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
the run’s display transcript (the run suffix of
Definition [S3.8](#A3.Thmtheorem8 "Definition S3.8 (Display transcript). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
and the coins, with no residual dependence on
$`\mathcal{M}_{\mathsf{U}}`$. Consequently, for any observer who knows
these fixed inputs and the initial matched class, and any prior over
untrusted-store contents consistent with that class, the posterior after
observing the run to horizon $`n`$ equals the prior conditioned on
consistency with $`\mathsf{DT}`$ alone: knowledge about untrusted memory
increases only at display events, never through undisplayed behaviour.

###### Proof.

By
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
any two untrusted-store contents consistent with the same
$`\mathsf{DT}`$ (within the fixed initial matched class, matched coins,
coupled typed stream and slot skeleton,
conventions ([C1](#A1.I2.i1 "Item C1 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))/([C9](#A1.I2.i9 "Item C9 ‣ S1.3 Standing conventions ‣ Appendix S1 Structure of the Proof, Notation, and Conventions ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")))
yield identical behaviour, so the likelihood of the observed behaviour
is constant across such contents; Bayes’ rule then collapses the
posterior to the prior restricted to $`\mathsf{DT}`$-consistency. ∎

The observer here is granted $`\omega`$ and the typed stream, strictly
more than any real attacker knows. The statement is claimed for this
strong observer only: for an observer ignorant of $`\omega`$,
conditioning on the transcript can correlate the hidden store with the
coins, and behaviour may then reveal information about $`\omega`$ that,
jointly with the transcript, reveals more about untrusted memory than
the transcript alone; marginalising over $`\omega`$ therefore does not
yield the weaker-observer statement in general. Deployments wanting the
weaker-observer form may include the public coin outcomes in the release
history, whereupon this proposition applies verbatim with $`\omega`$
read as released.

#### S8.5 Zipf case study for the budget

This subsection instantiates the saturation cost bound
(Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"))
under a Zipf rank-popularity law, as a worked example;
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
needs only sublinear distinct-count growth (with
[A10](#Thmassumptionx10 "Assumption A10 (Temporal smoothness, fractional form). ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).
We caution that empirical rank exponents for human reference streams are
frequently at or below one [Breslau et al. (1999)](#bib.bib6), and the
rank/Heaps link has finite-size deviations [Lü et al.
(2010)](#bib.bib29); the clean rate below holds in the top-heavy regime
$`\alpha>1`$. Throughout, the demand-independent per-item cap is
$`\hat{N}:=A(M)`$ with $`A(M)`$ as in
Lemma [S8.18](#A8.Thmtheorem18 "Lemma S8.18 (Explicit forms of 𝐴(𝑀) and 𝐵_fl). ‣ S8.3 Explicit ledger constants ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the front-loaded part $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\bar{\gamma}\,n_{v}`$ of the
ledger is carried separately (after summation it contributes at most
$`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\bar{\gamma}\,d`$ per user, uniformly over the
popularity law), so the head/tail analysis concerns the $`\hat{N}`$
part, with the $`B_{\mathrm{fl}}\bar{\gamma}\,d`$ term added at the end.
The demand-independent invitation cap
$`K=E_{\max}(c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{p}}k+1)`$ of
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv)
is likewise carried separately, as $`K\,V(M)/M`$
(Lemma [S8.21](#A8.Thmtheorem21 "Lemma S8.21 (Head/tail decomposition). ‣ S8.5 Zipf case study for the budget ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"));
it plays no role in the head/tail split. When $`\hat{N}`$ grows with
$`M`$ (through $`N(M)`$, $`\kappa(M)`$, and $`f(M)`$ under co-scaling),
the head term below becomes
$`\hat{N}^{\,1-1/\alpha}Z^{-1/\alpha}M^{-(1-1/\alpha)}`$, which still
vanishes whenever $`A(M)=o(M)`$, amply covered by
$`A(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$.

###### Lemma S8.21 (Head/tail decomposition).

With head $`H_{M}=\{v:Mp_{v}\geq\hat{N}\}`$, tail
$`L_{M}=\mathcal{V}\setminus H_{M}`$, and
$`K=E_{\max}(c_{\mathrm{tool}}N^{+}+c_{\mathrm{p}}k+1)`$ as in
Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iv),
and with $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}_{M}]`$ read over the pipeline component
(Lemma [S6.7](#A6.Thmtheorem7 "Lemma S6.7 (Per-item confirmation ledger, 𝒪-form). ‣ S6.3 The per-item confirmation ledger ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the ledger residual adds the separately bounded term of
Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii)
on top, uniformly over the popularity law, vanishing under that
theorem’s additional rate conditions),

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}_{M}]\ \leq\ \frac{\hat{N}\,|H_{M}|}{M}+c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)+K\,\frac{V(M)}{M}+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d.
``` |  |

###### Proof.

Head items are bounded by clause (iii) alone
($`\mathbb{E}[C_{v}]\leq\hat{N}+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\bar{\gamma}\,\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]`$);
tail items by clause (iv) in expectation
($`\mathbb{E}[C_{v}]\leq c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,Mp_{v}+K\,\mathbb{P}[n_{v}\geq 1]`$,
since $`\mathbb{E}[n_{v}]=Mp_{v}`$); summing the head term and the
front-loaded parts over all items gives the first and last terms after
division by $`M`$; the tail items’ $`K`$-terms are further enlarged to
the all-items sum $`K\,V(M)`$, giving the third term. The quantity
$`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)`$ is the expected number of distinct tail items
a single user demands: sub-threshold demand not yet amortised. ∎

###### Theorem S8.22 (Zipf decay, head and tail).

Under $`p_{r}=r^{-\alpha}/Z`$ (read as the homogeneous special case
$`p_{u,v,t}\equiv p_{v,t}`$ of the reference model),
$`Z=\sum_{j=1}^{|\mathcal{V}|}j^{-\alpha}`$. Clauses (i)–(iii) concern
$`\alpha>1`$, where $`Z\leq\zeta(\alpha)`$:

1.  (i)
    rank $`r`$ is in the head iff
    $`r\leq R_{M}:=(M/(\hat{N}Z))^{1/\alpha}`$, so
    $`|H_{M}|=\min\{\lfloor R_{M}\rfloor,U\}\leq R_{M}`$ and
    $`\hat{N}|H_{M}|/M\leq Z^{-1/\alpha}\,(\hat{N}/M)^{1-1/\alpha}`$;
2.  (ii)
    let $`U:=|\mathcal{V}|`$ and $`m_{\star}:=\lfloor R_{M}\rfloor+1`$;
    for the finite universe,
    $`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)=\tfrac{1}{Z}\sum_{m_{\star}\leq r\leq U}r^{-\alpha}`$,
    empty (and zero) if $`m_{\star}>U`$. For $`m_{\star}\leq U`$, the
    floor-aware two-sided comparison
    $`\int_{m_{\star}}^{U+1}x^{-\alpha}\,dx\ \leq\ \sum_{r=m_{\star}}^{U}r^{-\alpha}\ \leq\ m_{\star}^{-\alpha}+\int_{m_{\star}}^{U}x^{-\alpha}\,dx`$
    gives

    |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \frac{m_{\star}^{1-\alpha}-(U{+}1)^{1-\alpha}}{Z(\alpha-1)}\ \leq\ \mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)\ \leq\ \frac{1}{Z}\Big(m_{\star}^{-\alpha}+\frac{m_{\star}^{1-\alpha}-U^{1-\alpha}}{\alpha-1}\Big)\ \leq\ \frac{1}{Z}\Big(R_{M}^{-\alpha}+\frac{R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha}}{\alpha-1}\Big),
    ``` |  |

    using $`m_{\star}>R_{M}`$ and $`\alpha>1`$; since
    $`R_{M}^{-\alpha}\leq R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha}`$ for $`R_{M}\geq 1`$, and
    $`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}\leq d=1`$ always (absorbing $`R_{M}<1`$),
    $`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)=\mathcal{O}\big((\hat{N}Z/M)^{1-1/\alpha}\big)`$
    uniformly; the matching lower order
    $`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}(M)=\Theta\big((\hat{N}Z/M)^{1-1/\alpha}\big)`$
    holds under the two additional (sufficient) non-saturation
    conditions $`R_{M}\to\infty`$ (equivalently $`\hat{N}Z/M\to 0`$) and
    $`U/R_{M}\to\infty`$: then $`m_{\star}/R_{M}\to 1`$, so
    $`m_{\star}^{1-\alpha}=(1+o(1))\,R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha}`$, and the
    $`m_{\star}^{-\alpha}`$ term and the $`U`$-corrections are
    $`o(R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha})`$. Neither condition may be omitted from
    this sufficient criterion in general: along a sequence with
    $`R_{M}\to\infty`$, taking $`U=m_{\star}`$ leaves a single tail term
    of order $`R_{M}^{-\alpha}=o(R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha})`$, so the matching
    order fails though $`R_{M}\to\infty`$ holds; while $`R_{M}\to 0`$ (a
    per-item cap outgrowing the population, e.g. $`U=Z=1`$,
    $`\hat{N}=M^{2}`$) leaves tail mass $`\Theta(1)`$ against a
    diverging comparison scale $`(\hat{N}Z/M)^{1-1/\alpha}`$, though
    $`U/R_{M}\to\infty`$ holds. For an infinite universe,
    $`U/R_{M}\to\infty`$ is automatic while $`R_{M}\to\infty`$ remains
    an additional requirement; $`R_{M}\to\infty`$ holds in the
    fixed-adversary, fixed-constants regime of
    Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii)
    and in the corridor of
    Theorem [S6.13](#A6.Thmtheorem13 "Theorem S6.13 (Joint scaling of safety, wrongful-eviction risk, and cost). ‣ Status of the corridor. ‣ S6.5 Conditional co-scaling ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    (where $`\hat{N}=A(M)=o(M^{1-\beta})`$), while $`U/R_{M}\to\infty`$
    remains a separate universe non-saturation condition in either
    regime. Part (iii) consumes only the uniform upper bound and
    requires neither condition;
3.  (iii)
    hence
    $`\mathbb{E}[\bar{C}_{M}]=\mathcal{O}\big((A(M)/M)^{1-1/\alpha}\big)+\mathcal{O}\big(K(M)\,V(M)/M\big)+B_{\mathrm{fl}}\,\bar{\gamma}\,d`$,
    plus the residual of
    Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(iii),
    the head and tail terms decaying at the common rate
    $`\mathcal{O}((A(M)/M)^{1-1/\alpha})`$ (as upper bounds) and the
    invitation term $`K\,V(M)/M`$ vanishing whenever $`K(M)\,V(M)=o(M)`$
    — under fixed protocol constants *with* $`f(M)=\mathcal{O}(1)`$ and
    $`\rho_{\mathrm{seat}}`$ bounded below ($`A(M),K(M)=\Theta(1)`$; the
    hypotheses of
    Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii))
    automatic, giving the clean rate
    $`\mathcal{O}(M^{-(1-1/\alpha)})+\mathcal{O}(V(M)/M)`$; under
    co-scaling,
    $`K(M)=\mathcal{O}(E_{\max}(c_{\mathrm{tool}}N+c_{\mathrm{p}}k))=o(M^{1-\beta})`$
    by the corridor schedules, so $`K\,V(M)/M=o(1)`$ exactly as for
    $`A(M)`$. The front-loading term survives exactly as in
    Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    vanishing under $`\bar{\gamma}(M)(1+\kappa(M))\to 0`$
    ([A13](#Thmassumptionx13 "Assumption A13 (Bounded per-user demand mass). ‣ Heuristic sufficiency and compatibility. ‣ S6.1 Model ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    is automatic here: $`d=\sum_{r}p_{r}=1`$).

For the boundary case $`\alpha=1`$, read along finite-universe sequences
$`U:=|\mathcal{V}|\to\infty`$, with
$`Z:=H_{U}=\sum_{r=1}^{U}r^{-1}=\ln U+\mathcal{O}(1)`$ and
$`R_{M}:=M/(\hat{N}Z)`$: in the nonempty-head regime $`1\leq R_{M}<U`$
(below universe saturation), $`R_{M}\sim M/(\hat{N}\ln U)`$ and the head
term $`\hat{N}|H_{M}|/M=\Theta(1/\ln U)`$ — the $`\hat{N}=A(M)`$
dependence cancels; for $`R_{M}<1`$ the head is empty and the head term
zero — while after universe saturation ($`R_{M}\geq U`$) the head term
equals $`\hat{N}\,U/M`$. For $`1\ll R_{M}<U`$, the tail sum
$`\sum_{R_{M}<r\leq U}r^{-1}/Z=\big(\ln(U/R_{M})+\mathcal{O}(1)\big)/\big(\ln U+\mathcal{O}(1)\big)`$,
governed by how far the head boundary sits below the universe; (floor
corrections at the boundary rank are absorbed into the
$`\mathcal{O}(1)`$; the tail is empty for $`m_{\star}>U`$); no power
rate is asserted without an explicit relation between $`U`$ and
$`R_{M}`$, decay being controlled by saturation rather than the
exponent, which is why the main development is stated for sublinear
distinct-count growth
(Remark [S8.23](#A8.Thmtheorem23 "Remark S8.23. ‣ S8.5 Zipf case study for the budget ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")).

###### Proof.

(i) $`Mp_{r}\geq\hat{N}\iff r\leq R_{M}`$, and
$`|H_{M}|=\min\{\lfloor R_{M}\rfloor,U\}\leq R_{M}=\mathcal{O}((M/\hat{N})^{1/\alpha})`$;
$`Z`$ is bounded for $`\alpha>1`$. (ii) with
$`m_{\star}=\lfloor R_{M}\rfloor+1`$: if $`m_{\star}>U`$ the tail is
empty and every bound holds trivially; otherwise apply the floor-aware
comparison as displayed (the lower bound from
$`r^{-\alpha}\geq\int_{r}^{r+1}x^{-\alpha}\,dx`$ termwise, the upper
from splitting off the first term and bounding the rest by
$`\int_{m_{\star}}^{U}x^{-\alpha}\,dx`$); dropping the nonnegative
$`U`$-terms and using $`m_{\star}>R_{M}`$ (so
$`m_{\star}^{-\alpha}<R_{M}^{-\alpha}`$ and
$`m_{\star}^{1-\alpha}<R_{M}^{1-\alpha}`$) yields the uniform upper
bound, with the trivial guard $`\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}\leq d=1`$ absorbing
$`R_{M}<1`$; under $`R_{M}\to\infty`$ and $`U/R_{M}\to\infty`$,
$`m_{\star}/R_{M}\to 1`$, so the floor correction is negligible, the
$`U`$-corrections and the $`m_{\star}^{-\alpha}`$ term are
$`o(R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha})`$, and both ends are
$`\Theta(R_{M}^{\,1-\alpha})`$, giving the matching order; substitute
$`R_{M}=(M/(\hat{N}Z))^{1/\alpha}`$. (iii) sum in
Lemma [S8.21](#A8.Thmtheorem21 "Lemma S8.21 (Head/tail decomposition). ‣ S8.5 Zipf case study for the budget ‣ Appendix S8 Probabilistic Tools and Supplementary Results ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
the tail term $`c_{\mathrm{tool}}\,\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}`$ absorbs the old
constant into $`\mathcal{O}(\cdot)`$, and the invitation term is
$`K\,V(M)/M`$ verbatim. The $`\alpha=1`$ clauses follow, along
$`U\to\infty`$, from $`R_{M}=M/(\hat{N}\ln U)(1+o(1))`$ read in the
regime $`R_{M}\geq 1`$ (where $`\lfloor R_{M}\rfloor\geq R_{M}/2`$; the
head is empty for $`R_{M}<1`$), cancellation of $`\hat{N}`$ in
$`\hat{N}R_{M}/M`$, the exact identity $`|H_{M}|=U`$ when
$`R_{M}\geq U`$ (where the tail is empty), and, separately in the
nonsaturated regime $`1\ll R_{M}<U`$, the harmonic-tail estimate
$`\sum_{R_{M}<r\leq U}r^{-1}=\ln(U/R_{M})+\mathcal{O}(1)`$ [Breslau
et al. (1999)](#bib.bib6). ∎

###### Remark S8.23.

The $`\alpha=1`$ boundary case is why the main development is stated in
terms of sublinear distinct-count growth
(Theorem [S6.9](#A6.Thmtheorem9 "Theorem S6.9 (Confirmation cost under saturation). ‣ S6.4 Saturation ‣ Appendix S6 The Memory-Verification Budget ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
which holds across $`\alpha`$: the Zipf form sharpens the rate in the
top-heavy regime $`\alpha>1`$ but is used nowhere in any proof.

### Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4

We mechanize the single-user core of PerMIT in Lean 4 (toolchain
leanprover/lean4:v4.31.0; Mathlib v4.31.0, revision fabf563a). The
development defines an executable interpreter for the memory interface
and proves
Theorems [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
over it for arbitrary Protected-LLM strategies, retrievers, attackers,
and horizons, within the deployment, input, and starting-state
conditions stated below. Building the development is the verification:
Lean’s kernel checks every theorem, and every executable scenario is a
build-time assertion.

###### Scope.

The mechanized surface is the single-user interface without run-level
batched iteration: tool invocation, $`\mathsf{write}_{P}`$,
$`\mathsf{recall}`$, $`\mathsf{fill}`$, $`\mathsf{crystallize}`$,
$`\mathsf{confirm}`$ (tool and reasoning targets),
$`\mathsf{retrieve}`$, $`\mathsf{display}`$, $`\mathsf{evict}`$, and the
typed and paste channels. The batch-confirmation surface of
Rule [R9](#Thmrulex9 "Rule R9 (Batch gate under untrusted-driven iteration). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is mechanized as a standalone layer. Paper arguments alone cover the
integration of $`\mathsf{map}`$ into the run-level interpreter, durable
endorsement on aborted invocations
(delta [6](#A9.I3.i6 "Item 6 ‣ Modeling deltas. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
arbitrary mid-run matched pairs, the index-oracle reduction
(delta [2](#A9.I3.i2 "Item 2 ‣ Modeling deltas. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")),
Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
beyond the gate level and
Option [O3](#Thmoptionx3 "Option O3 (Local scope leases (requirements level; not formally instantiated)). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
and the federated tier with every probabilistic and budget result.

###### Model.

The interpreter execOp is a total function with one arm per operation,
so every invocation has defined behavior
(Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(b)).
Its state IState represents the extended configuration of
Definition [S2.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Definition S2.6 (Extended configuration). ‣ S2.2 Operational semantics ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
subject to the modeling deltas below; the display transcript,
sensitive-sink log, and operation log are ghost state. Four modeling
choices carry the proofs.

- •
  *Replies.* The inductive type Reply (acknowledgment, handle, failure,
  decision, bytes) is the reply grammar of
  Rule [R10](#Thmrulex10 "Rule R10 (Constant-alphabet interface, with totality). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
  no other reply can be constructed. Bytes are returned only by
  $`\mathsf{recall}`$ of a non-$`\mathsf{U}`$ block and by trusted
  retrieval.
- •
  *Two-sorted identifiers.* Endorsed-sort identifiers (BlockId.e) are
  allocated only by coupled events: typed input, the agent’s writes, and
  accepted confirmations. Untrusted-sort identifiers (BlockId.u) are
  allocated by attacker-dependent events: the initial untrusted store,
  paste, tool-output capture, and crystallization. Every endorsement
  writes a fresh copy at the next endorsed-sort identifier.
- •
  *Views.* The Protected-LLM view Obs is computed from the endorsed
  store alone (memEOf), with the decision history, typed input, and
  handle count; the retriever likewise receives only the endorsed store.
- •
  *Actors.* The Protected LLM is an arbitrary function of its emitted
  operations, reply stream, view, and coins (PStrat). The attacker
  supplies the initial untrusted store, every tool output (count and
  content), every paste event, and the Quarantined Reader’s candidates
  and summaries. The user supplies the typed stream and the decision and
  selection at each confirmation.

###### Checked statements.

Table [S5](#A9.T5 "Table S5 ‣ Checked statements. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
gives the correspondence. Action Integrity is a projection of an
inductive invariant, Inv, established initially and preserved by every
transition. It is proved from the empty endorsed store and from any
state satisfying Inv. A precedence corollary places each endorsing
confirmation in the transcript that exists when the sink event is
recorded.

Reasoning Integrity is a lockstep simulation over MatchW, which equates
everything the Protected LLM can observe and everything the transcript
records, while leaving untrusted stores and hidden handle resolutions
free. It is proved from empty endorsed stores and from any shared
endorsed seed with independently chosen untrusted stores. Its
conclusions exceed what
Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
requires: equal transcripts force equal raw sink logs, operation
sequences, reply streams, and final views.

Proposition [S3.27](#A3.Thmtheorem27 "Proposition S3.27 (The taint-gating baseline fails Reasoning Integrity). ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
is witnessed by computation. A taint-gating baseline, with data taint
carried inside the model, yields equal (empty) transcripts but different
ungated sink projections. PerMIT’s interpreter under the analogous
strategy is attack-invariant.

Eight scenarios check, by computation:

- •
  the typed fast path;
- •
  a blocked injection;
- •
  endorsement followed by fast-path reuse;
- •
  occupancy hiding;
- •
  a finite noninterference instance;
- •
  attack-surface confinement;
- •
  ungated data-tool flow of agent-composed bytes;
- •
  the post-endorsement boundary, whose closure under
  Option [O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is witnessed in Hardening.lean.

###### Trusted base.

Lean’s kernel checks every theorem, and the build fails on any failed
proof or false \#guard. An omitted proof (sorry) produces only a
warning, so completeness rests on the \#print axioms report, reproduced
verbatim in the artifact’s README from a clean build. It shows that the
top-level theorems, and hence every lemma they use, depend only on
propext and Quot.sound, and none on sorryAx. The \#guard scenarios
additionally trust Lean’s evaluator. The correspondence between the
mechanized model and the paper’s semantics is not machine-checked;
Table [S5](#A9.T5 "Table S5 ‣ Checked statements. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and the deltas below argue it.

###### Modeling deltas.

None is silent. Deltas
[1](#A9.I3.i1 "Item 1 ‣ Modeling deltas. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
and
[3](#A9.I3.i3 "Item 3 ‣ Modeling deltas. ‣ Appendix S9 Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4 ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
strengthen the checked statements.

1.  (1)
    *Reader.* The Quarantined Reader is folded into the attacker, which
    chooses the reader’s candidates and summaries directly.
2.  (2)
    *Index oracles.* User decisions and selections, and attacker
    outputs, are functions of event ordinals. Any run of a reactive user
    or attacker is the run of the oracle equal to its realized sequence.
    In
    Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust"),
    both runs share the user oracle, and transcript equality pins every
    decision a display-reactive user makes (Supplement,
    Proposition [S3.29](#A3.Thmtheorem29 "Proposition S3.29 (Index-oracle coverage of display-reactive behaviour). ‣ Mechanization. ‣ S3.5 Baseline separation and hardening monotonicity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust");
    a paper argument).
3.  (3)
    *Channels.* Compared runs share only the slot skeleton and the typed
    stream; each attacker chooses paste presence and content
    independently.
4.  (4)
    *Starting states.*
    Theorem [S3.21](#A3.Thmtheorem21 "Theorem S3.21 (Personal Action Integrity). ‣ S3.3 Action Integrity ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    is proved from the empty endorsed store and from any state
    satisfying Inv.
    Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    is proved from empty or shared endorsed seeds, the canonical matched
    class of
    Definition [S3.5](#A3.Thmtheorem5 "Definition S3.5 (Sorted configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust").
    Arbitrary mid-run matched pairs are covered by the paper proof.
5.  (5)
    *Collection handles.* Without run-level $`\mathsf{map}`$, a handle
    to a multi-element capture is confirmed at a direct call by
    selecting one displayed element, so at most one displayed value
    flows per accepting decision.
6.  (6)
    *Aborted invocations.* The mechanized interpreter writes endorsed
    copies only when an invocation executes.
    Rule [R2](#Thmrulex2 "Rule R2 (Atomic gating; durable per-value endorsement). ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    also writes durable copies for the accepted positions of an aborted
    invocation; that case is covered by the paper proof only.
7.  (7)
    *Decision history.* The mechanized history also records the
    selection index and marks null-resolution aborts, so the mechanized
    view extends the paper’s $`h`$. The operation semantics do not
    inspect these extra fields; both are transcript-recorded and
    therefore agree in the matched executions used by the proof.
8.  (8)
    *Selections.* An out-of-range selection clamps to the first
    candidate; the flowed bytes remain the displayed bytes.
9.  (9)
    *Representation.* One typed event is one $`\mathsf{T}`$-block; bytes
    are lists of naturals; provenance marks are subsumed by labels and
    ghost logs. Inv checks endorsement against the transcript, without
    the sanitized-history record of
    Definition [S3.3](#A3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition S3.3 (Well-formed configuration). ‣ S3.1 Definitions ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(ii).
10. (10)
    *Outside the interpreter.*
    Options [O1](#Thmoptionx1 "Option O1 (Sink-scoped trusted values). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")–[O2](#Thmoptionx2 "Option O2 (Exact-target mediation at data tools). ‣ Deployment-selectable hardening. ‣ S2.3 Interface rules ‣ Appendix S2 Formal Specification of the Memory Interface ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
    are checked at the gate level only. The covered-gate and
    reasoning-coverage clauses of
    Rule [R13](#Thmrulex13 "Rule R13 (Dispute and demand-paced panel resolution). ‣ Required deployment parameters. ‣ S4.2 Protocol rules ‣ Appendix S4 The Federated Protocol (PerMIT-Attest) ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")(i)
    are federated accounting conventions, not transitions.

###### Specification corrections.

Mechanization corrected the specification in three places, each adopted
in the paper.

- •
  Endorsement must write a fresh copy at an operation-determined
  identifier. Relabeling the untrusted source in place would expose an
  attacker-dependent identifier in the endorsed store and break the
  matched-pair invariant; this is why identifiers are two-sorted.
- •
  Channel events must be acknowledged to the channel, not to the
  Protected LLM. Otherwise an uncoupled paste would emit a visible
  acknowledgment, and
  Theorem [S3.25](#A3.Thmtheorem25 "Theorem S3.25 (Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript). ‣ S3.4 Reasoning Integrity modulo the display transcript ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  would fail.
- •
  The fast-path case analysis of
  Lemma [S3.13](#A3.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma S3.13 (Whitelist mediation, by tool class). ‣ S3.2 Structural lemmas ‣ Appendix S3 Single-User Guarantees ‣ Part III Complete Formal Development ‣ PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agentsvia Machine-Checked Integrity Theoremsand Scalable Community Trust")
  is disjunctive: typed and endorsed matches may co-occur, and
  processArgs_spec proves exhaustiveness without exclusivity.
````
